paras.en: Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties, including those highlighted in the section titled “Risk Factors” immediately following this prospectus summary. These risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations, which could cause the market price of our Class A common stock to decline and could result in a loss of all or part of your investment. Additional risks, beyond those summarized below or discussed elsewhere in this prospectus, may apply to our business, activities, or operations as currently conducted or as we may conduct them in the future and in the markets in which we operate or may in the future operate. These risks include the following:
paras.zh: 我们的业务面临众多风险和不确定性，包括紧随本招股说明书摘要之后题为“风险因素”一节中重点提示的风险。这些风险可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响，进而可能导致我们的 A 类普通股市场价格下跌，并可能使您的全部或部分投资遭受损失。除下文概述或本招股说明书其他部分讨论的风险之外，还可能存在适用于我们当前开展或未来可能开展的业务、活动或运营，以及我们当前或未来可能经营所在市场的其他风险。这些风险包括以下各项：

paras.en: - Our success depends in large part on our ability to continue to develop the most advanced and capable AI models, and any failure to do so could adversely affect our business.
paras.zh: - 我们的成功在很大程度上取决于我们能否持续开发最先进、能力最强的 AI 模型，若未能做到，可能对我们的业务产生不利影响。

paras.en: - If we are unable to secure adequate compute or if we fail to direct our compute effectively across our workloads, we may be unable to train models that remain competitive with those of our competitors or adequately serve our customers.
paras.zh: - 如果我们无法获得充足的算力，或未能将算力在我们的各项工作负载之间有效配置，我们可能无法训练出与竞争对手相比仍具竞争力的模型，或无法充分服务我们的客户。

paras.en: - Constraints on the critical inputs supporting compute could limit our ability to secure adequate compute.
paras.zh: - 支撑算力的关键投入受到限制，可能制约我们获得充足算力的能力。

paras.en: - We are highly dependent on the continued service of our co-founders, senior management team, and key technical employees, and the loss of any of these individuals may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: - 我们高度依赖联合创始人、高级管理团队和关键技术人员持续任职，上述任何人员的流失都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: - Our company culture has contributed to our success and, if we cannot maintain this culture as we grow, our business could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: - 我们的公司文化为我们的成功作出了贡献，如果我们在发展过程中无法保持这一文化，我们的业务可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: - We face intense competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: - 我们面临激烈竞争，如果我们无法有效竞争，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: - If the market for our models, platform, and applications develops more slowly than we expect or declines, our growth may slow or stall, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: - 如果我们的模型、平台和应用所在市场的发展慢于我们的预期或出现萎缩，我们的增长可能放缓或停滞，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: - If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse, our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: - 如果使用我们的 AI 模型造成损害，无论是通过恶意行为者的使用还是其他第三方的滥用，或者如果我们的模型护栏或保障措施未能防止此类滥用，我们的声誉和品牌、业务、财务状况和经营成果可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: - Our AI models may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed, which could adversely affect our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: - 我们的 AI 模型可能以非预期、目标错位或自主的方式行事，包括采取任何用户或第三方均未指示的有害行为，这可能对我们的声誉和品牌、业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: - We may be exposed to liability, litigation, and regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models, and our contractual protections and insurance may be insufficient, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: - 我们可能因与我们的 AI 模型相关的损害而面临责任、诉讼和监管行动，且我们的合同保护和保险可能不足，上述任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: - A substantial portion of our revenue and accounts receivable is driven by a limited number of customers and distribution channels, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in, spend from one or more of our top customers or disruption through those channels could adversely affect our prospects, business, and financial condition.
paras.zh: - 我们的收入和应收账款中有相当大一部分由数量有限的客户和分销渠道驱动，失去一个或多个最大客户，或来自这些客户的支出大幅减少，或通过这些渠道出现中断，都可能对我们的前景、业务和财务状况产生不利影响。

paras.en: - We have a limited operating history in an evolving and nascent industry, which makes it difficult to evaluate our future prospects and may increase the risk that we will not be successful.
paras.zh: - 我们在一 个不断演变的新兴行业中运营历史有限，这使得难以评估我们的未来前景，并可能增加我们无法成功的风险。

paras.en: - We are at an early stage of our revenue growth, we have experienced rapid growth in recent periods, and our historical growth rates are not indicative of future performance or our ability to sustain or forecast future revenue growth.
paras.zh: - 我们正处于收入增长的早期阶段，近年来经历了快速增长，我们的历史增长率并不预示未来业绩，也不代表我们有能力维持或预测未来的收入增长。

paras.en: - Our business is subject to an evolving and uncertain regulatory and political environment, which could increase our costs, restrict our operations, or adversely affect demand for our models, platform, and applications.
paras.zh: - 我们的业务受到不断演变且不确定的监管和政治环境影响，这可能增加我们的成本、限制我们的运营，或对我们模型、平台和应用程序的需求产生不利影响。

paras.en: - Our reliance on a limited number of CSPs and suppliers, some of which have strategic and investment relationships with us and are our customers, creates complex dynamics that could give rise to conflicts of interest and adversely affect our access to compute.
paras.zh: - 我们对数量有限的云服务商（CSP）和供应商的依赖——其中一些与我们存在战略和投资关系，并且是我们的客户——形成了复杂的动态，可能引发利益冲突，并对我们获取算力产生不利影响。

paras.en: - Our capital stock structure features certain provisions that are novel or otherwise not common among other corporations with multiple-class structures, and may effectively eliminate the ability of holders of our Class A common stock to influence important decisions, including a change in control.
paras.zh: - 我们的股本结构具有某些新颖或在其他多类别结构公司中并不常见的条款，可能实际上消除我们 A 类普通股持有人影响重要决策（包括控制权变更）的能力。

paras.en: - Our capital structure will concentrate voting power with the LTBT and the Founder LLC for the foreseeable future and will result in the LTBT and the Founder LLC having voting power that is not derived from or proportionate to economic interests in our company.
paras.zh: - 在可预见的未来，我们的资本结构将使投票权集中于长期利益信托（LTBT）和创始人有限责任公司，并将导致长期利益信托（LTBT）和创始人有限责任公司拥有的投票权并非源自或按比例对应于本公司的经济利益。

paras.en: - Our focus on the long-term best interests of our company as a PBC, and the duty of our directors to balance the pecuniary interests of our stockholders, the best interests of those stakeholders materially affected by our conduct, and our Company Purpose, may conflict with short-, medium-, or long-term financial interests and business performance, which may negatively impact the value of our Class A common stock.
paras.zh: - 作为公益公司（PBC），我们对公司长期最佳利益的关注，以及我们的董事在平衡股东金钱利益、受我们行为重大影响的利益相关方的最佳利益与我们的公司宗旨方面的义务，可能与短期、中期或长期财务利益和业务表现相冲突，这可能对我们 A 类普通股的价值产生负面影响。

paras.en: The principal purposes of this offering are to increase our capitalization and financial flexibility, create a public market for our Class A common stock, facilitate an orderly distribution of shares for the selling stockholders, and enable access to the public equity markets for us and our stockholders. We intend to use the net proceeds from this offering for general corporate purposes, including working capital, operating expenses, and capital expenditures, including investments in compute and infrastructure, as well as hiring and retention of highly skilled personnel. Additionally, we may use a portion of the net proceeds to acquire or invest in businesses, products, services, or technologies. However, we do not have agreements or commitments for any material acquisitions or investments at this time. We also intend to use a portion of the net proceeds to satisfy our anticipated tax withholding and remittance obligations related to the settlement of certain of our outstanding restricted stock units (“RSUs”). See the section titled “Use of Proceeds” for more information.
paras.zh: 本次发行的主要目的是增加我们的资本和财务灵活性、为我们的 A 类普通股建立公开市场、促进出售股东有序分配股份，并使我们及我们的股东能够进入公开股票市场。我们拟将本次发行的净收益用于一般公司用途，包括营运资金、经营费用和资本支出（包括对算力和基础设施的投资），以及招聘和留用高技能人员。此外，我们可能将部分净收益用于收购或投资于业务、产品、服务或技术。但是，我们目前没有任何重大收购或投资的协议或承诺。我们还拟将部分净收益用于履行与结算我们某些未偿限制性股票单位（“RSU”）相关的预计税款代扣代缴和汇缴义务。更多信息请参见标题为“募集资金用途”的章节。

paras.en: Voting rights per share. Shares of our Class N common stock have no voting rights, except as otherwise required by law. The share of our Class T common stock has no voting rights with respect to matters submitted to stockholders generally, except as set forth within our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, including with respect to the election of a majority of our board of directors or as required by law. The share of our Class F common stock will be entitled to an aggregate number of votes that represents 50.1% of the total voting power of our outstanding shares as of the applicable record date on all matters submitted to a vote of stockholders generally, including the election of the directors other than the Class T directors. Shares of our Class E common stock will be entitled to one vote per share with respect to certain limited matters.

full.sec: Risks Related to our Business and Industry
full.secZh: 与我们的业务和行业相关的风险

paras.en: **Our success depends in large part on our ability to continue to develop the most advanced and capable AI models, and any failure to do so could adversely affect our business.**
paras.zh: **我们的成功在很大程度上取决于我们能否持续开发最先进、最强大的 AI 模型，若未能做到，可能对我们的业务产生不利影响。**

paras.en: Our success depends in large part on our ability to continuously develop, improve, and deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models. Achieving and maintaining this position depends on our ability to:
paras.zh: 我们的成功在很大程度上取决于我们能否持续开发、改进和部署最先进、最强大且最有用的 AI 模型。实现并保持这一地位取决于我们能否：

paras.en: - advance the frontier of AI capabilities through breakthrough research, innovative architectures, and efficient training methodologies;
paras.zh: - 通过突破性研究、创新架构和高效训练方法，推进 AI 能力的前沿；

paras.en: - ensure our models are safe, reliable, and trustworthy while maintaining competitive performance;
paras.zh: - 确保我们的模型安全、可靠、值得信赖，同时保持有竞争力的性能；

paras.en: - secure the compute and infrastructure necessary to power and support our increasing needs;
paras.zh: - 获取为满足我们日益增长的需求提供动力和支持所需的算力和基础设施；

paras.en: - advance compute efficiency through algorithmic and architectural innovations, including compute multiplier advancements;
paras.zh: - 通过算法和架构创新（包括算力乘数的进步）提升算力效率；

paras.en: - retain the continued service of our co-founders, senior management team, and key technical employees, and attract, retain, and motivate leading researchers, engineers, and technical talent in an intensely competitive and evolving market;
paras.zh: - 留住我们的联合创始人、高级管理团队和关键技术人员继续任职，并在竞争激烈且不断变化的市场中吸引、留住和激励顶尖研究人员、工程师和技术人才；

paras.en: - continue revenue growth and maintain access to sufficient capital, including through potential equity and debt financing, to make the investments we believe are necessary to support our growth trajectory;
paras.zh: - 持续实现收入增长并保持获得充足资本的能力（包括通过潜在的股权和债务融资），以进行我们认为支持增长轨迹所必需的投资；

paras.en: - secure and maintain relationships with data providers, licensors, and partners to obtain the diverse, high-quality datasets necessary for world-class model performance;
paras.zh: - 建立并维持与数据提供方、许可方和合作伙伴的关系，以获取世界级模型性能所需的多样化、高质量数据集；

paras.en: - secure and maintain relationships with cloud, ecosystem, and other partners to facilitate the diffusion of Claude;
paras.zh: - 建立并维持与云、生态系统及其他合作伙伴的关系，以促进 Claude 的推广；

paras.en: - build, operate, and maintain the infrastructure required to deploy frontier models cost-effectively and at scale;
paras.zh: - 建设、运营和维护以具有成本效益的方式大规模部署前沿模型所需的基础设施；

paras.en: - translate model capabilities into products that meet evolving customer needs and achieve meaningful adoption;
paras.zh: - 将模型能力转化为满足不断变化的客户需求并实现有意义采用的产品；

paras.en: - allocate substantial financial resources efficiently across research, infrastructure, and operations; and
paras.zh: - 在研发、基础设施和运营之间高效配置大量财务资源；以及

paras.en: - navigate an evolving, uncertain, and at times divergent global regulatory landscape and engage with legislators, regulators, and other stakeholders to promote the development of regulatory frameworks that we believe are good for society, our customers, and the long-term health of the global economy.
paras.zh: - 应对不断演变、充满不确定性且有时存在分歧的全球监管格局，并与立法者、监管机构及其他利益相关方沟通，以推动建立我们认为有益于社会、我们的客户以及全球经济长期健康的监管框架。

paras.en: Our failure to achieve any of the foregoing could prevent us from maintaining our competitive position, cause us to fall behind competitors, reduce customer adoption of, or demand for, our models, platform, and applications, and impair our revenue growth. Limitations to our revenue growth could, in turn, constrain our ability to fund the substantial and increasing expenditures required for frontier AI development, including investments in compute, model training, data acquisition, and safety and security systems, as well as our ability to attract, retain, and appropriately compensate highly skilled technical and operational personnel in a highly competitive market. Any such constraints could slow our rate of development and innovation, degrade model performance or reliability relative to competitors, limit our participation in industry standards-setting and regulatory processes, and reduce our attractiveness to enterprises and prosumers. These effects could create a self-reinforcing or compounding cycle in which diminished growth limits our capacity to invest in the resources necessary to remain competitive, which in turn could further weaken our ability to sustain or increase our revenue growth, making it increasingly difficult and costly to regain technological leadership and operate at the frontier of AI. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们若未能实现上述任何一项，都可能使我们无法维持竞争地位，导致我们落后于竞争对手，降低客户对我们模型、平台和应用的采用率或需求，并损害我们的收入增长。收入增长受限反过来可能制约我们为前沿 AI 开发所需的巨额且不断增加的支出提供资金的能力，包括在算力、模型训练、数据获取以及安全与安保系统方面的投资，以及我们在竞争激烈的市场中吸引、留住并合理补偿高技能技术和运营人员的能力。任何此类制约都可能减缓我们的开发和创新速度，使模型性能或可靠性相对竞争对手下降，限制我们参与行业标准制定和监管流程，并降低我们对企业和专业消费者的吸引力。这些影响可能形成自我强化或不断累积的循环：增长减弱限制了我们投资于保持竞争力所需资源的能力，而这反过来又可能进一步削弱我们维持或提高收入增长的能力，使我们越来越难以且越来越高昂地重新获得技术领先地位并在 AI 前沿开展运营。上述任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: Our ability to maintain our position at the frontier of AI depends in part on our use of AI systems to accelerate our research processes, a recursive dynamic we refer to as “closing the loop,” in which successive versions of our models assist in building the next, with the goal of compounding capability gains over time. Our models have been and are increasingly becoming critical tools in designing, training, testing, and optimizing next-generation AI systems. If we fail to direct sufficient compute and research efforts to AI-assisted development, or if our competitors more effectively leverage AI to enhance their own innovation cycles, we risk falling progressively further behind as competitors continuously use AI to further enhance their own development capabilities, enabling the creation of increasingly advanced systems at an accelerating pace. As our reliance on our own AI systems to write production code, conduct research, and build subsequent model versions deepens, any systemic flaw, bias, or error in our current models could propagate into the next versions of models and products built using those systems, compounding across successive versions of Claude models in ways that may be difficult to detect or remediate. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our ability to deploy the most advanced, capable, and useful AI models could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们能否保持在 AI 前沿的地位，部分取决于我们利用 AI 系统加速研究流程的能力，我们将这种递归动态称为“闭环”，即模型的 successive 版本协助构建下一代模型，目标是随时间推移实现能力增益的复利效应。我们的模型一直是、并且正日益成为设计、训练、测试和优化下一代 AI 系统的关键工具。如果我们未能将足够的算力和研究投入引导至 AI 辅助开发，或者如果我们的竞争对手更有效地利用 AI 来增强其自身的创新周期，我们就有可能随着竞争对手持续利用 AI 进一步增强其自身开发能力、以加速的步伐创造出日益先进的系统而逐步落后。随着我们越来越依赖自身的 AI 系统来编写生产代码、开展研究并构建后续模型版本，我们当前模型中的任何系统性缺陷、偏差或错误都可能传播到使用这些系统构建的下一代模型和产品中，在 successive 版本的 Claude 模型之间以可能难以检测或补救的方式不断累积。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们部署最先进、最强大、最有用的 AI 模型的能力可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, our increasing use of AI systems to accelerate our own research and development may cause the capabilities of our models to advance more rapidly than our ability to develop, validate, and implement corresponding safety, alignment, and security measures. Much of our evidence regarding the pace of such AI-driven acceleration is derived from lagging indicators, and our ability to forecast or measure the rate at which our capabilities are advancing, including any acceleration attributable to our most recent or unreleased models, is limited. As a result, we may not identify a significant acceleration in our rate of development until after it has occurred. If our capabilities were to outpace our safety, alignment, and security measures, or if we were unable to anticipate the pace of such advancement, we may be unable to adequately assess or mitigate the resulting risks, which could increase the likelihood of safety incidents, regulatory intervention, or reputational harm, and could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. In light of these uncertainties, including limits on our ability to observe the pace at which our capabilities are advancing, we have adopted, and may continue to adopt, precautionary safety, alignment, and security measures to allow our safety efforts to advance together with model capabilities. In the past these measures have included delaying the release of models and limiting their initial availability, such as with Mythos through Project Glasswing, and in the future, as we learn more about model capabilities and behavior, they could include additional measures that affect whether, how, and when we develop or deploy new models or capabilities. We cannot predict with precision when we will determine that such measures are necessary, what measures will be required, or how long they will remain in place, and as the capabilities of our models advance, such measures may become more frequent and more costly. These measures could slow our capability gains relative to competitors that do not adopt similar constraints, and could adversely affect our competitive position, revenue growth, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，我们日益使用 AI 系统来加速自身的研发，可能导致我们模型能力的提升速度快于我们开发、验证和实施相应安全、对齐与保障措施的能力。关于此类 AI 驱动加速步伐的许多证据来自滞后指标，而我们预测或衡量自身能力提升速度（包括归因于我们最新或尚未发布模型的任何加速）的能力有限。因此，我们可能在开发速度出现显著加速之后才能识别到这一加速。如果我们的能力提升超出我们的安全、对齐与保障措施，或者我们无法预见此类提升的步伐，我们可能无法充分评估或缓解由此产生的风险，这可能增加安全事故、监管干预或声誉损害的可能性，并可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。鉴于这些不确定性，包括我们观察自身能力提升步伐的能力存在局限，我们已采取并可能继续采取预防性的安全、对齐与保障措施，以使我们的安全工作与模型能力同步推进。过去，这些措施包括推迟模型发布并限制其初始可用范围，例如通过 Project Glasswing 对 Mythos 的处理；未来，随着我们对模型能力和行为了解得更多，这些措施可能包括影响我们是否、如何以及何时开发或部署新模型或新能力的额外措施。我们无法精确预测何时会认定此类措施必要、需要采取哪些措施或这些措施将持续多久，而且随着我们模型能力的提升，此类措施可能变得更加频繁且成本更高。这些措施可能使我们的能力提升相对于未采取类似限制的竞争对手放缓，并可能对我们的竞争地位、收入增长和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: The development of frontier AI models requires substantial investments of compute resources, capital, and human capital to conduct large-scale training runs that may span weeks or months and cost many million s of dollars. There is no guarantee that any given training run will succeed—a run may fail for a number of reasons, such as failing to achieve the targeted capability or safety thresholds, producing unexpected or undesirable behaviors that cannot be adequately remediated, or yielding a model that is ultimately not competitive with alternatives available in the market. We would also face the additional cost and delay of initiating a new training run to attempt to achieve the intended model improvements. We have in the past experienced, and may in the future experience, such failed or underperforming training runs, resulting in a loss of invested resources with limited or no corresponding benefit to our business. Given the scale of compute and other resources required for frontier model training and the extended timelines involved, a failed or underperforming training run could also delay our product roadmap, affect our competitive position, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 前沿 AI 模型的开发需要投入大量算力资源、资金和人力资本，以开展大规模训练运行，此类训练可能持续数周或数月，并耗费数百万美元。无法保证任何一次训练运行都能成功——一次训练运行可能因多种原因失败，例如未能达到目标能力或安全阈值、产生无法充分补救的意外或不良行为，或产出的模型最终无法与市场上的替代方案竞争。我们还将面临启动新的训练运行以尝试实现预期模型改进所带来的额外成本和延迟。我们过去曾经历、未来也可能经历此类失败或表现不佳的训练运行，导致投入的资源损失，而对我们业务产生的相应收益有限甚至没有。鉴于前沿模型训练所需的算力和其他资源规模以及所涉时间跨度较长，一次失败或表现不佳的训练运行还可能延误我们的产品路线图、影响我们的竞争地位，并对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, new models, features, or capabilities may not be introduced on schedule, may not perform as intended, may require significant iteration after release, may fail to gain meaningful adoption, or may take longer than expected to gain meaningful adoption, any of which could reduce customer demand or place us at a competitive disadvantage. In addition, considerations relating to model safety, interpretability, alignment, and welfare may lead us to limit or delay the deprecation of older models or to continue supporting legacy versions alongside newer releases, creating trade-offs in product development and compute distribution that could adversely affect innovation velocity, infrastructure utilization, and revenue. In addition, customers who have integrated older models into their workflows may resist migration to newer versions, and any accelerated or forced deprecation could result in customer attrition, contractual disputes, or reputational harm. We have also changed, and may in the future change, usage limits, rate limits, or model and product capabilities, which could adversely affect our reputation and the perceived value of our offerings. Some of these changes have resulted, and could in the future result, in claims that our disclosures regarding model access or capabilities were inadequate or misleading.
paras.zh: 此外，新模型、新功能或新能力可能无法按计划推出，可能无法达到预期表现，可能在发布后需要大量迭代，可能无法获得有意义的采用，或可能需要比预期更长的时间才能获得有意义的采用，其中任何一项都可能降低客户需求或使我们处于竞争劣势。此外，与模型安全、可解释性、对齐和福祉相关的考量可能导致我们限制或推迟旧模型的弃用，或在发布新版本的同时继续支持旧版本，从而在产品开发和算力分配方面形成权衡，可能对创新速度、基础设施利用率和收入产生不利影响。此外，已将旧模型集成到其工作流程中的客户可能抵制迁移到新版本，任何加速或强制弃用都可能导致客户流失、合同纠纷或声誉损害。我们过去也曾改变、未来也可能改变使用限制、速率限制或模型和产品能力，这可能对我们的声誉和我们产品的感知价值产生不利影响。其中部分变更已经导致、未来也可能导致相关主张，即我们关于模型访问或能力的披露不充分或具有误导性。

paras.en: Further, the industry benchmarks commonly used to test AI models may not accurately reflect real-world performance or utility, and even models that perform well on such benchmarks may not meet customer expectations when deployed in production environments, which could lead to customer dissatisfaction, reduced usage, or reputational harm. If we are unable to effectively innovate and improve our models, platform, and applications while addressing these challenges, or if competitors are able to deliver AI solutions that are perceived as more capable, safer, or more reliable, or that offer adequate performance at a lower cost, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 此外，用于测试 AI 模型的行业基准可能无法准确反映真实世界的性能或效用，即使是在此类基准上表现良好的模型，在部署到生产环境时也可能无法满足客户预期，这可能导致客户不满、使用量下降或声誉受损。如果我们无法在应对这些挑战的同时有效创新并改进我们的模型、平台和应用，或者如果竞争对手能够提供被认为能力更强、更安全或更可靠，或以更低成本提供足够性能的 AI 解决方案，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, innovation in AI involves addressing complex and evolving challenges related to data quality, data integrity, training methodologies, bias, safety, accuracy, and the behavior of model outputs. AI algorithms may be flawed, and AI systems may contain bugs, errors, or defects or fail to follow instructions or produce inaccurate, misleading, offensive, inappropriate, or otherwise harmful outputs; reflect or amplify unwanted or unknown biases present in training data; or raise concerns relating to intellectual property, privacy, or other legal and ethical considerations. We must continually invest resources to identify, mitigate, remediate, and reduce the occurrence of such issues, including through managing and improving datasets, training techniques, evaluation methods, safeguards, and human oversight. However, we may not be able to obtain the datasets that we need, including through licenses or strategic data partnerships. In addition, we or our data providers may use synthetic or AI-generated data in the training process, which could introduce quality issues, amplify biases or errors, contribute to model degradation, or raise novel legal questions regarding ownership, licensing, or intellectual property rights that may not be timely or clearly resolved by courts or regulators. Such unintended consequences, failures, or misuse of our models could impair customer trust, slow adoption, expose us to legal or regulatory scrutiny, or adversely affect our brand and reputation.
paras.zh: 此外，AI 领域的创新涉及应对与数据质量、数据完整性、训练方法、偏见、安全性、准确性以及模型输出行为相关的复杂且不断演变的挑战。AI 算法可能存在缺陷，AI 系统可能包含漏洞、错误或缺陷，或未能遵循指令，或产生不准确、误导性、冒犯性、不当或其他有害的输出；反映或放大训练数据中存在的不希望出现或未知的偏见；或引发与知识产权、隐私或其他法律和伦理考量相关的担忧。我们必须持续投入资源，以识别、缓解、补救并减少此类问题的发生，包括通过管理和改进数据集、训练技术、评估方法、防护措施和人工监督。然而，我们可能无法获得所需的数据集，包括通过许可或战略数据合作的方式。此外，我们或我们的数据提供方可能在训练过程中使用合成数据或 AI 生成的数据，这可能引入质量问题、放大偏见或错误、导致模型退化，或引发关于所有权、许可或知识产权的新颖法律问题，而法院或监管机构可能无法及时或明确地解决这些问题。此类意外后果、故障或对我们模型的滥用可能损害客户信任、减缓采用、使我们面临法律或监管审查，或对我们的品牌和声誉造成不利影响。

paras.en: **If we are unable to secure adequate compute or if we fail to direct our compute effectively across our workloads, we may be unable to train models that remain competitive with those of our competitors or adequately serve our customers.**
paras.zh: **如果我们无法获得充足的算力，或未能有效地将算力分配到我们的各项工作负载中，我们可能无法训练出与竞争对手相比仍具竞争力的模型，或无法充分服务我们的客户。**

paras.en: Our ability to develop, train, improve, and deploy frontier models depends on our access to enormous and increasing quantities of specialized compute. The training of Claude models has required, and we expect will continue to require, substantial compute. Industry participants, academic researchers, and our own experience suggest that, in certain contexts, applying greater amounts of compute during model training has been associated with improvements in model capabilities. These observations are consistent with aspects of broader empirical relationships among model performance, model size, training data, and compute scale that are commonly referred to as “Scaling Laws,” although the extent, efficiency, and durability of such improvements are uncertain, and these relationships may plateau, diminish, or fail to materialize at larger scales or under different conditions. Accordingly, our ability to remain at the frontier of AI capabilities is substantially dependent on our ability to secure compute at the scale required to sustain all our workloads, including to train next-generation models, and we cannot provide assurance that increased investment in compute will result in commensurate improvements in model performance.
paras.zh: 我们开发、训练、改进和部署前沿模型的能力，取决于我们能否获取海量且不断增长的专业算力。Claude 模型的训练一直需要大量算力，我们预计未来仍将持续需要大量算力。行业参与者、学术研究人员以及我们自身的经验表明，在某些情境下，在模型训练过程中投入更多算力与模型能力的提升相关。这些观察结果与模型性能、模型规模、训练数据和算力规模之间更广泛的经验性关系中的某些方面相一致，这些关系通常被称为“规模定律”（Scaling Laws），尽管此类提升的程度、效率和持久性尚不确定，且这些关系在更大规模或不同条件下可能趋于平缓、减弱或无法实现。因此，我们能否保持在 AI 能力的前沿，在很大程度上取决于我们能否获得维持全部工作负载（包括训练下一代模型）所需的算力规模，且我们无法保证增加算力投入会带来模型性能的相应提升。

paras.en: The market for compute is intensely competitive. We compete for access to compute with some of the world’s largest and most well-capitalized technology companies, many of which develop their own competitive AI models and have significantly greater financial resources than us. Many own and operate cloud computing data center infrastructure, maintain captive chip manufacturing or design capabilities, have long-standing strategic relationships with key hardware suppliers, or have significant equity investments from, or other financial arrangements with, such suppliers. These competitors can outbid us for scarce compute, secure priority allocations from chip manufacturers and CSPs, and make long-term capital commitments that we cannot match. We expect demand for advanced compute to continue to grow, and the cost of compute could rise significantly, particularly if AI-driven demand accelerates or if the ability to build highly capable models becomes more broadly available and shifts competition toward access to advanced compute. Additionally, numerous well-funded AI companies are pursuing large-scale AI model development, further increasing demand for limited compute. Certain CSPs from which we obtain substantial compute also develop and offer their own AI models and related services. As a result, our commercial relationships with these providers may not always be fully aligned with our long-term interests, and if the compute we have access to from third parties is curtailed, repriced, or terminated, whether for competitive reasons or otherwise, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 算力市场竞争激烈。我们在获取算力方面与全球一些规模最大、资本最雄厚的科技公司展开竞争，其中许多公司开发自己的竞争性 AI 模型，并拥有远超我们的财务资源。许多公司拥有并运营云计算数据中心基础设施，具备自有的芯片制造或设计能力，与关键硬件供应商保持着长期战略关系，或获得此类供应商的重大股权投资或其他财务安排。这些竞争对手能够在稀缺算力上出价高于我们，从芯片制造商和云服务商（CSP）处获得优先分配，并做出我们无法匹敌的长期资本承诺。我们预计对先进算力的需求将持续增长，算力成本可能大幅上升，尤其是当 AI 驱动的需求加速增长，或构建高能力模型的能力变得更加普及、从而使竞争转向对先进算力的获取时。此外，众多资金充裕的 AI 公司正在推进大规模 AI 模型开发，进一步加剧了对有限算力的需求。我们从中获取大量算力的某些 CSP 也开发和提供自己的 AI 模型及相关服务。因此，我们与这些供应商的商业关系可能并非始终与我们的长期利益完全一致，如果我们从第三方获取的算力被削减、重新定价或终止（无论出于竞争原因还是其他原因），我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition to competition from third parties, our ability to secure compute is subject to allocation decisions by our CSPs. Although our CSPs are generally subject to contractual commitments with us regarding the provision of compute, our ability to obtain such capacity remains dependent on those providers’ operational execution, adherence to the terms of such contractual provisions, and broader business considerations, such as capacity constraints, internal demand for compute to support their own AI and computing operations, relationships with or contractual obligations to third parties (which may include other AI companies), and risk management considerations. As a result, we may not receive the full amount of compute we seek, or such compute may not be delivered on the timelines we require, even where contractual arrangements are in place. Additionally, we have in the past sought quantities of compute from CSPs in excess of what those partners were willing to provide. If our CSPs reduce, limit, or fail to increase our allocations to keep pace with our growing requirements for any reason, we may need to seek alternative compute sources on less favorable terms or timelines, and we may be unable to secure adequate alternative compute, or any at all. Any such shortfall could constrain our ability to train models, serve customers, or maintain our competitive position.
paras.zh: 除来自第三方的竞争外，我们获取算力的能力还受制于我们云服务商（CSP）的分配决策。尽管我们的云服务商通常就提供算力与我们订有合同承诺，但我们能否获得该等算力仍取决于这些供应商的运营执行情况、是否遵守该等合同条款，以及更广泛的商业考量，例如产能限制、为支持其自身 AI 与计算业务而对算力的内部需求、与第三方（可能包括其他 AI 公司）的关系或合同义务，以及风险管理方面的考量。因此，即使已有合同安排，我们仍可能无法获得我们所寻求的全部算力，或该等算力可能无法按我们要求的时间表交付。此外，我们过去曾向云服务商寻求的算力数量超出这些合作伙伴愿意提供的数量。如果我们的云服务商出于任何原因减少、限制或未能增加对我们的分配以跟上我们不断增长的需求，我们可能需要在更不利的条款或时间表下寻求替代算力来源，并且我们可能无法获得充足的替代算力，甚至完全无法获得。任何此类短缺都可能制约我们训练模型、服务客户或维持竞争地位的能力。

paras.en: Even if we are able to secure compute, we must still direct it efficiently across the full range of workloads that are a part of our business, including research, model development, serving customers, and internal usage of Claude. While we manage our compute as a single, fungible pool and direct available compute between workloads based on where the marginal unit is expected to be most productive at any given time, there can be no assurance that this approach to compute will be the most efficient or that it will support the needs of each of our workloads. Because demand for compute has historically exceeded available capacity, any constraint on our ability to procure, maintain, or expand that capacity could adversely affect multiple aspects of our business simultaneously, including our ability to serve customers at the quality and scale they expect, to train and improve our models, and to develop new products and capabilities. While we actively manage and balance such compute capacity across these workloads via our capacity management system, if this system fails to perform as intended, or if our ability to dynamically rebalance capacity across workloads is disrupted, customer-facing service quality or model and product development timelines could be adversely affected. There can be no assurance that we will make optimal resourcing decisions, and any significant inefficiencies, including those related to deployment and rebalancing, could adversely affect both our near-term results of operations and our long-term strategic position. These compute resourcing challenges are heightened by the growth of our agentic offerings, which involve multi-step reasoning chains, iterative tool invocations, extended context windows, and sustained inference sessions that consume significantly more compute per user interaction than single-turn API calls or chat-based interactions. As agentic workloads grow as a proportion of our total compute demand, the aggregate compute required to serve our customers could increase disproportionately relative to the associated revenue, placing additional strain on our compute workload management decisions.
paras.zh: 即使我们能够获得算力，我们仍必须在业务所涉及的各类工作负载之间高效地分配算力，包括研究、模型开发、服务客户以及 Claude 的内部使用。尽管我们将算力作为一个单一、可互换的资源池进行管理，并根据在任意给定时间边际单位预计最具生产力的方向在工作负载之间调配可用算力，但无法保证这种算力管理方式是最有效的，也无法保证其能够满足我们每一项工作负载的需求。由于算力需求历来超过可用容量，任何对我们获取、维持或扩展该容量能力的限制，都可能同时对我们业务的多个方面产生不利影响，包括我们以客户期望的质量和规模服务客户的能力、训练和改进模型的能力，以及开发新产品和新能力的能力。尽管我们通过容量管理系统在这些工作负载之间积极管理和平衡此类算力容量，但如果该系统未能按预期运行，或者我们跨工作负载动态重新平衡容量的能力受到干扰，面向客户的服务质量或模型和产品开发时间表可能会受到不利影响。无法保证我们会做出最优的资源配置决策，任何重大低效（包括与部署和重新平衡相关的低效）都可能对我们近期的经营业绩和长期战略地位产生不利影响。我们的智能体产品增长加剧了这些算力资源配置挑战，此类产品涉及多步推理链、迭代式工具调用、扩展上下文窗口和持续推理会话，每次用户交互消耗的算力显著高于单轮 API 调用或基于聊天的交互。随着智能体工作负载在我们总算力需求中所占比例增长，服务客户所需的总算力可能相对于相关收入出现不成比例的增长，从而给我们算力工作负载管理决策带来额外压力。

paras.en: The majority of our compute is procured under multi-year commitments that are typically entered into well in advance of the periods in which that compute is deployed. Because different AI accelerators have varying performance characteristics across workload types, the composition of our committed compute portfolio, including the mix of accelerator architectures procured from our partners, reflects our demand forecasts and development roadmap assumptions at the time those commitments are made. If the magnitude or mix of workloads we need to support differs materially from those forecasts, whether due to changes in model architecture, customer demand, internal operations, or research priorities, the composition of our available compute may not optimally match our needs in a given period. This could affect our ability to serve customers, develop models, and support internal operations.
paras.zh: 我们的大部分算力是根据多年期承诺采购的，这些承诺通常在该算力部署期之前很久就已签订。由于不同 AI 加速器在各类工作负载下的性能特征各不相同，我们承诺算力组合的构成（包括从合作伙伴处采购的加速器架构组合）反映了我们在作出这些承诺时的需求预测和开发路线图假设。如果我们所需支持的工作负载的规模或组合与这些预测存在重大差异（无论是由于模型架构、客户需求、内部运营还是研究优先事项的变化），我们可用算力的构成在特定时期内可能无法与我们的需求实现最优匹配。这可能影响我们服务客户、开发模型和支持内部运营的能力。

paras.en: If we fail to secure sufficient compute, or if we fail to effectively direct the limited compute we have across our workloads to develop and deploy models with capabilities at least comparable to those of our competitors, we risk falling behind the technological frontier. The pace of AI development is extremely rapid, with successive versions of models emerging in compressed timeframes, often measured in months rather than years. As a result, even a brief period without access to sufficient compute could cause us to fall behind quickly. With AI development, the gap between frontier models and those one or two versions behind can be significant in terms of capability, performance, and commercial applicability. Customers, partners, and software developers may shift to competitors whose models offer superior capabilities, and we may be unable to attract or retain the technical talent necessary for frontier research if our researchers lack access to adequate compute or if we are not perceived as operating at the forefront of model development. Any inability to maintain our position at the frontier could result in loss of customers and revenue, diminished brand and reputation, and a decline in our competitive position, each of which may be difficult to regain. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法获得充足的算力，或者无法有效地将我们有限的算力在各工作负载之间进行调配，以开发和部署能力至少可与竞争对手相媲美的模型，我们就有可能落后于技术前沿。AI 的发展速度极快，模型的 successive 版本在压缩的时间框架内相继涌现，通常以月而非年计。因此，即使短暂一段时间无法获得充足算力，也可能使我们迅速落后。在 AI 开发中，前沿模型与落后一两个版本的模型之间在能力、性能和商业适用性方面可能存在显著差距。客户、合作伙伴和软件开发者可能会转向其模型提供更优能力的竞争对手，而如果我们的研究人员无法获得充足的算力，或者如果外界不认为我们处于模型开发的最前沿，我们可能无法吸引或留住前沿研究所需的技术人才。任何无法保持前沿地位的情况都可能导致客户和收入流失、品牌和声誉受损以及竞争地位下降，而其中每一项都可能难以重新获得。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If our actual compute requirements differ materially from our projections, we may fail to secure sufficient compute to meet our needs or we may be committed to excess compute that remains underutilized.**
paras.zh: **如果我们的实际算力需求与我们的预测存在重大差异，我们可能无法获得满足需求的充足算力，或者我们可能已承诺获得过剩算力而该等算力仍未得到充分利用。**

paras.en: The competitive and structural dynamics of the compute market require us to make binding financial commitments for compute months or years in advance of our day-to-day delivery and use. Chip manufacturers, CSPs, and data center developers require advance commitments in order to allocate production capacity, plan infrastructure investments, and manage their own supply chains. As a result, we must forecast our compute requirements well in advance of their deployment and commit capital accordingly, often with limited ability to adjust commitments if our needs change.
paras.zh: 算力市场的竞争和结构动态要求我们在日常交付和使用之前数月或数年就做出具有约束力的算力财务承诺。芯片制造商、云服务商（CSP）和数据中心开发商需要提前承诺，以便分配产能、规划基础设施投资并管理其自身供应链。因此，我们必须在部署之前很早就预测算力需求并相应投入资本，而在需求发生变化时调整承诺的能力往往有限。

paras.en: These forecasts for future compute usage are inherently uncertain. Our actual compute requirements depend on numerous factors that are difficult to predict, including the pace of our research progress, the compute intensity of training techniques we develop or adopt, changes in the competitive landscape that may require us to accelerate or modify our development plans, customer demand for inference compute, and the evolution of hardware or other technological efficiencies and changes. If we underestimate our compute requirements, we may be unable to secure sufficient compute to support our forecasted customer demand and model development roadmap. In the past, we have significantly underestimated our compute requirements, which left us capacity constrained and impacted both product development and deployment. Further, the timing of compute coming online may not align with the timing of demand growth, which could result in periods of excess or underutilized compute and committed cash outflows that do not produce immediate revenue.
paras.zh: 这些对未来算力使用量的预测本身具有不确定性。我们的实际算力需求取决于众多难以预测的因素，包括我们研究进展的速度、我们开发或采用的训练技术的算力密集程度、竞争格局的变化（这可能要求我们加快或调整开发计划）、客户对推理算力的需求，以及硬件或其他技术效率的演进与变化。如果我们低估了自身的算力需求，我们可能无法获得足够的算力来支撑我们预测的客户需求和模型开发路线图。过去，我们曾大幅低估自身的算力需求，导致我们产能受限，并影响了产品开发和部署。此外，算力上线的时间可能与需求增长的时间并不一致，这可能导致出现算力过剩或利用不足的时期，以及无法立即产生收入的已承诺现金流出。

paras.en: Our ability to forecast and secure the compute we need is further challenged by our ongoing transition from a cloud-only, fixed-time arrangement compute model to a hybrid model that includes directly leased chips that are hosted in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification. This transition introduces additional variables into our procurement planning, including the timing of facility completion, the pace at which newly commissioned facilities achieve full operational capacity, our ability to operate, maintain, and integrate on-premise capacity with cloud-based infrastructure, the operational execution of our suppliers, and the performance of hardware in new facility environments. Delays in securing energy, water, and other critical services for these facilities could further slow the pace at which newly commissioned compute becomes available for use. Errors in forecasting any of these transition-related variables could compound our risks related to securing sufficient compute and result in either capacity shortfalls or underutilized capacity during the transition period.
paras.zh: 我们预测和获取所需算力的能力还进一步受到以下挑战：我们正从仅依赖云端的固定期限安排算力模式，持续转型为混合模式，即包含直接租赁的芯片，这些芯片托管在由我们租赁、按我们的规格代我们运营的专用数据中心设施中。这一转型为我们的采购规划引入了额外变量，包括设施竣工的时间、新投运设施达到满负荷运营产能的速度、我们运营、维护并将本地算力与云端基础设施整合的能力、我们供应商的运营执行情况，以及硬件在新设施环境中的性能表现。为这些设施获取电力、水和其他关键服务方面的延迟，可能进一步放缓新投运算力可供使用的速度。对任何此类转型相关变量的预测出现误差，都可能加剧我们与获取足够算力相关的风险，并在转型期间导致产能短缺或产能利用不足。

paras.en: We have entered into, and expect to continue to enter into, long-term agreements for compute and other compute resources that involve minimum purchase commitments, take-or-pay provisions, and other terms that obligate us to pay for resources regardless of actual utilization. These commitments represent substantial fixed obligations. As of and subsequent to September 30, 2026, we have entered into purchase commitments and lease agreements, including short-term commitments, as well as leases not yet commenced, with an aggregate committed spend of more than $ [__] , substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure. These commitments include approximately $ [__] expected to be incurred before December 31, 2030, and substantially all of the remainder is expected to be incurred between 2031 and 2045. Approximately $ [__] of these commitments are due in the next 12 months. See the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Contractual Obligations” for more information.
paras.zh: 我们已签订并预计将继续签订算力及其他算力资源的长期协议，这些协议包含最低采购承诺、照付不议条款及其他条款，使我们无论实际使用情况如何均有义务为资源付费。这些承诺构成重大固定义务。截至及自 2026 年 9 月 30 日之后，我们已签订采购承诺和租赁协议，包括短期承诺以及尚未开始的租赁，合计承诺支出超过 $[__]，其中绝大部分与算力及基础设施相关。这些承诺包括预计在 2030 年 12 月 31 日之前发生的约 $[__]，其余绝大部分预计将在 2031 年至 2045 年之间发生。这些承诺中约 $[__] 将在未来 12 个月内到期。更多信息请参见“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析——流动性与资本资源——合同义务”一节。

paras.en: Our ability to meet the substantial and growing financial obligations of these requirements to secure compute depends on our ability to generate significant revenue growth. We must grow our customer base and expand revenue rapidly in order to generate the cash flows necessary to satisfy these commitments. However, our revenue is primarily consumption-based, and much of it is not subject to long-term contractual commitments, while our compute and infrastructure commitments generally extend over multiple years. As a result, we may enter into these obligations based on revenue expectations that may not be realized. If our revenue growth does not keep pace with our compute-related payment obligations, if we are unable to successfully convert our compute investment into revenue-generating customer workloads, if we fail to raise additional capital on acceptable terms, or if we experience other adverse developments affecting our liquidity, we may be unable to satisfy these obligations. Any such failure could also result in defaults under our agreements, loss of access to critical resources, and reputational harm. In particular, a default under certain commercial agreements could trigger cross-default provisions under the A&R Credit Agreement (as defined below), and certain of our outstanding convertible promissory notes, potentially resulting in the acceleration of substantially all of our outstanding, and any future, indebtedness. Such cross-defaults could set off a cascading series of adverse consequences, including the exercise of remedies by multiple creditors, the termination of key commercial arrangements, enforcement actions against our assets, and severe liquidity constraints. An acceleration of our indebtedness, combined with the loss of access to critical data center infrastructure, among other things, could impair our ability to train and deploy models, serve customers, and fund ongoing operations, which could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and results of operations. For more information, see the sections titled “—We have incurred significant indebtedness in order to operate and grow our business, including to fund our substantial compute commitments, and our ability to service this indebtedness may be constrained by our cash flows and liquidity” and “—We may not have the ability to raise the funds necessary to repay the principal and accrued interest of our outstanding convertible promissory notes or the A&R Credit Agreement in cash when required by the terms of the notes or the A&R Credit Agreement, as applicable, or at their maturity.”
paras.zh: 我们能否履行这些为确保算力而产生的重大且不断增长的财务义务，取决于我们能否实现显著的收入增长。我们必须迅速扩大客户群并提升收入，以产生履行这些承诺所需的现金流。然而，我们的收入主要基于用量消费，其中很大一部分不受长期合同承诺约束，而我们的算力和基础设施承诺通常跨越多年。因此，我们可能基于未必能实现的收入预期而承担这些义务。如果我们的收入增长未能跟上与算力相关的付款义务，如果我们未能成功将算力投资转化为可产生收入的客户工作负载，如果我们未能以可接受的条款筹集额外资本，或者如果我们遭遇影响流动性的其他不利进展，我们可能无法履行这些义务。任何此类失败还可能导致我们违反协议项下的违约、失去对关键资源的访问权限以及声誉受损。特别是，某些商业协议项下的违约可能触发《修订及重述信贷协议》（定义见下文）以及我们某些未偿还可转换本票项下的交叉违约条款，可能导致我们几乎所有未偿债务及任何未来债务被加速到期。此类交叉违约可能引发一连串不利后果，包括多个债权人行使救济措施、关键商业安排终止、针对我们资产的强制执行行动以及严重的流动性限制。我们债务的加速到期，加之失去对关键数据中心基础设施的访问权限等，可能损害我们训练和部署模型、服务客户以及为持续运营提供资金的能力，进而可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。更多信息请参见标题为“——我们为运营和发展业务已产生重大债务，包括为我们的重大算力承诺提供资金，而我们偿还该等债务的能力可能受到现金流和流动性的制约”和“——我们可能没有能力在未偿还可转换本票或《修订及重述信贷协议》（视适用情况）条款要求时或在其到期时筹集必要的资金，以现金偿还未偿还可转换本票或《修订及重述信贷协议》的本金和应计利息。”的章节。

paras.en: Additionally, the rapid pace of technological change across AI infrastructure, hardware, software, system architectures, and model development techniques means that compute secured today may become less efficient or economically attractive relative to future alternatives. We may find ourselves committed to using older-generation hardware and infrastructure while competitors gain access to more advanced systems, or we may be paying premium prices for resources that have declined in market value. These dynamics could adversely affect our cost structure and competitive position. Certain of our financing arrangements require us to enter into exclusive or preferential supply commitments with particular chip suppliers with respect to the compute financed pursuant to such arrangements. These commitments may limit our ability to shift procurement to alternative suppliers or newer chip architectures if our needs or the technology landscape evolve, potentially leaving us committed to platforms that are suboptimal for our actual workload requirements and reducing our ability to adjust our compute portfolio in response to changed circumstances. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 此外，AI 基础设施、硬件、软件、系统架构和模型开发技术等领域技术变革的快速步伐意味着，今天获得的算力相对于未来的替代方案可能会变得效率更低或经济吸引力更弱。我们可能会发现自己不得不使用较旧一代的硬件和基础设施，而竞争对手则能获得更先进的系统，或者我们可能为市场价值已经下降的资源支付溢价。这些动态可能对我们的成本结构和竞争地位产生不利影响。我们的某些融资安排要求我们就此类安排所融资的算力，与特定芯片供应商签订排他性或优惠性供应承诺。如果我们的需求或技术格局发生变化，这些承诺可能会限制我们将采购转向替代供应商或更新芯片架构的能力，可能使我们受制于对我们实际工作负载需求而言并非最优的平台，并削弱我们根据情况变化调整算力组合的能力。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **Constraints on the critical inputs supporting compute could limit our ability to secure adequate compute.**
paras.zh: **支撑算力的关键投入所面临的制约可能会限制我们获得充足算力的能力。**

paras.en: The compute necessary for training and deploying frontier models depends on a supply chain with multiple potential points of constraint or failure. The availability, pricing, and lead times for compute are affected by the supply of advanced chips and other IT equipment, the availability of sufficient electrical power and the infrastructure required to generate and deliver it, and the capacity of data center infrastructure. Each of these inputs faces significant constraints that may limit our ability to secure the compute we need. In addition, increasing demand for compute has contributed to, and may continue to contribute to, increases in the cost of such resources, which could limit our ability to invest in, develop, or deploy our models, platform, and applications at the pace we anticipate.
paras.zh: 训练和部署前沿模型所需的算力依赖于一条存在多个潜在制约点或故障点的供应链。算力的可用性、定价和交付周期受到先进芯片及其他 IT 设备供应、充足电力及发电和输电所需基础设施的可用性以及数据中心基础设施容量的影响。上述每一项投入都面临重大制约，可能限制我们获得所需算力的能力。此外，算力需求的不断增长已经导致并可能继续导致此类资源成本上升，这可能限制我们按预期速度投资、开发或部署我们的模型、平台和应用程序的能力。

paras.en: Supply and Concentration of Chips, Memory, and Data Center Equipment
paras.zh: 芯片、内存和数据中心设备的供应与集中度

paras.en: The specialized chips required for AI workloads, particularly high-performance AI accelerators and memory, are produced by a limited number of manufacturers. The production of advanced chips is extraordinarily complex, requiring manufacturing processes at the leading edge of technological capability.
paras.zh: AI 工作负载所需的专用芯片，尤其是高性能 AI 加速器和内存，由数量有限的制造商生产。先进芯片的生产极其复杂，需要处于技术能力最前沿的制造工艺。

paras.en: The majority of the world’s most advanced chip manufacturing capacity is concentrated in Taiwan, primarily at Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (“TSMC”). This geographic concentration creates significant risks, including exposure to natural disasters such as earthquakes and typhoons, potential disruption from geopolitical tensions between Taiwan and China, vulnerability to any interruption in Taiwan’s power grid, water supply, or other critical infrastructure, and susceptibility to developing trade regulations and restrictions. Any military conflict, tariffs and trade restrictions, economic coercion, blockade, natural disaster, or other incident affecting Taiwan could severely disrupt the global supply of advanced chips, with effects that could persist for years given the time required to construct and qualify alternative fabrication facilities. Efforts to establish sufficient advanced chip manufacturing capacity outside of Taiwan, including in the United States, remain in early stages and may not produce adequate compute to materially reduce these concentration risks within the foreseeable future. In addition, due to the demand for advanced chip manufacturing, TSMC has, at times, been unable to fully satisfy market demand for chip manufacturing capacity, and as a result, we have not always been able to obtain sufficient quantities of chips on a timely basis. Accordingly, any restrictions or delays on the supply of advanced chips out of Taiwan or TSMC would adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 全球大多数最先进的芯片制造产能集中于台湾，主要集中在台积电（Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company，“TSMC”）。这种地理集中带来了重大风险，包括面临地震和台风等自然灾害的风险、台湾与中国之间地缘政治紧张局势可能造成的中断、台湾电网、供水或其他关键基础设施任何中断的脆弱性，以及易受不断演变的贸易法规和限制的影响。任何军事冲突、关税和贸易限制、经济胁迫、封锁、自然灾害或其他影响台湾的事件，都可能严重扰乱全球先进芯片供应，鉴于建设并验证替代性晶圆厂所需的时间，其影响可能持续数年。在台湾以外（包括美国）建立足够先进芯片制造产能的努力仍处于早期阶段，在可预见的未来可能无法产出足够的算力以实质性降低这些集中风险。此外，由于对先进芯片制造的需求，台积电有时无法完全满足市场对芯片制造产能的需求，因此我们并非总能及时获得足够数量的芯片。相应地，来自台湾或台积电的先进芯片供应的任何限制或延迟，都将对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, both high bandwidth memory, which is a key component in high performance AI accelerators, and other high performance memory products used in compute infrastructure, are largely manufactured by SK hynix Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., and Micron Technology, Inc. Each of these manufacturers is working to expand its production capacity to meet demand. However, there is no guarantee that these efforts will result in adequate supply fast enough to meet demand, particularly if large customers or competitors secure exclusive supply commitments or otherwise reserve substantially all of a manufacturer’s available production capacity.
paras.zh: 此外，高带宽内存（高性能 AI 加速器的关键组件）以及用于算力基础设施的其他高性能内存产品，主要由 SK hynix Inc.、Samsung Electronics Co. 和 Micron Technology, Inc. 生产。这些制造商均在努力扩大产能以满足需求。然而，无法保证这些努力能够足够快地形成充足供应以满足需求，尤其是如果大客户或竞争对手获得独家供应承诺或以其他方式预订了某制造商几乎全部可用产能。

paras.en: The concentration and constraints in manufacturing supply expose us to the risk that manufacturers may make allocation decisions or strategic shifts that adversely affect our access to the advanced chips needed for our business. We also face risks that specialized chips may contain defects, or that their production or delivery may be delayed or disrupted, which, given long replacement lead times, could constrain available compute and adversely affect our operations and ability to scale. A meaningful portion of the components we and our partners rely on is sourced from or manufactured outside of the United States, and new or increased tariffs, import restrictions, or trade disputes could delay deliveries, force supply-chain changes, or raise our costs, some of which we bear directly under pass-through arrangements. For more information, see the section titled “—Governmental trade controls, including export and import controls, sanctions, customs requirements, and related regimes, could subject us to liability or loss of contracting privileges or limit our ability to compete in certain markets.”
paras.zh: 制造供应环节的集中度与约束使我们面临如下风险：制造商可能作出分配决策或战略调整，从而对我们获取业务所需先进芯片造成不利影响。我们还面临专用芯片可能存在缺陷，或其生产或交付可能延迟或中断的风险；鉴于更换周期较长，这可能限制可用算力，并对我们的运营和扩展能力造成不利影响。我们及合作伙伴所依赖的组件中，有相当一部分来自美国境外或在美国境外制造，新增或提高的关税、进口限制或贸易争端可能导致交付延迟、迫使供应链调整或抬高我们的成本，其中部分成本根据转嫁安排由我们直接承担。更多信息请参见标题为“——政府贸易管制，包括出口和进口管制、制裁、海关要求及相关制度，可能使我们承担责任或丧失合同权利，或限制我们在某些市场的竞争能力”的章节。

paras.en: We also depend on third-party chip design and services companies for the design, manufacture, and support of certain custom accelerator platforms, as well as for related infrastructure financing arrangements. Disruption to these relationships, or any failure by these parties to deliver hardware or services on expected timelines and specifications, could adversely affect the availability, performance, or cost of accelerator platforms on which we rely [__] .
paras.zh: 我们还依赖第三方芯片设计和服务公司为某些定制加速器平台提供设计、制造和支持，以及相关基础设施融资安排。这些关系的中断，或这些方未能按预期时间表和规格交付硬件或服务，可能对我们所依赖的加速器平台的可用性、性能或成本造成不利影响[__]。

paras.en: Data centers also require electrical, generation, and transmission equipment, cooling systems, backup generators, and networking hardware, some of which are made by only a few manufacturers, must be ordered years in advance, and require substantial pre-delivery payments that we may not recover if our plans change. In addition, certain equipment, such as high-voltage transformers, switchgear, turbines, generators, substations, and transmission components, has been subject to extended delivery timelines, price increases, tariffs and national security requirements, and allocation constraints as demand from data center operators and other large electricity consumers has grown. If such equipment is delayed or unavailable, we may be able to replace it only at higher prices or under less favorable long-term commitments. In order to secure near-term access to compute, we may also elect, or be required, to procure long-lead-time generation and electrical equipment at prices above prevailing market rates on the expectation that it can be deployed on an accelerated timeline to unlock capacity in the near term. Realizing the benefit of paying such prices depends on the timely and successful engineering, procurement, and construction of the associated facilities, which requires specialized expertise that is currently in short supply and involves significant execution risk. Delays, cost overruns, or failure to secure energy on the anticipated schedule could mean that we do not obtain the energy and capacity for which we paid such prices. In some cases, these arrangements also depend on a developer or other counterparty agreeing to purchase the equipment at such prices, finance such purchase, and recover those costs and associated financing costs from us over time, and we may bear these costs even if the underlying capacity is delayed or never realized. Our equipment supply framework agreements and similar arrangements may expose us to further risks, including minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitments, price escalation, and obligations that we are unable to align with our actual deployment needs.
paras.zh: 数据中心还需要电力、发电和输电设备、冷却系统、备用发电机以及网络硬件，其中部分设备仅由少数几家制造商生产，必须提前数年订购，并且需要支付大额预付款，若我们的计划发生变化，这些预付款可能无法收回。此外，随着数据中心运营商和其他大型用电消费者需求的增长，某些设备（如高压变压器、开关设备、涡轮机、发电机、变电站和输电组件）一直面临交付周期延长、价格上涨、关税和国家安全要求以及分配限制等问题。如果此类设备延迟交付或无法获得，我们可能只能以更高的价格或在更不利的长期承诺下进行替换。为了确保近期获得算力，我们还可能选择或被要求以高于现行市场价格的价格采购长交付周期的发电和电气设备，期望其能够加速部署以在近期释放产能。支付此类价格能否带来收益，取决于相关设施能否及时、成功地完成工程、采购和建设，而这需要目前供不应求的专业技术，并涉及重大执行风险。延迟、成本超支或未能按预期时间表获得能源，可能意味着我们无法获得为此类价格所支付的能源和产能。在某些情况下，这些安排还取决于开发商或其他交易对手同意以此类价格购买设备、为此类采购提供融资，并在一段时间内从我方收回这些成本及相关融资成本，而即使底层产能延迟或从未实现，我们仍可能承担这些成本。我们的设备供应框架协议及类似安排可能使我们面临进一步风险，包括最低采购或照付不议承诺、价格升级，以及我们无法与实际部署需求相匹配的义务。

paras.en: Additionally, the U.S. government has imposed and may continue to impose export controls restricting the sale of advanced chips and chip manufacturing equipment to certain countries, including China. These restrictions have affected global chip and related equipment supply allocation, and future changes in export control policy could affect the availability or pricing of the compute resources on which we rely. Future export controls could be more restrictive, for example, by placing restrictions on the countries in which advanced chips may be installed or in which model weights may be stored, which could limit where we or our partners are able to build data centers, constrain our international expansion, or increase our costs.
paras.zh: 此外，美国政府已经实施并可能继续实施出口管制，限制向包括中国在内的某些国家销售先进芯片和芯片制造设备。这些限制已影响全球芯片及相关设备的供应分配，出口管制政策的未来变化可能影响我们所依赖的算力资源的可用性或定价。未来的出口管制可能更加严格，例如对先进芯片可安装的国家或模型权重可存储的国家施加限制，这可能限制我们或我们的合作伙伴建设数据中心的地点，制约我们的国际扩张，或增加我们的成本。

paras.en: Electrical Power and Fuel Constraints
paras.zh: 电力与燃料限制

paras.en: The operation of data centers at the scale required for frontier AI development and deployment consumes substantial quantities of electrical power. The availability of sufficient electrical power has emerged as a significant constraint on data center development and expansion in many geographies, including the United States. Electrical grid infrastructure in the United States and other countries was not designed to accommodate the rapid increase in demand associated with AI development, and the lead times required to build new generation capacity, transmission infrastructure, and grid interconnections can extend for years. Demand on electric grid infrastructure is also increasing as a result of the increased electrification of homes, vehicles, and industry, and this growing demand is occurring at a time when power generation capacity additions, transmission expansion, and grid modernization efforts have not kept pace and certain existing generation resources are being retired, all of which has contributed to higher electricity prices and longer interconnection timelines in certain regions. We have publicly committed to covering the cost of electricity price increases to consumers caused by our data centers, including both the cost of electricity itself and the infrastructure necessary to deliver it.
paras.zh: 以前沿 AI 开发和部署所需规模运营数据中心会消耗大量电力。充足电力的可获得性已成为包括美国在内的许多地区数据中心开发和扩建的重大制约因素。美国及其他国家的电网基础设施在设计之初并未考虑满足 AI 开发相关的需求快速增长，而建设新增发电容量、输电基础设施和电网互联所需的交付周期可能长达数年。同时，随着住宅、车辆和工业电气化程度提高，对电网基础设施的需求也在增加，而这种不断增长的需求出现之际，新增发电容量、输电扩建和电网现代化工作未能同步跟上，且部分现有发电资源正在退役，所有这些都导致某些地区电价上涨和并网时间延长。我们已公开承诺承担因我们的数据中心导致的消费者电价上涨成本，包括电力本身成本以及输送电力所需的基础设施成本。

paras.en: Our access to electrical power also depends on our ability, and the ability of the third parties on which we rely for the construction, management, and operation of our data center facilities, to negotiate and maintain contracts with utility providers and grid operators and to obtain approvals from public utility commissions and other regulators. These parties may be unable or unwilling to approve, or may condition or delay, the connections, capacity expansions, special or negotiated rate arrangements, and infrastructure investments necessary to support data center growth, or may grant them only at costs that limit the economic efficiency and viability of certain facilities, such as by requiring us to bear grid upgrade or interconnection costs beyond those attributable to serving our facilities—representing a larger share of costs than is required under existing or prior regulatory constructs. Interconnection queues for large new electricity loads have also lengthened substantially in many regions, which could delay or limit our access to grid power. Utility providers and regulators may also reallocate previously committed capacity that our data center facilities may require. In many jurisdictions, a single utility provider has substantial control over the terms, timing, and cost of the service and infrastructure necessary to power our data center facilities. The commercial and regulatory priorities of utility providers may differ from ours, including with respect to which infrastructure investments are made, how their costs are allocated, and whether alternative or self-supplied generation arrangements are permitted and on what conditions. Utility providers and other stakeholders may also seek regulatory or legislative measures affecting large electricity loads, self-supply, or alternative power generation arrangements. The outcomes of our negotiations and regulatory proceedings involving utilities are uncertain, and unfavorable results could increase our costs, delay our projects, or limit the alternatives available to us. More broadly, regulatory proceedings relating to cost allocation, rate design, and the treatment of large electricity loads are ongoing in numerous jurisdictions, and adverse outcomes, changes in policy, or the imposition of new tariffs, surcharges, or curtailment obligations applicable to data centers could increase our costs or limit our access to electrical power.
paras.zh: 我们获取电力还取决于我们以及我们为数据中心设施的建设、管理和运营所依赖的第三方，能否与公用事业供应商和电网运营商谈判并维持合同，以及能否获得公共事业委员会和其他监管机构的批准。这些相关方可能无法或不愿批准，或可能对支持数据中心增长所需的并网、容量扩容、特殊或协商费率安排以及基础设施投资附加条件或予以拖延，或仅在限制某些设施经济效率与可行性的成本水平上予以批准，例如要求我们承担超出服务我们设施所应承担范围的电网升级或互联成本——这比现行或以往监管框架下所要求的成本份额更大。在许多地区，大型新增电力负荷的并网排队也大幅延长，这可能延迟或限制我们获取电网电力。公用事业供应商和监管机构还可能重新分配我们数据中心设施可能需要的此前已承诺容量。在许多司法管辖区，单一公用事业供应商对我们数据中心设施供电所需服务的条款、时间和成本以及基础设施拥有实质性控制权。公用事业供应商的商业和监管优先事项可能与我们不同，包括在哪些基础设施投资、其成本如何分摊，以及是否允许替代或自供电发电安排及在何种条件下允许等方面。公用事业供应商和其他利益相关方还可能寻求影响大型电力负荷、自供电或替代发电安排的监管或立法措施。我们与公用事业相关的谈判和监管程序的结果具有不确定性，不利结果可能增加我们的成本、延迟我们的项目或限制我们可用的替代方案。更广泛而言，与成本分摊、费率设计及大型电力负荷处理相关的监管程序正在众多司法管辖区进行，不利结果、政策变化或对数据中心施加新的电价、附加费或限电义务，可能增加我们的成本或限制我们获取电力。

paras.en: In addition, the construction of the generation and transmission infrastructure on which we depend is itself capital-intensive and exposed to labor shortages, supply chain disruptions, permitting delays, changes in interest rates, tariffs, other cost overruns, and financing constraints. The significant and increasing capital required to fund these generation, transmission, and related infrastructure investments, whether incurred by us, our utility and energy supply providers, or our data center development partners, is sensitive to prevailing interest rates and the availability of debt or equity financing on acceptable terms. Any inability of our partners to access capital when needed, and the limitations, cost, and competition for such capital, could increase the cost of the power on which we depend, delay or halt projects, or render certain facilities commercially unviable, and under certain of our arrangements, we bear these financing and capital costs directly or on a pass-through basis. Furthermore, newer sources of generation, such as solar, wind, battery storage, nuclear, and geothermal power, may not be available in the quantities or on the timelines we require, or may be available only at higher cost. Our facilities separately depend on access to reliable water for cooling, which in some regions is scarce, subject to use restrictions, or increasingly costly. Any of the foregoing could adversely affect the availability of the power or water we require, increase our costs, or limit our ability to develop, expand, or operate our data center facilities, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，我们所依赖的发电和输电基础设施的建设本身即属资本密集型，并面临劳动力短缺、供应链中断、许可延迟、利率变化、关税、其他成本超支以及融资约束等风险。为这些发电、输电及相关基础设施投资提供资金所需的巨额且不断增加的资本——无论是由我们、我们的公用事业和能源供应商，还是我们的数据中心开发合作伙伴承担——都对现行利率以及能否以可接受的条件获得债务或股权融资十分敏感。我们的合作伙伴若无法在需要时获得资本，以及此类资本所受的限制、成本及竞争，可能推高我们所依赖的电力成本、导致项目延迟或停滞，或使某些设施在商业上不可行；且根据我们的某些安排，我们直接或通过转嫁方式承担这些融资和资本成本。此外，太阳能、风能、电池储能、核能和地热能等较新的发电来源，可能无法按我们所需的数量或时间表提供，或只能以更高成本获得。我们的设施还分别依赖于获得可靠的冷却用水，而在某些地区，水资源稀缺、受使用限制或成本日益高昂。上述任何情况都可能对我们所需电力或水的可获得性产生不利影响、增加我们的成本，或限制我们开发、扩建或运营数据中心设施的能力，进而可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense, and we compete for such access with well-capitalized CSPs, some of which produce and develop competing AI models, cryptocurrency mining operations, and other large-scale electricity consumers. In addition to, or sometimes in lieu of, grid-based electricity, an increasing share of data centers are being developed with dedicated on-site power generation capacity that supplies electricity directly to the facility independent of any utility-operated electric grid. The reliability of such off-grid power generation solutions varies by the underlying technology, the equipment used, and the operator and will reflect site-by-site operational and environmental profiles. Development of this new capacity in turn requires power generation and electrical infrastructure that are themselves subject to supply challenges and operational complexity. For example, certain of our planned data center facilities rely on dedicated on-site natural gas-fired generation, which exposes us to fuel price volatility and supply disruptions that are outside of our control and for which we bear the cost on a pass-through basis. These facilities are also subject to constraints on pipeline capacity and firm fuel transportation necessary to deliver natural gas. As data center operators increasingly rely on natural gas-fired generation, and because behind-the-meter and on-site arrangements are feasible only in some jurisdictions given the applicable regulatory frameworks, we expect increased competition among users for the same natural gas supply and pipeline capacity in those areas. This competition could drive up the price of natural gas in such areas and may adversely affect our ability to contract for firm fuel supply and transportation and to secure the pipeline connections and laterals our facilities require.
paras.zh: 争夺电力供应充足的数据中心选址及接入电力资源的竞争十分激烈，我们需与资金雄厚的云服务商（CSP）（其中部分亦生产并开发竞争性 AI 模型）、加密货币挖矿业务及其他大规模用电主体争夺此类资源。除电网供电外（有时甚至取代电网供电），越来越多的数据中心在开发时配套建设专用现场发电设施，直接向数据中心供电，不依赖任何公用事业运营的电网。此类离网发电解决方案的可靠性因底层技术、所用设备及运营方而异，并将体现各站点自身的运营与环境特征。开发此类新增发电能力又需要发电及电力基础设施，而这些基础设施本身也面临供应挑战与运营复杂性。例如，我们部分规划中的数据中心设施依赖专用现场天然气发电，这使我们面临燃料价格波动及供应中断风险，此类风险超出我们的控制范围，且相关成本由我们以转嫁方式承担。此类设施还受制于管道容量及输送天然气所需的稳定燃料运输能力的约束。随着数据中心运营商日益依赖天然气发电，且鉴于适用监管框架，表后（behind-the-meter）及现场供电安排仅在部分司法辖区可行，我们预计上述地区内用户之间对同一天然气供应及管道容量的竞争将加剧。此类竞争可能推高上述地区的天然气价格，并可能对我们签订稳定燃料供应及运输合同、以及获取设施所需管道连接及支线的能力产生不利影响。

paras.en: These dynamics present several related risks. We may be unable to secure firm gas supply and transportation during the development of a facility, causing a planned site to be delayed or abandoned; we may face fuel supply or delivery disruptions once a facility is operating; and because our arrangements generally provide for fuel and related costs to be borne by us on a pass-through basis without cost caps, we remain exposed to increases in the cost of natural gas and its transportation. More broadly, the cost of electricity is subject to significant variability that is largely outside of our control, as wholesale electricity prices fluctuate with changing supply and demand, weather, fuel prices, tariffs or surcharges, and grid stress, and can rise sharply during periods of peak demand or constrained supply, and such increases in energy costs could adversely affect our results of operations.
paras.zh: 上述动态带来若干相关风险。我们可能在设施开发期间无法获得稳定的天然气供应及运输，导致规划选址被延迟或放弃；设施投入运营后，我们可能面临燃料供应或交付中断；且由于我们的安排通常规定燃料及相关成本由我们以转嫁方式承担且不设成本上限，我们仍面临天然气及其运输成本上涨的风险。更广泛而言，电力成本存在重大波动性，且在很大程度上超出我们的控制范围，因为批发电价会随供需变化、天气、燃料价格、关税或附加费以及电网压力而波动，并可能在需求高峰或供应受限期间急剧上涨，此类能源成本上涨可能对我们的经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: In some regions, including certain regions where we have contracted compute commitments, data center development has prompted public controversy and regulatory scrutiny regarding environmental impact, land and water use, and the allocation of limited power resources. For example, if our efforts to secure electrical power are perceived to affect other utility customers and the broader grid, regulators may impose conditions, standby charges, or other requirements intended to address such impacts. More broadly, our access to electrical power is subject to an evolving regulatory framework characterized by complexity, jurisdictional overlap, and rules that were largely designed around service by incumbent utility providers and existing generation arrangements and that may not readily accommodate new entrants or alternative approaches, which can result in significant delay or prevent the development of the generation we require. Grid-tied electrical supply, for instance, is subject to the jurisdiction of federal and state energy regulators, regional grid operators, and public utility commissions, while behind-the-meter and on-site generation is subject to a distinct set of exclusive service franchise protections, permitting, environmental, air quality, interconnection, and siting requirements. In addition, environmental standards applicable to power generation continue to evolve, including as a result of changing governmental priorities and shifting public and political views regarding climate change and the appropriate treatment of various power generation sources. Any failure to secure access to adequate electrical power, any legal, regulatory, or other administrative action or change limiting the availability of electricity, or any significant increase in energy or compliance costs, could adversely affect our cost structure and limit our ability to scale our compute infrastructure, develop and deploy our models, and service our customers. We have also made, and may in the future make, voluntary commitments to offset the impact of our data center energy consumption on local communities and electricity ratepayers, including commitments to cover grid infrastructure upgrade costs, procure new power generation to match our energy needs, invest in curtailment systems to reduce strain on the grid during peak demand periods, and address environmental impacts. These commitments have increased, and we expect will continue to increase, our operating costs. Moreover, we believe this is part of a broader emerging trend in the AI industry, and such commitments, or similar obligations, may become increasingly standard or required, which could further increase our costs. In addition, the physical effects of climate change may increase our operating costs over time, as higher average temperatures can increase the power consumption and water usage required to cool equipment at the facilities on which we depend.
paras.zh: 在某些地区，包括我们已签约算力承诺的某些地区，数据中心开发已就环境影响、土地与水资源使用以及有限电力资源的分配引发公众争议和监管审查。例如，如果我们获取电力的努力被认为会影响其他公用事业客户和更广泛的电网，监管机构可能施加条件、备用费用或其他旨在应对此类影响的要求。更广泛而言，我们获取电力须遵守一个不断演变的监管框架，该框架具有复杂性、管辖权重叠的特点，且其规则在很大程度上是围绕现有公用事业提供商的供电服务和现有发电安排设计的，可能难以容纳新进入者或替代方案，这可能导致我们所需的发电项目出现重大延误或无法开发。例如，并网电力供应须受联邦和州能源监管机构、区域电网运营商和公共事业委员会的管辖，而表后和现场发电则须遵守一套不同的独家服务特许保护、许可、环境、空气质量、互联和选址要求。此外，适用于发电的环境标准持续演变，包括因政府优先事项变化以及公众和政治对气候变化及各类发电来源适当处理方式的看法转变所致。任何未能获得充足电力供应、任何限制电力供应的法律、监管或其他行政行动或变化，或任何能源或合规成本的显著增加，都可能对我们的成本结构产生不利影响，并限制我们扩展算力基础设施、开发和部署模型以及服务客户的能力。我们已作出、且未来可能作出自愿承诺，以抵消数据中心能耗对当地社区和电费缴纳者的影响，包括承诺承担电网基础设施升级成本、采购新的发电以匹配我们的能源需求、投资于削减系统以减少高峰需求期间电网压力，以及应对环境影响。这些承诺已增加、且我们预计将继续增加我们的运营成本。此外，我们认为这是 AI 行业更广泛新兴趋势的一部分，此类承诺或类似义务可能日益成为标准或必需，这可能进一步增加我们的成本。此外，气候变化的物理影响可能随时间推移增加我们的运营成本，因为平均气温升高可能增加我们依赖的设施冷却设备所需的电力消耗和用水量。

paras.en: Data Center Infrastructure
paras.zh: 数据中心基础设施

paras.en: Even where chips and electrical power are available, the development of data center facilities requires substantial time, capital, and specialized expertise. Data center construction involves lengthy permitting processes, complex supply chains for specialized equipment, and significant lead times for the installation and commissioning of cooling systems, electrical infrastructure, and networking equipment. Labor shortages, including shortages of, and competition for, electricians, facility technicians, and other skilled tradespeople, supply chain disruptions, permitting delays, and other factors can extend construction timelines and increase costs. Further, given data center development projects require advanced and significant capital commitments with dedicated end users, we have in some cases relied, and expect to continue to rely, on arrangements for financing or with partners who guarantee the lease obligations to support the development of data center capacity that is expected to host such partner’s chips or computing infrastructure. In addition, there are a limited number of qualified third-party vendors with the expertise we require and that support the particular infrastructure we wish to implement. Accordingly, we rely on this limited number of third parties for the construction, management, and operation of certain of our data center facilities, some of which have limited operating history or may have less experience operating data center infrastructure at the scale and complexity our operations require. In certain cases, these third-party operators are trained or supervised by our chip partners to manage facilities on our behalf but are not affiliates of those partners and may not have the same depth of expertise, operational resilience, or resources. Any failure by these third-party operators to perform as expected could disrupt our access to compute. In addition, safety or environmental incidents at facilities built or operated for us, whatever their cause, could expose us to claims, fines, or suspensions of construction or operations, the costs of which we may bear. We also depend on an extended network of suppliers, builders, and facility operators. If any of them engage in practices that are unsafe, unlawful, or contrary to the labor, human rights, environmental, or other standards we or our partners require, we could face legal liability, lose the ability to use affected suppliers or facilities, and suffer harm to our reputation, even where we did not direct or know of the conduct.
paras.zh: 即使芯片和电力可用，数据中心设施的建设仍需要大量时间、资金和专业能力。数据中心建设涉及漫长的许可审批流程、专用设备的复杂供应链，以及冷却系统、电力基础设施和网络设备安装与调试的较长交付周期。劳动力短缺（包括电工、设施技术人员及其他熟练技工的短缺和竞争）、供应链中断、许可延迟及其他因素，都可能延长建设周期并增加成本。此外，鉴于数据中心开发项目需要与特定终端用户作出提前且重大的资本承诺，我们在某些情况下已经依赖、并预计将继续依赖融资安排，或依赖由合作伙伴担保租赁义务的安排，以支持预计将承载该合作伙伴芯片或计算基础设施的数据中心产能的开发。此外，具备我们所要求专业知识、并能支持我们希望实施的特定基础设施的合格第三方供应商数量有限。因此，我们依赖数量有限的第三方来建设、管理和运营我们的部分数据中心设施，其中一些第三方运营历史有限，或在运营我们业务所需规模和复杂度的数据中心基础设施方面经验较少。在某些情况下，这些第三方运营商由我们的芯片合作伙伴培训或监督，以代表我们管理设施，但它们并非这些合作伙伴的关联方，可能不具备同等深度的专业知识、运营韧性或资源。这些第三方运营商若未能按预期履约，可能扰乱我们获取算力的渠道。此外，为我们建设或运营的设施若发生安全或环境事件，无论原因如何，都可能使我们面临索赔、罚款或建设或运营被暂停，相关成本可能由我们承担。我们还依赖由供应商、建设商和设施运营商组成的广泛网络。如果其中任何一方从事不安全、违法或违反我们或合作伙伴所要求的劳工、人权、环境或其他标准的行为，我们可能面临法律责任、失去使用受影响供应商或设施的能力，并遭受声誉损害，即使我们并未指示或知悉该等行为。

paras.en: Our collective data center infrastructure is currently concentrated primarily in the United States, which exposes us to risks associated with regional regulatory changes, power grid constraints or failures, disruptions to network connectivity between facilities, natural disasters, physical attacks—including those motivated by geopolitical events, opposition to AI, and opposition to data center development—and other disruptions that could affect multiple facilities. Certain state, local, and municipal jurisdictions in the United States are also considering or have approved moratoriums on new data center construction, citing public health, safety, and environmental concerns. Such jurisdictions and other regulators, grid operators, or utilities may also adopt other measures that subject users of large electricity loads, including data centers, to curtailment, interruptions, forced reductions, disconnection, or other restrictions during periods of grid stress, whether through changes in law or policy, market or reliability constraints, limits on transmission and distribution infrastructure, or a preference for protecting other utility customers and the broader grid. New large loads on the electrical grid may be increasingly subject to mandatory curtailment in regions where there is insufficient grid-connected power generation to reliably supply existing and new electricity loads. For example, states such as New York and Texas have recently moved to regulate large-scale data centers, whether by pausing state permitting for new large facilities, as New York has, or by subjecting large electricity loads to curtailment or disconnection during grid emergencies, as Texas has. Such moratoriums, or similar actions, could delay or prevent the construction or expansion of facilities on which we depend for compute. Opposition to data center development has also become more organized and coordinated across jurisdictions and our public profile may draw particular attention to projects associated with us. The loss of, or a significant disruption at, any major facility may not be readily absorbed by our remaining or future infrastructure. We are expanding our data center capacity internationally as part of our efforts to diversify our infrastructure footprint and reduce concentration risks associated with operating a significant portion of our compute infrastructure in the United States and to support our international growth strategy, including by entering into letters of intent and negotiating lease and related agreements for data center facilities in multiple non-U.S. jurisdictions, which exposes us to additional risks related to foreign regulatory requirements and approvals, data sovereignty and localization laws, governmental access or assistance requirements, cross-border data transfer restrictions, foreign tax regimes, and increased operational complexity. Our ability to enter into definitive agreements for data center capacity and operations in non-U.S. jurisdictions depends on the timely formation, registration, and receipt of governmental approval of local subsidiaries, as well as the establishment of local banking arrangements, and any delay or failure in completing these steps could delay or prevent us from mitigating our infrastructure concentration risks, executing our international growth strategy, securing planned compute capacity, or could result in substantial additional taxes, penalties, or other liabilities. In addition, regulatory, legal, and other constraints in many jurisdictions may limit the locations in which we can practically site or contract for data center capacity, which could constrain our ability to diversify our infrastructure footprint as quickly or as broadly as we currently intend.
