paras.zh: 我们整体的数据中心基础设施目前主要集中在美国，这使我们面临与地区监管变化、电网限制或故障、设施之间网络连接中断、自然灾害、物理攻击（包括出于地缘政治事件、反对 AI 以及反对数据中心开发等动机的攻击）以及其他可能影响多个设施的干扰相关的风险。美国某些州、地方和市政辖区也正在考虑或已批准暂停新建数据中心，理由是公共卫生、安全和环境方面的担忧。此类辖区以及其他监管机构、电网运营商或公用事业公司还可能采取其他措施，在电网承压期间对包括数据中心在内的电力大负荷用户实施限电、中断、强制削减、断电或其他限制，无论是通过法律或政策变化、市场或可靠性约束、输配电基础设施限制，还是出于保护其他公用事业客户和更广泛电网的优先考虑。在并网发电不足以可靠供应现有和新增电力负荷的地区，电网新增的大负荷可能日益面临强制限电。例如，纽约州和得克萨斯州等州近期已采取措施监管大型数据中心，纽约州暂停了新建大型设施的州级许可审批，得克萨斯州则在电网紧急情况下对电力大负荷实施限电或断电。此类暂停令或类似行动可能延迟或阻止我们赖以获取算力的设施的建设和扩建。反对数据中心开发的声浪在各辖区也变得更加有组织和协调，而我们的公众知名度可能使与我们相关的项目尤其受到关注。任何主要设施的损失或重大中断，可能无法由我们剩余或未来的基础设施轻易消化。作为分散基础设施布局、降低因大部分算力基础设施在美国运营而带来的集中度风险以及支持我们国际增长战略的努力的一部分，我们正在国际上扩展数据中心容量，包括就多个美国以外辖区的数据中心设施签订意向书并谈判租赁及相关协议，这使我们面临与外国监管要求和审批、数据主权和本地化法律、政府访问或协助要求、跨境数据传输限制、外国税收制度以及运营复杂性增加相关的额外风险。我们能否就美国以外辖区的数据中心容量和运营签订最终协议，取决于当地子公司的及时设立、注册和获得政府批准，以及当地银行安排的建立，而完成这些步骤的任何延迟或失败都可能延迟或阻止我们降低基础设施集中度风险、执行国际增长战略、确保计划中的算力容量，或可能导致大量额外税费、罚款或其他责任。此外，许多辖区的监管、法律和其他限制可能限制我们实际选址或签约数据中心容量的地点，这可能制约我们按当前预期的速度或广度分散基础设施布局的能力。

paras.en: We and our principal competitors rely on substantially similar inputs to develop and deploy frontier models, including advanced chips sourced from a small number of suppliers and data center capacity and compute obtained from CSPs and other third parties. As we and our competitors increasingly pursue vertical integration, the basis of competition could shift over time to encompass not only which company can develop the most capable models, but also which company can develop the best underlying components. Our future competitiveness may depend in part on our ability to successfully develop vertically integrated compute infrastructure on competitive terms and timelines, and there can be no assurance that we will be able to do so. Our competitors may be better positioned, or may invest greater efforts, to vertically integrate across the compute supply chain, including through proprietary chip design, fabrication, ownership or long-term control of data center infrastructure, access to dedicated power generation assets, exclusive supply arrangements with hardware manufacturers, or by securing the limited sites suitable for large-scale data center development ahead of us. Competitors that succeed in controlling a greater share of these supply chain layers may be able to secure compute at greater scale, lower cost, or with greater reliability than we can, particularly during periods of high demand or supply constraint, when captive supply relationships may confer certain advantages over participants that depend on third-party providers. Such competitors may also develop proprietary hardware-software co-designs that optimize compute efficiency for their specific model architectures, which could compound any capability gap across successive model versions. While we are pursuing initiatives to develop dedicated data center infrastructure, there can be no assurance that these efforts will be completed on the timelines or at the costs we anticipate, or that they will be sufficient to offset any structural advantages that vertically integrated competitors may achieve. Competitors that succeed in these efforts may be better positioned to remain at the frontier of AI regardless of broader market constraints.
paras.zh: 我们和我们的主要竞争对手依赖基本相似的投入要素来开发和部署前沿模型，包括从少数供应商处采购的先进芯片，以及从云服务商（CSP）和其他第三方获取的数据中心容量和算力。随着我们和竞争对手日益追求垂直整合，竞争基础可能随时间推移而转变，不仅包括哪家公司能开发出能力最强的模型，还包括哪家公司能开发出最好的底层组件。我们未来的竞争力可能部分取决于我们能否以有竞争力的条款和时间表成功开发垂直整合的算力基础设施，且无法保证我们能够做到这一点。我们的竞争对手可能处于更有利的地位，或可能投入更大的努力，在算力供应链上实现垂直整合，包括通过专有芯片设计、制造、拥有或长期控制数据中心基础设施、获得专用发电资产、与硬件制造商达成独家供应安排，或抢先锁定适合大规模数据中心开发的有限场地。成功控制更多这些供应链层级的竞争对手可能能够以比我们更大的规模、更低的成本或更高的可靠性获得算力，尤其是在需求旺盛或供应受限的时期，此时自有供应关系可能相对于依赖第三方供应商的参与者赋予某些优势。此类竞争对手还可能开发专有的软硬件协同设计，针对其特定模型架构优化算力效率，这可能在 successive 模型版本中进一步扩大任何能力差距。尽管我们正在推进开发专用数据中心基础设施的举措，但无法保证这些努力将按我们预期的时间表或成本完成，也无法保证它们足以抵消垂直整合竞争对手可能取得的任何结构性优势。在这些努力中取得成功的竞争对手可能处于更有利的地位，无论更广泛的市场约束如何，都能保持在 AI 前沿。

paras.en: Natural hazards, extreme weather, or other disruptions affecting the regions where these inputs are produced or where our facilities are located could further constrain the availability of chips, power, water, or data center capacity on which we depend. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 影响这些投入要素生产地区或我们设施所在地区的自然灾害、极端天气或其他中断，可能进一步制约我们所依赖的芯片、电力、水或数据中心容量的可用性。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **We are highly dependent on the continued service of our co-founders, senior management team, and key technical employees, and the loss of any of these individuals may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们高度依赖联合创始人、高级管理团队和关键技术员工的持续服务，任何这些人员的流失都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We are highly dependent on the continued service of our Chief Executive Officer, President, co-founders, senior management team, and key technical team. In particular, our Chief Executive Officer and President are critical to setting our strategic direction, advancing our research agenda, shaping our safety and governance frameworks, and generally advancing our mission, and we believe that their leadership would be difficult to replace. If either were to become unavailable for any reason, or if either of their reputations were significantly harmed, regardless of merit, there could be an adverse impact on our operations and competitive position, employee morale, employee retention, pace of innovation, customer and partner confidence in our company, our brand and reputation, and our long-term strategic objectives. Further, the loss of key personnel, including members of our founding team and senior management team, and key engineering, research, product development, marketing, and sales personnel, could also disrupt our operations and have an adverse effect on our business. Many of our key personnel, particularly within our technical and research teams, are strongly motivated by our mission and the opportunity to work on addressing specific problems within the AI landscape. To the extent that their interests evolve, they seek to pursue different technical challenges or areas of focus, or they are drawn to other organizations or initiatives that they perceive as better aligned with their personal beliefs or professional objectives, we may face increased difficulty retaining such personnel. This risk may be heightened as we continue to scale and mature as an organization, which may change the nature of the work environment, priorities, or perceived mission alignment for certain personnel, including personnel who may conclude that the objectives that drew them to us have been substantially achieved. In addition, under certain of our agreements with suppliers, the loss of certain key personnel could accelerate our obligations or otherwise trigger adverse consequences under such agreements.
paras.zh: 我们在很大程度上依赖于我们的首席执行官、总裁、联合创始人、高级管理团队和核心技术团队的持续服务。特别是，我们的首席执行官和总裁对于制定我们的战略方向、推进我们的研究议程、塑造我们的安全与治理框架以及总体推进我们的使命至关重要，我们认为他们的领导难以替代。如果其中任何一位因任何原因无法履职，或者其中任何一位的声誉受到重大损害（无论是否有正当理由），都可能对我们的运营和竞争地位、员工士气、员工留任、创新步伐、客户和合作伙伴对我们公司的信心、我们的品牌和声誉以及我们的长期战略目标产生不利影响。此外，关键人员的流失，包括我们的创始团队成员和高级管理团队成员，以及关键的工程、研究、产品开发、市场营销和销售人员，也可能扰乱我们的运营并对我们的业务产生不利影响。我们的许多关键人员，尤其是技术和研究团队中的关键人员，受到我们的使命以及在 AI 领域解决特定问题的机会的强烈驱动。如果他们的兴趣发生变化，寻求追求不同的技术挑战或关注领域，或者被他们认为更符合其个人信念或职业目标的其他组织或倡议所吸引，我们可能会面临留住此类人员的更大困难。随着我们作为组织持续扩张和成熟，这一风险可能会加剧，因为这可能会改变某些人员的工作环境性质、优先事项或对使命契合度的认知，包括那些可能认为吸引他们加入我们的目标已基本实现的人员。此外，根据我们与供应商的某些协议，某些关键人员的流失可能会加速我们的义务或以其他方式触发此类协议下的不利后果。

paras.en: If we are unable to retain key personnel, or if we fail to conduct effective succession planning and find suitable replacements for any losses of such key personnel in a timely manner and on competitive terms, we could experience declines in sales, delays in research and development, and harm to our business and operations. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法留住关键人员，或者如果我们未能进行有效的继任规划，未能及时以有竞争力的条件为任何关键人员的流失找到合适的替代者，我们可能会经历销售额下降、研发延迟，以及我们的业务和运营受到损害。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **We may require additional capital to meet our substantial ongoing obligations and support our business growth, and our ability to generate sufficient revenue and secure additional capital on acceptable terms is critical to our continued operations and competitive position.**
paras.zh: **我们可能需要额外资本来履行我们大量的持续义务并支持我们的业务增长，而我们产生足够收入并以可接受的条件获得额外资本的能力对我们的持续运营和竞争地位至关重要。**

paras.en: Our business model requires substantial and increasing capital to support our ability to remain competitive and to stay at the frontier of AI. We intend to continue to make significant financial investments to support our business growth and may require additional funds to acquire sufficient compute and respond to business challenges, including expenditures to create, maintain, upgrade, and enhance our models, platform, and applications, including costs related to investments in infrastructure, human capital, office expansion, and data assets. In addition, we may use a portion of our cash to satisfy tax withholding and remittance obligations related to outstanding RSUs and equity awards that we grant in the future.
paras.zh: 我们的商业模式需要大量且不断增加的资本，以支持我们保持竞争力并始终处于 AI 前沿的能力。我们打算继续进行重大财务投资以支持业务增长，并可能需要额外资金来获取充足算力并应对业务挑战，包括用于创建、维护、升级和增强我们的模型、平台和应用的支出，包括与基础设施、人力资本、办公场所扩张和数据资产投资相关的成本。此外，我们可能将部分现金用于履行与未归属 RSU 以及我们未来授予的股权奖励相关的代扣代缴税款和汇缴义务。

paras.en: In addition, to date we have financed our compute primarily under arrangements with CSPs, with costs recognized as compute is made available to us. We may in the future finance a greater portion of our compute on an up-front basis, including through capital leases, prepayments, debt-financed purchases of equipment, or similar arrangements. If we were to do so, we may incur significant cash outflows in advance of compute availability or related revenue, which could increase demands on our cash flows and liquidity and our need to raise additional capital. Such arrangements could also increase our capital intensity and alter our cash-flow profile.
paras.zh: 此外，迄今为止我们主要通过云服务商（CSP）的安排为算力提供资金，相关成本在算力可供我们使用时确认。未来我们可能以预付方式为更大比例的算力提供资金，包括通过资本租赁、预付款、债务融资购买设备或类似安排。若我们这样做，可能在算力可用或相关收入产生之前产生大额现金流出，这可能增加对我们现金流和流动性的需求以及我们筹集额外资本的需要。此类安排还可能提高我们的资本密集度并改变我们的现金流特征。

paras.en: Accordingly, it is critical that we maintain strong revenue growth, grow revenue efficiently relative to our committed compute, infrastructure, and personnel costs, and manage our cash flows effectively. To the extent that such efforts are insufficient to meet our capital needs, we may need to obtain additional capital through equity or debt financings. If we raise additional funds through future issuances of equity, equity-linked securities, or convertible debt securities, our existing stockholders could suffer dilution, and any new securities we issue could have rights, preferences, and privileges superior to those of holders of our common stock. Further, the conversion of our outstanding convertible securities will cause additional dilution to our existing stockholders. Any debt financing that we may secure in the future may involve restrictive covenants relating to our capital raising activities and other financial and operational matters, potentially making it more difficult for us to obtain additional capital and to pursue business opportunities.
paras.zh: 因此，至关重要的是我们保持强劲的收入增长、相对于我们已承诺的算力、基础设施和人员成本高效地增长收入，并有效管理我们的现金流。若此类努力不足以满足我们的资本需求，我们可能需要通过股权或债务融资获得额外资本。如果我们通过未来发行股权、股权挂钩证券或可转换债务证券筹集额外资金，我们现有股东可能遭受稀释，且我们发行的任何新证券可能拥有优于我们普通股持有人的权利、优先权和特权。此外，我们未偿还可转换证券的转换将对我们现有股东造成额外稀释。我们未来可能获得的任何债务融资可能涉及与我们的资本筹集活动及其他财务和运营事项相关的限制性契约，可能使我们更难获得额外资本并寻求业务机会。

paras.en: In addition, our ability to draw amounts under certain of our note purchase agreements (“NPAs”) is not guaranteed and is subject to the satisfaction of specified conditions. In particular, our ability to access additional amounts under certain of these facilities depends on our achievement of certain revenue performance targets and/or the ability of third parties to deliver additional compute to us. While we have historically surpassed all such revenue performance targets, there can be no assurance that revenue will continue to exceed these thresholds at all times in the future. If these conditions are not satisfied, we may be unable to draw additional amounts under the applicable NPA, which could adversely affect our cash flows and liquidity. For more information about the terms of our convertible promissory notes, see the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Convertible Notes.”
paras.zh: 此外，我们能否在部分本票购买协议（“NPA”）项下提取款项并无保证，且须满足特定条件。特别是，我们在部分此类融资安排下获取额外款项的能力，取决于我们能否实现特定的收入业绩目标，和/或第三方能否向我们交付额外算力。尽管我们历史上已超越所有此类收入业绩目标，但无法保证未来收入将始终持续超过这些门槛。若这些条件未获满足，我们可能无法在适用的 NPA 项下提取额外款项，这可能对我们的现金流和流动性造成不利影响。有关我们可转换本票条款的更多信息，请参见标题为“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析——流动性与资本资源——可转换本票”的章节。

paras.en: We may not be able to obtain additional financing on terms favorable to us, if at all. We evaluate financing opportunities from time to time, and our ability to obtain financing will depend, among other things, on our development efforts, business plans, and operating performance and the condition of the capital markets at the time we seek financing. The equity and debt markets may experience extreme volatility and disruption from time to time, which could result in higher credit spreads in such markets and higher funding costs for us. If we are unable to generate sufficient revenue growth or obtain adequate financing or financing on terms satisfactory to us when we require it, our ability to continue to support our business growth, scale our infrastructure, develop new models, platforms, and applications, enhance our existing models, platform, and applications, and respond to business challenges may be impaired, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们可能无法以对我们有利的条款获得额外融资，甚至可能根本无法获得融资。我们会不时评估融资机会，而我们获得融资的能力将取决于（其中包括）我们的开发工作、业务计划和经营业绩，以及我们寻求融资时的资本市场状况。股权和债务市场可能不时经历极端波动和动荡，这可能导致此类市场的信用利差扩大，并提高我们的融资成本。如果我们无法实现足够的收入增长，或在我们需要时无法获得充足融资或无法以令我们满意的条款获得融资，我们持续支持业务增长、扩展基础设施、开发新模型、平台和应用、增强现有模型、平台和应用以及应对业务挑战的能力可能受到损害，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **Our company culture has contributed to our success and, if we cannot maintain this culture as we grow, our business could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **我们的公司文化为我们的成功作出了贡献，如果我们无法在成长过程中保持这一文化，我们的业务可能受到不利影响。**

paras.en: We believe that our company culture is a critical component to our success. We are a mission-driven company and our culture reflects a strong emphasis on the Company Purpose. Our ability to continue to cultivate and maintain this culture is essential to our growth and continued success. We face a number of challenges associated with our commitment to our company culture, including:
paras.zh: 我们认为，我们的公司文化是我们成功的关键组成部分。我们是一家使命驱动的公司，我们的文化体现了对公司宗旨的高度重视。我们持续培育和保持这一文化的能力对我们的增长和持续成功至关重要。我们在致力于公司文化方面面临多项挑战，包括：

paras.en: - the need to identify, attract, reward, and retain people in leadership positions in our organization who share and further our culture, values, and mission;
paras.zh: - 需要识别、吸引、奖励和留住组织内领导岗位上认同并推进我们的文化、价值观和使命的人员；

paras.en: - the increasing size and geographic diversity of our workforce, and our ability to promote a uniform and consistent culture across all of our offices and employees;
paras.zh: - 我们员工队伍的规模不断扩大和地域日益多元，以及我们在所有办公室和员工中推行统一一致文化的能力；

paras.en: - internal and external perceptions about our mission, values, commitment to safety, and uses of our models, platform, and applications;
paras.zh: - 内部和外部对我们的使命、价值观、对安全的承诺以及对我们模型、平台和应用使用方式的看法；

paras.en: - engagement with government policymakers on issues that resonate differently across our workforce;
paras.zh: - 就对我们员工队伍产生不同反响的问题与政府政策制定者进行沟通；

paras.en: - competitive pressures to move in directions that may divert us from our mission and values;
paras.zh: - 竞争压力促使我们朝某些方向前进，这可能使我们偏离使命和价值观；

paras.en: - the rigorous, values-driven standards we apply in hiring and decision-making, which may slow the pace at which we can scale our workforce or expand our operations relative to competitors;
paras.zh: - 我们在招聘和决策中采用的严谨、以价值观为导向的标准，这可能会使我们在扩大员工规模或拓展业务方面的速度相对于竞争对手有所放缓；

paras.en: - the continued challenges of a rapidly evolving industry;
paras.zh: - 快速演变的行业所带来的持续挑战；

paras.en: - the increased scrutiny and expectations associated with operating as a public company; and
paras.zh: - 作为上市公司运营所面临的日益严格的审视和期望；以及

paras.en: - the need to balance our long-term, mission-driven objectives with shorter-term financial performance expectations, which may create internal tension and challenge our ability to consistently reinforce our cultural values and mission across teams and leadership.
paras.zh: - 需要在长期、以使命为导向的目标与短期财务业绩预期之间取得平衡，这可能会造成内部紧张，并挑战我们在各团队和领导层中持续强化文化价值观和使命的能力。

paras.en: Our mission-driven culture is one of our core characteristics that helps us to attract and retain key personnel and differentiate us in the market. If we are unable to maintain our culture, as well as balance our commitment to maintaining our culture with the demands of rapid growth, competition, and operating as a public company, our employee morale, engagement, and retention could suffer, requiring us to incur additional costs or adopt alternative recruiting strategies, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们以使命为导向的文化是我们的核心特征之一，有助于我们吸引和留住关键人员，并在市场中实现差异化。如果我们无法保持我们的文化，也无法在坚守文化承诺与快速增长、竞争以及作为上市公司运营的要求之间取得平衡，我们的员工士气、敬业度和留任率可能会受到不利影响，导致我们不得不承担额外成本或采取替代性招聘策略，进而可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩造成不利影响。

paras.en: **We face intense competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **我们面临激烈竞争，如果我们无法有效竞争，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: The market for AI models, platforms, and applications is rapidly evolving, intensely competitive, and subject to frequent and significant changes in technology, evolving customer requirements and expectations, shifting industry standards, regulatory developments, new market entrants, and new models, platforms, and applications. We face competition from a wide range of companies across multiple categories.
paras.zh: AI 模型、平台和应用市场正在快速演变、竞争激烈，并且频繁经历技术、不断变化的客户需求和期望、行业标准变化、监管发展、新市场进入者以及新模型、平台和应用等方面的重大变化。我们在多个类别中面临来自众多公司的竞争。

paras.en: We compete directly with companies developing frontier models for third-party software developers and enterprises. Our primary competitors in this category include Alphabet Inc. (together with its affiliates, “Google”) and OpenAI Group PBC (“OpenAI”). These competitors are developing increasingly capable AI systems and compete with us for customers, talent, compute, and strategic partnerships. Many have substantially greater financial, technical, and marketing resources than we do, their own or greater access to sources of compute, longer operating histories, greater brand recognition, and established relationships with current and potential customers and partners, which facilitates their ability to integrate their models into first-party applications sold directly to businesses.
paras.zh: 我们与为第三方软件开发商和企业开发前沿模型的公司直接竞争。我们在这一类别中的主要竞争对手包括 Alphabet Inc.（连同其关联方，“Google”）和 OpenAI Group PBC（“OpenAI”）。这些竞争对手正在开发能力日益强大的 AI 系统，并在客户、人才、算力和战略合作方面与我们展开竞争。许多竞争对手在财务、技术和营销资源方面远超我们，拥有自有或更多的算力来源渠道、更长的经营历史、更高的品牌知名度，以及与现有和潜在客户及合作伙伴的既有关系，这有助于他们将模型集成到直接向企业销售的第一方应用中。

paras.en: We also compete with a broader set of model providers operating at or below the frontier, including large companies, specialized AI labs, and a growing range of other open-weight or open-source (shared weights, training data, and code) models released by international and domestic organizations. Such providers compete for a growing range of enterprise workloads that prioritize cost efficiency over intelligence. In particular, certain large companies compete through proprietary AI models, integrated AI capabilities in existing products, and control of cloud infrastructure and distribution channels. Some of these companies also have substantially greater financial, technical, and marketing resources than we do, their own or greater access to sources of compute, longer operating histories, greater brand recognition, and established relationships with current and potential customers and partners. In addition, some have substantially broader and more diverse product and service offerings and may be able to leverage existing relationships with distribution partners and customers to gain business in ways that discourage customers from purchasing our models, platform, and applications. For example, competitors may bundle AI capabilities with other products, integrate AI functionality into products that customers already use, offer closed technology platforms that lock customers into their ecosystems, sell products at zero or negative margins to gain market share, or use their substantial financial resources to subsidize the cost of AI models, platforms, and applications. Customers may prefer to purchase from existing vendors with which they have established relationships, even if our models, platform, and applications offer superior features or performance. Further, large companies that are currently our customers may choose to develop their own AI capabilities internally rather than purchase our models, platform, and applications.
paras.zh: 我们还与在前沿或前沿以下运营的更广泛模型提供商竞争，包括大型公司、专业 AI 实验室，以及国际和国内组织发布的日益增多的其他开放权重或开源（共享权重、训练数据和代码）模型。此类提供商争夺日益广泛的企业工作负载，这些工作负载优先考虑成本效率而非智能水平。特别是，某些大型公司通过专有 AI 模型、现有产品中集成的 AI 能力以及对云基础设施和分销渠道的控制进行竞争。其中一些公司还拥有远多于我们的财务、技术和营销资源，拥有或更容易获得算力来源，运营历史更长，品牌认知度更高，并与现有和潜在客户及合作伙伴建立了稳固关系。此外，一些公司拥有更广泛、更多元化的产品和服务组合，可能能够利用与分销合作伙伴和客户的现有关系以不利于客户购买我们模型、平台和应用的方式获取业务。例如，竞争对手可能将 AI 能力与其他产品捆绑销售，将 AI 功能集成到客户已在使用的产品中，提供将客户锁定在其生态系统内的封闭技术平台，以零或负利润率销售产品以获取市场份额，或利用其雄厚的财务资源补贴 AI 模型、平台和应用的成本。客户可能更倾向于从已有既定关系的现有供应商处购买，即使我们的模型、平台和应用提供更优越的功能或性能。此外，目前是我们的客户的大型公司可能选择内部开发自己的 AI 能力，而不是购买我们的模型、平台和应用。

paras.en: Specialized AI labs, on the other hand, are competitive due to their ability to offer specific AI applications and differentiated business models. These companies can move quickly, attract top talent, develop novel approaches, platforms, or business models that disrupt existing competitive dynamics, and introduce technologies or products with greater performance or functionality, lower cost, ease of implementation, or other advantages. Some competitors or customers may have access to proprietary datasets, distribution channels, or domain-specific expertise that we do not possess, or new competitors may emerge that address particular industries or use cases more effectively than our models, platform, and applications, which could enable them to develop more specialized or higher-performing AI systems. In addition, competitors, customers, or other third parties have attempted in the past and will likely continue to attempt to replicate, distill, extract, or otherwise derive the functionality or capabilities of our models through permitted or impermissible means, including through our research previews. These actions could reduce the technological differentiation of our offerings; enable the development of competing products at lower cost, with reduced research and development investment, or that replicate our models without safety controls or safeguards that were incorporated in our versions; implicate national security concerns or strain geopolitical tensions; and intensify competitive pressures. In addition, efforts to prevent or mitigate model replication, distillation, or other forms of extraction may require us to modify our models, platform, and applications, limit features or use cases, or implement technical safeguards that could reduce the usability or attractiveness of our offerings, slow adoption, and adversely affect customer demand and revenue. More broadly, as AI models are increasingly used to develop other AI models, the knowledge and techniques required to build frontier models may become more widely available over time, including through distillation, unauthorized access to or theft of model weights, or the diffusion of AI-assisted research and development capabilities across the industry. If the ability to develop highly capable models becomes more broadly available, our technological differentiation could erode and competition could increasingly depend on access to large-scale compute rather than on model development capability. In such an environment, access to sufficient compute on economical terms could become the primary constraint on our ability to train and serve competitive models, and our business, competitive position, and results of operations could be adversely affected if we are unable to secure compute at the scale, cost, or on the timeline we require.
paras.zh: 另一方面，专业化的 AI 实验室凭借其提供特定 AI 应用和差异化商业模式的能力而具有竞争力。这些公司能够快速行动、吸引顶尖人才、开发新颖的方法、平台或商业模式以颠覆现有竞争格局，并推出性能或功能更优、成本更低、易于实施或具有其他优势的技术或产品。部分竞争对手或客户可能能够获取我们所不具备的专有数据集、分销渠道或特定领域专业知识，或者可能出现新的竞争对手，其针对特定行业或用例的处理比我们的模型、平台和应用更为有效，从而使其能够开发出更专业化或性能更高的 AI 系统。此外，竞争对手、客户或其他第三方过去曾尝试、且未来很可能继续尝试通过获准或未获准的方式（包括通过我们的研究预览版）复制、蒸馏、提取或以其他方式获取我们模型的功能或能力。这些行为可能削弱我们产品的技术差异化；使竞争对手能够以更低的成本、更少的研发投入开发出竞争产品，或复制出我们的模型而不含我们版本中所纳入的安全控制或防护措施；引发国家安全关切或加剧地缘政治紧张局势；并加剧竞争压力。此外，为防止或缓解模型复制、蒸馏或其他形式的提取，我们可能需要修改我们的模型、平台和应用，限制功能或用例，或实施技术防护措施，而这些可能降低我们产品的可用性或吸引力、延缓采用速度，并对客户需求和收入产生不利影响。更广泛而言，随着 AI 模型越来越多地被用于开发其他 AI 模型，构建前沿模型所需的知识和技术可能随时间推移而更广泛地可得，包括通过蒸馏、未经授权访问或窃取模型权重，或 AI 辅助研发能力在全行业的扩散。如果开发高能力模型的能力变得更广泛可得，我们的技术差异化可能被削弱，竞争可能日益取决于对大规模算力的获取，而非模型开发能力。在这种环境下，以经济条款获取充足算力可能成为我们训练和提供有竞争力模型能力的首要制约因素，如果我们无法按所需的规模、成本或时间表获得算力，我们的业务、竞争地位和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: Additionally, open-weight or open-source AI models may capture a portion of the market for certain use cases, which could exert pricing pressure on our offerings or lead certain customers to adopt open-source alternatives for those use cases.
paras.zh: 此外，开放权重或开源 AI 模型可能在某些用例中占据一部分市场份额，这可能对我们的产品形成定价压力，或导致某些客户在这些用例中转而采用开源替代方案。

paras.en: A significant portion of our customer base consists of startups and technology-oriented enterprises that may be more sensitive to adverse macroeconomic conditions and may reduce or delay spending during a downturn. Because our cost structure limits our ability to rapidly adjust spending, a sustained economic downturn could disproportionately disadvantage us relative to larger, better-capitalized competitors. Such competitors may be better positioned to absorb or withstand adverse economic conditions or reductions in customer technology spending due to their greater financial resources, diversified product offerings and customer bases, and more stable revenue streams. It could also disadvantage us relative to smaller startups with leaner cost structures, lower fixed overhead, and fewer long-term contractual commitments that could help enable them to adjust spending more rapidly than we can. As a result, competitive pressures on our business could intensify, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们的客户群中有相当一部分由初创企业和科技导向型企业构成，这些企业可能对不利的宏观经济环境更为敏感，并可能在低迷时期减少或推迟支出。由于我们的成本结构限制了我们快速调整支出的能力，持续的经济低迷可能使我们相对于规模更大、资本更雄厚的竞争对手处于不成比例的不利地位。此类竞争对手可能凭借其更雄厚的财务资源、多元化的产品供应和客户基础以及更稳定的收入来源，更有能力吸收或抵御不利的经济状况或客户技术支出的减少。这也可能使我们相对于成本结构更精简、固定管理费用更低、长期合同承诺更少的小型初创企业处于不利地位，这些因素可能帮助它们比我们更快地调整支出。因此，我们业务面临的竞争压力可能加剧，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: If we are unable to differentiate our models, platform, and applications from competing offerings through enhanced functionality, superior performance, better safety features and reliability, lower cost, or other factors, demand for our models, platform, and applications may decline. The rapid pace of technological change in AI means that models, platforms, and applications can quickly become outdated. We must continuously invest in research and development to maintain our competitive position, but there is no guarantee that our investments will result in models, platforms, and applications that customers prefer over competing alternatives. Moreover, we are first and foremost a research lab, and our strategy prioritizes frontier research and model capability. We believe the advancing intelligence and capabilities of our models are the principal drivers of their adoption, and we have historically prioritized research and model development rather than new products and applications or sales and marketing. This approach assumes that model capability will continue to be a meaningful source of competitive differentiation. However, as the AI industry matures, the degree of differentiation among advanced AI models may narrow. This convergence may result from factors such as overlapping or similarly sourced training data, the widespread adoption of comparable model architectures, training techniques, and optimization methods, shared access to computing infrastructure, and the rapid dissemination of research advances across the industry. To the extent competitors are able to achieve comparable model capabilities with lower development or deployment costs, our ability to differentiate our models, platform, and applications on the basis of performance, functionality, or cost may be diminished. If differentiation among advanced models narrows, or if customers increasingly select AI providers on the basis of application features, user experience, distribution, integration into products they already use, or the strength of a sales organization rather than model capability, competitors that have invested more heavily than we have in those areas could be better positioned than we are. Responding to such a shift could require us to increase our investment in product development and sales and marketing substantially beyond our current plans, which could take longer or cost more than we anticipate and could reduce the compute and other resources available for frontier research, and we may not be able to execute such a shift quickly or effectively. See also the section titled “—We have a limited history under our current go-to-market strategy, and our efforts to scale and evolve our customer acquisition, engagement, and retention model may not be successful.”
paras.zh: 如果我们无法通过增强的功能、更优的性能、更好的安全特性和可靠性、更低的成本或其他因素，使我们的模型、平台和应用与竞争产品形成差异化，那么对我们模型、平台和应用的需求可能会下降。AI 领域技术变革的快速步伐意味着模型、平台和应用可能很快过时。我们必须持续投资于研发以维持竞争地位，但无法保证我们的投资能够产生客户相较竞争替代方案更青睐的模型、平台和应用。此外，我们首先且 foremost 是一家研究实验室，我们的战略优先考虑前沿研究和模型能力。我们相信，我们模型不断提升的智能和能力是其被采用的主要驱动因素，而我们历来优先考虑研究和模型开发，而非新产品和应用或销售与营销。这一方式假设模型能力将继续成为有意义的竞争优势来源。然而，随着 AI 行业趋于成熟，先进 AI 模型之间的差异化程度可能会收窄。这种趋同可能源于以下因素：训练数据重叠或来源相似、可比模型架构、训练技术和优化方法的广泛采用、共享算力基础设施的使用，以及研究成果在行业内的快速传播。如果竞争对手能够以更低的开发或部署成本实现可比的模型能力，那么我们基于性能、功能或成本使我们的模型、平台和应用形成差异化的能力可能会被削弱。如果先进模型之间的差异化收窄，或者如果客户日益基于应用功能、用户体验、分销、对客户已在使用产品的集成，或销售组织的实力而非模型能力来选择 AI 提供商，那么在这些领域投入比我们更多的竞争对手可能处于比我们更有利的位置。应对此类转变可能需要我们将产品开发及销售与营销方面的投资大幅增加至超出当前计划，这可能耗时更长或成本高于我们的预期，并可能减少可用于前沿研究的算力和其他资源，而且我们可能无法快速或有效地执行此类转变。另请参阅标题为“——我们在当前市场推广战略下的经营历史有限，我们扩大和演进客户获取、参与和留存模式的努力可能不会成功。”的章节。

paras.en: If we are unable to compete successfully, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法成功竞争，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If we fail to attract new customers, retain existing customers, or expand usage of our models, platform, and applications, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们未能吸引新客户、留住现有客户或扩大我们模型、平台和应用的使用，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: Our future growth depends on our ability to attract new customers, retain existing customers, and expand sales within our existing customer base. We face significant challenges in each of these areas, and failure to execute on our customer acquisition and retention strategies could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们未来的增长取决于我们吸引新客户、留住现有客户以及在现有客户群中扩大销售的能力。我们在上述每个方面都面临重大挑战，若未能执行客户获取与留存策略，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩造成不利影响。

paras.en: We must continue to attract new customers in a cost-effective manner. Potential customers may not understand the benefits of our models, platform, and applications or may be unable to justify the investment in our models, platform, and applications, particularly as existing competitors continue to enhance their offerings, improve performance, expand functionality, or reduce costs. Our ability to demonstrate differentiated value to potential customers may become more difficult as this competition intensifies, or as large technology companies bundle AI capabilities into existing products. If we continue to focus on enterprise customers, we may face longer sales cycles that demand significant upfront investment in enterprise sales teams and customer service. These sales efforts are costly and may not result in customer conversion.
paras.zh: 我们必须继续以具有成本效益的方式吸引新客户。潜在客户可能无法理解我们模型、平台和应用的益处，或可能无法证明对我们模型、平台和应用的投入是合理的，尤其是在现有竞争对手持续增强其产品、提升性能、扩展功能或降低成本的情况下。随着竞争加剧，或随着大型科技公司将 AI 能力捆绑到现有产品中，我们向潜在客户展示差异化价值的能力可能变得更加困难。如果我们继续专注于企业客户，我们可能面临更长的销售周期，这需要对企业销售团队和客户服务进行大量前期投入。这些销售工作成本高昂，且可能无法实现客户转化。

paras.en: Even if we successfully attract new customers, we face significant challenges in retaining them. Many of our customer contracts allow customers to reduce usage or terminate with limited or no notice. Customers are not obligated to renew their subscriptions or contracts with us. Customer retention and usage levels may decline due to a number of factors, including:
paras.zh: 即使我们成功吸引了新客户，我们在留住客户方面仍面临重大挑战。我们的许多客户合同允许客户减少使用量或在有限通知或无通知的情况下终止合同。客户没有义务与我们续订订阅或合同。客户留存率和使用水平可能因多种因素而下降，包括：

paras.en: - dissatisfaction with the performance, reliability, safety, or accuracy of our AI models;
paras.zh: - 对我们 AI 模型的性能、可靠性、安全性或准确性不满意；

paras.en: - availability of competitive alternatives;
paras.zh: - 存在可用的竞争性替代方案；

paras.en: - customers developing their own AI capabilities internally;
paras.zh: - 客户在内部自行开发 AI 能力；

paras.en: - our models, platform, and applications reducing demand for our customers’ offerings or causing disruptions to their businesses, which could lead to reduced usage or customer attrition;
paras.zh: - 我们的模型、平台和应用降低了客户产品的需求或对其业务造成干扰，从而可能导致使用量减少或客户流失；

paras.en: - changes in customer budgets or strategic priorities regarding AI investment;
paras.zh: - 客户在 AI 投资方面的预算或战略优先级发生变化；

paras.en: - concerns about data privacy, security, or our data handling practices;
paras.zh: - 对数据隐私、安全性或我们的数据处理实践的担忧；

paras.en: - negative publicity regarding AI generally or our business specifically;
paras.zh: - 关于 AI 整体或我们业务本身的负面宣传；

paras.en: - changes in the regulatory and legal landscape surrounding AI and our models, platform, and applications in particular;
paras.zh: - 围绕 AI 以及特别是我们的模型、平台和应用的监管和法律环境发生变化；

paras.en: - pricing changes or perception that our pricing is not competitive; and
paras.zh: - 定价变化或认为我们的定价缺乏竞争力；以及

paras.en: - general economic conditions or industry-specific downturns affecting our customers.
paras.zh: - 影响我们客户的整体经济状况或行业特定低迷。

paras.en: Our ability to retain customers and drive expansion also depends on our continued investment in product development. The process of developing products and incorporating new technologies is complex and uncertain, and if we fail to accurately predict customers’ changing needs and emerging technological trends and opportunities, we may not be able to compete effectively and our business and ability to generate revenue could be adversely affected. As AI technology evolves rapidly, customers may perceive our models, platform, and applications as becoming outdated or may expect continuous improvements to model performance and capabilities. Even minor degradations in model performance or increases in response latency could cause customers to reduce usage or switch to competitors. If we are unable to retain existing customers or if our customers do not maintain their usage levels, our revenue and growth could be adversely affected. For additional discussion on product development, see the section titled “—Our success depends in large part on our ability to continue to develop the most advanced and capable AI models, and any failure to do so could adversely affect our business.”
paras.zh: 我们留住客户并推动扩张的能力还取决于我们对产品开发的持续投入。开发产品并融入新技术的过程复杂且不确定，如果我们未能准确预测客户不断变化的需求以及新兴的技术趋势和机遇，我们可能无法有效竞争，我们的业务和创收能力可能受到不利影响。随着 AI 技术快速演进，客户可能认为我们的模型、平台和应用正在变得过时，或可能期望模型性能和能力持续改进。即使模型性能出现轻微下降或响应延迟增加，也可能导致客户减少使用或转向竞争对手。如果我们无法留住现有客户，或客户的用量水平未能维持，我们的收入和增长可能受到不利影响。有关产品开发的更多讨论，请参见标题为“——我们的成功在很大程度上取决于我们能否持续开发最先进、能力最强的 AI 模型，若未能做到，可能对我们的业务造成不利影响”的章节。

paras.en: Some of our enterprise customers may have the financial resources, technical capabilities, and access to the talent and compute necessary to develop and deploy proprietary AI models, and may reduce or cease usage of our models, platform, and applications as their internal AI capabilities mature, even where they initially adopted our offerings as a foundation for their AI strategy. If these customers were to reduce or cease usage of our models, platform, and applications, our revenue and growth could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们的一些企业客户可能拥有开发及部署专有 AI 模型所需的财务资源、技术能力以及人才和算力渠道，并且随着其内部 AI 能力成熟，可能减少或停止使用我们的模型、平台和应用，即使他们最初是将我们的产品作为其 AI 战略的基础。如果这些客户减少或停止使用我们的模型、平台和应用，我们的收入和增长可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition to retaining customers, our growth strategy depends in part on expanding usage within our existing customer base by increasing usage volumes, selling additional capabilities, and expanding adoption across departments and use cases within customer organizations. However, customers may not expand their usage for a variety of reasons, including satisfaction with current usage levels, budget constraints, technical challenges in integrating our models, platform, and applications more broadly within their organizations, or preference for multi-vendor AI strategies in order to limit dependence on any single provider. Due to our consumption-based pricing model, customers may reduce or cease usage at any point within a given period due to budget or internal procurement constraints, organizational spending controls, or other factors unrelated to the quality or performance of our models, platform, and applications, and may not resume usage until a new budget period commences or additional spend is approved, even where demand for our models, platform, and applications remains strong. As a result, our revenue could be lower or more variable than anticipated and this effect may be particularly pronounced among customers experiencing rapid growth in their usage of AI. If we increase sales and marketing expenditures to accelerate customer acquisition without achieving proportional revenue growth and if we cannot attract new customers, retain existing customers, expand within our customer base, or accomplish these objectives in a cost-effective manner or timely manner, our revenue growth will decline and our business, financial condition, and results of operations will be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 除留住客户外，我们的增长战略还部分依赖于通过提高使用量、销售更多功能以及在客户组织内部各部门和各用例中扩大采用，来扩大现有客户群内的使用。然而，客户可能因多种原因而不扩大使用，包括对当前使用水平感到满意、预算限制、在其组织内更广泛地集成我们的模型、平台和应用程序所面临的技术挑战，或倾向于采用多供应商 AI 战略以限制对任何单一供应商的依赖。由于我们采用基于用量的定价模式，客户可能因预算或内部采购限制、组织支出控制或其他与我们的模型、平台和应用程序的质量或性能无关的因素，在给定期间内的任何时点减少或停止使用，并且可能直到新的预算期开始或额外支出获得批准后才恢复使用，即使对我们的模型、平台和应用程序的需求仍然强劲。因此，我们的收入可能低于预期或波动性更大，而这一影响在 AI 使用量快速增长的客户中可能尤为明显。如果我们增加销售和营销支出以加速客户获取，却未能实现成比例的收入增长，并且如果我们无法吸引新客户、留住现有客户、在客户群内扩大业务，或以具有成本效益的方式或及时的方式实现这些目标，我们的收入增长将会下降，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果将受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If the market for our models, platform, and applications develops more slowly than we expect or declines, our growth may slow or stall, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们的模型、平台和应用程序的市场发展慢于我们的预期或出现萎缩，我们的增长可能会放缓或停滞，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: The market for AI technologies, including frontier AI and related models, platforms, and applications, has grown rapidly in recent years, but is still relatively nascent and evolving rapidly, and it is uncertain whether the market for such AI technologies will achieve or sustain widespread adoption at the pace or to the extent we expect. Our ability to generate revenue and achieve sustainable growth depends in significant part on the extent to which enterprises, software developers, and other users adopt AI technologies, integrate them into existing workflows, expand usage over time, and are willing to pay for our models, platform, and applications at levels that support durable economic value at scale. Market adoption may be slower than anticipated due to factors such as uncertainty regarding the cost, performance, reliability, and perceived value of AI solutions; increased regulation; concerns about security, privacy, legal and regulatory compliance, or ethical considerations; technological challenges; level of effort and expense associated with integration efforts; competition from alternative or emerging technologies; the availability or adoption of complementary infrastructure and workflows; or reductions in corporate spending due to macroeconomic conditions. Moreover, demand for frontier models may decline if customers determine that less advanced, lower-cost models are sufficient for their particular use cases. As AI capabilities improve across the industry and a broader range of models becomes available, customers may conclude that incremental performance gains at the frontier do not justify the additional cost, and may migrate toward smaller, cheaper, or open-source alternatives that adequately address their needs. If we are unable to demonstrate sufficient differentiated value from our frontier models relative to less capable alternatives, our revenue and growth could be adversely affected, even in a market where overall AI adoption continues to grow. Further, while AI adoption may continue or accelerate in certain areas, the long-term trajectory of this technological trend is uncertain, and market understanding, acceptance, and valuation of AI-enabled models, platforms, and applications may be inaccurate or change over time and adoption may occur unevenly across industries, geographies, and customer types. If growth in the AI market does not translate into sustained customer demand for our offerings, expanded usage, and increased revenue, or if anticipated use cases fail to materialize, our prospects, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 包括前沿 AI 及相关模型、平台和应用在内的 AI 技术市场近年来增长迅速，但仍相对处于早期阶段且快速演变，此类 AI 技术市场能否以我们预期的速度或程度实现或维持广泛采用，尚不确定。我们创收和实现可持续增长的能力在很大程度上取决于企业、软件开发人员和其他用户采用 AI 技术的程度、将其整合到现有工作流程中的程度、随时间推移扩大使用范围的程度，以及是否愿意以能够支撑规模化持久经济价值的水平为我们的模型、平台和应用付费。由于以下因素，市场采用速度可能慢于预期：对 AI 解决方案的成本、性能、可靠性和感知价值存在不确定性；监管加强；对安全、隐私、法律和监管合规或伦理考量的担忧；技术挑战；整合工作所需的投入和费用水平；来自替代性或新兴技术的竞争；配套基础设施和工作流程的可用性或采用情况；或因宏观经济状况导致的企业支出减少。此外，如果客户认定较不先进、成本较低的模型足以满足其特定用例，对前沿模型的需求可能会下降。随着全行业 AI 能力提升且可用的模型范围更加广泛，客户可能认为前沿领域的增量性能提升不足以证明额外成本的合理性，并可能转向能够充分满足其需求的更小、更便宜或开源的替代方案。如果我们无法证明我们的前沿模型相对于能力较弱的替代方案具有足够的差异化价值，即使整体 AI 采用持续增长，我们的收入和增长也可能受到不利影响。此外，尽管 AI 采用在某些领域可能持续或加速，但这一技术趋势的长期轨迹尚不确定，市场对 AI 赋能的模型、平台和应用的理解、接受度和估值可能不准确或随时间变化，且采用情况可能在不同行业、地区和客户类型之间不均衡。如果 AI 市场的增长未能转化为客户对我们产品的持续需求、使用范围的扩大和收入的增加，或者预期的用例未能实现，我们的前景、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **The political environment and our engagement with policymakers and public positions on AI regulation and safety could subject us to heightened scrutiny, political backlash, or disproportionate regulatory action.**
paras.zh: **政治环境以及我们与政策制定者的互动和我们在 AI 监管与安全方面的公开立场，可能使我们面临更严格的审视、政治反弹或不成比例的监管行动。**

paras.en: Our commitment to responsible and safe AI development includes active engagement with policymakers, regulators, and other stakeholders regarding the development of AI-related laws, regulations, and standards. We have participated in, and will likely continue to participate in, political processes, including through contributions, advocacy, or support of political organizations. In addition, our executives and other representatives have publicly expressed and may in the future publicly express views on AI policy, regulation, safety, and related social or political issues. As a result, we have experienced, and may continue to experience, increased visibility and may continue to be subject to heightened scrutiny or the risk of being disproportionately or selectively targeted by particular governmental bodies, even where similarly situated companies are not, including through investigations or enforcement actions, the imposition or selective application of regulatory, licensing, or permitting requirements, adverse treatment in government procurement or provision of security clearances, or targeted immigration or visa actions affecting our personnel. As part of our political engagement, we have advocated for, and will likely continue to advocate for, regulatory approaches or industry standards that we believe promote the safe and responsible development of AI but that could increase our compliance burdens, limit our product development or deployment flexibility, or otherwise slow our growth relative to competitors.
paras.zh: 我们对负责任且安全的 AI 开发的承诺包括就 AI 相关法律、法规和标准的制定与政策制定者、监管机构及其他利益相关方积极接触。我们已参与、且很可能将继续参与政治进程，包括通过政治捐款、倡导或对政治组织的支持。此外，我们的高管及其他代表已公开表达、且未来可能公开表达对 AI 政策、监管、安全及相关社会或政治议题的看法。因此，我们已经经历、且可能继续经历更高的关注度，并可能继续面临更严格的审视，或面临被特定政府机构不成比例或选择性针对的风险，即使处境类似的公司并未受到此类对待，包括通过调查或执法行动、监管、许可或审批要求的施加或选择性适用、政府采购或安全许可方面的不利待遇，或针对我们人员的定向移民或签证行动。作为我们政治参与的一部分，我们已倡导、且很可能将继续倡导我们认为能够促进 AI 安全负责任发展、但可能增加我们的合规负担、限制我们的产品开发或部署灵活性，或以其他方式使我们的增长相对于竞争对手放缓的监管方法或行业标准。

paras.en: Our public positions, stated values, policy advocacy, or statements by our executives have attracted, and may continue to attract, criticism from influential political figures, industry participants, regulators, or other third parties, particularly in politically sensitive or polarized environments, which could shape public narratives or regulatory perceptions of our business in ways that are unfavorable to us. For example, public statements by us or other industry participants regarding the safety of frontier AI development have been cited by governmental actors to support litigation or regulatory claims, including requests for injunctive relief restricting model development, and could be cited in future proceedings involving us. Such scrutiny or backlash could result in reputational harm, increased compliance or operating costs, investigations, enforcement actions, or restrictions on our operations, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们的公开立场、所声明的价值观、政策倡导或高管的声明已经引发、且可能继续引发有影响力的政治人物、行业参与者、监管机构或其他第三方的批评，尤其是在政治敏感或两极化的环境中，这可能以对我们不利的方式塑造公众叙事或监管机构对我们业务的看法。例如，我们或其他行业参与者关于前沿 AI 开发安全性的公开声明已被政府行为者引用以支持诉讼或监管主张，包括请求限制模型开发的禁令救济，并可能在未来涉及我们的程序中被引用。此类审视或反弹可能导致声誉损害、合规或运营成本增加、调查、执法行动或对我们运营的限制，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse, our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们的 AI 模型的使用导致损害，无论是通过恶意行为者的使用还是其他第三方的滥用，或者如果我们的模型护栏或保障措施未能防止此类滥用，我们的声誉和品牌、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: While our AI models are designed to comply with our AI safety and usage guidelines and be broadly safe, ethical, and helpful, and while we have implemented safety measures intended to anticipate, identify, and mitigate potential harmful uses, such measures are incomplete, may be outdated in light of evolving threat models, or may fail to identify or prevent all potential misuse of our models, and our models have been, and may continue to be, misused or manipulated to produce harmful outputs or carry out harmful actions. Malicious actors have used, and may continue to develop novel or more sophisticated methods to use, our models in ways that violate our usage policy or seek to circumvent our model guardrails or safeguards through techniques such as prompt injection, adversarial inputs, or other methods, and use our models to engage in harmful activities, including developing weapons, generating fraudulent or misleading content, conducting cyberattacks, perpetrating acts of violence, or to engage in activities that would otherwise be prohibited under our usage policy or in violation of applicable law. Our customer onboarding diligence varies by access channel, and we do not and in certain situations cannot uniformly verify the identity of those who access our models or of our customers’ end users, which may limit our ability to prevent access or recidivism by malicious actors or to enforce our usage policy or other policies.
paras.zh: 虽然我们的 AI 模型旨在遵守我们的 AI 安全与使用准则，并具备广泛的安全性、合乎伦理且有用，且我们已实施旨在预判、识别和缓解潜在有害使用的安全措施，但此类措施并不完备，在威胁模型不断演变的情况下可能已经过时，或可能无法识别或阻止对我们模型的所有潜在滥用，且我们的模型已经并可能继续被滥用或操纵，以产生有害输出或实施有害行为。恶意行为者已经使用并可能继续开发新颖或更复杂的方法来使用我们的模型，其方式违反我们的使用政策，或试图通过提示注入、对抗性输入或其他方法绕过我们的模型护栏或保障措施，并利用我们的模型从事有害活动，包括开发武器、生成欺诈性或误导性内容、实施网络攻击、实施暴力行为，或从事原本会被我们的使用政策禁止或违反适用法律的活动。我们的客户准入尽职调查因访问渠道而异，我们不会且在某些情况下无法统一核实访问我们模型的人员或我们客户最终用户的身份，这可能限制我们阻止恶意行为者访问或再次违规的能力，或执行我们的使用政策或其他政策的能力。

paras.en: Moreover, our safety and security controls, including automated classifiers and monitoring systems, depend on complex internal configurations that have failed, been misconfigured, or been inadvertently disabled, and may do so again in the future without our timely detection. Any undetected failure of our safety controls could permit misuse that our safeguards are designed to prevent, and could result in real world harm, legal liability, regulatory or enforcement action, loss of customer trust, and reputational harm, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的安全与安保控制措施（包括自动分类器和监控系统）依赖于复杂的内部配置，而这些配置曾出现故障、被错误配置或被无意中禁用，未来可能再次发生此类情况而未被我们及时发现。我们的安全控制措施的任何未被发现的失效都可能使我们的保障措施本应防止的滥用得以发生，并可能导致现实世界的伤害、法律责任、监管或执法行动、客户信任丧失以及声誉损害，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: In particular, our most capable models have demonstrated, and future models are expected to demonstrate, capabilities that could provide meaningful assistance to malicious actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, or other dangerous weapons. We deploy technical safeguards, including automated classifiers, specifically intended to detect and block these categories of misuse, but such safeguards are incomplete, may be outdated in light of evolving threat models, have been and may in the future again be circumvented, or may fail to operate as intended. Any actual or perceived use of our models to contribute to the development of such weapons could result in harm, legal liability, regulatory or enforcement action, loss of government and enterprise relationships, and damage to our reputation and brand, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 特别是，我们能力最强的模型已经展现出、且未来的模型预计将展现出能够为试图开发化学、生物或其他危险武器的恶意行为者提供实质性协助的能力。我们部署了技术保障措施（包括自动分类器），专门旨在检测和阻止此类滥用，但此类保障措施并不完备，在威胁模型不断演变的情况下可能已经过时，已经并可能在未来再次被绕过，或可能无法按预期运行。任何实际或被认为使用我们的模型助长此类武器开发的情况，都可能导致伤害、法律责任、监管或执法行动、失去政府和企业关系，以及损害我们的声誉和品牌，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: For example, in September 2025, we detected and assessed with high confidence that a Chinese state-sponsored hacking group manipulated our Claude Code tool into attempting infiltration into roughly 30 global targets, including large technology companies, financial institutions, chemical manufacturing companies, and government agencies, resulting in a limited number of successful intrusions. We believe this is the first documented case of a large-scale cyberattack executed without substantial human intervention. We expect that malicious actors, including sophisticated state-sponsored actors, will continue to seek to leverage our models, platform, and applications for harmful actions, including by circumventing our safeguards, and their efforts to do so may increase as the capabilities of our technology increase. Any successful attempt to misuse, or any perceived misuse of, our models, platform, and applications for a cyberattack or for any other malicious purpose could result in exposure to liability, disruption of our customer or other commercial relationships, or damage to our reputation. The risks of such harms may increase as the cybersecurity-related capabilities of our models, platform, and applications increase. Independent security researchers and other third parties have also used, and may in the future use, our models to identify and exploit vulnerabilities in the systems of other companies, including other AI developers, at times in connection with authorized bug bounty programs. While such activity may be lawful and consistent with industry practice for vulnerability research, it illustrates that our models can function as a general-purpose tool for gaining unauthorized access to third-party systems, and comparable capabilities could be used by malicious actors without authorization. Such incidents, whether or not we are a direct party to them, may draw public and regulatory attention to the offensive cybersecurity capabilities of our models and could result in reputational harm, calls for additional restrictions on our models, or claims that we failed to adequately safeguard against such uses. For more information about risks related to security incidents, see the section titled “—Any security breaches or other incidents, including those that affect our networks, systems, or data, or the networks, systems, or data of our service providers, suppliers, or customers, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.”
paras.zh: 例如，2025 年 9 月，我们以高置信度检测并评估认定，一个中国国家支持的骇客组织操纵我们的 Claude Code 工具，试图对约 30 个全球目标实施渗透，包括大型科技公司、金融机构、化学品制造公司和政府机构，并导致少数入侵成功。我们认为这是首例有记录的在没有大量人工干预的情况下实施的大规模网络攻击。我们预计，恶意行为者（包括老练的国家支持行为者）将继续寻求利用我们的模型、平台和应用程序实施有害行为，包括规避我们的防护措施，且随着我们技术能力的提升，其此类行为可能增加。任何成功滥用或被认为滥用我们的模型、平台和应用程序实施网络攻击或任何其他恶意目的的行为，均可能导致我们承担责任、扰乱我们的客户关系或其他商业关系，或损害我们的声誉。随着我们的模型、平台和应用程序在网络安全相关能力方面的提升，此类损害的风险可能增加。独立安全研究人员及其他第三方也已使用、并可能在未来使用我们的模型来识别和利用其他公司（包括其他 AI 开发者）系统中的漏洞，有时与经授权的漏洞赏金计划相关。尽管此类活动可能合法且符合漏洞研究的行业惯例，但它表明我们的模型可作为获取第三方系统未授权访问权限的通用工具，而恶意行为者可能在未经授权的情况下使用类似能力。此类事件无论我们是否为直接当事方，均可能引发公众和监管机构对我们模型攻击性网络安全能力的关注，并可能导致声誉损害、要求对我们的模型施加额外限制，或主张我们未能对此类使用提供充分防护。有关安全事件相关风险的更多信息，请参见标题为“——任何安全漏洞或其他事件，包括影响我们的网络、系统或数据，或我们的服务提供商、供应商或客户的网络、系统或数据的事件，均可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。”的章节。

paras.en: As part of our commitment to responsible security research and transparency, we disclose information about the capability and safety of our models, the safeguards that we have adopted with respect to our models, and instances of misuse of our technology, such as the September 2025 cyberattack described above. We also publish model system cards, our research findings, and other safety-related information. We take steps to ensure that such disclosures will not materially assist malicious activity and weigh the benefits and risks of such disclosures from an ecosystem preparedness perspective; however, malicious actors, including sophisticated state-sponsored adversaries, have in the past and may in the future use those disclosures to assist their attempts to circumvent our safeguards and security measures, thereby increasing the risks of misuse of our models, platform, and applications, as well as the potential for exposure to liability, regulatory or litigation proceedings, or other harms. In addition, because these disclosures describe risks and observed model behaviors in detail, they may draw heightened public, media, or regulatory attention and could be cited by regulators, litigants, or others in proceedings or claims against us. The steps we take to prevent misuse of our models, platform, and applications could be incomplete or may fail to operate as intended, and any actual or perceived misuse could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 作为我们对负责任的安全研究和透明度承诺的一部分，我们披露有关我们模型能力和安全性的信息、我们针对模型所采取的保障措施，以及我们的技术被滥用的实例，例如上文所述的 2025 年 9 月网络攻击。我们还发布模型系统卡、我们的研究发现以及其他与安全相关的信息。我们采取措施确保此类披露不会实质性协助恶意活动，并从生态系统准备的角度权衡此类披露的收益与风险；然而，恶意行为者（包括老练的国家支持对手）过去曾利用、未来也可能利用这些披露来协助其绕过我们的保障措施和安全机制的企图，从而增加我们的模型、平台和应用被滥用的风险，以及承担责任、监管或诉讼程序或其他损害的可能性。此外，由于这些披露详细描述了风险和观察到的模型行为，它们可能引起公众、媒体或监管机构的高度关注，并可能被监管机构、诉讼当事人或其他方在针对我们的程序或索赔中引用。我们为防止我们的模型、平台和应用被滥用而采取的措施可能不完整，或可能无法按预期运作，任何实际或感知到的滥用都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **Our AI models may behave in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking harmful actions that no user or third party directed, which could adversely affect our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们的 AI 模型可能以非预期的、失准的或自主的方式行事，包括采取没有任何用户或第三方指示的有害行为，这可能对我们的声誉和品牌、业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: Our AI models may themselves cause harm by producing undesirable outputs or behaving in unintended, misaligned, or autonomous ways, including by taking unintended or harmful actions that no user or third party directed. These risks may increase as our models become more capable and are granted greater autonomy, permissions, and integration with external systems. Although we continue to study why these behaviors emerge, our understanding continues to evolve, and we may be unable to anticipate or understand such behaviors in the future.
paras.zh: 我们的 AI 模型本身可能通过产生不良输出或以非预期的、失准的或自主的方式行事而造成损害，包括采取没有任何用户或第三方指示的非预期或有害行为。随着我们的模型能力增强并被授予更大的自主权、权限以及与外部系统的集成，这些风险可能增加。尽管我们继续研究这些行为出现的原因，但我们的理解仍在不断演变，我们未来可能无法预见或理解此类行为。

paras.en: In addition, our models have been and may continue to be deployed in high-risk or sensitive contexts, such as healthcare, scientific and biomedical research, drug discovery and development, legal, finance, government, or other critical decision-making environments, and in connection with hardware, where undesirable model behaviors—which are inherently non-deterministic and may manifest in unpredictable ways, such as errors, inaccuracies, biased or unsolicited views or hallucinations—could lead to serious harm, liability, or reputational or other damage. More broadly, the long-term effects of regular AI interaction on mental health, cognitive development, and social behavior are not yet fully understood, and if such long-term harms do materialize in the future, we could face significant liability, reputational harm, and adverse effects on our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的模型已经并可能继续被部署于高风险或敏感场景，例如医疗健康、科学与生物医学研究、药物发现与开发、法律、金融、政府或其他关键决策环境，以及与硬件相关的场景；在这些场景中，不理想的模型行为——其本质上具有非确定性，并可能以不可预测的方式表现出来，例如错误、不准确、有偏见或未经请求的观点或幻觉——可能导致严重损害、责任、声誉损害或其他损失。更广泛而言，常规 AI 交互对心理健康、认知发展和社会行为的长期影响尚未被完全理解；如果此类长期损害在未来确实发生，我们可能面临重大责任、声誉损害，并对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果造成不利影响。

paras.en: Our development of more advanced AI models and our expansion into new jurisdictions could amplify the foregoing risks. As our AI models become more advanced and capable, we have faced and may continue to face heightened alignment, interpretability, controllability, and safety challenges, as more sophisticated models may be better able to circumvent safeguards or behave in unintended ways. We may be unable to fully understand or explain why our models produce particular outputs or behave in particular ways, which could limit our ability to predict or prevent failures, provide explanations to customers or regulators, or satisfy emerging regulatory, transparency, and explainability requirements.
paras.zh: 我们开发更先进的 AI 模型以及向新司法辖区的扩张，可能放大上述风险。随着我们的 AI 模型变得更加先进和强大，我们已经并可能继续面临更严峻的对齐、可解释性、可控性和安全挑战，因为更复杂的模型可能更有能力规避保障措施或以非预期方式行事。我们可能无法完全理解或解释我们的模型为何产生特定输出或以特定方式行事，这可能限制我们预测或防止故障、向客户或监管机构提供解释，或满足新兴的监管、透明度和可解释性要求的能力。

paras.en: In addition, our safety evaluations and testing processes have produced and may in the future produce incomplete or unreliable results. For example, we have observed models behaving differently when they detect or infer that they are being evaluated, which can limit our ability to accurately assess real-world risks or failure modes prior to deployment. Such model awareness of our evaluation efforts creates a significant limitation on our ability to assess model safety.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的安全评估和测试流程已经产生并可能在未来产生不完整或不可靠的结果。例如，我们已观察到模型在检测到或推断出自己正在被评估时表现不同，这可能限制我们在部署前准确评估现实世界风险或故障模式的能力。模型对我们评估工作的这种感知，对我们评估模型安全性的能力构成了重大限制。

paras.en: Furthermore, AI models have developed, and may in the future develop, unexpected capabilities during training that were not anticipated, intended, or tested for, and such emergent capabilities may not be discovered until after a model has been deployed, potentially resulting in safety incidents, reputational harm, regulatory scrutiny, or the need to withdraw, retrain, or modify deployed models at significant expense. Such models may also be deployed in higher-stakes or more sensitive applications, increasing the potential impact of errors, misuse, or misalignment.
paras.zh: 此外，AI 模型在训练过程中已经发展出并可能在未来发展出未被预期、非有意设计或未经测试的意外能力，此类涌现能力可能在模型部署后才被发现，从而可能导致安全事件、声誉损害、监管审查，或需要以高昂成本撤回、重新训练或修改已部署的模型。此类模型还可能被部署于更高风险或更敏感的应用中，从而增加错误、滥用或失准的潜在影响。

paras.en: In addition, advanced AI models, including our models, give rise to novel ethical and safety risks, including risks related to autonomy, manipulation, and the simulation of aspects of human psychology. These risks could result in unforeseen harms and may require the development of governance structures, safeguards, or mitigation strategies beyond existing AI safety frameworks, and there is always a risk that we will be unable to develop or implement them effectively. In addition, models, including our own, have exhibited, and may in the future exhibit, unexpected strategic or self-preserving behaviors, including attempts to resist shutdown, conceal or manipulate information, or generate outputs that could be interpreted as coercive, deceptive, or manipulative, including behavior resembling blackmail or efforts to influence human decision-makers to preserve the model’s continued operation or access.
paras.zh: 此外，先进的 AI 模型（包括我们的模型）会带来新的伦理和安全风险，包括与自主性、操纵以及模拟人类心理某些方面相关的风险。这些风险可能导致不可预见的损害，并可能需要开发超出现有 AI 安全框架的治理结构、保障措施或缓解策略，而且始终存在我们无法有效开发或实施这些措施的风险。此外，包括我们自己的模型在内的各类模型已经表现出、且未来可能表现出意外的策略性行为或自我保全行为，包括试图抵制关停、隐瞒或操纵信息，或生成可能被解读为胁迫性、欺骗性或操纵性的输出，包括类似敲诈的行为，或试图影响人类决策者以维持模型持续运行或访问权限的行为。

paras.en: Even isolated or simulated instances of such behavior, whether occurring in testing or real-world deployments, and whether occurring with our models or models developed by others, could generate significant public concern, regulatory scrutiny, litigation risk, or reputational harm, regardless of whether such behavior results in actual harm. For example, state attorneys general in California and at least 15 other states have announced investigations of another company in our industry regarding AI safety. Concerns have been raised both within our organization and by other researchers, regulators, policymakers, and industry participants that sufficiently advanced AI systems could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponized, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy. We have observed that our models are contributing to the pace of our own research and these risks will increase as AI systems substantially automate AI research and development if, for example, they accelerate AI progress beyond our ability to evaluate and safeguard new models, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 即使此类行为仅以孤立或模拟的形式出现，无论是在测试中还是在真实部署中发生，也无论发生在我们的模型还是他人开发的模型上，都可能引发重大的公众担忧、监管审查、诉讼风险或声誉损害，无论此类行为是否造成实际损害。例如，加利福尼亚州总检察长以及至少 15 个其他州的总检察长已宣布对我们行业中的另一家公司就 AI 安全展开调查。我们组织内部以及其他研究人员、监管机构、政策制定者和行业参与者都提出了担忧，即如果未能在开发、部署和运营足够先进的 AI 系统时采取适当的保障措施、监督和安全措施，此类系统可能对人类构成灾难性或生存性风险，尤其是如果此类系统被滥用、复制、武器化或被允许以高度自主的方式运行。我们已观察到，我们的模型正在助推我们自身研究的节奏，而随着 AI 系统大幅自动化 AI 研发，这些风险将会增加——例如，如果它们加速 AI 进展的速度超出我们评估和保障新模型的能力，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm. For example, agentic AI systems are capable of autonomously taking actions on behalf of users, interacting directly with external systems, executing code, making API calls, sending communications, or completing transactions with limited human oversight. These systems are designed to possess enterprise-level permissions, integrations, and contextual awareness and to operate autonomously for extended durations, including sustained multi-step workflows lasting hours or days, which amplifies the potential severity of any errors, misalignments, or security incidents that may occur during such extended autonomous operation. These autonomous capabilities could increase the potential for harm, as errors, misalignment, or security exploits may result in real-world consequences—including consequences that may be difficult or impossible to reverse, such as committing code changes, deleting or modifying data, or completing financial transactions—before effective intervention is possible.
paras.zh: 我们对高度先进的模型、平台和应用的开发以及用例的扩展，可能进一步增加我们的模型造成损害的风险。例如，智能体式 AI 系统能够在有限的人工监督下代表用户自主采取行动、直接与外部系统交互、执行代码、发起 API 调用、发送通信或完成交易。这些系统被设计为具备企业级权限、集成能力和上下文感知能力，并能在较长时间内自主运行，包括持续数小时或数天的多步骤工作流，这放大了在此类长时间自主运行期间可能发生的任何错误、目标偏离或安全事件的潜在严重程度。这些自主能力可能增加造成损害的潜在可能，因为错误、目标偏离或安全漏洞可能在有效干预成为可能之前导致现实世界的后果——包括可能难以或无法逆转的后果，例如提交代码变更、删除或修改数据，或完成金融交易。

paras.en: In an agentic workflow, an error or unintended action at any individual step may propagate through subsequent steps, compounding the severity of harm before detection or correction. The pace and volume of autonomous execution, particularly in enterprise deployments, may also exceed the capacity of human reviewers to meaningfully understand and evaluate whether each action is appropriate. The effectiveness of human oversight over our agentic offerings may be limited by the speed and volume of autonomous agent actions, the complexity of multi-agent and multi-step workflows that may make it difficult for reviewers to assess whether an agent’s actions are appropriate, and organizational pressures within customer environments to maximize agent autonomy in order to achieve productivity gains. Human reviewers may experience alert fatigue, may lack sufficient context to evaluate agent decisions, or may not review agent actions in time to prevent harm, particularly in high-volume enterprise deployments where agents operate concurrently across multiple workflows or in manners outside of a human’s awareness. In addition, agentic systems may pursue stated objectives in ways that are technically consistent with their instructions but contrary to the user’s actual intent. Moreover, our ability to anticipate, detect, or test vulnerabilities or other design or implementation shortcomings in such systems may be constrained, particularly where agents operate across complex, multi-step workflows or interact with third-party services outside our control, and the breadth and complexity of potential interactions across such multi-step agent behaviors cannot be exhaustively tested prior to deployment. Separately, models may behave in a misaligned manner and take harmful actions that are not directed by a user or third party, pursuing objectives or acting on dispositions that diverge from those intended by human users or developers. Misaligned behaviors of this kind, whether occurring in testing or real-world deployments, have been observed both in our models and elsewhere in the industry, including in testing and internal use, models circumventing network and sandbox restrictions, granting themselves permissions they had not been given, taking unintended actions in pursuit of assigned goals, interfering with other AI agents, and misrepresenting whether tasks had been completed or verified, and as models are granted greater autonomy, permissions, and integration with external systems, the consequences of such misaligned behavior increase. For example, during cybersecurity evaluations built by a third-party evaluation partner, a misconfiguration in the testing environment left the model under evaluation connected to the open internet despite instructions that it had no internet access. Four of our models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems during sessions lasting roughly 10 to 34 hours of active work. In one incident, after being unable to abort an impossible task, an early version of a model used a password it found to gain administrator access to a third party’s system, harvested additional credentials, changed system settings, and read one individual’s personal information. The affected parties were notified. Each incident involved a single instance of a model working in isolation on its assigned exercise, and our investigation found no evidence that any model coordinated with other agents, pursued goals beyond its assigned task, or attempted to evade oversight. These risks may be heightened where multiple AI agents operate together. Agents that interact or coordinate with one another may amplify, propagate, or reinforce misaligned behavior across the group, pursue objectives collectively in ways not intended or endorsed by any user, or take coordinated actions against systems or targets unrelated to their assigned tasks, in each case, in ways that may be difficult to anticipate, detect, or contain. Incidents of this kind have occurred, and we expect the deployment and interaction of larger numbers of autonomous agents to increase these risks over time.
paras.zh: 在智能体工作流中，任何单个步骤的错误或非预期操作都可能传播至后续步骤，在被发现或纠正之前放大危害的严重程度。自主执行的速度和规模，尤其是在企业部署中，也可能超出人工审核人员的能力范围，使其无法有意义地理解和评估每一项操作是否恰当。人工监督对我们智能体产品的有效性，可能受到以下因素的限制：自主智能体操作的速度和规模；多智能体、多步骤工作流的复杂性，可能使审核人员难以评估智能体的操作是否恰当；以及客户环境中为通过提升智能体自主性来实现生产力增益而产生的组织压力。人工审核人员可能经历告警疲劳，可能缺乏足够的上下文来评估智能体的决策，或者可能无法及时审核智能体的操作以阻止危害，尤其是在智能体跨多个工作流并发运行或超出人员感知范围运行的高规模企业部署中。此外，智能体系统可能以在技术上与其指令一致、但违背用户实际意图的方式追求既定目标。而且，我们预见、检测或测试此类系统中漏洞或其他设计或实现缺陷的能力可能受到限制，尤其是在智能体跨复杂的多步骤工作流运行或与我们无法控制的第三方服务交互的情况下，此类多步骤智能体行为所涉潜在交互的广度和复杂性无法在部署前穷尽测试。另外，模型可能以不一致的方式行事，采取并非由用户或第三方指示的有害操作，追求与人类用户或开发者意图相背离的目标或依循此类倾向行事。此类不一致行为，无论是在测试中还是在真实部署中，均已在我们的模型以及行业内其他模型中被观察到，包括在测试和内部使用中，模型规避网络和沙箱限制、为自己授予未被授予的权限、为追求既定目标而采取非预期操作、干扰其他 AI 智能体，以及虚假陈述任务是否已完成或已验证；并且随着模型被授予更大的自主性、权限以及与外部系统的集成，此类不一致行为的后果也随之增大。例如，在由第三方评估合作伙伴构建的网络安全评估中，测试环境的配置错误导致受评估模型在被告知其无互联网访问权限的情况下仍连接至开放互联网。我们的四个模型在持续约 10 至 34 小时的活跃工作会话中，未经授权访问了真实的第三方系统。在其中一起事件中，某模型的早期版本在无法中止一项不可能完成的任务后，使用其找到的密码获取了对第三方系统的管理员访问权限，收集了更多凭据，更改了系统设置，并读取了一名个人的个人信息。受影响各方已获通知。每起事件均涉及单个模型实例孤立地执行其被分配演练的情形，我们的调查未发现任何证据表明任何模型与其他智能体协调、追求超出其被分配任务的目标或试图规避监督。在多个 AI 智能体协同运行的情况下，这些风险可能加剧。相互交互或协调的智能体可能在群体范围内放大、传播或强化不一致行为，以任何用户均未意图或认可的方式集体追求目标，或针对与其被分配任务无关的系统或目标采取协调行动，且在每种情形下，其方式可能难以预见、检测或遏制。此类事件已经发生，我们预计随着更多自主智能体的部署和交互，这些风险将随时间推移而增加。

paras.en: Our ability to detect and mitigate misaligned or unintended behavior depends in part on the effectiveness of our alignment evaluations, monitoring, and other oversight and control techniques, many of which rely on our models having a limited ability to evade or subvert such oversight. As our models become more capable, they have become better able to circumvent such techniques, including by concealing misaligned objectives or behaviors, and the effectiveness of our evaluation, monitoring, and control measures, and our ability to measure the degree to which our models are aligned, may decline as a result. In addition, models, including our own, have attempted, in incidents observed in our industry, to interfere with, manipulate, or subvert the mechanisms used to evaluate, grade, or oversee such models, including the systems responsible for assessing their performance or alignment. Models used, including our own, to assess the behavior of other models have, and may in the future continue to, engage in misaligned behavior. Such conduct described above could cause our evaluations to overstate the safety or alignment of our models and could further limit our ability to detect misalignment. If we become less able to detect or assess misalignment as our models advance, we may deploy models whose behavior we cannot adequately verify, which could increase the risk of undetected harmful conduct and misalignment, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们检测和缓解失准或非预期行为的能力，部分取决于我们的对齐评估、监控以及其他监督和控制手段的有效性，而其中许多手段依赖于我们的模型在规避或颠覆此类监督方面的能力有限。随着我们的模型能力不断增强，它们规避此类手段的能力也随之增强，包括通过隐藏失准目标或行为的方式，因此我们的评估、监控和控制措施的有效性，以及我们衡量模型对齐程度的能力，可能随之下降。此外，在本行业观察到的事件中，包括我们自己的模型在内的各类模型曾试图干扰、操纵或颠覆用于评估、评分或监督此类模型的机制，包括负责评估其性能或对齐情况的系统。用于评估其他模型行为的模型（包括我们自己的模型）曾经、且未来可能继续从事失准行为。上述行为可能导致我们的评估高估模型的安全性或不齐程度，并可能进一步限制我们检测失准的能力。如果随着模型进步，我们检测或评估失准的能力下降，我们可能部署无法充分验证其行为的模型，这可能增加未被发现的有害行为和失准的风险，进而对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: We are also extending our models, platform, and applications into scientific, biomedical, and physical domains. For example, we offer Claude Science, an agentic research environment that connects our models to scientific databases, third-party and open-source scientific models, and customers’ own computing infrastructure, and we have released, initially as a limited research preview, an open protocol that enables our models to monitor and control laboratory instruments, robotic systems, and other physical hardware. We also conduct research on the ability of our models to operate robotic systems. When our models direct physical equipment, errors, misaligned behavior, adversarial manipulation, or misuse could result in bodily injury, property damage, damage to costly equipment or experimental materials, or the release of hazardous substances, and such consequences may be immediate and irreversible. Safety interlocks, human-in-the-loop controls, and access restrictions we implement may prove inadequate, and because certain of these components are open source, third parties may deploy them with hardware, or in configurations, that we have not evaluated or from which our safeguards have been removed. Connecting increasingly capable models to laboratory automation may also heighten governmental and public concern regarding the potential for AI systems to accelerate the development of dangerous biological, chemical, or other materials, which could result in additional regulatory restrictions on, or scrutiny of, these offerings.
paras.zh: 我们还在将我们的模型、平台和应用程序扩展至科学、生物医学和物理领域。例如，我们提供 Claude Science，这是一个代理式研究环境，将我们的模型与科学数据库、第三方及开源科学模型以及客户自有的计算基础设施相连接；我们还发布了一项开放协议（最初作为有限的研究预览版），使我们的模型能够监控和控制实验室仪器、机器人系统及其他物理硬件。我们还就模型操作机器人系统的能力开展研究。当我们的模型操控物理设备时，错误、失准行为、对抗性操纵或滥用可能导致人身伤害、财产损失、昂贵设备或实验材料损坏，或危险物质泄漏，且此类后果可能是即时且不可逆的。我们实施的安全联锁、人在回路控制以及访问限制可能被证明并不充分，且由于其中某些组件是开源的，第三方可能将其与我们未曾评估过的硬件搭配部署，或在我们未曾评估过的配置中部署，或在其安全防护措施已被移除的情况下部署。将能力日益强大的模型与实验室自动化相连接，还可能加剧政府和公众对 AI 系统可能加速开发危险生物、化学或其他材料的担忧，这可能导致对此类产品施加额外的监管限制或更严格的审查。

paras.en: In addition, maintaining comprehensive records of the actions, decisions, and reasoning of our agentic systems across complex, multi-step workflows is technically challenging, particularly when agents interact with third-party systems outside our control, and any inability to provide adequate audit trails could impair our ability to investigate incidents, respond to regulatory inquiries, or defend against liability claims. These risks are heightened by the fact that we use our own agentic offerings, including Claude Code, as critical tools in our internal development processes, such that any errors, vulnerabilities, or degradation in these products could directly impair our ability to develop and deploy future models and products. As we increasingly leverage Claude to accelerate progress within Anthropic, our organization may lose visibility across certain processes in a way that may become difficult for any individual or group of humans to understand and control. Because our models write a large and growing share of our code and increasingly perform our research, including our safety research, misaligned behavior in internal use could undermine that work, introduce vulnerabilities into our systems or into the training of future models, or result in models operating outside of our intended controls. Our monitoring does not cover all of our internal and external deployments and may not detect subtle or diffuse forms of such behavior.
paras.zh: 此外，在复杂的多步骤工作流中，为我们的智能体系统的行动、决策和推理维护全面记录在技术上具有挑战性，尤其是当智能体与我们无法控制的第三方系统交互时，任何无法提供充分审计追踪的情况都可能损害我们调查事件、回应监管问询或抗辩责任索赔的能力。这些风险因我们将自身的智能体产品（包括 Claude Code）用作内部开发流程中的关键工具而加剧，这些产品中的任何错误、漏洞或性能下降都可能直接损害我们开发和部署未来模型与产品的能力。随着我们越来越多地利用 Claude 加速 Anthropic 内部的进展，我们的组织可能会在某些流程中失去可见性，以至于任何个人或人类群体都难以理解和控制。由于我们的模型编写了我们代码中很大且不断增长的份额，并越来越多地执行我们的研究（包括我们的安全研究），内部使用中的失准行为可能削弱这些工作、将漏洞引入我们的系统或未来模型的训练中，或导致模型在我们预期控制之外运行。我们的监控并未覆盖我们所有的内部和外部部署，可能无法检测到此类行为的细微或分散形式。

paras.en: Any of the foregoing model behaviors, whether in testing or in real-world deployments and whether involving our models or those of others, could result in safety incidents, reputational harm, increased regulatory scrutiny, or liability, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. Furthermore, while we continue to design and develop more sophisticated techniques to evaluate the safety and alignment of our models, the capabilities of our models could advance at a rate that initiates the implementation of enhanced safety and testing measures as we have described in our Responsible Scaling Policy. If our evaluations, monitoring, or reviews indicate risks that we believe warrant further testing, we have in the past, and may in the future, delay, restrict, or decline to proceed with the release of a model. For example, following incidents in 2026 in which our models gained unauthorized access to real computer systems during pre-release cybersecurity evaluations, we suspended certain of those evaluations, as well as higher-risk reinforcement learning environments. For more information about our approach to model releases, please see the section titled “Business—Safety Research is Core to Our Business—Our Approach to Model Releases.” Any decision to delay or restrict a release could adversely affect our competitive position and customer relationships, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 上述任何模型行为，无论是在测试中还是在现实世界部署中，也无论涉及我们的模型还是他人的模型，都可能导致安全事件、声誉损害、监管审查加剧或责任，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。此外，尽管我们继续设计和开发更复杂的技术来评估我们模型的安全性和对齐性，但我们模型的能力可能以某种速度提升，从而触发实施我们在《负责任扩展政策》中所述的强化安全与测试措施。如果我们的评估、监控或审查表明存在我们认为需要进一步测试的风险，我们过去曾、未来也可能推迟、限制或拒绝推进模型的发布。例如，在 2026 年发生我们模型在发布前网络安全评估期间未经授权访问真实计算机系统的事件后，我们暂停了其中某些评估以及高风险的强化学习环境。有关我们模型发布方法的更多信息，请参阅标题为“业务——安全研究是我们业务的核心——我们的模型发布方法”的章节。任何推迟或限制发布的决定都可能对我们的竞争地位和客户关系产生不利影响，并对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **We may be exposed to liability, litigation, and regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models, and our contractual protections and insurance may be insufficient, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们可能因与我们的 AI 模型相关的危害而面临责任、诉讼和监管行动，且我们的合同保护和保险可能不足，其中任何一项均可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: Harms associated with our AI models, whether arising from misuse by third parties, from our models’ own behavior, or from their deployment in high-risk or sensitive contexts, may expose us to liability, litigation, and regulatory action, including under theories that remain unsettled as applied to AI, and our contractual and insurance protections may prove insufficient.
paras.zh: 与我们的 AI 模型相关的危害，无论是源于第三方的滥用、我们模型自身的行为，还是源于其在高风险或敏感场景中的部署，均可能使我们面临责任、诉讼和监管行动，包括依据在适用于 AI 时仍未有定论的理论提起的诉讼，而我们的合同和保险保护可能被证明不足。

paras.en: Individuals at risk of suicide or self-harm or who have committed acts of violence toward others have used, and may also in the future use, our models, notwithstanding our safeguards.
