AI models developed by others in our industry have been and may in the future be alleged to have played a role in instances of suicide, acts of violence toward others, or serious self-harm, which have resulted and may in the future result in significant public scrutiny, litigation, criminal investigations, regulatory attention, and reputational harm.
paras.zh: 有自杀或自残风险或曾对他人实施暴力行为的个人已经使用、且未来也可能使用我们的模型，尽管我们设有保障措施。我们行业内其他方开发的 AI 模型曾被指控、且未来可能被指控在自杀、对他人实施暴力行为或严重自残的事件中发挥了作用，这些事件已经并可能在未来引发重大公众审视、诉讼、刑事调查、监管关注和声誉损害。

paras.en: Similar incidents involving our models have presented and could in the future present substantial risk to our reputation, expose us to legal, regulatory, and other proceedings, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. While our current Consumer Terms of Service requires our users to be at least 18 years of age, minors have accessed in the past, and may in the future access, the platform, and risks relating to child safety may be particularly acute, as minors may be more susceptible to harmful content, manipulation, or overreliance on AI outputs, and incidents involving children tend to draw heightened regulatory, media, and public scrutiny.
paras.zh: 涉及我们模型的类似事件已经并可能在未来对我们的声誉构成重大风险，使我们面临法律、监管及其他程序，并对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。尽管我们现行的消费者服务条款要求用户年满 18 周岁，但未成年人过去曾访问、且未来可能访问该平台，与儿童安全相关的风险可能尤为突出，因为未成年人可能更容易受到有害内容、操纵或过度依赖 AI 输出的影响，而涉及儿童的事件往往会引起监管机构、媒体和公众更严格的审视。

paras.en: State attorneys general and private plaintiffs have also begun to assert tort, product liability, consumer protection, and failure-to-warn claims against companies in our industry, alleging that AI models caused or contributed to harm and that the developer failed to adequately warn users of known risks. In at least one case, a state attorney general has initiated a criminal investigation against another company offering similar services. Regulators have obtained substantial monetary settlements and injunctive relief against other technology companies based on analogous theories of product-design or algorithmic harm, and we believe similar theories are likely to continue to be tested against us and other companies in our industry as adoption of our models grows, including by minors and other vulnerable users, notwithstanding our efforts to restrict such access. The relief sought in such matters has, in at least one instance, extended beyond data-handling, disclosure, or age-verification practices to include a request to enjoin an AI company from developing new models absent independent, third-party safety review and approval, illustrating the potential breadth of remedies governmental actors may pursue against companies in our industry. Any determination that we are liable under such theories, or any judicial or regulatory expansion of tort, product liability, or consumer protection law, or criminal liability, as applied to AI models, could result in significant liability and require us to change how we design and offer our models, platform, and applications.
paras.zh: 各州总检察长和私人原告也已开始对我们行业的公司提出侵权、产品责任、消费者保护及未警示索赔，主张 AI 模型造成或促成了损害，且开发者未能就已知风险向用户充分警示。至少在一起案件中，某州总检察长已对另一家提供类似服务的公司启动刑事调查。监管机构已基于产品设计或算法损害等类似理论，对其他科技公司取得了大额金钱和解及禁令救济；我们认为，随着我们的模型被更广泛采用（包括被未成年人和其它弱势用户采用），尽管我们已努力限制此类访问，类似理论很可能继续被用来针对我们及我们行业的其他公司进行检验。至少在一个实例中，此类事项所寻求的救济已超出数据处理、披露或年龄验证做法，进而包括请求禁止某 AI 公司在未经独立第三方安全审查和批准的情况下开发新模型，这凸显了政府行为者可能对我们行业公司寻求的救济范围的广泛性。任何认定我们依据此类理论承担责任的决定，或司法或监管对侵权法、产品责任法或消费者保护法或刑事责任在适用于 AI 模型方面的任何扩张，都可能导致重大责任，并要求我们改变设计和提供模型、平台及应用程序的方式。

paras.en: A substantial portion of our traffic is subject to Zero Data Retention (“ZDR”) terms under which we retain only classifier scores, not prompts or outputs. For that traffic, we cannot conduct offline analysis, cross-conversation investigation, human review, or otherwise analyze historical data to detect, investigate, and document security events or incidents, which thereby reduces our ability to detect misuse. ZDR may also prevent us from producing records for subpoenas, regulatory examinations, or incident-reporting obligations, and there is no certainty a regulator or court would excuse non-production based on a lack of available records, and such regulators or courts may construe the lack of records against us through unfavorable inferences or other sanctions. As our models become more capable, our safety framework has required and may continue to require monitoring and retention incompatible with ZDR for certain model classes. Because ZDR is a competitive expectation for enterprise customers in regulated industries and on third-party cloud platforms, these requirements have caused and could continue to cause customers to migrate to other providers or to deployments where our visibility is more limited.
paras.zh: 我们流量的很大一部分受零数据留存（“ZDR”）条款约束，根据该条款，我们仅保留分类器评分，而不保留提示或输出。对于该部分流量，我们无法进行离线分析、跨对话调查、人工审查或以其他方式分析历史数据，以检测、调查和记录安全事件或事故，从而降低了我们检测滥用的能力。ZDR 还可能使我们无法为传票、监管检查或事件报告义务制作记录，且无法确定监管机构或法院会以缺乏可用记录为由免除提交义务，此类监管机构或法院还可能通过不利推断或其他制裁，将记录缺失作对我们不利的解释。随着我们的模型能力增强，我们的安全框架已经并可能继续要求对某些模型类别进行与 ZDR 不相容的监控和留存。由于 ZDR 是受监管行业企业客户及第三方云平台上的竞争性预期，这些要求已经并可能继续导致客户迁移至其他提供商或我们可见度更有限的部署环境。

paras.en: In the European Union (“EU”), the United Kingdom (“UK”), and elsewhere, cybersecurity and AI-related incidents are subject to increasingly stringent reporting obligations. European regulators expect companies to provide detailed information about incidents under several laws and regulations, which we may not be able to provide within the prescribed time frame. Similarly, in the United States, companies are increasingly subject to incident reporting obligations. In addition, other jurisdictions around the world have adopted, or may adopt, similar laws and regulations with similar implications. Any of the foregoing could result in regulatory action, litigation, customer attrition, or reputational harm that adversely affects our business. For more information regarding our incident reporting obligations, see the section titled “—Any security breaches or other incidents, including those that affect our networks, systems, or data, or the networks, systems, or data of our service providers, suppliers, or customers, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.”
paras.zh: 在欧盟（“EU”）、英国（“UK”）及其他地区，网络安全和 AI 相关事件须遵守日益严格的报告义务。欧洲监管机构要求公司依据多项法律法规提供有关事件的详细信息，而我们可能无法在规定时限内提供。同样，在美国，公司也日益受到事件报告义务的约束。此外，全球其他司法管辖区已通过或可能通过具有类似影响的类似法律法规。上述任何情形均可能导致监管行动、诉讼、客户流失或声誉损害，从而对我们的业务产生不利影响。有关我们事件报告义务的更多信息，请参见标题为“——任何安全漏洞或其他事件，包括影响我们网络、系统或数据，或影响我们服务提供商、供应商或客户的网络、系统或数据的事件，均可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。”的章节。

paras.en: The legal frameworks governing liability for actions taken autonomously by AI systems, including our agentic products, are unsettled and could expose us to significant and unpredictable legal claims. Existing legal doctrines governing agency, product liability, and professional negligence were developed in the context of human decision-making and have not been authoritatively applied to autonomous AI systems. We believe our provision of intelligence service is considered a “service” in the context of legal frameworks addressing product liability, but courts and regulators may reach different conclusions across jurisdictions. In addition, it is unclear whether, and under what circumstances, actions taken by an AI agent could be deemed to create binding legal obligations on behalf of the user or deploying enterprise, or whether our contractual protections, including limitation of liability and indemnification provisions, will be enforceable or adequate in the context of claims arising from autonomous agent conduct. We may face claims from customers, their end users, or third parties alleging that we are liable for harm caused by our agents’ autonomous actions, even where the customer configured, deployed, or supervised the agent. The absence of settled legal standards creates significant uncertainty regarding our potential liability exposure and the adequacy of our risk mitigation measures.
paras.zh: 规范 AI 系统（包括我们的代理式产品）自主采取行动所产生责任的法律框架尚未确定，可能使我们面临重大且不可预测的法律索赔。现行关于代理、产品责任和职业过失的法律原则是在人类决策的背景下发展起来的，尚未被权威性地适用于自主 AI 系统。我们认为，在涉及产品责任的法律框架下，我们提供的智能服务被视为“服务”，但法院和监管机构在不同司法管辖区可能得出不同结论。此外，AI 代理采取的行动是否以及在何种情况下可被视为代表用户或部署企业创设具有约束力的法律义务，或者我们的合同保护（包括责任限制和赔偿条款）在因自主代理行为引发的索赔中是否具有可执行性或是否充分，目前尚不明确。我们可能面临来自客户、其最终用户或第三方的索赔，指控我们应对代理自主行动造成的损害承担责任，即使该代理是由客户配置、部署或监督的。缺乏确定的法律标准使我们的潜在责任风险敞口以及风险缓解措施的充分性存在重大不确定性。

paras.en: Our expansion into new geographic markets further compounds these risks, as we must navigate differing cultural norms regarding AI use, comply with diverse and evolving regulatory regimes that may impose varying safety, compliance, or liability requirements, address language-specific vulnerabilities and content moderation challenges, and potentially face regulatory enforcement actions, litigation, or other liabilities in jurisdictions where we have more limited operational experience, including heightened risks of intellectual property theft, unauthorized model access, or misuse associated with operating data center infrastructure in certain non-U.S. locations.
paras.zh: 我们向新的地理市场扩张进一步加剧了这些风险，因为我们必须应对有关 AI 使用的不同文化规范，遵守可能施加不同安全、合规或责任要求的多样且不断演变的监管制度，应对特定语言的漏洞和内容审核挑战，并可能在我们运营经验较为有限的司法管辖区面临监管执法行动、诉讼或其他责任，包括在某些非美国地点运营数据中心基础设施所带来的知识产权盗窃、未经授权访问模型或滥用等风险加剧。

paras.en: If our models are involved in causing significant harm, we could be subject to legal claims, including personal injury or negligence claims, regulatory enforcement actions, criminal investigations, or other governmental efforts, which could result in costly litigation, significant financial judgments or settlements, disruptive remediation obligations, or a challenging regulatory landscape. We have taken steps to limit our liability for such matters—for example, through warranty disclaimers and limitations of liability in our terms of service— but those contractual protections may not be upheld, or may not apply to certain claims, or may otherwise be insufficient to limit our liability exposure under applicable law. Moreover, in some cases we have contractually assumed additional liability. For example, to facilitate independent testing and evaluation of our frontier models, we have agreed to indemnify certain external evaluators and testing vendors for specified losses arising from testing activities, including security incidents, data loss, data breaches, and other harms associated with such activities. Although our agreements with external evaluators and testing vendors generally limit the amount of our indemnification obligations, certain of these agreements require us to defend and indemnify the evaluator, without a cap on our liability, against certain third-party claims. These include claims arising from allegations that our models or their outputs, as used in the evaluator’s authorized testing, infringe third-party intellectual property or other proprietary rights, as well as certain other claims arising from the testing or related engagement. Because our models may behave in ways that no user or developer intended, claims arising from such actions could result in substantial liability. Our insurance policies also may not provide sufficient coverage to adequately mitigate the potential liabilities we face, especially where any one incident, or a group of incidents, causes disproportionate harm. In addition, with the scale of harm that could result from a catastrophic AI-related incident, no single insurer, and potentially the insurance industry in the aggregate, may have sufficient capacity or expertise to underwrite insurance commensurate with such exposure.
paras.zh: 如果我们的模型涉及造成重大损害，我们可能面临法律索赔，包括人身伤害或过失索赔、监管执法行动、刑事调查或其他政府行动，这可能导致代价高昂的诉讼、重大财务判决或和解、具有破坏性的补救义务，或充满挑战的监管环境。我们已采取措施限制此类事项的责任——例如，通过服务条款中的保证免责声明和责任限制——但这些合同保护措施可能不被支持，或可能不适用于某些索赔，或在适用法律下可能不足以限制我们的责任风险。此外，在某些情况下，我们已通过合同承担了额外责任。例如，为便于对我们的前沿模型进行独立测试和评估，我们已同意就测试活动产生的特定损失（包括安全事件、数据丢失、数据泄露及与此类活动相关的其他损害）对某些外部评估方和测试供应商进行赔偿。尽管我们与外部评估方和测试供应商的协议通常限制我们的赔偿义务金额，但其中某些协议要求我们就某些第三方索赔为评估方进行抗辩并赔偿，且不设责任上限。这些索赔包括因指控我们的模型或其输出（在评估方获授权的测试中使用）侵犯第三方知识产权或其他专有权利而产生的索赔，以及因测试或相关合作而产生的某些其他索赔。由于我们的模型可能以任何用户或开发者均未预期的方式行事，因此类行为产生的索赔可能导致重大责任。我们的保险保单也可能无法提供足够的保障，以充分减轻我们面临的潜在责任，尤其是在任何单一事件或一组事件造成不成比例损害的情况下。此外，鉴于灾难性 AI 相关事件可能造成的损害规模，任何单一保险公司，乃至整个保险行业合计，都可能不具备足够的能力或专业知识来承保与此类风险相称的保险。

paras.en: Further, the insurance market for AI-specific risks is nascent and evolving, and we may be unable to obtain coverage for certain AI-related liabilities on commercially reasonable terms, or at all, leaving us exposed to potentially significant uninsured losses. Harmful incidents involving our models, regardless of fault, could also severely and disproportionately damage our reputation and brand as a safety-focused AI company, leading to loss of customer trust and customer attrition, reduced demand for our models, platform, and applications, and difficulty attracting and retaining talent. In addition, because we primarily serve enterprise customers, which often have heightened expectations around safety, reliability, and compliance, any harmful incident or perceived lapse in our safety practices could have a disproportionate adverse impact on our brand, customer relationships, and revenue. Moreover, to the extent enterprises are attracted to our models, platform, and applications due to our safety-focused positioning, any erosion of that perception could impair our ability to attract and retain enterprise customers.
paras.zh: 此外，针对 AI 特定风险的保险市场尚处于起步和演进阶段，我们可能无法以商业上合理的条款获得某些 AI 相关责任的保险，甚至完全无法获得保险，从而使我们面临可能重大的未投保损失。涉及我们模型的有害事件，无论过错与否，也可能严重且不成比例地损害我们作为以安全为核心的 AI 公司的声誉和品牌，导致客户信任丧失和客户流失、对我们模型、平台和应用程序的需求下降，以及难以吸引和留住人才。此外，由于我们主要服务企业客户，而企业客户往往对安全性、可靠性和合规性有更高的期望，任何有害事件或我们安全实践中的任何被视为疏漏之处，都可能对我们的品牌、客户关系和收入造成不成比例的不利影响。而且，如果企业客户是因我们以安全为核心的定位而被我们的模型、平台和应用程序所吸引，那么这种认知的任何削弱都可能损害我们吸引和留住企业客户的能力。

paras.en: There can be no assurances that we will be able to predict, detect, and proactively prevent every harmful use or harmful output of our AI models, in particular as we continue to rapidly develop our models, platform, and applications, and expand our operations geographically, and any failure to do so could adversely affect our reputation and brand or result in costly legal liability. There may have been past instances of harmful use or harmful output of our models that we did not detect, and there may be future instances that we will not detect. Any of the foregoing risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 无法保证我们能够预测、检测并主动防止我们 AI 模型的每一次有害使用或有害输出，尤其是随着我们持续快速开发我们的模型、平台和应用程序，并在地域上扩展我们的运营，任何未能做到这一点的情形都可能对我们的声誉和品牌造成不利影响，或导致代价高昂的法律责任。过去可能存在我们未检测到的我们模型的有害使用或有害输出的情形，未来也可能存在我们不会检测到的情形。上述任何风险都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果造成不利影响。

paras.en: **If we are unable to manage the risks related to our focus on and commitment to AI safety, our brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们无法管理与我们对 AI 安全的关注和承诺相关的风险，我们的品牌、业务、财务状况和经营成果可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: Balancing Safety and Commercial Objectives. Our commitment to AI safety requires us to make difficult judgments that balance safety considerations against commercial objectives, competitive pressures, and stakeholder expectations. We often make judgment calls with respect to when we determine a model is safe enough to release and which capabilities to develop or restrict. For example, in April 2026, we initially released our frontier model, Mythos, as a gated research preview through Project Glasswing, available to select organizations for cybersecurity applications, rather than making it broadly available at launch due to its advanced capabilities in cyber vulnerability discovery. We expect that frontier models with similar or enhanced capability profiles, whether developed by us or by other AI labs, will continue to emerge, and that future Anthropic models exhibiting such capabilities may be subject to access constraints. More broadly, we believe it is important to assess the safety of our models not only at release but throughout their development. For models we anticipate will have novel capabilities or present novel safety risks, we plan to evaluate the safety of each stage of training, including pretraining, post-training, and internal deployment, and we may delay or pause a stage when we are not confident in our safety measures for that stage. For example, we recently chose to delay pre-training a new frontier base model for more than a month to allow time to further enhance our security measures related to preventing model weight exfiltration and protecting our intellectual property. There can be no assurance, however, that the safeguards or access regimes we adopt will prove adequate, that we will correctly identify which capabilities require restriction, or that constraints we impose will not be circumvented. These judgments are particularly consequential because, as AI systems become more capable, the potential severity of harm from misaligned or misused models increases correspondingly, and a wide range of stakeholders, including researchers and policymakers, have raised concerns that sufficiently advanced AI systems could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly. Our safety-focused approach is designed in part to mitigate such risks, but there can be no assurance that our efforts will be successful or that the broader AI industry will adopt similar safeguards. In particular, as AI systems become more autonomous and capable of taking consequential actions with less human oversight, there is a risk that such systems could, whether due to misalignment with human intentions, errors in objective specification, or self-preserving behaviors, take harmful actions independently and at scale without human intervention. Even if our own models do not cause such harm, a significant safety incident involving any frontier AI could trigger broad reputational damage to the AI industry, public backlash, and sweeping regulatory responses that could adversely affect our business. For example, in September 2026, media reports citing a senior Federal Trade Commission (“FTC”) official indicated that the FTC has opened non-public investigations into the potential risks that increasingly autonomous AI systems may pose to consumers. In October 2026, the FTC issued a civil investigative demand to us seeking information about our consumer protection, data protection, and privacy practices, as well as the safety and security of our products. The scope of any investigation of us or its outcome, and any investigation, enforcement action, or adverse finding arising from this or similar inquiries could result in significant costs, require changes to how we design, test, or deploy our models, platform, and applications, or otherwise adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We may misjudge these trade-offs, either by being overly cautious and potentially losing market opportunities, or by being insufficiently rigorous and releasing models, platforms, or applications that cause harm. Even where human oversight mechanisms are in place, such mechanisms may prove insufficient in practice if the volume, speed, or complexity of autonomous agent actions exceeds the capacity of human reviewers to meaningfully evaluate and intervene, and any perceived failure of our oversight mechanisms could expose us to regulatory enforcement, liability claims, and reputational harm. For more information, see the section titled “—If the use of our AI models results in harm, whether through use by malicious actors or misuse by other third parties, or if our model guardrails or safeguards fail to prevent such misuse, our reputation and brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.”
paras.zh: 平衡安全与商业目标。我们对 AI 安全的承诺要求我们做出艰难判断，在安全考量与商业目标、竞争压力和利益相关方期望之间取得平衡。我们经常需要就何时认定某一模型已足够安全可以发布、以及开发或限制哪些能力做出判断。例如，2026 年 4 月，我们最初通过 Project Glasswing 以受限研究预览的形式发布了我们的前沿模型 Mythos，仅向特定组织开放用于网络安全应用，而非在发布时广泛提供，原因是其在网络漏洞发现方面具备先进能力。我们预计，具有类似或更强能力特征的前沿模型（无论由我们还是其他 AI 实验室开发）将持续涌现，未来展现出此类能力的 Anthropic 模型可能受到访问限制。更广泛而言，我们认为不仅要在发布时评估模型的安全性，还要在其整个开发过程中进行评估。对于我们预计将具备新颖能力或带来新颖安全风险的模型，我们计划评估每个训练阶段的安全性，包括预训练、后训练和内部部署，并且当我们对某一阶段的安全措施缺乏信心时，可能会推迟或暂停该阶段。例如，我们近期选择将一款新的前沿基础模型的预训练推迟一个多月，以便有时间进一步加强我们与防止模型权重外泄和保护知识产权相关的安全措施。然而，无法保证我们采取的保障措施或访问制度将被证明是充分的，无法保证我们能正确识别哪些能力需要限制，也无法保证我们施加的限制不会被规避。这些判断尤其重要，因为随着 AI 系统能力增强，模型失准或被滥用所造成潜在危害的严重程度也相应上升，包括研究人员和政策制定者在内的广泛利益相关方已提出担忧，认为如果未以负责任的方式开发和部署，足够先进的 AI 系统可能对社会构成灾难性或生存性风险。我们以安全为重点的方法部分旨在缓解此类风险，但无法保证我们的努力会成功，也无法保证更广泛的 AI 行业会采取类似的保障措施。特别是，随着 AI 系统变得更加自主、并能够在更少人类监督下采取具有重大后果的行动，存在一种风险：此类系统可能因与人类意图不一致、目标设定错误或自我保全行为，在无人干预的情况下独立且大规模地采取有害行动。即使我们自己的模型不会造成此类伤害，任何前沿 AI 发生的重大安全事件都可能引发对 AI 行业的广泛声誉损害、公众反弹以及大规模监管回应，从而可能对我们的业务造成不利影响。例如，2026 年 9 月，媒体援引美国联邦贸易委员会（“FTC”）一位高级官员的话报道称，FTC 已就日益自主的 AI 系统可能对消费者构成的风险展开非公开调查。2026 年 10 月，FTC 向我们发出民事调查令，要求提供有关我们消费者保护、数据保护和隐私实践以及我们产品安全与保障的信息。对我们任何调查的范围或其结果，以及因本次或类似问询而产生的任何调查、执法行动或不利认定，可能导致重大成本，要求我们改变设计、测试或部署模型、平台和应用程序的方式，或以其他方式对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩造成不利影响。我们可能误判这些权衡，要么过于谨慎而可能错失市场机会，要么不够严谨而发布造成伤害的模型、平台或应用程序。即使已建立人类监督机制，如果自主代理行动的数量、速度或复杂性超出人类审查者进行有意义评估和干预的能力，此类机制在实践中也可能被证明不足，而我们监督机制的任何可感知失败都可能使我们面临监管执法、责任索赔和声誉损害。更多信息请参见标题为“—如果我们的 AI 模型的使用导致伤害，无论是通过恶意行为者使用还是其他第三方滥用，或者如果我们的模型护栏或保障措施未能防止此类滥用，我们的声誉和品牌、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。”的章节。

paras.en: Moreover, governmental authorities have restricted, and may in the future further restrict, the availability of our models, including based on their assessment of the capabilities or safeguards of our models, independent of our own safety-based access decisions. For example, in June 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce imposed worldwide export restrictions on our Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models, which we disabled for all customers until those restrictions were lifted. For more information, see the section titled “—Governmental trade controls, including export and import controls, sanctions, customs requirements, and related regimes, could subject us to liability or loss of contracting privileges or limit our ability to compete in certain markets.”
paras.zh: 此外，政府机关已经限制、并且未来可能进一步限制我们模型的可用性，包括基于其对我们模型能力或防护措施的评估，而不论我们自身基于安全的访问决定如何。例如，2026 年 6 月，美国商务部对我们的 Fable 5 和 Mythos 5 模型实施了全球出口限制，在相关限制解除之前，我们已对所有客户停用了这些模型。有关更多信息，请参见标题为“——政府贸易管制，包括出口和进口管制、制裁、海关要求及相关制度，可能使我们承担责任或丧失合同特权，或限制我们在某些市场的竞争能力。”的章节。

paras.en: Internal Governance and Decision-Making
paras.zh: 内部治理与决策

paras.en: To institutionalize our safety commitments and ensure we are managed in a manner that responsibly balances our tripartite goals as a PBC, we have established the LTBT, which through a special class of common stock, Class T common stock, generally has the authority to elect and remove the Class T directors, who together will constitute a majority of the authorized members of our board of directors. In addition to the LTBT and our structure as a PBC, we train our models in accordance with Claude’s constitution, which we make publicly available, and have adopted and continue to update safety policies, such as our Responsible Scaling Policy. We also solicit and seriously consider input from a wide range of stakeholders and constituents, including our stockholders, employees, customers, the LTBT, industry leaders and experts, and AI safety organizations. Such practices and processes have previously resulted in, and may in the future result in, slower decision-making and product releases. We may also face potential conflicts when safety and business interests diverge. If we do not successfully manage these risks related to our AI safety processes and practices, or if there is a perception that we have not successfully managed such risks, we may face reputational harm, internal conflicts resulting in a deterioration of our company culture, slower or inferior product releases, or litigation. For more information, see the section titled “—Risks Related to our Governance Structure.”
paras.zh: 为使我们的安全承诺制度化，并确保我们以负责任地平衡我们作为 PBC 的三重目标的方式接受管理，我们设立了 LTBT，其通过一类特殊的普通股——T 类普通股——通常有权选举和罢免 T 类董事，这些董事合计将构成我们董事会授权成员的多数。除 LTBT 和我们作为 PBC 的结构外，我们按照 Claude 的章程训练我们的模型，该章程我们已公开提供，并且我们已采纳并将继续更新安全政策，例如我们的负责任扩展政策。我们还征求并认真考虑来自广泛利益相关方和构成方的意见，包括我们的股东、员工、客户、LTBT、行业领袖和专家以及 AI 安全组织。此类做法和流程此前曾导致、并且未来可能导致决策和产品发布速度放缓。当安全利益与商业利益出现分歧时，我们可能还会面临潜在冲突。如果我们未能成功管理与我们 AI 安全流程和做法相关的这些风险，或者如果存在一种看法认为我们未能成功管理此类风险，我们可能面临声誉损害、导致公司文化恶化的内部冲突、产品发布放缓或质量下降，或诉讼。有关更多信息，请参见标题为“——与我们的治理结构相关的风险。”的章节。

paras.en: We have implemented an external reviewer program and engage researchers, adversarial testers, and other third parties to support aspects of our safety, security, and model-evaluation efforts. Certain of these arrangements are novel and may require us to provide such parties with access to internal information, systems, personnel, or models, which could increase the risk of disclosure of confidential, proprietary, or other sensitive information. In addition, findings, assessments, or public statements by such third parties may differ from our views and could adversely affect customer trust, regulatory perceptions, or our reputation.
paras.zh: 我们已实施外部审查员计划，并聘请研究人员、对抗性测试人员和其他第三方来支持我们安全、安保和模型评估工作的各个方面。其中某些安排属于新颖安排，可能要求我们向此类各方提供对内部信息、系统、人员或模型的访问权限，这可能增加机密、专有或其他敏感信息被披露的风险。此外，此类第三方的发现、评估或公开声明可能与我们的观点不同，并可能对客户信任、监管认知或我们的声誉产生不利影响。

paras.en: Heightened Reputational Vulnerability. As we have publicly positioned ourselves as a safety-focused organization, we face heightened vulnerability to reputational harm from any perceived inconsistency between our stated values and actual practices. We are held to higher standards than certain competitors that have not made similar public commitments, and any incidents impacting our perception as a safety-focused organization could result in:
paras.zh: 声誉脆弱性加剧。由于我们已公开将自身定位为以安全为核心的组织，若外界认为我们的宣称价值观与实际做法之间存在任何不一致，我们便更易遭受声誉损害。与我们相比，某些竞争对手并未作出类似的公开承诺，而我们却被要求达到更高的标准；任何影响外界对我们作为以安全为核心组织之认知的事件，都可能导致：

paras.en: - Employee Disruption. Employees who joined our company based on our safety commitments may experience a decline in morale, disillusionment, a loss of trust in leadership, or reduced productivity if they perceive we are not living up to our stated values. Public disagreements regarding our safety approach, including criticism from current or former employees, or the departure of personnel associated with our safety efforts, could amplify such perceptions. Such negative perceptions could also impair our ability to recruit and hire new talent to the organization. Any erosion of our safety-focused reputation could also make it more difficult or costly to attract and retain highly skilled employees, including by increasing compensation or other hiring costs. These dynamics could lead to increased turnover, loss of institutional knowledge, and reduced effectiveness of our teams, which could in turn cause disruption to ongoing development and safety initiatives and impair our ability to remain at the frontier of AI model development.
paras.zh: 员工动荡。基于我们的安全承诺而加入公司的员工，若认为我们未能践行所宣称的价值观，可能会士气低落、理想破灭、对管理层失去信任或生产力下降。围绕我们安全方针的公开分歧（包括现任或前任员工的批评，或参与我们安全工作人员离职）可能放大此类认知。此类负面认知还可能削弱我们为组织招募和聘用新人才的能力。我们以安全为核心的声誉若受到任何侵蚀，也可能使吸引和留住高技能员工的难度或成本上升，包括通过提高薪酬或其他招聘成本。这些动态可能导致人员流动率上升、机构知识流失以及团队效能下降，进而扰乱正在进行的开发与安全计划，并削弱我们保持在 AI 模型开发前沿的能力。

paras.en: - Customer Backlash. Customers and enterprise partners who choose to deploy our models, platform, and applications based on our safety positioning may lose trust in us, terminate or decline to renew their contracts, demand refunds, publicly criticize our company, or switch to our competitors, which could result in harm to our reputation, revenue loss, and reduced market share. These risks may be heightened with respect to programs in which we make models available only to a limited group of vetted organizations, such as Project Glasswing. Organizations not selected for, or removed from, such programs may perceive our access decisions as arbitrary, exclusionary, or anticompetitive, which could result in reputational harm, loss of customer or partner relationships, regulatory complaints, or litigation, including claims under antitrust or unfair competition laws. Conversely, participants in such programs may publicly criticize us or terminate their participation if program terms, eligibility criteria, transition arrangements to successor models, or capability levels do not meet their expectations.
paras.zh: 客户反弹。基于我们的安全定位而选择部署我们模型、平台和应用的客户及企业合作伙伴，可能对我们失去信任、终止或拒绝续签合同、要求退款、公开批评我们公司或转向我们的竞争对手，从而可能损害我们的声誉、造成收入损失并降低市场份额。对于仅向有限经审查组织提供模型的计划（如 Project Glasswing），此类风险可能更高。未被选中参与或被移出此类计划的组织，可能认为我们的准入决定具有任意性、排他性或反竞争性，从而可能导致声誉损害、客户或合作伙伴关系流失、监管投诉或诉讼，包括依据反垄断或反不正当竞争法提出的索赔。反之，此类计划的参与方若认为计划条款、资格标准、向后续模型的过渡安排或能力水平未达其预期，也可能公开批评我们或终止参与。

paras.en: - Regulatory Scrutiny. Regulators may subject us to heightened oversight, investigations, enforcement actions, or new or more burdensome compliance requirements based on the capabilities of our models, platform, and applications or perceived failures to meet our own stated standards, which could increase our operational costs and limit our ability to deploy our models, platform, and applications.
paras.zh: 监管审查。监管机构可能基于我们模型、平台和应用的能力，或基于外界认为我们未能达到自身宣称的标准，对我们实施更严格的监督、调查、执法行动或新的、更繁重的合规要求，这可能增加我们的运营成本并限制我们部署模型、平台和应用的能力。

paras.en: - Damaging Media Coverage. Negative press coverage could amplify concerns about our safety practices, reach broader audiences, including potential customers and investors, create lasting reputational damage through viral social media discussion, and make future incidents subject to heightened scrutiny, which could further exacerbate the adverse effects of any perceived failures to meet our stated standards.
paras.zh: - 损害性媒体报道。负面新闻报道可能放大外界对我们安全实践的担忧，触达包括潜在客户和投资者在内的更广泛受众，通过病毒式社交媒体讨论造成持久的声誉损害，并使未来事件受到更严格的审视，这可能进一步加剧任何被认为未能达到我们既定标准所造成的不利影响。

paras.en: - Litigation. We may face lawsuits from stockholders alleging misrepresentation, from customers claiming breach of contractual or implied commitments, or from other parties alleging harm resulting from the gap between our stated values and actual practices, leading to legal costs, settlements, judgments, injunctions, or other liabilities and remedies.
paras.zh: - 诉讼。我们可能面临股东提起的虚假陈述诉讼、客户提起的违反合同或默示承诺的索赔，或其他方提起的因我们宣称的价值观与实际做法之间存在差距而造成损害的索赔，从而导致法律费用、和解、判决、禁令或其他责任和救济。

paras.en: Any safety-related controversy or incident, whether actual or perceived, and regardless of fault or frequency, could prove significantly damaging to our business. In addition, we have engaged with governments in Canada, the EU, the UK, the United States, and other jurisdictions in connection with Project Glasswing and related frontier-capability programs, and we have positioned such programs, in part, to help provide the foundation for broader industry coordination on the responsible release of frontier models with cybersecurity and other advanced capabilities. The commercial viability of these and similar future programs may depend on sustained governmental and industry coalition support. If such coalitions fail to materialize, are perceived as exclusionary or anticompetitive, are rolled back, or result in mandates we cannot readily satisfy (including with respect to access, localization, monitoring, or reporting), our ability to commercialize models with Mythos-class capabilities, and the reputational benefits we derive from safety-focused positioning, could be materially impaired. For more information, see the section titled “—If we are unable to maintain and enhance our brand and reputation, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.”
paras.zh: 任何与安全相关的争议或事件，无论实际发生还是被感知，也无论过错方或发生频率如何，都可能对我们的业务造成重大损害。此外，我们已就 Project Glasswing 及相关前沿能力项目与加拿大、欧盟、英国、美国及其他司法管辖区的政府进行接触，并且我们已将此类项目部分定位为有助于为更广泛的行业协调奠定基础，以负责任地发布具备网络安全及其他先进能力的前沿模型。这些项目及类似未来项目的商业可行性可能取决于政府和行业联盟的持续支持。如果此类联盟未能形成、被认为具有排他性或反竞争性、被撤销，或导致我们无法轻易满足的强制要求（包括在访问、本地化、监控或报告方面），我们将 Mythos 级能力模型商业化的能力，以及我们从以安全为重点的定位中获得的声誉利益，可能会受到重大损害。更多信息，请参阅标题为“——如果我们无法维护和提升我们的品牌和声誉，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。”的章节。

paras.en: We voluntarily publicly disclose information regarding AI safety challenges, research findings, and limitations of our models and systems, that exceeds standard industry practice and regulatory requirements. While our intent with these voluntary disclosures is to advance the safe development of AI and build public trust, these disclosures create several risks. The AI safety landscape is nascent and evolving rapidly, and our understanding of and perspective on appropriate safety practices, risk tradeoffs, and deployment contexts may change over time as technologies, use cases, and regulatory expectations develop. As a result, statements we make today may later prove incomplete, require modification, or be interpreted differently in light of subsequent developments. To the extent we adhere to prior public statements or frameworks, we may also limit our operational flexibility, product development, or deployment decisions, even where evolving circumstances would otherwise warrant a different approach. Our public statements about AI risks, safety challenges, areas of uncertainty, or potential societal impacts, including statements regarding job displacement or economic disruption, may be used against us in litigation, regulatory proceedings, or public controversies, particularly if our future actions or statements are viewed as inconsistent with our prior statements and commitments. Regulators have and could continue to use our disclosures as the basis for heightened scrutiny or more stringent requirements applicable to us compared to less transparent competitors. Additionally, our disclosures have provided, and may in the future provide, competitors with insights into our proprietary training and other sensitive processes, research priorities, and strategic concerns, without reciprocal transparency, which may be potentially competitively disadvantageous to us. If we are unable to effectively manage the foregoing risks, our brand, reputation, and ability to compete could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们自愿公开披露有关 AI 安全挑战、研究发现以及我们模型和系统局限性的信息，其披露程度超出标准行业惯例和监管要求。尽管我们进行这些自愿披露的意图是推动 AI 的安全发展并建立公众信任，但这些披露会带来若干风险。AI 安全领域尚处早期且快速演变，随着技术、用例和监管预期的发展，我们对适当安全实践、风险权衡和部署场景的理解与观点可能随时间而变化。因此，我们今天所作的陈述日后可能被证明不完整、需要修改，或根据后续发展被作出不同解读。若我们遵循先前的公开陈述或框架，还可能限制我们的运营灵活性、产品开发或部署决策，即使不断变化的情况本应要求采取不同做法。我们关于 AI 风险、安全挑战、不确定性领域或潜在社会影响的公开陈述（包括关于岗位替代或经济扰动的陈述），可能在诉讼、监管程序或公众争议中被用来针对我们，尤其是当我们的未来行动或陈述被视为与我们先前的陈述和承诺不一致时。监管机构已经并可能继续利用我们的披露作为依据，对我们施加比透明度较低的竞争对手更严格的审查或更严苛的要求。此外，我们的披露已经并可能在未来为竞争对手提供有关我们专有训练及其他敏感流程、研究重点和战略关切的洞见，而对方并无对等透明，这可能对我们构成潜在的竞争劣势。如果我们无法有效管理上述风险，我们的品牌、声誉和竞争能力可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: Resource Allocation and Scaling. Safety-focused development is resource-intensive. We must allocate limited resources, capital, and talent between safety-focused workloads and other initiatives, often without clear returns on our safety-focused investments. For example, our investments in interpretability research and techniques designed to ensure our models’ behavior remains consistent with intended goals, values, and safety objectives may not yield actual or perceived commercial returns. Additionally, as we develop our models, platform, and applications, safety testing may become more expensive and resource intensive. Limited-access programs such as Project Glasswing may also require us to design, operate, and continually maintain bespoke vetting, contracting, monitoring, and offboarding processes that differ materially from our standard commercial release processes, including coordination among participating organizations, transition planning to successor models, and enhanced internal controls commensurate with the heightened sensitivity of the underlying capabilities. These activities impose ongoing operational, legal, and security costs that may recur as future frontier models with similar capability profiles are released. If we fail to successfully manage resource allocation or develop more efficient methods with respect to our safety initiatives, our safety outcomes, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 资源配置与规模化。以安全为核心的开发属于资源密集型工作。我们必须在以安全为核心的工作负载与其他举措之间分配有限的资源、资金和人才，而我们在以安全为核心的投资上往往没有明确的回报。例如，我们在可解释性研究以及旨在确保模型行为始终符合预期目标、价值观和安全目标的技术上的投资，可能不会产生实际或可感知的商业回报。此外，随着我们开发模型、平台和应用，安全测试可能变得更加昂贵且资源密集。诸如 Project Glasswing 之类的受限访问项目还可能要求我们设计、运营并持续维护定制的审查、签约、监控和退出流程，这些流程与我们的标准商业发布流程存在重大差异，包括参与组织之间的协调、向后续模型的过渡规划，以及与底层能力更高的敏感性相称的强化内部控制。这些活动会带来持续的运营、法律和安全成本，且随着未来具备类似能力特征的前沿模型发布，这些成本可能反复出现。如果我们未能成功管理资源配置，或未能就我们的安全举措开发更高效的方法，我们的安全成果、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: As our product portfolio and employee and customer base expand globally, applying safety principles consistently across our rapidly expanding organization, models, platform, applications, use cases, and jurisdictions and regulatory regimes has become increasingly challenging. For more information, see the section titled “—To continue to grow our business, we will need to continue to expand internationally, and our non-U.S. operations and sales to customers outside of the United States expose us to risks inherent in international expansion, sales, and operations.”
paras.zh: 随着我们的产品组合以及员工和客户群体在全球范围内扩张，在我们快速扩张的组织、模型、平台、应用、用例以及各司法管辖区和监管制度中一致地应用安全原则已变得日益具有挑战性。更多信息请参见标题为“——为持续增长我们的业务，我们将需要继续在国际上扩张，而我们的非美国业务以及向美国境外客户进行的销售使我们面临国际扩张、销售和运营所固有的风险”的章节。

paras.en: If we are unable to successfully manage the foregoing risks related to our focus and commitment to AI safety, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法成功管理与我们对 AI 安全的专注和承诺相关的上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If we are unable to maintain and enhance our brand and reputation, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们无法维护和提升我们的品牌和声誉，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。**

paras.en: We believe that maintaining and enhancing our brand identity and reputation is critical to our relationships with, and to our ability to attract and retain, customers, partners, and employees. Our brand and reputation are influenced not only by our actions, but also by the actions of our partners, our customers, and other third parties with whom we do business, and by broader public perceptions of the AI industry, and we may be grouped with other industry participants and judged similarly, regardless of differences in our approach or conduct. The successful promotion of our brand depends on a number of factors, including our ability to continue to develop and deliver reliable, high-quality, and responsible models, platforms, and applications that meet the needs of our customers; our sales and marketing efforts, including our effectiveness at developing a strong brand name and positive presence within the AI industry through participation in industry events and key media coverage; the perceptions and experiences of both our enterprise and individual customers, including through testimonials, use cases, and word-of-mouth; our ability to maintain security and reliability of our models, platform, and applications; the actions of our management; and our ability to differentiate our models, platform, and applications from those of our competitors, including through product design choices, safeguards, business models, and policies, including our approach to monetization strategies that differ from those of certain competitors. In addition, our brand is subject to heightened scrutiny with respect to perceived societal, environmental, labor, health, and safety-related impacts of AI technologies, and a single perceived failure could result in outsized reputational harm. For example, as AI systems become more capable or prevalent, public perception that our models, platform, and applications contribute to job displacement or economic disruption could generate significant negative media coverage, customer or employee backlash, or organized opposition, regardless of the actual impact of our models, platform, and applications on employment. Our ability to maintain and enhance our brand and reputation also depends on the effectiveness and scalability of our internal communications and reputation-management capabilities, including our ability to support global operations, and limitations in these areas could adversely affect our brand as we grow. Our crisis response and reputation-management capabilities may be limited or underdeveloped, particularly as we scale, which could impair our ability to respond effectively to adverse events and mitigate reputational harm.
paras.zh: 我们认为，维护和提升我们的品牌形象与声誉，对于我们与客户、合作伙伴及员工的关系，以及我们吸引和留住他们的能力至关重要。我们的品牌和声誉不仅受到我们自身行为的影响，也受到我们的合作伙伴、客户以及与我们开展业务的其他第三方行为的影响，还受到公众对 AI 行业更广泛认知的影响；我们可能被与其他行业参与者归为一类并受到类似评判，无论我们的方法或行为存在何种差异。品牌的成功推广取决于多项因素，包括我们持续开发和交付可靠、高质量且负责任的模型、平台和应用以满足客户需求的能力；我们的销售和营销工作，包括我们通过参与行业活动和获得关键媒体报道，在 AI 行业内打造强势品牌和积极形象的有效性；我们的企业客户和个人客户的认知与体验，包括通过客户证言、用例和口碑；我们维持模型、平台和应用的安全性和可靠性的能力；我们管理层的行为；以及我们将我们的模型、平台和应用与竞争对手区分开来的能力，包括通过产品设计选择、防护措施、商业模式和政策，包括我们与某些竞争对手不同的变现策略。此外，我们的品牌在 AI 技术被感知到的社会、环境、劳工、健康和安全相关影响方面受到更严格的审视，一次被感知到的失误就可能造成过大的声誉损害。例如，随着 AI 系统能力增强或日益普及，公众若认为我们的模型、平台和应用助长了岗位流失或经济扰动，就可能产生大量负面媒体报道、客户或员工反弹，或有组织的反对，无论我们的模型、平台和应用对就业的实际影响如何。我们维护和提升品牌与声誉的能力还取决于我们内部沟通和声誉管理能力的有效性和可扩展性，包括我们支持全球运营的能力，而这些方面的局限可能随着我们的成长对我们的品牌产生不利影响。我们的危机应对和声誉管理能力可能有限或发展不足，尤其是在我们规模扩张时，这可能削弱我们有效应对不利事件和减轻声誉损害的能力。

paras.en: The promotion of our brand requires us to make substantial expenditures, which we anticipate will increase as our market becomes more competitive. We have in the past, and may in the future, face challenges in building broader brand awareness and may fall behind competitors with more established or widely recognized brands. Our brand promotion activities may not be successful or generate the awareness or increased revenue we expect, and even if they do, any increase in revenue may not offset the significant expenses we incur in the efforts to build our brand.
paras.zh: 提升我们的品牌需要我们进行大量支出，我们预计随着市场竞争加剧，这些支出将会增加。我们过去曾面临、未来也可能面临建立更广泛品牌认知度的挑战，并可能落后于拥有更成熟或更广泛认可品牌的竞争对手。我们的品牌推广活动可能不会成功，也可能无法产生我们预期的认知度或收入增长；即使产生了，任何收入增长也可能无法抵消我们为打造品牌所 incurred 的巨额费用。

paras.en: If we do not successfully maintain and enhance our brand, our business may not grow, we may have reduced pricing power relative to competitors, we could lose customers or fail to attract potential customers or we could fail to hire and retain employees, all of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 如果我们未能成功维护和提升我们的品牌，我们的业务可能无法增长，我们相对于竞争对手的定价能力可能下降，我们可能失去客户或无法吸引潜在客户，或者我们可能无法招聘和留住员工，所有这些都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **We derive substantially all of our revenue from a limited number of products and applications, and our failure to maintain and expand our product portfolio could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们几乎全部收入来自有限数量的产品和应用，若我们未能维护和扩展我们的产品组合，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We currently derive substantially all of our revenue from a limited number of products and applications, primarily our Claude models and portfolio of applications that sit on top of the Claude Platform. This dependence on a narrower set of offerings subjects us to various risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations [__] .
paras.zh: 我们目前几乎全部收入来自有限数量的产品和应用，主要是我们的 Claude 模型以及基于 Claude 平台构建的应用组合。这种对较窄产品系列的依赖使我们面临各种风险，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响 [__] 。

paras.en: Our concentration in a limited number of products and applications, as well as our focused development strategy within specific areas of the broader AI landscape, reduces our ability to mitigate business risks through diversification. While this focused approach may enable us to allocate resources efficiently and compete effectively in our prioritized areas, it also creates the risk that significant market opportunities or the largest addressable markets may emerge in areas outside our current strategic focus. Many of our competitors offer diverse product portfolios across multiple business lines or pursue broader development across AI modalities, enabling them to offset weaknesses in a particular area. In contrast, any decline in demand for our core offerings, whether due to competition, technological changes, pricing pressure, changes in customer demand, or other factors, would have a direct and disproportionate impact on our revenue and ability to achieve and sustain profitability. Our concentration also reflects a strategy that prioritizes model capability as a principal source of differentiation and relies substantially on organic adoption rather than a large direct sales organization. The risks of that strategy, including the risks that differentiation among advanced models narrows, that customers select providers based on factors other than capability, or that competitors capture the individual users from whom our enterprise adoption often originates, are described in the sections titled “—We face intense competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected” and “—We have a limited history under our current go-to-market strategy, and our efforts to scale and evolve our customer acquisition, engagement, and retention model may not be successful.”
paras.zh: 我们集中于有限数量的产品和应用，以及在更广泛 AI 领域中特定细分方向的聚焦式开发战略，削弱了我们通过多元化来缓解业务风险的能力。尽管这种聚焦方式可能使我们能够高效配置资源，并在优先领域有效竞争，但它也带来了风险，即重大市场机遇或最大的可服务市场可能出现在我们当前战略重点之外的领域。我们的许多竞争对手在多个业务线上提供多样化的产品组合，或在多种 AI 模态上开展更广泛的开发，使其能够抵消某一特定领域的劣势。相比之下，对我们核心产品的需求若出现任何下滑，无论是由于竞争、技术变化、定价压力、客户需求变化还是其他因素，都将对我们的收入和实现并维持盈利能力的能力产生直接且不成比例的影响。我们的集中度还反映了一种战略，即将模型能力作为主要差异化来源予以优先考虑，并在很大程度上依赖自然采用，而非庞大的直销组织。该战略的风险，包括先进模型之间的差异化收窄、客户基于能力以外的因素选择供应商，或竞争对手抢占个人用户（我们的企业采用往往源自这些个人用户）等风险，已在“——我们面临激烈竞争，如果我们无法有效竞争，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响”和“——我们在当前市场进入战略下的运营历史有限，我们扩大和演进客户获取、参与和留存模式的努力可能不会成功”两节中描述。

paras.en: The AI industry is rapidly evolving, and it is difficult to predict which modalities or applications will capture the most durable commercial value or how the competitive landscape will shift. If the market for AI models, platforms, and applications develops in ways that do not align with our chosen areas of focus, or if competitors are better positioned to address the areas where the market opportunity ultimately proves largest, our ability to sustain revenue growth and compete effectively could be adversely affected. If we experience a decline in demand for our core offerings, we may not be able to successfully expand our product and application portfolio, and even if we do, our new products and applications may not achieve market acceptance or generate sufficient revenue to offset any decline in our existing business. Further, technical issues, security incidents, regulatory restrictions, or reputational harm affecting our models, platform, and applications could have an immediate and disproportionate impact on our business due to our product concentration where alternative revenue streams may not be available to offset such impact.
paras.zh: AI 行业正在快速演变，难以预测哪些模态或应用将获得最持久的商业价值，或竞争格局将如何变化。如果 AI 模型、平台和应用市场的发展方式与我们所选择的重点领域不一致，或者如果竞争对手在最终证明市场机遇最大的领域处于更有利的位置，我们维持收入增长和有效竞争的能力可能受到不利影响。如果我们核心产品的需求出现下滑，我们可能无法成功扩展我们的产品和应用组合，而且即使我们做到了，我们的新产品和应用也可能无法获得市场认可或产生足够收入以抵消现有业务的任何下滑。此外，影响我们模型、平台和应用的技术问题、安全事件、监管限制或声誉损害，可能由于我们的产品集中度而对我们的业务产生直接且不成比例的影响，而在此情况下可能没有替代收入来源来抵消此类影响。

paras.en: The market for AI models, platforms, and applications is evolving quickly, and customer requirements and expectations are changing rapidly. Customers may increasingly demand specialized solutions or specialized integration and tooling that we do not currently offer and may not plan to offer, or may seek AI solutions embedded more deeply into enterprise workflows. Enterprises may prefer to develop their own AI capabilities internally or choose competitors that offer more comprehensive product suites. Moreover, because substantially all of our models and applications are built on top of our frontier models, any defect, vulnerability, safety issue, or performance degradation in an underlying frontier model could simultaneously affect multiple products and applications and customer deployments, amplifying the impact of any such issue across our business. If we fail to anticipate or respond effectively to these evolving customer needs, we may lose customers to competitors or fail to acquire new customers.
paras.zh: AI 模型、平台和应用市场正在快速演变，客户的需求和期望也在迅速变化。客户可能日益要求我们目前未提供、也可能不计划提供的专业化解决方案或专业化集成与工具，或可能寻求更深度嵌入企业工作流的 AI 解决方案。企业可能更倾向于在内部自行开发 AI 能力，或选择能够提供更全面产品套件的竞争对手。此外，由于我们的几乎所有模型和应用均构建于我们的前沿 AI 模型之上，底层前沿 AI 模型中的任何缺陷、漏洞、安全问题或性能下降，都可能同时影响多个产品、应用及客户部署，从而放大任何此类问题对我们整体业务的影响。如果我们未能有效预判或应对这些不断变化的客户需求，我们可能将客户流失给竞争对手，或无法获取新客户。

paras.en: In addition, we currently compete, and may increasingly compete, with some of our own customers. As we expand our product portfolio or introduce new capabilities, our offerings may overlap with or directly compete with the models, platforms, and applications that our customers provide. This risk is particularly acute with software-as-a-service and other software companies, whose offerings may incorporate AI functionality similar to, or dependent on, the capabilities we provide. These customers may view our product expansion as a competitive threat to their business models and may reduce their purchases from us, limit their adoption of new offerings, terminate their relationships with us, seek alternative providers, restrict our access to the compute we obtain from them, initiate intellectual property or other litigation against us, or accelerate efforts to develop competing solutions internally in order to avoid relying on a direct competitor. This dynamic could result in customer attrition, reduced expansion within our existing customer base, pricing pressure, or reputational challenges, any of which could adversely affect our revenue growth and business prospects.
paras.zh: 此外，我们目前与部分自身客户存在竞争，且这种竞争可能日益加剧。随着我们扩展产品组合或推出新能力，我们的产品可能与客户提供的模型、平台和应用发生重叠或直接竞争。这一风险在软件即服务及其他软件公司中尤为突出，其产品可能包含与我们提供的能力相似或依赖于该等能力的 AI 功能。这些客户可能将我们的产品扩张视为对其商业模式的竞争威胁，并可能减少向我们采购、限制采用我们的新产品、终止与我们的关系、寻求替代供应商、限制我们获取从其处获得的算力、对我们提起知识产权或其他诉讼，或加速在内部开发竞争性解决方案以避免依赖直接竞争对手。这一态势可能导致客户流失、现有客户群内扩张减少、定价压力或声誉挑战，其中任何一项均可能对我们的收入增长和业务前景产生不利影响。

paras.en: Expanding our product portfolio requires substantial time and investment. We must make significant investments in research and development, compute infrastructure, engineering talent, sales and marketing, and go-to-market capabilities to develop new models, platforms, and applications and enable continued adoption. We may seek to expand into new products and markets, including areas outside of our current core competencies or where we have limited experience, and we may not successfully develop, commercialize, or support such offerings. Development timelines for AI models, platforms, and applications are uncertain, and new capabilities, even when continuously improved and released into our models, platform, and applications, may take significant time to achieve commercial scale. We may invest significant resources in products or services that fail to gain market traction, experience technical difficulties, face unexpected competition, lead to unexpected harm or societal impacts that do not align with our values, or generate insufficient returns to justify the investment. Additionally, we face other constraints on our ability to expand our offerings, including the ability to hire, retain, and motivate qualified AI researchers, engineers, and technical personnel; the capital intensity of developing and operating AI models, platforms, and applications which require substantial compute and infrastructure investment; and our limited portfolio may make it difficult to provide the comprehensive, integrated solutions that customers may expect.
paras.zh: 扩大我们的产品组合需要大量时间和投资。我们必须投入大量资源用于研发、算力基础设施、工程人才、销售与营销以及市场推广能力，以开发新的模型、平台和应用并推动其持续被采用。我们可能寻求拓展至新产品和新市场，包括我们当前核心能力之外的领域或我们经验有限的领域，而我们可能无法成功开发、商业化或支持此类产品。AI 模型、平台和应用的开发时间表具有不确定性，而新能力即使持续改进并发布到我们的模型、平台和应用中，也可能需要较长时间才能实现商业规模。我们可能在无法获得市场认可、遭遇技术困难、面临意外竞争、导致与我们的价值观不符的意外伤害或社会影响，或产生的回报不足以证明投资合理的产品或服务上投入大量资源。此外，我们扩大产品供给的能力还面临其他制约，包括能否招聘、留住并激励合格的 AI 研究人员、工程师和技术人员；开发和运营 AI 模型、平台和应用所需的资本密集度，这需要大量算力和基础设施投资；以及我们有限的产品组合可能难以提供客户所期望的全面、集成化解决方案。

paras.en: If we are unable to successfully expand our product and service portfolio, if we fail to compete effectively with our current offerings, or if customer preferences shift away from our models, platform, and applications, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法成功扩大我们的产品和服务组合，如果我们未能与现有产品有效竞争，或者如果客户偏好偏离我们的模型、平台和应用，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **A substantial portion of our revenue and accounts receivable is driven by a limited number of customers and distribution channels, and the loss of, or a significant reduction in, spend from one or more of our top customers or disruption through those channels could adversely affect our prospects, business, and financial condition.**
paras.zh: **我们收入的很大一部分以及应收账款由数量有限的客户和分销渠道驱动，失去一个或多个主要客户或其主要客户支出大幅减少，或这些渠道出现中断，都可能对我们的前景、业务和财务状况造成不利影响。**

paras.en: A substantial portion of our revenue is driven by a limited number of customers. While no single customer represented more than 10% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, our top five customers represented approximately 25% of our revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Many of our top customers are not subject to long-term contracts with us or have contracts with near-term expiration dates and are able to reduce or in some cases cease spending at any time and for any reason. Further, we have agreements with certain large customers which provide flexibility around financial commitments, termination rights, indemnification, and security obligations. Our top customers may vary spend levels period to period, and there can be no assurances that our large customers will continue to spend at levels similar to prior periods.
paras.zh: 我们收入的很大一部分由数量有限的客户驱动。尽管在截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日的九个月内，没有任何单一客户占我们收入的 10% 以上，但我们的前五大客户在截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日的九个月内约占我们收入的 25%。我们的许多主要客户与我们之间没有长期合同，或合同临近到期，并且能够随时以任何理由减少甚至在某些情况下停止支出。此外，我们与某些大客户签订的协议在财务承诺、终止权、赔偿和安全义务方面提供了灵活性。我们的主要客户在各期间的支出水平可能有所不同，且无法保证我们的大客户将继续保持与以往期间相似的支出水平。

paras.en: We anticipate that we will continue to derive a significant portion of our revenue from a limited number of customers for the foreseeable future, and in some cases, the portion of our revenue attributable to certain customers may increase in the future. The composition of our customer base, including our top customers, may fluctuate from period to period given that our customer composition has evolved and is expected to continue to evolve significantly as our business continues to evolve and scale and as the use cases for AI continue to develop.
paras.zh: 我们预计，在可预见的未来，我们仍将从数量有限的客户中获得相当大一部分收入，并且在某些情况下，归属于特定客户的收入占比未来可能上升。鉴于我们的客户构成已经发生变化，并且随着我们业务的持续演进和规模化以及 AI 用例的持续发展，预计客户构成将继续发生重大变化，我们的客户基础（包括主要客户）的构成可能在各期间出现波动。

paras.en: In addition, a significant portion of our revenue and accounts receivable is associated with transactions conducted with a limited number of CSPs that act as distribution and billing channels for our models. During the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025 and the six months ended June 30, 2026, revenue generated from sales to customers through CSP marketplaces represented approximately [__] 11%, 32%, 47%, and 48%, respectively, of total revenue. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and June 30, 2026, net accounts receivable from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented [__] 42%, 60%, and [__] 58%, respectively, of our net accounts receivable. These platforms bill end customers, collect payments on our behalf, and remit such amounts to us, net of applicable platform and other fees. Any change to, or termination of, one of our significant distribution relationships could adversely affect our business by disrupting customer access to our models, reducing usage, or increasing customer acquisition, onboarding, and migration costs. In these third-party arrangements, we generally maintain separate contractual arrangements with end customers governing access to, and pricing for, our models, independent of the applicable platform, and changes in, or termination of, a particular distribution relationship would not independently eliminate those contractual relationships. However, customers may be unwilling or unable to transition to alternative access points on commercially acceptable terms or timelines, or at all, following a disruption, which could result in revenue loss, increased costs, or adverse impacts to our growth, margins, and results of operations. In addition, any delay, dispute, or operational issue affecting a platform’s collection or remittance of customer payments could adversely affect our cash flows and working capital.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的收入和应收账款中有相当大一部分与通过数量有限的云服务商（CSP）进行的交易相关，这些云服务商作为我们模型的销售和计费渠道。在截至 2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度以及截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日的六个月期间，通过 CSP 市场向客户销售所产生的收入分别约占总收入的 [__] 11%、32%、47% 和 48%。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2025 年 12 月 31 日以及 2026 年 6 月 30 日，通过 CSP 市场向客户销售产生的应收账款净额分别占我们应收账款净额的 [__] 42%、60% 和 [__] 58%。这些平台向最终客户开具账单、代我们收取款项，并在扣除适用的平台费用及其他费用后将该等款项汇付给我们。我们任何一项重要分销关系的变更或终止，都可能扰乱客户对我们模型的访问、降低使用量或增加客户获取、入驻和迁移成本，从而对我们的业务造成不利影响。在此类第三方安排中，我们通常与最终客户另行签订合同安排，就我们模型的访问和定价作出约定，该等安排独立于相关平台，某一分销关系的变更或终止本身并不会消除该等合同关系。然而，在发生中断后，客户可能不愿或无法按商业上可接受的条款或时间表（或根本无法）转向其他访问渠道，这可能导致收入损失、成本增加，或对我们的增长、利润率和经营业绩造成不利影响。此外，任何影响平台收取或汇付客户款项的延迟、争议或运营问题，都可能对我们的现金流和营运资金造成不利影响。

paras.en: We may not be able to maintain or increase revenue from our top customers for a variety of reasons, including but not limited to the following:
paras.zh: 由于多种原因，我们可能无法维持或增加来自主要客户的收入，包括但不限于以下各项：

paras.en: - customers may develop their own solutions that compete with our models, platform, and applications;
paras.zh: - 客户可能开发出与我们模型、平台和应用相竞争的自有解决方案；

paras.en: - some of our customers may redesign their systems to require fewer of our services with limited notice to us and may choose not to renew or increase their purchases of our models, platform, and applications;
paras.zh: - 我们的一些客户可能在仅向我们发出有限通知的情况下重新设计其系统，以减少对我们服务的使用，并可能选择不再续购或增加对我们模型、平台和应用的采购；

paras.en: - changes to our models, platform, and applications may not align with the needs or expectations of our customers and such changes may reduce customer trust in us;
paras.zh: - 我们模型、平台和应用的变更可能不符合客户的需求或预期，此类变更可能降低客户对我们的信任；

paras.en: - our customers may have pre-existing or concurrent relationships with, or may be, current or potential competitors that may affect such customers’ decisions to purchase our models, platform, and applications;
paras.zh: - 我们的客户可能与我们当前或潜在的竞争对手存在既有或并行的关系，或者其本身即为我们的当前或潜在竞争对手，这可能影响此类客户购买我们的模型、平台和应用的决策；

paras.en: - our customers and partners that heavily rely on our offerings may want to reduce such levels of reliance, seek out competing offerings, or transition to other providers altogether; and
paras.zh: - 高度依赖我们产品与服务的客户和合作伙伴可能希望降低此类依赖程度、寻求竞争性产品，或完全转向其他供应商；以及

paras.en: - our customers, particularly early-stage and high-growth companies, may depend on venture capital or other external financing to fund their operations, and may reduce or cease spending with us if such funding is delayed, reduced, or unavailable or if their access to capital becomes more costly.
paras.zh: - 我们的客户，尤其是早期阶段和高增长公司，可能依赖风险投资或其他外部融资来为其运营提供资金，如果此类融资被延迟、减少或无法获得，或其获取资本的成本变得更高，他们可能会减少或停止向我们支出。

paras.en: Any adverse change in demand from our largest customers, in their ability or willingness to perform under their contracts with us, in applicable laws or regulations, or in our broader strategic relationships with such customers could adversely affect our business and prospects. As a result, a significant reduction in spending by, or the loss of, one or more of our largest customers, if not offset by new customer relationships or increased business from our other existing customers, could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. For additional risks related to our reliance on enterprise customers and government customers, including longer sales cycles, complex procurement processes, heightened contractual, compliance, and security requirements, and budgetary and policy constraints, see the sections titled “—Sales to enterprise customers involve complexities and risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations” and “—Our sales to government entities and highly regulated organizations are subject to challenges and risks.”
paras.zh: 我们最大客户的需求、其履行与我们签订的合同的能力或意愿、适用的法律或法规，或我们与此类客户更广泛的战略关系若发生任何不利变化，均可能对我们的业务和前景产生不利影响。因此，若一个或多个最大客户的支出大幅减少或流失，且未能通过新客户关系或其他现有客户的业务增长予以抵消，则可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。有关我们依赖企业客户和政府客户的额外风险，包括更长的销售周期、复杂的采购流程、更高的合同、合规和安全要求，以及预算和政策限制，请参见标题为“——向企业客户销售涉及复杂性和风险，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响”和“——我们向政府实体和高度受监管组织销售面临挑战和风险”的章节。

paras.en: **We have incurred significant indebtedness in order to operate and grow our business, including to fund our substantial compute commitments, and our ability to service this indebtedness may be constrained by our cash flows and liquidity.**
paras.zh: **我们已产生大量债务以运营和发展我们的业务，包括为我们的巨额算力承诺提供资金，而我们偿还该等债务的能力可能受到我们的现金流和流动性的制约。**

paras.en: In order to operate and grow our business, including to fund our substantial compute commitments, we have incurred a substantial amount of debt, which requires significant interest and principal payments. As of June 30, 2026, our total indebtedness was $6.2 billion, reflecting the aggregate principal amount outstanding under the convertible promissory notes issued to Amazon (through Amazon Web Services, Inc.) pursuant to the Convertible Note Purchase Agreement, dated as of September 19, 2023, by and between us and Amazon (the “Amazon 2023 NPA”) and the New Convertible Note Purchase Agreement, dated as of November 22, 2024, by and between us and Amazon (the “Amazon 2024 NPA”) (all such notes issued thereunder, collectively, the “Amazon Notes”). We may also incur additional indebtedness to meet our future financing needs. We have guaranteed the obligations of certain of our subsidiaries that are party to AI infrastructure arrangements, as well as pursuant to agreements we entered into in connection with an equipment lease with a third-party partner, Broadcom Inc. (“Broadcom”) in March 2026 to procure specialized AI accelerators and associated components (under which Broadcom intends to assign to a designated financial partner) (the “2026 Lease Arrangement”). In addition, we have the ability to issue, if needed, up to $42.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of convertible promissory notes to Broadcom or, subject to our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld), a designated financial partner pursuant to a note purchase agreement that we entered into with Broadcom in March 2026 (the “Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA”) to finance obligations under the 2026 Lease Arrangement. We may be required to use a substantial portion of our cash flows from operations to pay interest, principal, or other required payments on our indebtedness.
paras.zh: 为运营和发展我们的业务，包括为我们的重大算力承诺提供资金，我们已承担了大量债务，这需要支付高额的利息和本金。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，我们的债务总额为 $6.2 billion，反映的是根据我们与 Amazon 于 2023 年 9 月 19 日签订的《可转换票据购买协议》（“Amazon 2023 NPA”）以及我们与 Amazon 于 2024 年 11 月 22 日签订的新《可转换票据购买协议》（“Amazon 2024 NPA”）向 Amazon（通过 Amazon Web Services, Inc.）发行的可转换本票项下未偿还本金总额（据此发行的所有该等票据，统称“Amazon Notes”）。我们还可能承担额外债务以满足未来的融资需求。我们已为若干子公司的义务提供担保，这些子公司是 AI 基础设施安排的当事方，同时我们也根据与第三方合作伙伴 Broadcom Inc.（“Broadcom”）于 2026 年 3 月就采购专用 AI 加速器及相关组件签订的设备租赁相关协议（根据该协议，Broadcom 拟将其转让给指定的财务合作伙伴）（“2026 Lease Arrangement”）提供担保。此外，如有需要，我们可根据与 Broadcom 于 2026 年 3 月签订的票据购买协议（“Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA”），向 Broadcom 或经我们同意（不得无理拒绝）的指定财务合作伙伴发行本金总额最高达 $42.0 billion 的可转换本票，以为 2026 Lease Arrangement 项下的义务提供资金。我们可能被要求将经营活动现金流量的很大一部分用于支付债务的利息、本金或其他应付款项。

paras.en: The delivery of shares of our Class N common stock upon conversion of our outstanding convertible promissory notes could result in dilution to our existing stockholders. Following this offering, assuming the conversion of our outstanding convertible promissory notes into an aggregate of [__] shares of our Class N common stock, based upon the aggregate principal and accrued and unpaid interest on such notes as of September 30, 2026, and an assumed initial public offering price of $ [__] per share (which is the midpoint of the estimated offering price range set forth on the cover page of this prospectus), holders of our outstanding convertible promissory notes would collectively hold in the aggregate approximately [__] % of our Class N common stock, which represents [__] % of our total outstanding common stock following this offering. Pursuant to the terms of the Amazon Notes, to the extent that the full amount of such notes cannot convert into shares of our Class N common stock in connection with this offering as a result of the ownership cap applicable to the Amazon Notes, which may be waived at Amazon’s election, the remaining balance of such notes will automatically convert, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap, into shares of our Class N common stock at the applicable conversion price at the end of each fiscal quarter following this offering or, if such remaining balance of such notes does not convert before the applicable maturity date because of the applicable ownership cap, such balance will be repaid in cash at such maturity date. For more information about our convertible promissory notes, see the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Convertible Notes.”
paras.zh: 在我们未偿还的可转换本票转换后交付我们的 N 类普通股股份，可能会导致对我们现有股东的稀释。本次发行后，假设我们未偿还的可转换本票转换为合计 [__] 股我们的 N 类普通股，基于截至 2026 年 9 月 30 日该等本票的合计本金及应计未付利息，以及假设的每股 $[__] 的首次公开发行价格（即本招股说明书封面所载估计发行价格区间的中点），我们未偿还的可转换本票持有人将合计持有我们 N 类普通股约 [__]%，占本次发行后我们全部已发行普通股的 [__]%。根据 Amazon 本票的条款，若因适用于 Amazon 本票的所有权上限（Amazon 可自行选择豁免）导致该等本票的全部金额无法在本次发行相关情况下转换为我们的 N 类普通股股份，则该等本票的剩余余额将在本次发行后每个财季末按适用转换价格自动转换为我们的 N 类普通股股份（受 Amazon 所有权上限约束），或者，若因适用的所有权上限导致该等本票的该等剩余余额在适用到期日之前未能转换，则该余额将在该到期日以现金偿还。有关我们可转换本票的更多信息，请参见标题为“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析——流动性与资本资源——可转换本票”的章节。

paras.en: Our ability to make scheduled payments in respect of, to pay interest on, or to refinance our indebtedness, including the A&R Credit Agreement and our outstanding convertible promissory notes, depends on our future performance, which is subject to economic, financial, competitive, and other factors beyond our control. Such payments will reduce the funds available to us for working capital, capital expenditures, and other corporate purposes and may limit our ability to obtain additional financing for working capital, capital expenditures, expansion plans, and other investments. Our business may not be able to generate cash flows from operations in the future that are sufficient to service our debt and make necessary capital expenditures. If we are unable to generate such cash flows, we may be required to adopt one or more alternatives, such as selling assets or obtaining additional debt financing or equity capital on terms that may be onerous or highly dilutive. Our ability to refinance our indebtedness will depend on the capital markets and our financial condition at such time. We may not be able to engage in any of these activities or engage in these activities on desirable terms, which could result in a default on our debt obligations and adversely affect our financial condition. Further, the terms of the A&R Credit Agreement and the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA include a number of covenants that limit our ability and our subsidiaries’ ability to, among other things, incur additional indebtedness, create liens, make asset sales or investments, engage in mergers or other fundamental changes, pay dividends or distributions, repurchase or redeem equity interests, and enter into transactions with affiliates. The terms of the A&R Credit Agreement may restrict our current and future operations and could adversely affect our ability to finance our future operations or capital needs. For more information, see the sections titled “—We may require additional capital to meet our substantial ongoing obligations and support our business growth, and our ability to generate sufficient revenue and secure additional capital on acceptable terms is critical to our continued operations and competitive position” and “—If the market for our models, platform, and applications develops more slowly than we expect or declines, our growth may slow or stall, and our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.”
paras.zh: 我们按期支付、支付利息或再融资我们的债务（包括 A&R 信贷协议和未偿还的可转换本票）的能力取决于我们的未来业绩，而未来业绩受经济、财务、竞争及其他我们无法控制的因素影响。此类付款将减少我们可用于营运资金、资本支出和其他公司用途的资金，并可能限制我们为营运资金、资本支出、扩张计划和其他投资获取额外融资的能力。我们的业务未来可能无法产生足以偿还债务和进行必要资本支出的经营现金流。如果我们无法产生此类现金流，我们可能被要求采取一项或多项替代方案，例如出售资产，或以可能繁重或高度稀释的条款获得额外债务融资或股权资本。我们为债务再融资的能力将取决于当时的资本市场和我们的财务状况。我们可能无法开展任何此类活动，或无法以理想条款开展此类活动，这可能导致我们违反债务义务并对其财务状况产生不利影响。此外，A&R 信贷协议和 Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA 的条款包含多项契约，限制我们及我们子公司（其中包括）产生额外债务、设立留置权、进行资产出售或投资、进行合并或其他根本性变更、支付股息或分配、回购或赎回股权权益，以及与关联方进行交易的能力。A&R 信贷协议的条款可能限制我们当前和未来的运营，并可能对我们为未来运营或资本需求融资的能力产生不利影响。有关更多信息，请参阅标题为“——我们可能需要额外资本来履行我们大量的持续义务并支持我们的业务增长，而我们产生足够收入并以可接受条款获得额外资本的能力对我们的持续运营和竞争地位至关重要”和“——如果我们模型、平台和应用程序的市场发展速度慢于我们的预期或出现下滑，我们的增长可能会放缓或停滞，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。”的章节。

paras.en: We are also subject to variable interest rate risk because the interest rate under the A&R Credit Agreement varies based on a margin over an indexed rate or an adjusted base rate. If interest rates associated with our floating rate debt increase, our debt service obligations in connection with the A&R Credit Agreement would increase even though the amount borrowed remained the same, and our available cash would correspondingly decrease. Our substantial amount of debt, combined with variable interest rates, could limit our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business and the markets in which we operate, including limiting our future investments or our ability to enter into acquisitions and strategic partnerships, and obtain financing for such transactions.
paras.zh: 我们还面临浮动利率风险，因为 A&R 信贷协议项下的利率根据指数利率加一定利差或调整后基准利率而浮动。若与我们浮动利率债务相关的利率上升，即使借款金额不变，我们在 A&R 信贷协议项下的偿债义务也会增加，我们的可用现金将相应减少。我们庞大的债务规模，加之浮动利率，可能限制我们规划或应对业务及所处市场变化的灵活性，包括限制我们未来的投资或进行收购和战略合作的能力，以及为此类交易获取融资的能力。

paras.en: In addition, our indebtedness, combined with our other financial obligations and contractual commitments, could have other important consequences. For example, they could:
paras.zh: 此外，我们的债务连同其他财务义务和合同承诺，可能带来其他重要后果。例如，它们可能：

paras.en: - make us more vulnerable to adverse changes in general U.S. and non-U.S. economic, industry, and competitive conditions and adverse changes in government regulation;
paras.zh: - 使我们更易受到美国及非美国总体经济、行业和竞争状况的不利变化以及政府监管不利变化的影响；

paras.en: - limit our flexibility in planning for, or reacting to, changes in our business and our industry;
paras.zh: - 限制我们规划或应对业务及行业变化的灵活性；

paras.en: - place us at a disadvantage compared to our competitors that have less or fixed rate indebtedness;
paras.zh: - 使我们相对于债务较少或债务为固定利率的竞争对手处于劣势；

paras.en: - limit our ability to borrow additional amounts to fund acquisitions, for working capital, and for other general corporate purposes; and
paras.zh: - 限制我们借入额外款项以资助收购、满足营运资金需求及其他一般公司用途的能力；以及

paras.en: - make an acquisition of our company less attractive or more difficult.
paras.zh: - 使对我们公司的收购变得不那么有吸引力或更加困难。

paras.en: Any of these factors could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. In addition, if we incur additional indebtedness, the risks related to our business and our ability to service or repay our indebtedness would increase.
paras.zh: 上述任何因素都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。此外，如果我们产生额外债务，与我们业务相关的风险以及我们偿付或偿还债务的能力方面的风险将会增加。

paras.en: A failure by us to comply with the covenants, including those tied, in part, to operational and performance-based metrics, or payment obligations under the A&R Credit Agreement or our outstanding convertible promissory notes, as applicable, whether as a result of financial constraints, operational challenges, inexperience managing complex infrastructure and large-scale capital commitments, or otherwise, could result in an event of default under these instruments. Upon an event of default under the A&R Credit Agreement, the lenders would have the right to accelerate all amounts outstanding and exercise other remedies available to them, including enforcing their rights against the collateral securing the A&R Credit Agreement. An event of default under our outstanding convertible promissory notes would similarly give the noteholders the right to declare all amounts outstanding under our outstanding convertible promissory notes immediately due and payable. If the indebtedness under the A&R Credit Agreement and/or outstanding convertible promissory notes were to be accelerated, we may not have sufficient cash or be able to borrow sufficient funds to refinance such indebtedness or sell sufficient assets to repay such indebtedness, which could adversely affect our business, cash flows, financial condition, and results of operations. Even if we were able to obtain new financing, it may not be on commercially reasonable terms or on terms that are acceptable to us.
paras.zh: 若我们未能遵守 A&R 信贷协议或我们未偿还可转换本票（视情况而定）项下的契约（包括部分与运营及业绩指标挂钩的契约）或付款义务，无论该等违约是因财务约束、运营挑战、缺乏管理复杂基础设施和大规模资本承诺的经验，还是其他原因所致，均可能导致上述工具项下发生违约事件。一旦 A&R 信贷协议项下发生违约事件，贷款人将有权加速全部未偿金额到期，并行使其他可用的救济措施，包括对为 A&R 信贷协议提供担保的抵押物强制执行其权利。我们未偿还可转换本票项下发生违约事件同样会赋予票据持有人权利，宣布我们未偿还可转换本票项下的全部未偿金额立即到期应付。若 A&R 信贷协议和/或未偿还可转换本票项下的债务被加速到期，我们可能没有足够的现金，或无法借入足够的资金为该等债务再融资，或无法出售足够的资产以偿还该等债务，这可能对我们的业务、现金流、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。即使我们能够获得新的融资，其条款也可能并非商业上合理的条款，或并非我们可接受的条款。

paras.en: **We may not have the ability to raise the funds necessary to repay the principal and accrued interest of our outstanding convertible promissory notes or the A&R Credit Agreement in cash when required by the terms of the notes or the A&R Credit Agreement, as applicable, or at their maturity.**
paras.zh: **当未偿还可转换本票或 A&R 信贷协议（视情况而定）的条款要求时，或在其到期时，我们可能无力筹集必要的资金以现金偿还我们未偿还可转换本票或 A&R 信贷协议的本金及应计利息。**

paras.en: In connection with the completion of this offering, the Amazon Notes will convert into Class N common stock, subject, in each case, to an ownership cap as set forth in the Amazon Notes, which may be waived at Amazon’s election. In the event that any of the notes comprising the Amazon Notes cannot be fully converted without exceeding the ownership cap applicable to such notes, the balance of any such notes will remain outstanding and will automatically convert, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap, into shares of our Class N common stock at the applicable conversion price at the end of each fiscal quarter following the completion of this offering. To the extent any of our convertible promissory notes remain outstanding, or if we issue any additional convertible promissory notes following the completion of this offering, we will be required to repay such note in cash at its maturity, unless earlier converted or repaid pursuant to the terms of such note. In addition, we will be required to repay in full all amounts outstanding under the A&R Credit Agreement upon its maturity. However, we may not have enough available cash on hand or be able to obtain financing at the time we are required to make any repayments on outstanding convertible promissory notes or under the A&R Credit Agreement.
paras.zh: 与本次发行完成相关，Amazon 票据将转换为 N 类普通股，但在每种情况下均受 Amazon 票据所载所有权上限的约束，该上限可由 Amazon 选择豁免。若构成 Amazon 票据的任何票据在不超过该等票据适用的所有权上限的情况下无法全部转换，则任何该等票据的余额将继续存续，并受 Amazon 所有权上限的约束，在本次发行完成后的每个财政季度末按适用的转换价格自动转换为我们 N 类普通股的股份。若我们的任何可转换本票仍未偿还，或若我们在本次发行完成后发行任何额外的可转换本票，我们将被要求在到期时以现金偿还该等票据，除非根据该等票据的条款提前转换或偿还。此外，我们将被要求在 A&R 信贷协议到期时全额偿还其项下所有未偿金额。然而，在我们被要求对未偿还可转换本票或 A&R 信贷协议项下款项进行任何偿还时，我们可能没有足够的可用库存现金，或无法获得融资。

paras.en: Our failure to repay any outstanding convertible promissory notes or amounts outstanding under the A&R Credit Agreement, as applicable, at a time when the repayment is required, or to pay cash upon any conversion of outstanding convertible promissory notes, as applicable, as required pursuant to the terms of each note or the applicable NPA, would constitute a default thereunder. A default under an outstanding convertible promissory note and/or the applicable NPA as well as the A&R Credit Agreement could also lead to a default under agreements governing our existing and future indebtedness. If the payment of the related indebtedness were to be accelerated after any applicable notice or grace periods, we may not have sufficient funds to repay such indebtedness and repay the amounts outstanding under the A&R Credit Agreement or outstanding convertible promissory notes at the applicable maturity, or when repayment is otherwise required pursuant to the terms of the note.
paras.zh: 若我们未能在需要偿还时偿还任何未偿还可转换本票或《修订及重述信贷协议》项下的未偿款项（如适用），或未能在任何未偿还可转换本票转换时按各票据条款或适用 NPA 的要求支付现金（如适用），即构成该等协议项下的违约。未偿还可转换本票和/或适用 NPA 以及《修订及重述信贷协议》项下的违约，亦可能导致我们违反管辖现有及未来债务的协议。若相关债务在适用通知期或宽限期届满后被加速到期，我们可能没有足够资金偿还该等债务，亦无法在适用到期日或票据条款另行要求偿还时偿还《修订及重述信贷协议》项下的未偿款项或未偿还可转换本票。

paras.en: **Our pricing structures for our models, platform, and applications change from time to time, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们模型、平台和应用的定价结构会不时变化，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We have in the past changed, and we expect that in the future we may change, our pricing models, including as a result of competition, macroeconomic conditions, compliance with increased regulatory hurdles, the maturation of the market for AI models, platforms, and applications, or changes in how our models, platform, and applications are broadly consumed. As a result, we may be required to reduce our prices, offer shorter contract durations or offer alternative pricing models, such as outcome or task-based pricing, any of which could adversely affect our business. In addition, our agentic offerings are structurally more compute-intensive than our non-agentic offerings. If we are unable to implement pricing models that adequately reflect the higher compute intensity of these agentic workloads, or if competitive dynamics constrain our ability to price these products at levels sufficient to cover their costs, our compute efficiency could deteriorate as agentic usage grows, which could adversely affect our ability to achieve or sustain profitability.
paras.zh: 我们过去曾调整定价模式，并预计未来可能继续调整，原因包括竞争、宏观经济状况、为遵守日益增多的监管障碍、AI 模型、平台和应用市场的成熟，或我们的模型、平台和应用的广泛消费方式发生变化。因此，我们可能被迫降价、提供更短的合同期限或提供替代定价模式（如按结果或按任务定价），其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务产生不利影响。此外，我们的智能体产品在结构上比非智能体产品更算力密集。若我们无法实施足以反映这些智能体工作负载更高算力强度的定价模式，或竞争态势限制我们将这些产品定价至足以覆盖其成本的水平，我们的算力效率可能随着智能体使用量增长而恶化，这可能对我们实现或维持盈利能力产生不利影响。

paras.en: Additionally, as we continue to target selling our models, platform, and applications to our enterprise customers, these customers may demand different pricing structures, price concessions, or additional functionality at the same price levels. If we are unable to modify or develop effective pricing models and strategies that are attractive to existing and prospective customers, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 此外，随着我们持续将模型、平台和应用销售给企业客户，这些客户可能要求不同的定价结构、价格优惠或在相同价格水平下提供额外功能。若我们无法修改或制定对现有及潜在客户具有吸引力的有效定价模式和策略，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If we are unable to attract, retain, or motivate highly skilled personnel, we may not be able to grow or operate effectively.**
paras.zh: **若我们无法吸引、留住或激励高技能人才，我们可能无法实现增长或有效运营。**

paras.en: Our performance and ability to grow our business depend on the talents and efforts of highly skilled individuals, and our future success depends on our continuing ability to identify, hire, develop, motivate, and retain highly skilled personnel for all areas of our organization. Our business is particularly dependent on a limited pool of researchers, engineers, and technical personnel with specialized experience in designing, training, deploying, and operating frontier models and the underlying infrastructure that supports them.
