paras.en: **Our reliance on a limited number of CSPs and suppliers, some of which have strategic and investment relationships with us and are our customers, creates complex dynamics that could give rise to conflicts of interest and adversely affect our access to compute.**
paras.zh: **我们对数量有限的云服务商（CSP）和供应商的依赖——其中部分与我们存在战略和投资关系并且是我们的客户——形成了复杂的动态关系，可能引发利益冲突，并对我们获取算力产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We rely on a limited number of CSPs—Amazon.com, Inc. (together with its affiliates, “Amazon”), Google, and Microsoft Corporation (“Microsoft”)—and suppliers, such as Broadcom, for compute and critical components of our compute infrastructure. These relationships are governed by contractual arrangements that, while providing us with significant committed compute, also create dependencies and potential vulnerabilities. These CSPs may experience service outages, security incidents, or capacity constraints that affect our operations. The terms of our arrangements, including pricing, compute commitments, and service levels, are subject to negotiation upon renewal, and we may be unable to secure renewals on terms as favorable as our current arrangements. Migrating workloads to alternative providers would be costly, time-consuming, and operationally complex, and may not be feasible within timeframes that would avoid material disruption to our model development roadmap or our ability to serve customers. The engineering investment required to maintain the performance of our unified compute platform across new hardware environments means that any such migration could degrade our compute efficiency, increasing the compute and infrastructure costs required to support a given level of business activity during and following any such migration period.
paras.zh: 我们依赖数量有限的云服务商（CSP）——Amazon.com, Inc.（连同其关联方，简称“Amazon”）、Google 和 Microsoft Corporation（简称“Microsoft”）——以及供应商（如 Broadcom）提供算力及我们算力基础设施的关键组件。这些关系受合同安排约束，此类安排虽为我们提供了大量承诺算力，但也形成了依赖关系和潜在脆弱性。这些 CSP 可能发生服务中断、安全事件或容量限制，从而影响我们的运营。我们各项安排的条款（包括定价、算力承诺和服务水平）在续约时须经谈判确定，我们可能无法以与现有安排同样有利的条款获得续约。将工作负载迁移至替代供应商将成本高昂、耗时且运营复杂，并且可能无法在可避免对我们的模型开发路线图或客户服务能力造成重大干扰的时间范围内实现。为在新的硬件环境中维持我们统一算力平台的性能所需的工程投入意味着，任何此类迁移都可能降低我们的算力效率，从而在任何此类迁移期间及之后，提高为支撑特定业务活动水平所需的算力和基础设施成本。

paras.en: Our relationships with these CSPs are multifaceted and complex. Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, through their respective affiliates, have made significant equity investments in our company. At the same time, they may have made, and may in the future make, equity investments in, provide financing to, or otherwise support companies whose models, platforms, or applications compete with ours. These CSPs are also our customers, purchasing our intelligence service for internal use or for their own products and services. Their purchasing decisions may be influenced by their own competing offerings, which could affect their demand for our intelligence service. Additionally, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are among the largest technology companies in the world, each with substantial AI research and development programs, AI-powered models, platforms, and applications that compete with ours, and strategic interests that may not be fully aligned with our own. Amazon, Google, and Microsoft each offer AI services and develop and deploy competing AI models through their respective cloud platforms. We make certain of our models available through these cloud platforms, and our distribution relationships with Amazon, Google, and Microsoft generate revenue for us, but they also create dependencies, give them visibility into our pricing and commercial terms across the platforms they operate, and may influence their incentives regarding pricing, compute allocation, service quality, sales prioritization, and compensation structures. To the extent these CSPs promote, integrate, prioritize, or provide customer access to our models, platform, and applications on terms that are less favorable than those applicable to their own competing offerings or to the offerings of other companies, including with respect to pricing, commercial terms, product placement, integration, or access to compute or sales incentives, our competitive position, customer adoption, and business results could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们与这些云服务商（CSP）的关系是多层面且复杂的。Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 通过各自的关联方对我们的公司进行了重大股权投资。与此同时，它们可能已经、并且未来可能对与我们模型、平台或应用存在竞争关系的公司进行股权投资、提供融资或以其他方式提供支持。这些云服务商（CSP）同时也是我们的客户，为其内部使用或自身产品和服务购买我们的智能服务。它们的采购决策可能受到其自身竞争性产品的影响，从而可能影响它们对我们智能服务的需求。此外，Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 是全球最大的科技公司之一，各自拥有庞大的 AI 研发计划、与我们的产品存在竞争关系的 AI 驱动模型、平台和应用，以及可能与我们并不完全一致的战略利益。Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 各自通过其云平台提供 AI 服务并开发和部署具有竞争关系的 AI 模型。我们通过上述云平台提供我们的部分模型，我们与 Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 的分销关系为我们带来收入，但同时也形成了依赖关系，使它们能够了解我们在其运营的各平台上的定价和商业条款，并可能影响它们在定价、算力分配、服务质量、销售优先级和薪酬结构方面的激励。若这些云服务商（CSP）推广、整合、优先安排或向客户提供我们的模型、平台和应用时所依据的条款，不如适用于其自身竞争性产品或其他公司产品的条款有利，包括在定价、商业条款、产品展示位置、整合或算力获取或销售激励方面，则我们的竞争地位、客户采用情况和业务成果可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: Our relationships with our strategic partners—whether with these CSPs, who simultaneously serve as our investors, customers, distribution partners, and competitors, or with Broadcom, which simultaneously serves as a supplier and lessor—create potential conflicts of interest that are difficult to fully anticipate or mitigate. These CSPs may prioritize their own compute needs or those of their other customers, including competitors in which they have invested, may gain insight into our operations and compute requirements through their roles as providers that could inform their competitive strategies, or may make business decisions regarding their platforms that disadvantage our models, platform, and applications relative to their own offerings or the offerings of other companies they support. Similarly, Broadcom may prioritize the supply of AI accelerators and infrastructure capacity to other customers, alter the terms of our equipment lease or the operation of our dedicated facilities, or make decisions regarding the availability or pricing of hardware that adversely affect our access to the compute infrastructure they provide. Any deterioration in these relationships, or any decision by Amazon, Google, Microsoft, or Broadcom to reduce their support for our models, platform, and applications or limit our access to compute, could adversely affect our business. In addition, such relationships, including any exclusive or preferential arrangements, investment ties, bundling of services, or cooperative initiatives, have attracted and may in the future attract antitrust or competition law scrutiny from regulators and private plaintiffs in the United States or other non-U.S. jurisdictions, and any resulting investigations, enforcement actions, or required modifications to our business arrangements could be costly, distracting, and harmful to our business.
paras.zh: 我们与战略合作伙伴的关系——无论是与这些同时担任我们投资者、客户、分销合作伙伴和竞争对手的 CSP 的关系，还是与同时担任供应商和出租方的 Broadcom 的关系——都会产生难以完全预见或缓解的潜在利益冲突。这些 CSP 可能会优先考虑自身的算力需求或其其他客户（包括其已投资的竞争对手）的需求，可能会通过其作为提供商的身份了解我们的运营和算力需求，从而为其竞争战略提供参考，或者可能会就其平台做出不利于我们的模型、平台和应用程序相对于其自身产品或其所支持的其他公司产品的商业决策。同样，Broadcom 可能会优先向其他客户供应 AI 加速器和基础设施容量，改变我们设备租赁的条款或我们专用设施的运营方式，或就硬件的可用性或定价做出不利于我们获取其提供的算力基础设施的决定。这些关系的任何恶化，或 Amazon、Google、Microsoft 或 Broadcom 做出的任何减少对我们模型、平台和应用程序的支持或限制我们获取算力的决定，都可能对我们的业务产生不利影响。此外，此类关系（包括任何排他性或优惠安排、投资关系、服务捆绑或合作举措）已经并可能在未来引起美国或其他非美国司法管辖区监管机构和私人原告的反垄断或竞争法审查，由此产生的任何调查、执法行动或对我们业务安排要求的修改都可能代价高昂、分散精力并对我们的业务造成损害。

paras.en: If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **We are pursuing initiatives to develop our own data center infrastructure, which involves significant capital commitments, operational complexities, and execution risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **我们正在推进开发自有数据中心基础设施的举措，这涉及重大资本承诺、运营复杂性和执行风险，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: To help reduce our dependence on CSPs, address constraints on available compute, and secure access to compute at the scale necessary for frontier model development, we are pursuing initiatives to develop our own dedicated on-premise data center infrastructure. These efforts include long-term leases and partnerships with third-party partners to procure the underlying real estate, power, and data center facilities while we lease capacity in those facilities and contract with specialized third-party operators for ongoing facility management. We also procure certain compute and infrastructure equipment directly and operate them in dedicated data center facilities leased and operated on our behalf, to our specification. For example, under the 2026 Lease Arrangement, the rent payments over the five-year equipment lease are equal to an aggregate of approximately $125.2 billion excluding interest, with rent payable in quarterly installments and payment obligations typically commencing upon AI infrastructure equipment becoming “ready for service” at the applicable data center facility. The 2026 Lease Arrangement is non-cancelable by the parties to such agreement during the applicable lease period except in the case of a default. In addition, we deposited cash into a restricted account in April 2026 for the benefit of Broadcom to secure compute capacity, which amount may be released or applied toward obligations under the lease depending on the satisfaction of specified conditions. Under certain circumstances, we may be required to place additional cash into this restricted account for future amounts due under the 2026 Lease Arrangement. Upon the occurrence of certain uncured events of default, such as certain payment or performance failures pursuant to the terms of the 2026 Lease Arrangement, a substantial portion of our obligations under the 2026 Lease Arrangement would be accelerated and, while we have access to multiple sources of capital and are not dependent on the potential financing capacity provided in the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA that we entered into in connection with the 2026 Lease Arrangement, we may not be permitted to elect to issue the convertible promissory notes under the Infrastructure Partner 2026 NPA to finance such obligations. Furthermore, we may in the future continue to directly procure such data center infrastructure and we may also undertake other efforts to build out our own compute and infrastructure and invest more deeply in the compute supply chain, which could result in significantly higher upfront costs and adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations. For more information about such lease arrangements, see the sections titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources—Contractual Obligations” and “—If our actual compute requirements differ materially from our projections, we may fail to secure sufficient compute to meet our needs or we may be committed to excess compute that remains underutilized.” We have limited experience in managing such data center infrastructure projects at scale. Successfully executing on these data center infrastructure initiatives requires us to recruit personnel with relevant experience and manage complex multi-year deployment timelines and relationships with developers, contractors, and service providers.
paras.zh: 为帮助降低我们对云服务商（CSP）的依赖、应对可用算力的约束，并确保以开发前沿模型所需的规模获得算力，我们正在推进各项举措，以开发我们自有的专用本地数据中心基础设施。这些努力包括与第三方合作伙伴签订长期租赁和建立合作关系，以获取底层房地产、电力和数据中心设施，同时我们租赁这些设施中的容量，并与专业第三方运营商签约，由其负责设施的持续管理。我们还直接采购某些算力和基础设施设备，并在按我们的规格、由他人代我们租赁和运营的专用数据中心设施中运行这些设备。例如，根据 2026 年租赁安排，五年期设备租赁的租金付款合计约为 $125.2 billion（不含利息），租金按季度分期支付，付款义务通常在 AI 基础设施设备在相应数据中心设施“可供使用”时开始。2026 年租赁安排在相应租赁期内不可由该协议各方取消，违约情形除外。此外，我们于 2026 年 4 月将现金存入一个受限账户，受益人为 Broadcom，以担保算力容量，该金额可根据特定条件的满足情况予以释放或用于抵充租赁项下的义务。在某些情况下，我们可能被要求向该受限账户存入额外现金，以支付 2026 年租赁安排项下未来到期金额。一旦发生某些未获补救的违约事件，例如根据 2026 年租赁安排条款发生的某些付款或履约失败，我们在 2026 年租赁安排项下的大部分义务将被加速到期；尽管我们拥有多种资本来源，且并不依赖我们为 2026 年租赁安排而签订的基础设施合作伙伴 2026 年 NPA 所提供的潜在融资能力，但我们可能不被允许选择根据基础设施合作伙伴 2026 年 NPA 发行可转换本票来为此类义务提供融资。此外，我们未来可能继续直接采购此类数据中心基础设施，我们也可能采取其他举措来建设我们自己的算力和基础设施，并更深入地投资于算力供应链，这可能导致前期成本大幅增加，并对我们的财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。有关此类租赁安排的更多信息，请参见“管理层对财务状况和经营业绩的讨论与分析——流动性与资本资源——合同义务”和“——如果我们的实际算力需求与我们的预测存在重大差异，我们可能无法获得足够的算力来满足我们的需求，或者我们可能承诺了过剩的算力而该等算力仍未得到充分利用”等章节。我们在规模化管理此类数据中心基础设施项目方面经验有限。要成功执行这些数据中心基础设施举措，我们需要招聘具有相关经验的人员，并管理复杂的多年部署时间表以及与开发商、承包商和服务提供商的关系。

paras.en: As we continue to build out our own compute and infrastructure and further vertically integrate across the compute supply chain, these multi-party structures will become more prevalent and will expose us to a structural timing and liquidity risk in our payment obligations that differs from our historical compute arrangements. Historically, we have generally obtained compute from a limited number of CSPs under arrangements in which our compute and infrastructure expenses are paid as compute becomes available to us. In the future, we expect we will increasingly enter into separate arrangements with a greater number of different counterparties, each responsible for discrete services or inputs across the compute supply chain. Under many of these arrangements, we may be obligated to pay a counterparty once it performs its discrete obligation, even if delays or failures by others prevent us from assembling those discrete services or inputs into usable compute we can deploy to generate revenue. In addition, counterparties may deliver their services or inputs later than scheduled, or may fail to deliver them at all, and any such delay or non-delivery by a single counterparty could postpone or prevent our deployment of the associated compute. As a result, we could incur significant cash outflows without obtaining usable compute on a timely basis, which could adversely affect our liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 随着我们持续建设自有算力和基础设施，并在算力供应链上进一步垂直整合，这类多方结构将变得更加普遍，并使我们面临与以往算力安排不同的、在付款义务上的结构性时间与流动性风险。以往，我们通常从数量有限的云服务商（CSP）处获取算力，相关安排下我们的算力和基础设施费用在算力可供我们使用时支付。未来，我们预计将越来越多地与更多不同的交易对手方分别达成安排，每一方负责算力供应链上各自独立的服务或投入。在这类安排中的许多情形下，我们可能须在交易对手方履行其独立义务后即向其付款，即使其他方的延迟或失败导致我们无法将这些独立服务或投入组装成可部署用于创收的可用算力。此外，交易对手方可能晚于计划交付其服务或投入，或完全未能交付，而任一交易对手方的任何此类延迟或未交付都可能推迟或阻止我们对相关算力的部署。因此，我们可能在未能及时获得可用算力的情况下产生重大现金流出，这可能对我们的流动性、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: Certain of our data center infrastructure arrangements involve complex multi-party structures in which chips are procured from or through our CSPs, leased to us by third-party financing entities, installed in data center facilities procured by or through other third-party partners, and operated by yet another set of third-party service providers. The complexity of these arrangements increases execution risk, as delays or failures by any participant in the chain could affect the availability or performance of the resulting compute.
paras.zh: 我们的部分数据中心基础设施安排涉及复杂的多方结构，其中芯片由我们的云服务商（CSP）采购或通过其采购，由第三方融资实体租赁给我们，安装在其他第三方合作伙伴采购或通过其采购的数据中心设施中，并由另一组第三方服务提供商运营。此类安排的复杂性增加了执行风险，因为链条中任一参与方的延迟或失败都可能影响最终算力的可用性或性能。

paras.en: In addition, to meet the substantial energy demands of large-scale AI workloads, we have entered into, and may in the future enter into, arrangements involving dedicated power generation assets and/or the development, operation, or control of power stations or other energy infrastructure. Such arrangements expose us to new operational, regulatory, and environmental liabilities, and require expertise and capabilities that differ from our core competencies. Successfully executing on these power infrastructure projects requires us to recruit personnel with relevant experience and manage complex multi-year deployment timelines and relationships with developers, contractors, service providers, and regulators, including aligning project completion schedules with the data centers such projects are expected to serve in order to avoid timing delays that constrain our ability to utilize this compute and to generate revenue and recoup costs from such investments.
paras.zh: 此外，为满足大规模 AI 工作负载的巨大能源需求，我们已达成并可能在未来达成涉及专用发电资产和/或发电站或其他能源基础设施的开发、运营或控制的安排。此类安排使我们面临新的运营、监管和环境责任，并要求具备与我们核心能力不同的专业知识和能力。成功执行这些电力基础设施项目，要求我们招募具有相关经验的人员，并管理复杂的多年部署时间表以及与开发商、承包商、服务提供商和监管机构的关系，包括使项目完工时间表与这些项目预计服务的数据中心相协调，以避免时间延迟制约我们利用该算力并产生收入及收回此类投资成本的能力。

paras.en: Deployment of our data center and power infrastructure projects involves execution risks, including delays due to permitting issues, change in law, force majeure, lack of network connectivity between facilities, supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, or contractor performance; cost overruns due to equipment pricing changes, design modifications, or unanticipated requirements; and technical risks that facilities may not perform as specified or achieve expected reliability or efficiency levels. Certain of our arrangements are also subject to conditions precedent that must be satisfied before construction can commence, and completion guarantees that may terminate upon a lender foreclosure before construction is complete, leaving us without contractual recourse to compel completion. Certain of these arrangements also depend on the continued performance of credit support provided by a third party that is also a competitor, the loss or impairment of which could jeopardize the underlying arrangements. Such credit support provided to third-party data center developers or hardware providers, from which we derive no direct contractual rights or obligations, may also affect the availability and cost of data center capacity and hardware generally. Additionally, new tariffs or import fees enacted after the effective date of certain arrangements may be passed through to us as additional costs. Any delay in or limitation on the amount of compute delivered to us could adversely affect our business.
paras.zh: 我们数据中心和电力基础设施项目的部署涉及执行风险，包括因许可问题、法律变更、不可抗力、设施之间缺乏网络连接、供应链中断、劳动力短缺或承包商履约问题而导致的延误；因设备价格变动、设计修改或未预期需求而导致的成本超支；以及设施可能无法按规格运行或无法达到预期可靠性或效率水平的技术风险。我们的某些安排还受制于在施工开始前必须满足的先决条件，以及可能在施工完成前因贷款人止赎而终止的完工担保，从而使我们失去强制要求完工的合同救济途径。其中某些安排还依赖于第三方（该第三方同时也是竞争对手）持续提供信用支持，该信用支持的丧失或受损可能危及相关基础安排。向第三方数据中心开发商或硬件提供商提供的此类信用支持（我们并未由此获得任何直接合同权利或义务）也可能影响数据中心容量和硬件的总体可用性和成本。此外，在某些安排生效日期之后颁布的新关税或进口费用可能作为额外成本转嫁给我们。向我们交付的算力出现任何延迟或数量限制，都可能对我们的业务造成不利影响。

paras.en: The capital-intensive and long-term nature of leasing and equipping data center capacity creates financial risk, as large upfront investments and long-term payment commitments must be made months before facilities become fully operational. If our compute requirements or technology needs change, we may find ourselves with leased or dedicated infrastructure that is poorly suited to our actual needs, and technological changes in AI hardware or training methodologies could render such infrastructure less efficient than newer alternatives. Unlike CSP arrangements where compute can be adjusted relatively dynamically, long-term leases, reserved compute, and dedicated infrastructure investments are much less flexible and create long-term financial obligations regardless of whether the capacity continues to meet our needs. For example, certain of our dedicated power and data center infrastructure arrangements have initial terms of 20 years with annual escalators and include take-or-pay compute payment obligations and uncapped fuel cost pass-throughs that apply for the duration of the term regardless of actual utilization.
paras.zh: 租赁和配置数据中心容量具有资本密集和长期性的特点，会带来财务风险，因为必须在设施全面投入运营前数月进行大额前期投资并作出长期付款承诺。如果我们的算力需求或技术需求发生变化，我们可能会发现自己租赁或专用的基础设施与实际需求并不匹配，而 AI 硬件或训练方法的技术变革可能使此类基础设施的效率低于更新的替代方案。与算力可以相对动态调整的 CSP 安排不同，长期租赁、预留算力和专用基础设施投资的灵活性要低得多，并且无论容量是否继续满足我们的需求，都会产生长期财务义务。例如，我们的某些专用电力和数据中心基础设施安排的初始期限为 20 年，包含年度递增条款，并包含照付不议的算力付款义务以及无上限的燃料成本转嫁，这些义务在整个期限内无论实际使用情况如何均适用。

paras.en: Our increasing efforts to build out our compute and infrastructure require substantial capital expenditures and are changing the cash flow profile of our business. Whereas the compute purchased through our CSP arrangements is generally paid as the compute becomes available to us, we expect an increasing portion of our compute and infrastructure investment to take the form of capital expenditures and other commitments, including lease obligations, that require significant upfront payments well in advance of the related compute becoming operational. Our existing commitments are substantial, and we expect our capital expenditures to increase significantly as we continue to expand our compute and infrastructure build-out. See the section titled “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations—Liquidity and Capital Resources” for more information. As a result, we expect these investments to result in significant net cash used in operating and investing activities for the foreseeable future, and our net cash used in these activities may increase regardless of whether our financial performance improves. The magnitude and timing of these investments are inherently uncertain and may change materially over short periods, including as a result of decisions to accelerate or expand our build-out, and such changes could rapidly and significantly alter our expected results of operations and cash flows for a given period. If our cash flows from operations and available capital are insufficient to fund these investments, we may be required to raise additional capital on unfavorable terms or to reduce, defer, or forgo planned investments, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 我们为构建算力和基础设施而不断加大的投入需要大量资本支出，并且正在改变我们业务的现金流特征。通过我们的云服务商（CSP）安排购买的算力通常在算力可供我们使用时才付款，而我们预计，我们的算力和基础设施投资中越来越大的部分将以资本支出及其他承诺（包括租赁义务）的形式出现，这些支出需要在相关算力投入运营之前很早就进行大额预付款。我们现有的承诺规模庞大，并且随着我们继续扩大算力和基础设施建设，我们预计资本支出将大幅增加。更多信息请参见“管理层对财务状况和经营成果的讨论与分析——流动性与资本资源”一节。因此，我们预计这些投资将在可预见的未来导致经营活动和投资活动产生大量净现金流出，并且无论我们的财务表现是否改善，这些活动使用的净现金都可能增加。这些投资的规模和时点本身具有不确定性，并可能在短期内发生重大变化，包括因决定加速或扩大我们的建设而发生的变化，而此类变化可能迅速且显著地改变我们在某一期间的预期经营成果和现金流。如果我们的经营活动现金流和可用资本不足以支持这些投资，我们可能被要求以不利条件筹集额外资本，或减少、推迟或放弃计划中的投资，其中任何一项都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: If we are unable to successfully execute on our data center infrastructure initiatives, experience significant delays or cost overruns, or find that the infrastructure we lease, deploy, or build does not meet our evolving needs, we may not realize the expected benefits of these investments, which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 如果我们无法成功执行我们的数据中心基础设施计划、遭遇重大延迟或成本超支，或发现我们租赁、部署或建设的基础设施无法满足我们不断变化的需求，我们可能无法实现这些投资的预期收益，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。

paras.en: **We may not successfully build, expand, and deploy our sales and marketing organization in a timely manner, or we may not successfully hire, retain, train, and motivate our sales personnel.**
paras.zh: **我们可能无法及时成功建立、扩展和部署我们的销售与营销组织，或者我们可能无法成功招聘、留住、培训和激励我们的销售人员。**

paras.en: We have grown, and will continue to grow, our direct sales force. Whether we are able to increase our sales to existing customers, identify and engage new customers, and enter new U.S. and non-U.S. markets, each with a focus on broadening use of our models, platform, and applications across departments and entire organizations, will depend, among other things, on our ability to successfully test new market segments and customer types, validate product-market fit through early customer engagement, timely and effectively scale our sales motions, and adapt quickly when market conditions change. We have limited experience building, managing, and scaling a direct sales force. We have dedicated and plan to continue to dedicate significant resources to sales and marketing programs and to expand our sales and marketing capabilities to target potential customers and achieve broader market adoption of our models, platform, and applications, but there is no guarantee that we will be successful in attracting and maintaining additional customers. Moreover, identifying, recruiting, training, and managing sales personnel requires significant time, expense, and attention, including from our senior management and other key personnel, as there is significant competition for sales personnel with the skills and technical knowledge that we require, including the ability to understand and communicate complex and evolving AI use cases, regulatory considerations, customer risk sensitivities, and rapidly changing product capabilities. These challenges are particularly acute for international expansion, which requires qualified personnel with international experience, language skills, cultural competencies in the geographic markets which we target, and an aligned mission-oriented culture. If we are unable to successfully manage the foregoing risks, our prospects, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们已扩大并将继续扩大我们的直销团队。我们能否增加对现有客户的销售、识别并接触新客户、进入新的美国及非美国市场（每个市场的重点均在于推动我们的模型、平台和应用程序在各部门及整个组织中的更广泛使用），除其他因素外，将取决于我们能否成功测试新的细分市场和客户类型、通过早期客户互动验证产品与市场的契合度、及时有效地扩大销售动作，并在市场状况变化时迅速适应。我们在组建、管理和扩大直销团队方面经验有限。我们已投入并计划继续投入大量资源用于销售和营销项目，并扩展我们的销售和营销能力，以瞄准潜在客户并实现我们的模型、平台和应用程序更广泛的市场采用，但无法保证我们将成功吸引并留住更多客户。此外，识别、招聘、培训和管理销售人员需要大量时间、费用和精力，包括我们高级管理层和其他关键人员的投入，因为对于具备我们所要求的技能和技术知识的销售人员（包括理解和传达复杂且不断演变的 AI 用例、监管考量、客户风险敏感性以及快速变化的产品能力），存在激烈竞争。这些挑战在国际扩张中尤为突出，因为国际扩张需要具备国际经验、语言技能、目标地理市场文化能力以及契合的使命导向文化的合格人员。如果我们无法成功管理上述风险，我们的前景、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: We periodically make adjustments to our sales and marketing organization in response to market opportunities, product introductions or enhancements, acquisitions, and other internal and external considerations. Any future sales and marketing organization changes may result in a temporary reduction of productivity, which could negatively affect our rate of growth. In addition, any significant change to the way we structure and implement the compensation of our sales and marketing organization may be disruptive or may not be effective and may adversely affect our revenue growth. If we are unable to attract, hire, develop, retain, and motivate qualified sales and marketing personnel, if our new sales personnel are unable to achieve sufficient sales productivity levels in a reasonable period of time or at all, if our marketing programs are not effective, or if we are unable to effectively build, expand, and manage our sales organization and operations, our sales and revenue may grow more slowly than expected or decline, and our prospects, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们会定期对销售和营销组织进行调整，以应对市场机会、产品推出或增强、收购以及其他内部和外部考量。未来任何销售和营销组织的变动都可能导致生产力暂时下降，从而可能对我们的增长率产生负面影响。此外，对我们销售和营销组织的薪酬结构和实施方式进行的任何重大变更都可能具有破坏性，或可能无法奏效，并可能对我们的收入增长产生不利影响。如果我们无法吸引、聘用、培养、留住和激励合格的销售和营销人员，如果我们的新销售人员无法在合理时间内达到足够的销售生产力水平或根本无法达到，如果我们的营销项目无效，或者如果我们无法有效组建、扩展和管理我们的销售组织及运营，我们的销售和收入增长可能会慢于预期或出现下降，我们的前景、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **We have a limited history under our current go-to-market strategy, and our efforts to scale and evolve our customer acquisition, engagement, and retention model may not be successful.**
paras.zh: **在我们当前的上市策略下，我们的经营历史有限，我们为扩大和演进客户获取、互动与留存模式所做的努力可能不会成功。**

paras.en: We have a limited history selling consumption-based access and subscriptions to our models, platform, and applications under our current business model, and we are continuing to scale our operations and go-to-market strategy. Our future success depends in part on our ability to continue attracting, onboarding, expanding, and retaining customers under this model, including determining whether, when, and how to target, develop, and deepen relationships with individual customers over time. Scaling our operations, including hiring, training, and retaining additional sales, sales engineering, and customer-facing personnel, and evolving our go-to-market strategy may take more time and require more effort than anticipated, and the results of these efforts are difficult to predict. Our business and operating models have not been fully proven, and our limited history with our current approach makes it difficult to evaluate our prospects, plan for future growth, and forecast our results of operations.
paras.zh: 在我们当前的商业模式下，我们销售基于用量的模型、平台和应用访问权限及订阅服务的经营历史有限，我们仍在持续扩大运营规模和上市策略。我们未来的成功部分取决于我们能否在这一模式下持续吸引、引导入驻、扩展并留存客户，包括确定是否、何时以及如何随着时间推移锁定、发展并深化与个人客户的关系。扩大运营规模（包括招聘、培训和留任更多销售、销售工程及面向客户的人员）以及演进我们的上市策略，可能比预期耗费更多时间和精力，且这些努力的结果难以预测。我们的业务和运营模式尚未得到充分验证，加之我们采用当前方式的经营历史有限，使得我们难以评估自身前景、规划未来增长并预测经营业绩。

paras.en: In addition, our strategy and customer mix expose us to competitive and execution risks as the AI market continues to evolve. We have organized our research priorities, our product roadmap, and our go-to-market and Applied AI teams around enterprise use cases, and much of the diffusion of Claude to date has been organic— driven by individual users, including software developers and prosumers, who adopt Claude and often serve as internal champions for its broader adoption within their organizations—rather than by a large direct sales organization. This approach has allowed us to scale with a smaller team relative to other large enterprise technology companies, but it assumes that our applications and distribution will be sufficient to deliver the capabilities of our models to customers and that individual adoption will continue to translate into organizational adoption and expansion. Companies with stronger consumer-facing businesses, larger consumer user bases, more established brands, broader distribution, or deeper customer relationships may choose to increase their focus on enterprise customers or enterprise use cases and could leverage their scale, resources, and market presence to compete more effectively with us. In particular, if such competitors capture the individual users from whom our enterprise adoption often originates, whether through their consumer applications, by integrating AI functionality into products those users already use, or otherwise, our pipeline of enterprise opportunities could be reduced in ways that a direct sales organization of our current scale may not be able to offset. Building a substantially larger sales organization, or shifting investment toward consumer and application-layer products to compete for those users, would require significant time and resources beyond our current plans and would involve the trade-offs described in the section titled “—We face intense competition, and if we are unable to compete effectively, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.” Because we have a limited operating history with our current business model and go-to-market strategy, we have less experience predicting customer adoption, expansion, and retention patterns, and customers may be slower than expected to adopt our models, platform, and applications or expand usage. Any failure to successfully scale our operations or effectively execute on and refine our go-to-market strategy could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，随着 AI 市场持续演变，我们的战略和客户结构使我们面临竞争与执行风险。我们围绕企业用例来组织研究优先级、产品路线图以及市场推广团队和应用 AI 团队，而迄今为止 Claude 的许多扩散都是有机发生的——由个人用户（包括软件开发者和专业消费者）推动，他们采用 Claude，并往往在其组织内部成为推动更广泛采用的内部倡导者——而非由庞大的直销组织推动。这种方式使我们能够以相对于其他大型企业技术公司更小的团队实现规模化，但它假设我们的应用和分发足以将模型能力交付给客户，并且个人采用将持续转化为组织采用和扩展。拥有更强面向消费者业务、更大消费者用户基础、更成熟品牌、更广泛分发渠道或更深客户关系的公司，可能选择加大对企业的客户或企业用例的关注，并可能利用其规模、资源和市场影响力与我们更有效地竞争。特别是，如果此类竞争对手获取了我们的企业采用往往源自的个人用户——无论是通过其消费者应用、将 AI 功能集成到这些用户已在使用的产品中，还是其他方式——我们的企业机会管道可能会以我们当前规模的直销组织可能无法抵消的方式减少。建立规模大得多的销售组织，或将投资转向消费者和应用层产品以争夺这些用户，将需要超出我们当前计划的大量时间和资源，并会涉及标题为“——我们面临激烈竞争，如果我们无法有效竞争，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响”一节中所述的权衡。由于我们以当前商业模式和市场推广策略运营的历史有限，我们在预测客户采用、扩展和留存模式方面经验较少，客户采用我们的模型、平台和应用或扩大使用的速度可能慢于预期。任何未能成功扩展我们的运营或未能有效执行和优化我们的市场推广策略的情况，都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **Sales to enterprise customers involve complexities and risks that could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **向企业客户销售涉及复杂性和风险，可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We derive a large portion of our revenue from sales to enterprise customers. Our ability to attract, retain, and expand relationships with enterprise customers depends in significant part on our ability to meet their generally heightened operational, technical, security, reliability, and compliance requirements. Enterprises typically expect high levels of system uptime, performance consistency, data security, auditability, internal controls, and scalability, as well as robust support and service levels. These requirements may be heightened for our agentic offerings, where enterprise customers may require detailed logs of each action taken by an autonomous agent within their environment, including the agent’s reasoning, tool invocations, and interactions with external systems. Any inability on our part to provide such logs at the level of granularity customers require could limit adoption of our agentic offerings by enterprises or result in customer attrition. If we are unable to deliver models, platforms, and applications that satisfy these enterprise-grade requirements, or if we experience outages, performance degradation, security incidents, or other operational failures, our ability to retain and expand with enterprise customers could be adversely affected. In particular, as we deploy our Virtual Collaborators, like Claude Code and Claude Cowork, within enterprise environments, these systems will require broad permissions and deep integrations with customers’ internal tools, data, and workflows in order to operate effectively. The scope of access required for extended autonomous operation within enterprise environments increases the potential consequences of any security incident, unauthorized action, or system error, and customers may be reluctant to grant the level of access necessary for these systems to operate as designed if they are unable to satisfy themselves regarding the security, reliability, and controllability of such systems.
paras.zh: 我们的很大一部分收入来自向企业客户的销售。我们吸引、留存并拓展与企业客户关系的能力，在很大程度上取决于我们能否满足其普遍更高的运营、技术、安全、可靠性和合规要求。企业通常期望高水平的系统正常运行时间、性能一致性、数据安全、可审计性、内部控制和可扩展性，以及有力的支持和服务水平。对于我们的智能体产品，这些要求可能更高，因为企业客户可能要求提供自主智能体在其环境中采取的每一项操作的详细日志，包括智能体的推理过程、工具调用以及与外部系统的交互。如果我们无法按客户要求的细粒度提供此类日志，可能会限制企业对我们智能体产品的采用，或导致客户流失。如果我们无法交付满足这些企业级要求的模型、平台和应用，或者如果我们遭遇服务中断、性能下降、安全事件或其他运营故障，我们留存并拓展企业客户的能力可能会受到不利影响。特别是，当我们在企业环境中部署 Claude Code 和 Claude Cowork 等虚拟协作者时，这些系统需要广泛的权限，并与客户的内部工具、数据和工作流深度集成，才能有效运行。在企业环境中进行长时间自主运行所需的访问范围，会放大任何安全事件、未经授权的操作或系统错误的潜在后果；如果客户无法确信此类系统的安全性、可靠性和可控性，他们可能不愿授予这些系统按设计运行所需的访问权限。

paras.en: Our sales efforts targeted at enterprise customers also involve risks and challenges that may not be present, or that are present to a lesser extent, with sales to individuals or smaller organizations. These customers typically have longer decision-making cycles, require greater security, functionality, and scalability, expect a broader range of services, demand that providers take on a larger share of risks, require higher levels of customer service and support, and expect greater payment flexibility from vendors. We are often required to spend significant time and resources to familiarize potential customers with the value proposition of our models, platform, and applications, and this process can take substantially longer with enterprise customers. Enterprises may also require extensive customization, integration support, and vendor evaluations and demand more features than we currently offer or than we can deliver within their expected timeframes, including enterprise-grade functionality such as audit logs, compliance features, security controls, and monitoring tools, which may require us to make additional investments in product development or services capabilities, before committing to a purchase. As a result of these factors, sales opportunities with enterprises require us to devote greater sales and administrative support and professional services resources to each such enterprise customer, which increases our costs, lengthens our sales cycle, and diverts our sales and customer service resources to a smaller number of enterprise customers. We may spend substantial time, effort, and money in our sales efforts without successfully producing any sales. In addition, many enterprise customers procure and deploy our models, platform, and applications through third-party CSP marketplaces, which can introduce additional complexity into the sales and deployment process, including reliance on the CSPs’ procurement, security, and billing workflows and coordination with multiple counterparties. As a result, our ability to attract, retain, and expand relationships with enterprise customers may also depend in part on factors outside of our direct control, including the policies, priorities, and operational requirements of such CSPs.
paras.zh: 我们针对企业客户的销售工作还涉及一些风险和挑战，这些风险和挑战在向个人或较小组织销售时可能并不存在，或存在的程度较低。这类客户通常决策周期更长，要求更高的安全性、功能性和可扩展性，期望更广泛的服务范围，要求供应商承担更大比例的风险，要求更高水平的客户服务和支持，并期望供应商提供更大的付款灵活性。我们往往需要投入大量时间和资源，使潜在客户了解我们模型、平台和应用的价值主张，而这一过程在企业客户处可能耗时显著更长。企业还可能要求大量定制化、集成支持以及供应商评估，并要求我们提供比目前所提供或比我们能在其期望的时间范围内交付的更多功能，包括审计日志、合规功能、安全控制和监控工具等企业级功能，这可能要求我们在承诺购买之前对产品开发或服务能力进行额外投资。由于上述因素，与企业客户的销售机会要求我们为每一家此类企业客户投入更多的销售和行政支持以及专业服务资源，这增加了我们的成本、延长了我们的销售周期，并使我们的销售和客户服务资源被分流至数量较少的企业客户。我们可能在销售工作上投入大量时间、精力和资金，却未能成功实现任何销售。此外，许多企业客户通过第三方云服务商（CSP）市场采购和部署我们的模型、平台和应用，这可能给销售和部署流程带来额外的复杂性，包括依赖 CSP 的采购、安全和计费工作流程以及与多个交易对手方的协调。因此，我们吸引、留住企业客户并扩大与其关系的能力，也可能部分取决于我们无法直接控制的因素，包括此类 CSP 的政策、优先事项和运营要求。

paras.en: A number of factors influence the length and variability of our sales cycle. The need to educate potential customers about the uses and benefits of our models, platform, and applications, the discretionary nature of purchasing and budget cycles, competitive evaluation and purchasing approval processes, procurement requirements, legal review of contract terms, and internal budget authorization procedures all contribute to sales cycle variability. The length of our sales cycle, from identification of the opportunity to deal closure, may vary significantly from customer to customer. Sales to enterprises typically take longer to complete than sales to individuals or smaller organizations.
paras.zh: 诸多因素影响我们销售周期的长度和波动性。需要让潜在客户了解我们模型、平台和应用的用途与优势、采购和预算周期的自主决定性质、竞争性评估和采购审批流程、采购要求、合同条款的法律审查以及内部预算授权程序，都会导致销售周期的波动性。我们的销售周期从识别机会到交易完成，可能因客户不同而存在显著差异。与企业客户的销售通常比向个人或较小组织的销售需要更长时间才能完成。

paras.en: A meaningful portion of our revenue is attributable to a relatively small number of such enterprise customer relationships, which increases the variability of our financial results. Our revenue in any given quarter could be substantially affected if these customers decide to significantly reduce their spend.
paras.zh: 我们收入的相当一部分来自相对少数此类企业客户关系，这增加了我们财务业绩的波动性。若这些客户决定大幅削减支出，我们在任何特定季度的收入都可能受到重大影响。

paras.en: Enterprises may have deep existing relationships with our competitors for models, platforms, and applications we do not offer, or relationships with others in the ecosystem, which may delay our sales process or cause us to not succeed with such enterprises.
paras.zh: 企业客户可能已与我们竞争对手在模型、平台及我们未提供的应用方面建立了深厚关系，或与生态系统中的其他方存在关系，这可能延迟我们的销售流程，或导致我们无法成功赢得此类企业客户。

paras.en: Enterprise customers are particularly sensitive to our ability to maintain the uptime of our models, platform, and applications, and any degradation in uptime could adversely affect our ability to retain and expand with our enterprise customers. Sustaining the uptime, performance, and scale that enterprise customers expect can place additional demands on our overall compute, and any failure of our capacity management systems to direct sufficient compute to support such demands could adversely affect our ability to serve all workloads. For more information about the foregoing, see the section titled “—If we fail to manage our technical operations infrastructure, or experience service outages, interruptions, or delays in the deployment of our models, platform, and applications, our results of operations may be adversely affected.”
paras.zh: 企业客户尤其关注我们维持模型、平台和应用正常运行时间的能力，正常运行时间的任何下降都可能不利于我们留住并拓展企业客户。维持企业客户所期望的正常运行时间、性能和规模，可能对我们的整体算力提出额外需求，若我们的容量管理系统未能调配足够算力来支持此类需求，可能不利于我们服务所有工作负载的能力。有关前述内容的更多信息，请参见标题为“——如果我们未能管理好技术运营基础设施，或我们的模型、平台和应用的部署出现服务中断、中断或延迟，我们的经营业绩可能受到不利影响”的章节。

paras.en: Our sales strategy for these enterprise customers also depends on our ability to build and maintain an effective sales organization. If we fail to effectively manage these risks associated with sales to enterprises, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected. For additional discussion of our personnel related risks, see the section titled “—We may not successfully build, expand, and deploy our sales and marketing organization in a timely manner, or we may not successfully hire, retain, train, and motivate our sales personnel.”
paras.zh: 我们针对这些企业客户的销售策略还取决于我们建立并维持有效销售组织的能力。如果我们未能有效管理与向企业销售相关的这些风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。有关我们人员相关风险的更多讨论，请参见标题为“——我们可能无法及时成功建立、扩展和部署我们的销售与营销组织，或者我们可能无法成功招聘、留住、培训和激励我们的销售人员”的章节。

paras.en: **If our marketing strategies, such as our free trials and free tiers, fail to generate the benefits we expect, or if their costs exceed those benefits, our ability to grow our revenue could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们的营销策略（例如免费试用和免费层级）未能产生我们预期的收益，或其成本超过这些收益，我们增长收入的能力可能受到不利影响。**

paras.en: A portion of our users access our models, platform, and applications through free tiers or promotional offerings, and we seek to convert these users into paying customers over time. We may not always be successful in doing so, as free users may be satisfied with the limited functionality available in free tiers, may not have budgets to support paid subscriptions, or may choose to use our free offerings indefinitely without converting to paid plans. The availability of free tiers may cannibalize potential paid subscriptions, as some users who would have otherwise paid for our services may instead rely exclusively on free access. Additionally, providing free access to our models, platform, and applications involves costs, including compute and infrastructure, customer support, and other operational costs. In addition, we offer free access in significant part to build awareness of, familiarity with, and engagement with our products, and as a means of reaching individuals engaged in knowledge work outside of a business or organizational context [__] . [__] However, these benefits are inherently difficult to measure, free usage may not generate the awareness or advocacy we expect, and individual adoption of our products may not translate into organizational adoption or expansion. See the section titled “—We have a limited history under our current go-to-market strategy, and our efforts to scale and evolve our customer acquisition, engagement, and retention model may not be successful.” If the costs of supporting free users exceed the value we derive from their eventual conversion or other benefits such as network effects and word-of-mouth referrals, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们的部分用户通过免费层级或促销优惠访问我们的模型、平台和应用程序，我们力求随着时间推移将这些用户转化为付费客户。我们未必总能成功实现这一转化，因为免费用户可能对免费层级所提供的有限功能感到满意，可能没有预算支持付费订阅，也可能选择无限期使用我们的免费产品而不转化为付费计划。免费层级的提供可能会蚕食潜在的付费订阅，因为部分原本会为我们的服务付费的用户可能转而完全依赖免费访问。此外，向用户免费提供我们的模型、平台和应用程序涉及成本，包括算力和基础设施、客户支持以及其他运营成本。此外，我们提供免费访问在很大程度上是为了建立对我们产品的认知、熟悉度和参与度，并作为触达在企业或组织情境之外从事知识工作的个人的一种方式[__]。[__]然而，这些益处本质上难以衡量，免费使用可能无法产生我们预期的认知度或倡导效应，个人对我们产品的采用也可能无法转化为组织层面的采用或扩展。参见标题为“——我们在当前市场推广策略下的经营历史有限，我们扩大和演进客户获取、参与和留存模式的努力可能不会成功。”的章节。如果支持免费用户的成本超过我们从其最终转化或其他益处（如网络效应和口碑推荐）中获得的价值，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **If we fail to maintain high-quality customer support, our ability to retain and expand customers could suffer, which may adversely affect our prospects, business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **如果我们未能维持高质量的客户支持，我们留存和扩展客户的能力可能会受损，这可能会对我们的前景、业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。**

paras.en: Our customers rely on our customer support services to resolve issues and realize the full benefits that our models, platform, and applications provide. In order to deliver high-quality customer support and engagement, we must successfully assist our customers in deploying and continuing to use our models, platform, and applications, resolve performance issues, discover and deploy our models, platform, and applications in new use cases, provide hands-on technical implementation, customization and solution engineering support, provide training and guidance to help customers effectively adopt and scale their use of our models, platform, and applications, address interoperability challenges, and respond to security threats and cyberattacks and performance and reliability problems that may arise from time to time. The importance of our support function will increase as we expand our business and pursue new customers. Many enterprises have complex internal systems and require high levels of focused support to fully realize the benefits of our models, platform, and applications. If we do not help our customers quickly resolve issues and provide effective ongoing support and enablement, or a market perception develops that we do not maintain high-quality customer support and experience, our ability to maintain and expand our subscriptions to existing and new customers could suffer, particularly with respect to our enterprise customers.
paras.zh: 我们的客户依赖我们的客户支持服务来解决问题，并充分实现我们的模型、平台和应用程序所带来的全部效益。为提供高质量的客户支持与互动，我们必须成功协助客户部署并持续使用我们的模型、平台和应用程序，解决性能问题，在新的使用场景中发现并部署我们的模型、平台和应用程序，提供现场技术实施、定制化和解决方案工程支持，提供培训和指导以帮助客户有效采用并扩大对我们模型、平台和应用程序的使用，解决互操作性挑战，并应对不时出现的安全威胁和网络攻击以及性能和可靠性问题。随着我们扩展业务并争取新客户，我们支持职能的重要性将会提升。许多企业拥有复杂的内部系统，需要高度专注的支持才能充分实现我们模型、平台和应用程序的效益。如果我们不能帮助客户快速解决问题并提供有效的持续支持和赋能，或者市场形成一种看法认为我们未能维持高质量的客户支持与体验，那么我们维持并扩大现有客户和新客户订阅的能力可能会受到损害，尤其是在企业客户方面。

paras.en: In addition, our growth model depends significantly on driving deeper adoption and expanded use cases within our existing customer base. If we are unable to effectively provide support and integration efforts that enable customers to identify, deploy, and scale additional high-value use cases, demonstrate measurable return on investment, or integrate our models, platform, and applications into their core workflows, customers may limit usage, fail to renew at expected levels, or reduce their spend, which could materially slow our revenue growth.
paras.zh: 此外，我们的增长模式在很大程度上取决于推动现有客户群更深入的采用和扩展使用场景。如果我们无法有效提供支持和集成工作，使客户能够识别、部署并扩展更多高价值使用场景、展示可衡量的投资回报，或将我们的模型、平台和应用程序整合到其核心工作流程中，客户可能会限制使用、无法按预期水平续订或减少支出，这可能会实质性放缓我们的收入增长。

paras.en: Further, there can be no assurance that we will be able to hire sufficient support personnel as and when needed, particularly if our sales exceed our internal forecasts. We expect to continue to increase our customer base, and that growth may put additional pressure on our customer support teams, which may require additional personnel to respond to customer demand. We may be unable to respond quickly enough to accommodate short-term increases in customer demand for services. To the extent that we are unsuccessful in hiring, training, and retaining adequate support personnel, our ability to provide high-quality and timely support to our customers will be negatively impacted, and our customers’ satisfaction and their use and subscription of our models, platform, and applications could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 此外，无法保证我们能够在需要时聘用足够的支持人员，尤其是在我们的销售超出内部预测的情况下。我们预计将继续扩大客户群，而这种增长可能会给我们的客户支持团队带来额外压力，可能需要增加人员来响应客户需求。我们可能无法足够迅速地响应客户对服务的短期需求增长。若我们未能成功招聘、培训和留住足够的支持人员，我们向客户提供高质量、及时支持的能力将受到负面影响，客户的满意度及其对我们模型、平台和应用程序的使用和订阅可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, as we continue to grow our operations and reach a larger and increasingly global customer base, we need to be able to provide efficient services that meet our customers’ needs globally at scale, and our customer support teams may face additional challenges, including those associated with delivering support, training, and documentation in languages other than English and providing services across expanded time-zones. If we are unable to manage the foregoing risks, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 此外，随着我们持续扩大运营规模并触达规模更大、日益全球化的客户群体，我们需要能够在全球范围内大规模提供满足客户需求的高效服务，而我们的客户支持团队可能面临更多挑战，包括以英语以外的语言提供支持、培训和文档，以及在更多时区提供服务所带来的挑战。如果我们无法管理上述风险，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **Our product and investment decisions may not prioritize short-term financial results and may not align with investor expectations or preferences, which could adversely affect the market price of our Class A common stock.**
paras.zh: **我们的产品和投资决策可能不会优先考虑短期财务业绩，也可能与投资者的预期或偏好不一致，这可能对我们的 A 类普通股市场价格产生不利影响。**

paras.en: Our product and investment decisions are informed in large part by our commitment to AI safety, expanding our models, platform, and applications securely and responsibly, and providing high quality customer support, all of which, in addition to our status as a PBC, may not necessarily maximize short term financial results. While we generally believe that our product and investment strategy will improve our long-term financial results, we regularly make product and investment decisions that may or may be perceived to negatively impact our short-term revenue or ability to achieve and sustain profitability. For example, we have in the past delayed the release of new models or features, limited their availability, imposed usage restrictions, or constrained certain functionality until we determined that sufficient safety testing, evaluations, or mitigations were completed, such as with Mythos through Project Glasswing, which may have had a negative impact on our short-term revenue, and we may do so again in the future.
paras.zh: 我们的产品和投资决策在很大程度上以我们对 AI 安全的承诺为指导，即安全、负责任地扩展我们的模型、平台和应用，并提供高质量的客户支持；除我们作为 PBC 的身份外，所有这些未必能最大化短期财务业绩。尽管我们普遍认为我们的产品和投资策略将改善我们的长期财务业绩，但我们经常做出可能或被认为可能对我们的短期收入或实现并维持盈利能力产生负面影响的产品和投资决策。例如，我们过去曾推迟发布新模型或功能、限制其可用性、施加使用限制或约束某些功能，直至我们确定已完成充分的安全测试、评估或缓解措施，例如通过 Project Glasswing 对 Mythos 所做的处理，这可能对我们的短期收入产生了负面影响，我们未来也可能再次这样做。

paras.en: Our focus on AI safety and responsible deployment may also require us to incur significant additional costs, including increased research and development expenses, additional personnel and infrastructure, and foregone or delayed revenue opportunities relative to competitors that may prioritize speed to market, broader access, or more permissive use of their products. These decisions may reduce customer adoption, limit usage by certain customers or use cases, or make our offerings less attractive, particularly when compared to competitors that do not adopt similar constraints.
paras.zh: 我们对 AI 安全和负责任部署的关注还可能要求我们承担大量额外成本，包括增加的研发费用、额外的人员和基础设施，以及相对于可能优先考虑上市速度、更广泛可及性或对其产品采取更宽松使用政策的竞争对手而言放弃或延迟的收入机会。这些决策可能降低客户采用率、限制某些客户或使用场景的使用，或使我们的产品吸引力下降，尤其是在与不采取类似限制的竞争对手相比时。

paras.en: In addition, as we focus on responsibly growing our customer base and engagement across our models, platform, and applications, we may make product, pricing, or access decisions that lead to less short-term profits or engagement compared to our competitors. Customers, partners, or investors may not agree with or fully understand these decisions and may perceive them as limiting our competitiveness or commercial potential, which could adversely affect our reputation, customer relationships, market adoption, or valuation. We cannot assure you that our long-term strategy will ultimately result in superior financial performance or that the anticipated long-term benefits of these decisions will be realized on the timeline we expect, or at all. Any of the foregoing risks could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，在我们专注于以负责任的方式扩大客户群以及提升我们模型、平台和应用程序的用户参与度时，我们可能会做出产品、定价或访问权限方面的决策，这些决策可能导致我们的短期利润或用户参与度低于竞争对手。客户、合作伙伴或投资者可能不认同或无法完全理解这些决策，并可能认为这些决策限制了我们的竞争力或商业潜力，从而可能对我们的声誉、客户关系、市场采用或估值产生不利影响。我们无法向您保证，我们的长期战略最终将带来卓越的财务业绩，也无法保证这些决策的预期长期收益将按我们预期的时间表实现，或根本无法实现。上述任何风险均可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **Our investments in new products, technologies, and business initiatives may not produce the expected benefits and could adversely affect our business.**
paras.zh: **我们在新产品、新技术和新业务举措上的投资可能不会产生预期收益，并可能对我们的业务产生不利影响。**

paras.en: We regularly make decisions to invest in new products, technologies, business lines, and strategic initiatives, including in areas outside our current core offerings, and the outcomes of these investments are inherently uncertain. These initiatives often require significant upfront investments of capital, research and development resources, and management attention, and their outcomes may not achieve widespread market adoption, may not generate revenue at anticipated levels, may take longer than expected to mature, or may fail entirely. In addition, reallocating resources from our core offerings to pursue new initiatives could slow growth in existing products, reduce operating efficiency, or weaken our competitive position if those initiatives do not succeed. If our investments in new products or business lines do not produce the long-term benefits we anticipate, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 我们定期做出投资于新产品、新技术、业务线和战略举措的决策，包括在我们当前核心产品之外的领域进行投资，而这些投资的结果本质上是不确定的。这些举措通常需要大量的前期资本投入、研发资源和管理层的关注，其结果可能无法获得广泛的市场采用，可能无法产生预期水平的收入，可能需要比预期更长的时间才能成熟，或者可能完全失败。此外，如果这些举措不成功，从我们的核心产品中重新分配资源以追求新举措可能会减缓现有产品的增长、降低运营效率或削弱我们的竞争地位。如果我们对新产品的投资或业务线未能产生我们预期的长期收益，我们的业务、财务状况、经营业绩和前景可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: Certain of these initiatives, including our life sciences research program, which involves operating laboratory facilities, and our research in robotics and physical AI, require us to engage in activities outside our historical experience as a software and research organization, such as handling biological and chemical materials, operating laboratory and robotic equipment, and complying with biosafety, occupational health and safety, environmental, hazardous materials, and, potentially, preclinical and clinical research regulations. These activities expose us to categories of liability, including for workplace injury and environmental contamination, that differ from those associated with our core business, and any drug candidates or other discoveries resulting from these efforts would face the lengthy, costly, and uncertain development and regulatory pathways characteristic of the life sciences industry, and may never generate revenue.
paras.zh: 其中某些举措，包括我们的生命科学研究项目（涉及运营实验室设施）以及我们在机器人和物理 AI 方面的研究，要求我们从事超出我们作为软件和研究机构历史经验的活动，例如处理生物和化学材料、操作实验室和机器人设备，以及遵守生物安全、职业健康与安全、环境、危险材料以及可能涉及的临床前和临床研究法规。这些活动使我们面临与核心业务不同的责任类别，包括工伤和环境污染责任，并且这些努力产生的任何候选药物或其他发现都将面临生命科学行业特有的漫长、昂贵且不确定的开发和监管路径，且可能永远无法产生收入。

paras.en: **If we fail to manage our technical operations infrastructure, or experience service outages, interruptions, or delays in the deployment of our models, platform, and applications, our results of operations may be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们未能管理我们的技术运营基础设施，或在我们模型、平台和应用程序的部署过程中遇到服务中断、中断或延迟，我们的经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: Our systems and operations are subject to disruptions resulting from changes to our technology infrastructure. We have experienced, and may continue to experience, service interruptions or degraded performance due to software deployments, configuration changes, system updates, and new model introductions. These disruptions may adversely affect our ability to service customers and could result in lost revenue, customer attrition, or reputational harm. Further, our mitigation efforts and processes may be insufficient to prevent or minimize the impact of system changes on service availability, and we may lack adequate testing, rollback procedures, or monitoring capabilities to detect and remediate issues arising from system changes in a timely manner. For example, in March 2026, we experienced a service outage and periods of degraded performance resulting from a combination of factors, including a significant and rapid increase in usage demand, compute constraints in certain components of our infrastructure, and other factors. Although we have taken and continue to take steps to address these issues, including migrating to more scalable infrastructure and enhancing our operational processes, similar incidents may occur in the future.
paras.zh: 我们的系统和运营会受到技术基础设施变更所导致的中断影响。我们曾经经历、并且未来可能继续经历因软件部署、配置变更、系统更新和新模型引入而导致的服务中断或性能下降。这些中断可能对我们服务客户的能力造成不利影响，并可能导致收入损失、客户流失或声誉损害。此外，我们的缓解措施和流程可能不足以预防或最小化系统变更对服务可用性的影响，我们可能缺乏充分的测试、回滚程序或监控能力，以及时发现并修复系统变更引发的问题。例如，2026 年 3 月，我们经历了一次服务中断和多次性能下降，其成因包括使用需求大幅且快速上升、我们基础设施中某些组件的算力受限以及其他因素。尽管我们已采取并将继续采取措施解决这些问题，包括迁移至更具可扩展性的基础设施并改进运营流程，未来仍可能发生类似事件。

paras.en: In addition, continued growth in our customer base could place additional demands on our models, platform, and applications and could cause or exacerbate slowdowns or interrupt the availability of our models, platform, and applications. If there is a substantial increase in the volume of usage of our models, platform, and applications, we will be required to further expand and upgrade our technology and infrastructure. Any substantial increase in usage will also require increased compute. Because our compute is procured well in advance based on projected demand across all workloads, a significant acceleration in customer demand could cause aggregate capacity to fall short of the levels required to support all of our workloads concurrently at the scale we intend. If our committed compute proves insufficient, or the composition of our committed compute portfolio differs materially from our demand forecasts, we may experience service disruptions, degraded response times, or limitations on customer and user access to our models, platform, and applications, while also experiencing constraints on the compute available to support ongoing model development. There can be no assurance that we will be able to accurately project the rate or timing of increases, if any, in the use of our models, platform, and applications or expand and upgrade our systems and infrastructure to accommodate such increases on a timely basis. If our users are not able to access our models, platform, and applications or encounter slowdowns, we may lose customers or partners. In order to remain competitive, we must continue to enhance and improve the responsiveness, functionality, and features of our models, platform, and applications and the underlying compute infrastructure supporting them. Our disaster recovery plan may not be sufficient to address all aspects or any unanticipated consequence or incidents, and our insurance may not be sufficient to compensate us for the losses that could occur.
paras.zh: 此外，我们客户群的持续增长可能对我们的模型、平台和应用提出额外需求，并可能导致或加剧我们的模型、平台和应用的运行放缓或可用性中断。如果我们的模型、平台和应用的使用量大幅增加，我们将需要进一步扩展和升级我们的技术和基础设施。使用量的任何大幅增加也将需要更多算力。由于我们的算力是根据所有工作负载的预计需求提前采购的，客户需求的显著加速可能导致总容量不足以支撑我们所有工作负载同时以我们预期的规模运行。如果我们已承诺的算力被证明不足，或者我们已承诺算力组合的构成与我们的需求预测存在重大差异，我们可能会遭遇服务中断、响应时间下降，或客户和用户访问我们的模型、平台和应用受到限制，同时还可能面临可用于支持持续模型开发的算力受限。无法保证我们能够准确预测我们的模型、平台和应用使用量的增长速率或时间（如有），或及时扩展和升级我们的系统和基础设施以适应此类增长。如果我们的用户无法访问我们的模型、平台和应用，或遇到运行放缓，我们可能会失去客户或合作伙伴。为保持竞争力，我们必须继续增强和改进我们的模型、平台和应用以及支撑它们的底层算力基础设施的响应能力、功能和特性。我们的灾难恢复计划可能不足以应对所有方面或任何未预见的后果或事件，我们的保险也可能不足以补偿我们可能发生的损失。

paras.en: Moreover, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft provide substantial portions of the compute infrastructure that we use to host our models, platform, and applications and many of the internal tools we use to operate our business. Any significant disruption of, limitation of our access to, or other interference with this infrastructure would negatively impact our operations, degrade the availability and performance of our models, platform, and applications, and could cause us to lose customers who are unable to access or experience difficulties accessing our models, platform, and applications. Even absent a full disruption, the level of service provided by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft could affect the availability or speed of our models, platform, and applications, which may also impact the usage of, and our customers’ satisfaction with, our models, platform, and applications and could seriously harm our business and reputation.
paras.zh: 此外，Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 提供了我们用于托管模型、平台和应用的大量算力基础设施，以及我们用于运营业务的许多内部工具。对此类基础设施的任何重大中断、我们访问受限或其他干扰都将对我们的运营产生负面影响，降低我们的模型、平台和应用的可用性和性能，并可能导致我们失去无法访问或难以访问我们的模型、平台和应用的客户。即使没有完全中断，Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 提供的服务水平也可能影响我们的模型、平台和应用的可用性或速度，这也可能影响我们的模型、平台和使用的使用情况以及客户满意度，并可能严重损害我们的业务和声誉。

paras.en: Any transition of the services and infrastructure currently provided by Amazon, Google, and Microsoft to another CSP would require significant time and expense and could further disrupt or degrade delivery of our models, platform, and applications. Such a transition could require us to re-architect portions of our infrastructure, retrain or migrate models and large datasets, incur data transfer and duplication costs, and adapt our systems to new tools and configurations, which could result in operational delays and reduced performance during the transition period. If Amazon, Google, or Microsoft increases pricing terms, terminates or seeks to terminate our contractual relationship, whether for competitive reasons or otherwise, establishes more favorable relationships with our competitors, or changes or interprets its terms of service or policies in a manner that is unfavorable with respect to us, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 将目前由 Amazon、Google 和 Microsoft 提供的服务和基础设施迁移至其他 CSP，将需要大量时间和费用，并可能进一步扰乱或降低我们模型、平台和应用程序的交付。此类迁移可能要求我们重新设计部分基础设施架构、重新训练或迁移模型及大型数据集、产生数据传输与复制成本，并使我们的系统适配新的工具和配置，从而可能在迁移期间导致运营延迟和性能下降。如果 Amazon、Google 或 Microsoft 提高定价条款、终止或寻求终止我们的合同关系（无论出于竞争原因还是其他原因）、与我们的竞争对手建立更有利的关系，或以对我们不利的方式变更或解释其服务条款或政策，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: In addition, an increasing portion of our compute is hosted in dedicated data center facilities that are leased and operated on our behalf by third parties rather than by our CSPs, and we expect this portion to grow. Certain of these operators have a limited operating history, and these facilities may have less geographic redundancy, failover capacity, or operational tooling than those of large-scale cloud environments, such that an equipment failure, cooling or network disruption, or operator error at a single facility could affect a meaningful portion of our available capacity. Moreover, the continuous availability of our models, platform, and applications depends on the reliable supply of electrical power and water to the facilities that host our infrastructure, whether operated by our CSPs or on our behalf. Utility outages, shortages, price increases, or required curtailment of power during periods of peak demand, whether in connection with or outside of natural disasters or other catastrophic events, could interrupt or degrade the provision of our services in the ordinary course of our business. See the sections titled “—Constraints on the critical inputs supporting compute could limit our ability to secure adequate compute.” and “—Our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected by war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health crises, political crises, or other unexpected events.”
paras.zh: 此外，我们越来越多的算力托管在由第三方（而非我们的 CSP）代表我们租赁和运营的专用数据中心设施中，我们预计这一比例将会增长。其中部分运营商运营历史有限，且这些设施在地理冗余、故障转移能力或运营工具方面可能不如大规模云环境，因此单一设施的设备故障、冷却或网络中断或操作员失误可能影响我们可用容量的相当一部分。此外，我们模型、平台和应用程序的持续可用性取决于为我们基础设施所在设施（无论由我们的 CSP 运营还是代表我们运营）提供可靠的电力和水供应。公用事业停电、短缺、价格上涨或在用电高峰期间被要求限电（无论是否与自然灾害或其他灾难性事件相关），都可能在日常经营过程中中断或降低我们服务的提供。请参阅标题为“——支撑算力的关键投入受限可能限制我们获取充足算力的能力”和“——我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到战争、恐怖主义、自然灾害、公共卫生危机、政治危机或其他意外事件的不利影响”的章节。

paras.en: **If we are unable to make acquisitions and investments, or successfully integrate them into our business, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.**
paras.zh: **如果我们无法进行收购和投资，或无法成功将其整合到我们的业务中，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能会受到不利影响。**

paras.en: As part of our business strategy, we will continue to consider a wide array of potential strategic transactions, including acquisitions of businesses, new technologies, services, and other assets and strategic investments that complement our business. We have previously acquired and continue to evaluate targets that operate in relatively nascent markets, and there is no assurance that such acquired businesses will be successfully integrated into our business or generate substantial revenue. In addition, we may overpay for acquisition targets or make investments at valuations that do not ultimately prove justified by the targets’ performance, strategic value, or market conditions, which could adversely affect our financial condition.
paras.zh: 作为我们业务战略的一部分，我们将继续考虑广泛的潜在战略交易，包括收购与我们的业务互补的企业、新技术、服务及其他资产和战略投资。我们此前已进行过收购，并将继续评估在相对新兴市场中运营的目标，且无法保证此类被收购企业将成功整合入我们的业务或产生可观收入。此外，我们可能为收购目标支付过高对价，或以最终无法被目标公司的业绩、战略价值或市场状况证明合理的估值进行投资，这可能对我们的财务状况产生不利影响。

paras.en: We may be unable to identify or complete prospective and attractive strategic transactions for many reasons, including competition from other potential acquirers, the effects of consolidation in our industry, and potentially high valuations of acquisition candidates. Even if we identify strategic transactions or enter into agreements with respect to such transactions, applicable antitrust laws and other regulations may limit our ability to acquire targets or force us to divest all or a portion of our business or an acquired business. If we are unable to identify suitable targets or complete acquisitions, our growth prospects may suffer, and we may not be able to realize sufficient scale and technological advantages to compete effectively.
paras.zh: 由于诸多原因，我们可能无法识别或完成具有前景且具吸引力的战略交易，包括来自其他潜在收购方的竞争、我们所在行业的整合效应，以及收购候选对象可能较高的估值。即使我们识别出战略交易或就此类交易订立协议，适用的反垄断法及其他法规可能限制我们收购目标的能力，或迫使我们剥离全部或部分业务或已收购业务。如果我们无法识别合适的目标或完成收购，我们的增长前景可能受损，且我们可能无法实现足够的规模和技术优势以有效竞争。

paras.en: Acquisitions involve many risks, any of which could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations, including:
paras.zh: 收购涉及诸多风险，其中任何一项均可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响，包括：

paras.en: - intense competition for suitable acquisition targets, which could increase prices and adversely affect our ability to consummate deals on favorable or acceptable terms;
paras.zh: - 对合适收购目标的激烈竞争，这可能推高价格并对我们以有利或可接受条款完成交易的能力产生不利影响；

paras.en: - failure or material delay in closing a transaction;
paras.zh: - 交易未能完成或出现重大延迟；

paras.en: - transaction-related lawsuits or claims;
paras.zh: - 与交易相关的诉讼或索赔；

paras.en: - difficulties in integrating the technologies, operations, existing contracts, and personnel of an acquired company;
paras.zh: - 整合被收购公司的技术、运营、现有合同和人员方面存在困难；

paras.en: - difficulties in retaining key employees, business partners, or customers of an acquired company;
paras.zh: - 留住被收购公司的关键员工、业务合作伙伴或客户方面存在困难；

paras.en: - challenges with integrating the brand identity of an acquired company with our own;
paras.zh: - 将被收购公司的品牌形象与我们自身品牌进行整合面临挑战；

paras.en: - diversion of financial and management resources from existing operations or alternative acquisition opportunities;
paras.zh: - 财务和管理资源从现有运营或替代收购机会中被分流；

paras.en: - failure to realize the anticipated benefits or synergies of a transaction at all or within the expected timeframe;
paras.zh: - 完全未能实现或未能在预期时间内实现交易的预期收益或协同效应；

paras.en: - the incurrence of debt or dilution related to equity issuances in connection with a transaction;
paras.zh: - 就交易产生债务或与股权发行相关的稀释；

paras.en: - failure to identify or address the problems, liabilities, or other shortcomings or challenges of an acquired company or technology, including issues related to copyrights and other intellectual property, regulatory compliance practices, litigation, revenue recognition, or other accounting practices, or employee or user issues;
paras.zh: - 未能识别或解决被收购公司或技术存在的问题、负债或其他缺陷或挑战，包括与版权及其他知识产权、监管合规实践、诉讼、收入确认或其他会计实践、或员工或用户问题相关的事项；

paras.en: - risks that the acquired company could have a negative impact on our company culture;
paras.zh: - 被收购公司可能对我们的公司文化产生负面影响的风险；

paras.en: - risks that regulatory bodies may enact new laws or promulgate new regulations that are adverse to an acquired company or business;
paras.zh: - 监管机构可能制定新法律或颁布新法规，对被收购公司或业务不利的风险；

paras.en: - risks that regulatory bodies do not approve our acquisitions or business combinations or delay such approvals;
paras.zh: - 监管机构不批准我们的收购或业务合并，或延迟此类批准的风险；

paras.en: - theft of our trade secrets or confidential information that we share with potential acquisition candidates;
paras.zh: - 我们与潜在收购候选方共享的商业秘密或机密信息被盗取；

paras.en: - risk that an acquired company or investment in new services cannibalizes a portion of our existing business; and
paras.zh: - 被收购公司或对新服务的投资蚕食我们现有业务一部分的风险；以及

paras.en: - adverse market reaction to an acquisition.
paras.zh: - 市场对收购的负面反应。

paras.en: If we fail to address the foregoing risks or other problems encountered in connection with past or future acquisitions of businesses, new technologies, services, and other assets, strategic investments, and other strategic transactions, or if we otherwise fail to realize the expected benefits of such acquisitions or investments, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 如果我们未能解决上述风险，或在与过去或未来的业务、新技术、服务及其他资产收购、战略投资及其他战略交易相关中遇到的其他问题，或如果我们未能实现此类收购或投资的预期收益，我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果可能会受到不利影响。

paras.en: **Unfavorable media coverage regarding our business, our models, platform, and applications, the impacts of AI, and the AI industry more broadly could adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **关于我们的业务、我们的模型、平台和应用、AI 的影响以及更广泛的 AI 行业的不利媒体报道可能会对我们的业务、财务状况和经营成果产生不利影响。**

paras.en: As our business has grown and as interest in us and the AI industry overall has increased, we have attracted, and may continue to attract, significant media coverage, public commentary, and scrutiny from time to time. This coverage and commentary have included, and we expect will continue to include, recurring narratives concerning the potential adverse societal impacts of AI, including that AI may displace or eliminate jobs, may be misused or otherwise cause harm, and may pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity. We have been, and may continue to be, a particular focus of such narratives, and unfavorable coverage of the AI industry generally may be attributed to us, in each case regardless of whether the underlying concerns are well-founded or specifically applicable to our models, platform, or applications. Unfavorable publicity regarding us, our partners, or the AI industry more broadly could adversely affect our reputation and brand, as described in the section titled “—If we are unable to maintain and enhance our brand and reputation, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected.” Negative media coverage, including public figures making negative or threatening statements about our company, whether accurate or not, could also adversely affect our brand and reputation and may reduce market acceptance of our models, platform, and applications or impair our ability to attract and retain customers. As public awareness of our brand increases, any issues that draw media attention may have an amplified adverse effect on our reputation. If unfavorable media coverage or adverse public perceptions persist or intensify, the demand for our models, platform, and applications could decline and our brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.
paras.zh: 随着我们业务的增长，以及外界对我们和整个 AI 行业的关注度上升，我们不时吸引并可能继续吸引大量媒体报道、公众评论和审视。这些报道和评论已经包含、且我们预计将继续包含关于 AI 潜在负面社会影响的反复出现的叙事，包括 AI 可能取代或消除工作岗位、可能被滥用或以其他方式造成损害，以及可能对人类构成灾难性或生存性风险。我们一直是、且可能继续是此类叙事的特别关注对象，而对 AI 行业整体的不利报道可能会被归因于我们，在每种情况下无论相关担忧是否有充分依据或是否具体适用于我们的模型、平台或应用。有关我们、我们的合作伙伴或更广泛 AI 行业的不利宣传可能对我们的声誉和品牌造成不利影响，详见标题为“——如果我们无法维护和提升我们的品牌和声誉，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响”的章节。负面媒体报道，包括公众人物对我们公司发表负面或威胁性言论，无论是否准确，也可能对我们的品牌和声誉造成不利影响，并可能降低市场对我们模型、平台和应用的接受度，或损害我们吸引和留住客户的能力。随着我们品牌公众知名度的提高，任何引起媒体关注的问题都可能对我们的声誉产生放大的不利影响。如果不利媒体报道或负面公众看法持续存在或加剧，对我们模型、平台和应用的需求可能下降，我们的品牌、业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响。

paras.en: **We will incur increased costs and demands upon management as a result of complying with the laws and regulations affecting public companies, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.**
paras.zh: **由于遵守适用于上市公司的法律法规，我们将产生增加的成本并对管理层提出更高的要求，这可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩造成不利影响。**

paras.en: As a public company, we will incur greater legal, accounting, and other expenses than we incurred as a private company. For example, we are subject to the reporting requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (“Exchange Act”), the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002 (“Sarbanes-Oxley Act”), the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, the rules and regulations of the SEC, and the listing standards of the Nasdaq Global Select Market. The Exchange Act requires, among other things, that we file annual, quarterly, and current reports with respect to our business and results of operations. Compliance with these requirements will increase our legal, accounting, and financial compliance costs, and increase demand on our systems, making some activities more time-consuming and costly. In addition, changing laws, regulations, and standards relating to reporting obligations and corporate governance disclosure are creating uncertainty for public companies, which could result in continued uncertainty regarding compliance matters and higher costs. We expect these rules and regulations to make it more expensive for us to obtain director and officer liability insurance, and we may be required to accept reduced policy limits and coverage or incur substantially higher costs to maintain the same or similar coverage. As a result, it may be more difficult for us to attract and retain qualified individuals to serve on our board of directors or as our executive officers.
paras.zh: 作为一家上市公司，我们将产生比作为私营公司时更高的法律、会计及其他费用。例如，我们须遵守经修订的 1934 年《证券交易法》（“《交易法》”）、2002 年《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》（“《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》”）、多德-弗兰克华尔街改革与消费者保护法案、SEC 的规则与规定以及纳斯达克全球精选市场的上市标准。除其他事项外，《交易法》要求我们就业务和经营业绩提交年度、季度和当期报告。遵守这些要求将增加我们的法律、会计和财务合规成本，并增加对我们系统的需求，使某些活动更加耗时和昂贵。此外，与报告义务和公司治理披露相关的法律、法规和标准不断变化，正给上市公司带来不确定性，这可能导致合规事项持续存在不确定性并带来更高成本。我们预计这些规则和规定将使我们获取董事和高级管理人员责任保险的成本更高，我们可能被迫接受较低的保单限额和承保范围，或承担大幅更高的成本以维持相同或类似的承保范围。因此，我们可能更难吸引和留住合格人士担任我们的董事会成员或高级管理人员。

paras.en: As a public company, we expect to incur significant expenses and devote substantial management effort toward ensuring compliance with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. In that regard, we will need to hire additional accounting and financial staff with appropriate public company experience and technical accounting knowledge. In addition, as a public company, we may be subject to stockholder activism, which can lead to substantial costs, distract management, and impact the manner in which we operate our business in ways we cannot currently anticipate.
paras.zh: 作为一家上市公司，我们预计将产生重大费用并投入大量管理精力，以确保遵守《萨班斯-奥克斯利法案》第 404 条的审计师鉴证要求。在这方面，我们将需要聘用具备适当上市公司经验和技术会计知识的额外会计和财务人员。此外，作为一家上市公司，我们可能面临股东积极主义，这可能导致重大成本、分散管理层注意力，并以我们目前无法预见的方式影响我们的业务经营方式。

paras.en: As a result of disclosure of information in this prospectus and in our public filings with the SEC as required of a public company, our business and financial condition will become more visible, which we believe may result in threatened or actual litigation, including by competitors and other third parties. If such claims are successful, our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected, and even if the claims do not result in litigation or are resolved in our favor, these claims, and the time and resources necessary to resolve them, may divert the resources of our management and our board of directors, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 由于本招股说明书以及我们作为上市公司按要求向 SEC 提交的公开文件披露了相关信息，我们的业务和财务状况将变得更加透明，我们认为这可能导致威胁或实际诉讼，包括来自竞争对手和其他第三方的诉讼。如果此类索赔获得成功，我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到不利影响；即使此类索赔未导致诉讼或以对我们有利的方式解决，这些索赔以及解决它们所需的时间和资源也可能分散我们管理层和董事会的资源，并对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: Further, many members of our management team have limited experience managing a publicly traded company, interacting with public company investors, and complying with the increasingly complex laws and regulations pertaining to public companies. Our management team may not successfully or efficiently manage our transition to being a public company subject to significant regulatory oversight and reporting obligations under the federal securities laws and the continuous scrutiny of securities analysts and investors. These new obligations and constituents will require significant attention from our management and may divert their attention away from the day-to-day management of our business, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations.
paras.zh: 此外，我们管理团队的许多成员在管理上市公司、与上市公司投资者互动以及遵守与上市公司相关的日益复杂的法律法规方面经验有限。我们的管理团队可能无法成功或高效地管理我们向上市公司的转型，而上市公司须遵守联邦证券法下重大的监管监督和报告义务，并持续受到证券分析师和投资者的审视。这些新的义务和利益相关方将需要我们的管理层投入大量精力，并可能分散其对日常业务管理的注意力，从而可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。

paras.en: **Our business, financial condition, and results of operations may be adversely affected by war, terrorism, natural disasters, public health crises, political crises, or other unexpected events.**
paras.zh: **我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩可能受到战争、恐怖主义、自然灾害、公共卫生危机、政治危机或其他意外事件的不利影响。**

paras.en: War, terrorist attacks, and other acts of political violence, or any significant natural disaster, such as an earthquake, fire, hurricane, tornado, flood, or significant power outage, may disrupt our operations, mobile networks, the internet, data centers, or the operations of our partners or third-party service providers, and the impact of climate change may increase these risks. In particular, our corporate headquarters are located in the San Francisco Bay Area, a region known for seismic activity and increasingly for the threat of fires. In addition, any public health crises, pandemics, political crises, terrorist attacks, war and other political or social instability, other geopolitical developments, or other catastrophic events, whether in the United States or in non-U.S. geographies, may adversely affect our operations or macroeconomic conditions. For example, an act of terrorism, armed conflict, or escalation of geopolitical tensions could result in physical damage to or destruction of data centers and other critical infrastructure, whether owned or operated by us or our third-party providers, as well as disruptions to power, cooling, or network connectivity necessary to operate such facilities. The impact of any of the foregoing or other disruption to us, our partners, or other third parties may result in system interruptions and degradation, reputational harm, delays in our product development, lengthy interruptions in our services, data breaches, malware, and other security or hacking incidents, all of which may adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. All of the aforementioned risks may be further increased if our disaster recovery plans prove to be inadequate. Further, the insurance we maintain may be insufficient to cover our losses resulting from such business interruptions, and any incidents may result in loss of, or increased costs of, such insurance [__] .
paras.zh: 战争、恐怖袭击及其他政治暴力行为，或任何重大自然灾害（如地震、火灾、飓风、龙卷风、洪水或重大停电），可能扰乱我们的运营、移动网络、互联网、数据中心，或我们的合作伙伴或第三方服务提供商的运营，而气候变化的影响可能加剧这些风险。特别是，我们的公司总部位于旧金山湾区，该地区以地震活动著称，且日益面临火灾威胁。此外，任何公共卫生危机、流行病、政治危机、恐怖袭击、战争及其他政治或社会动荡、其他地缘政治事态发展或其他灾难性事件，无论发生在美国还是美国以外地区，都可能对我们的运营或宏观经济状况产生不利影响。例如，恐怖主义行为、武装冲突或地缘政治紧张局势升级，可能导致数据中心及其他关键基础设施（无论由我们或我们的第三方提供商拥有或运营）遭受物理损坏或毁坏，并可能导致运营此类设施所需的电力、冷却或网络连接中断。上述任何情况或其他对我们、我们的合作伙伴或其他第三方造成的干扰，可能导致系统中断和性能下降、声誉受损、产品开发延迟、服务长时间中断、数据泄露、恶意软件及其他安全或黑客事件，所有这些都可能对我们的业务、财务状况和经营业绩产生不利影响。如果我们灾难恢复计划被证明不充分，上述所有风险可能进一步加剧。此外，我们维持的保险可能不足以覆盖此类业务中断造成的损失，任何事件都可能导致此类保险的丧失或成本增加 [__] 。
