paras.en: We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheet of Anthropic, PBC (the Company) as of December 31, 2025, the related consolidated statement of operations, comprehensive loss, redeemable convertible preferred stock and stockholders’ deficit and cash flows for the year then ended, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the “consolidated financial statements”). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company at December 31, 2025, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for the year then ended, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.
paras.zh: 我们已审计了随附的 Anthropic, PBC（以下简称“公司”）截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的合并资产负债表，以及截至该日止年度的相关合并经营报表、综合亏损表、可赎回可转换优先股及股东权益赤字表和现金流量表，以及相关附注（统称为“合并财务报表”）。我们认为，合并财务报表在所有重大方面公允反映了公司于 2025 年 12 月 31 日的财务状况以及截至该日止年度的经营成果和现金流量，符合美国公认会计原则。

paras.en: These financial statements are the responsibility of the Company’s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s financial statements based on our audit. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (PCAOB) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.
paras.zh: 这些财务报表由公司管理层负责。我们的责任是在审计的基础上对公司财务报表发表意见。我们是一家在美国公众公司会计监督委员会（PCAOB）注册的会计师事务所，并须根据美国联邦证券法律以及美国证券交易委员会和 PCAOB 的适用规则和规定，对公司保持独立性。

paras.en: We conducted our audit in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audit, we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company’s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.
paras.zh: 我们按照 PCAOB 的标准开展审计。这些标准要求我们计划和执行审计，以就财务报表是否不存在因错误或舞弊导致的重大错报获取合理保证。公司无须对其财务报告内部控制进行审计，我们亦未受聘执行该等审计。作为审计的一部分，我们须了解财务报告内部控制，但并非为对公司财务报告内部控制的有效性发表意见。因此，我们不发表此类意见。

paras.en: Our audit included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audit also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.
paras.zh: 我们的审计包括执行程序以评估财务报表是否存在因错误或舞弊导致的重大错报风险，并执行应对该等风险的程序。此类程序包括在测试基础上检查有关财务报表中金额和披露的证据。我们的审计还包括评价管理层采用的会计原则和作出的重大估计，以及评价财务报表的整体列报。我们认为，我们的审计为我们的意见提供了合理基础。

paras.en: The critical audit matters communicated below are matters arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that were communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relate to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective or complex judgments. The communication of critical audit matters does not alter in any way our opinion on the consolidated financial statements, taken as a whole, and we are not, by communicating the critical audit matters below, providing separate opinions on the critical audit matters or on the accounts or disclosures to which they relate.
paras.zh: 下文所述关键审计事项系本期财务报表审计中产生、已向或需向审计委员会沟通的事项，且该等事项：(1)涉及对财务报表具有重大性的科目或披露；(2)涉及我们尤其具有挑战性、主观性或复杂性的判断。沟通关键审计事项并不以任何方式改变我们对合并财务报表整体的审计意见，且我们通过下文沟通关键审计事项，并非就关键审计事项或其所涉科目或披露提供单独意见。

paras.en: **Loss Contingencies**
paras.zh: **或有损失**

paras.en: Description of the Matter As further described in Note 13 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company is involved in various legal claims, proceedings and other regulatory and administrative proceedings, certain of which may include claims for substantial or indeterminate amounts of damages. The Company’s assessment of loss contingency matters requires significant judgment in determining both the likelihood and estimated amount of potential losses.
paras.zh: 事项描述 如合并财务报表附注 13 进一步所述，公司涉及多项法律索赔、诉讼程序及其他监管和行政程序，其中某些可能包含金额重大或不确定的损害赔偿请求。公司对或有损失事项的评估需要作出重大判断，以确定潜在损失的可能性和估计金额。

paras.en: Auditing the Company’s accounting for and disclosure of certain loss contingencies was especially challenging due to the significant judgment required to evaluate management’s assessments of the probability of loss and its estimate of the potential amounts or range of such losses.
paras.zh: 审计公司对某些或有损失的会计处理和披露尤其具有挑战性，因为评估管理层对损失可能性的判断及其对潜在损失金额或区间的估计需要作出重大判断。

paras.en: How We Addressed the Matter in Our Audit
paras.zh: 我们在审计中如何应对该事项

paras.en: We performed audit procedures that included, among others, obtaining an understanding of the identification and evaluation of loss contingencies, including the Company’s assessment of the likelihood that a loss will be incurred and its ability to reasonably estimate the loss or range of possible losses. We read the Company’s board minutes, requested and received legal counsel confirmation letters, met with legal counsel to discuss the nature of certain matters and obtained representations from management on these matters. We also evaluated the appropriateness of the related disclosures included in the consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 我们执行的审计程序包括（但不限于）：了解或有损失的识别和评估流程，包括公司对损失发生可能性的评估及其合理估计损失或可能损失区间的能力。我们阅读了公司董事会会议纪要，索取并收到了法律顾问确认函，与法律顾问会面讨论某些事项的性质，并取得了管理层就上述事项的陈述。我们还评估了合并财务报表中相关披露的适当性。

paras.en: **Fair Value of Convertible Notes**
paras.zh: **可转换票据的公允价值**

paras.en: Description of the Matter
paras.zh: 事项描述

paras.en: The Company accounts for its convertible promissory notes at fair value. As discussed in Note 4 to the consolidated financial statements, the estimated fair value of convertible promissory notes as of December 31, 2025, was $41.7 billion and the recognized loss for the change in the fair value of the convertible promissory notes for the year ended December 31, 2025, was $34.5 billion. The Company estimated the fair value of the convertible promissory notes using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis method and a common stock equivalent method which involved the use of complex and subjective estimates, judgments and assumptions.
paras.zh: 公司按公允价值计量其可转换本票。如合并财务报表附注 4 所述，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，可转换本票的估计公允价值为 $41.7 billion，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度确认的可转换本票公允价值变动损失为 $34.5 billion。公司采用混合方法估计可转换本票的公允价值，该方法由或有索取权分析法和普通股等价物法组成，涉及使用复杂且主观的估计、判断和假设。

paras.en: Auditing the Company’s estimated fair value of convertible notes was especially challenging due to the significant judgment required to assess management’s selection of the valuation methodology, determination of the relative weight applied to the contingent claims analysis and the common stock equivalent methods, which involved key judgments and assumptions, including the Company’s stage of development, likelihood of an initial public offering (IPO), need for and terms of financings, and secondary and other market transactions. The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is particularly sensitive to changes in the relative weight applied to the two valuation methods.
paras.zh: 审计公司对可转换本票估计公允价值的判断尤其具有挑战性，因为评估管理层对估值方法的选择、确定应用于或有索偿权分析和普通股等价物方法的相对权重，需要作出重大判断，其中涉及关键判断和假设，包括公司的发展阶段、首次公开发行（IPO）的可能性、融资需求及条款，以及二级市场和其他市场交易。可转换本票的估计公允价值对两种估值方法所应用相对权重的变化尤为敏感。

paras.en: How We Addressed the Matter in Our Audit
paras.zh: 我们在审计中如何处理该事项

paras.en: We performed audit procedures that included, among others, evaluating the Company’s selection of the valuation methodology, evaluating the key judgments and assumptions noted above used by the Company’s valuation specialist, and evaluating the completeness and accuracy of the underlying data supporting the key judgments and assumptions. We involved our valuation specialists to assist with our evaluation of the methodology used by the Company and the key judgments and assumptions. Specifically, we focused on the Company’s determination of the relative weight applied to the contingent claims analysis and common stock equivalent methods and the key judgments and assumptions that affected the weighting. For example, we evaluated the stage of the Company’s development, inspected the Company’s written plans and internal presentations relating to an IPO process, and evaluated secondary and other market transactions during the period and their impact on the relative weight applied to the two valuation methods by the Company.
paras.zh: 我们执行的审计程序包括但不限于：评估公司对估值方法的选择，评估公司估值专家所使用的上述关键判断和假设，以及评估支持关键判断和假设的基础数据的完整性和准确性。我们引入了本所的估值专家，协助评估公司所使用的方法及关键判断和假设。具体而言，我们重点关注公司对或有索偿权分析和普通股等价物方法所应用相对权重的确定，以及影响该权重的关键判断和假设。例如，我们评估了公司的发展阶段，查阅了公司与 IPO 流程相关的书面计划和内部演示材料，并评估了该期间的二级市场和其他市场交易及其对公司所应用两种估值方法相对权重的影响。

paras.en: We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheet of Anthropic, PBC (a Delaware public benefit corporation) and subsidiaries (the “Company”) as of December 31, 2024, the related consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, redeemable convertible preferred stock and stockholders’ deficit, and cash flows for each of the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the “consolidated financial statements”). In our opinion, the consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.
paras.zh: 我们已审计了随附的 Anthropic, PBC（一家特拉华州公益公司）及其子公司（以下简称“公司”）截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日的合并资产负债表，以及截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2023 年 12 月 31 日止各年度的相关合并经营报表、综合亏损表、可赎回可转换优先股及股东权益赤字表和现金流量表，以及相关附注（统称“合并财务报表”）。我们认为，合并财务报表在所有重大方面公允反映了公司截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日的财务状况，以及截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2023 年 12 月 31 日止各年度的经营成果和现金流量，符合美国公认会计原则。

paras.en: #### Basis for opinion
paras.zh: #### 意见基础

paras.en: These consolidated financial statements are the responsibility of the Company’s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company’s consolidated financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (“PCAOB”) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.
paras.zh: 这些合并财务报表由公司管理层负责。我们的责任是在审计的基础上对公司的合并财务报表发表意见。我们是一家在美国公众公司会计监督委员会（“PCAOB”）注册的公共会计师事务所，并须根据美国联邦证券法以及美国证券交易委员会和 PCAOB 的适用规则和规定，对公司保持独立。

paras.en: We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company’s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.
paras.zh: 我们按照 PCAOB 的标准执行了审计。这些标准要求我们计划和执行审计，以就财务报表是否不存在因错误或舞弊导致的重大错报获取合理保证。公司无需对其财务报告内部控制进行审计，我们亦未受聘执行该审计。作为审计的一部分，我们须了解财务报告内部控制，但并非为了对公司财务报告内部控制的有效性发表意见。因此，我们不对其发表此类意见。

paras.en: Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.
paras.zh: 我们的审计包括执行程序以评估财务报表是否存在因错误或舞弊导致的重大错报风险，并执行应对该等风险的程序。此类程序包括在测试基础上检查有关财务报表中金额和披露的证据。我们的审计还包括评价管理层采用的会计原则和作出的重大估计，以及评价财务报表的整体列报。我们认为，我们的审计为我们的意见提供了合理基础。

full.sec: 1. Description of Business and Summary of Significant Accounting Policies
full.secZh: 1. 业务描述与重要会计政策摘要

paras.en: Anthropic, PBC (the “Company”) is a public benefit corporation (“PBC”) incorporated under Delaware law in January 2021. The Company develops and maintains advanced artificial intelligence (“AI”) models and provides its intelligence service through its platform and applications to customers. The Company’s public benefit purpose is to responsibly develop and maintain advanced AI for the long-term benefit of humanity. The Company is headquartered in San Francisco, California.
paras.zh: Anthropic, PBC（以下简称“公司”）是一家公益公司（PBC），于 2021 年 1 月依据特拉华州法律注册成立。公司开发并维护先进的人工智能（AI）模型，并通过其平台和应用程序向客户提供智能服务。公司的公益宗旨是负责任地开发并维护先进 AI，以造福人类的长期利益。公司总部位于加利福尼亚州旧金山。

paras.en: #### Basis of Presentation
paras.zh: #### 列报基础

paras.en: The accompanying consolidated financial statements have been prepared in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (“GAAP”). The Company consolidates its wholly owned subsidiaries over which it exercises control, as well as variable interest entities (“VIEs”) where the Company is deemed to be the primary beneficiary. All intercompany balances and transactions between consolidated entities have been eliminated in consolidation.
paras.zh: 随附的合并财务报表系按照美国公认会计原则（“GAAP”）编制。公司合并其控制的全资子公司，以及公司被视为主要受益人的可变利益实体（“VIE”）。合并实体之间的所有公司间余额和交易均已在合并中抵销。

paras.en: #### Change in Presentation and Reclassification of Prior Periods
paras.zh: #### 列报方式变更及以前期间重分类

paras.en: Certain amounts reported in the Company’s prior period consolidated financial statements have been reclassified to conform to the current period presentation. During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company changed its presentation of operating expenses from a functional classification under which cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative were presented as separate line items, to a classification based on the nature of expenses. As a result of this change in presentation, cost of revenue, gross profit (loss), research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative are no longer presented as separate line items in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 公司以前期间合并财务报表中列报的某些金额已进行重分类，以符合本期列报方式。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度内，公司将经营费用的列报方式从按功能分类(即将收入成本、毛利（亏损）、研发、销售和营销以及一般及行政费用作为单独项目列报)变更为按费用性质分类。由于此项列报方式变更，收入成本、毛利（亏损）、研发、销售和营销以及一般及行政费用不再在合并经营报表中作为单独项目列报。

paras.en: Under the new presentation, expenses are presented by major categories, including compute and infrastructure; personnel; sales, marketing, and partnerships; Bartz settlement; and other operating and administrative. In addition, the Company combined certain captions on its consolidated balance sheets and consolidated statements of cash flows. These reclassifications and certain other prior period amounts have been recast for all prior periods presented to conform to the current period presentation. These reclassifications affect presentation only and did not impact total assets, total liabilities, total stockholders’ equity (deficit), total operating loss, net loss, or net cash provided by (used in) operating, investing, or financing activities.
paras.zh: 在新的列报方式下，费用按主要类别列报，包括算力和基础设施；人员；销售、营销和合作伙伴关系；Bartz 和解；以及其他经营和行政费用。此外，公司合并了合并资产负债表和合并现金流量表上的某些项目。这些重分类以及某些其他以前期间金额已对所有列报的前期进行了追溯调整，以符合本期列报方式。这些重分类仅影响列报方式，并未影响总资产、总负债、股东权益（赤字）总额、经营亏损总额、净亏损，或经营活动、投资活动或融资活动提供（使用）的现金净额。

paras.en: #### Unaudited Interim Consolidated Financial Information
paras.zh: #### 未经审计的中期合并财务信息

paras.en: The accompanying interim consolidated balance sheet as of June 30, 2026 and the interim consolidated statements of operations, comprehensive loss, redeemable convertible preferred stock and stockholders’ deficit, and cash flows for the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 and the related notes to such interim consolidated financial statements are unaudited. These unaudited interim consolidated financial statements are presented in accordance with the rules and regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and do not include all disclosures normally required in annual consolidated financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP. In management’s opinion, the unaudited interim consolidated financial statements have been prepared on the same basis as the annual consolidated financial statements and reflect all normal and recurring adjustments necessary for the fair statement of the Company’s financial position as of June 30, 2026 and the Company’s consolidated results of operations and cash flows for the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026. The results of operations for the six months ended June 30, 2026 are not necessarily indicative of the results to be expected for the full year or any other future interim or annual period.
paras.zh: 随附的截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日的中期合并资产负债表，以及截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月的中期合并经营报表、综合亏损表、可赎回可转换优先股及股东权益赤字表和现金流量表，以及该等中期合并财务报表的相关附注，均未经审计。该等未经审计的中期合并财务报表系按照美国证券交易委员会的规则和规定编制，并未包含按照 GAAP 编制的年度合并财务报表通常要求的所有披露。管理层认为，该等未经审计的中期合并财务报表与年度合并财务报表采用相同基础编制，并反映了为公允列报公司截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日的财务状况以及公司截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月的合并经营成果和现金流量所必需的所有正常且经常性的调整。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月的经营成果不一定预示全年或任何其他未来中期或年度期间的预期业绩。

paras.en: #### Stock Split
paras.zh: #### 股票拆分

paras.en: On September 17, 2026, the Company effected a 10-for-1 stock split of its authorized, issued, and outstanding shares of Class A common stock and Class N common stock. The conversion rate of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock was proportionately adjusted to factor in the stock split. On the same date, the Company also effected a 1-for-1,000 reverse stock split of its authorized and issued shares of Class T common stock. All share and per share information has been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split and reverse stock split for all periods presented.
paras.zh: 2026 年 9 月 17 日，公司对其已授权、已发行和流通在外的 A 类普通股和 N 类普通股实施了 10 比 1 的股票拆分。公司可赎回可转换优先股的转换比例已按比例调整，以反映该股票拆分。同日，公司还对其已授权和已发行的 T 类普通股实施了 1 比 1,000 的反向股票拆分。所有股份及每股信息均已追溯调整，以反映所列报各期间的股票拆分和反向股票拆分。

paras.en: #### Use of Estimates
paras.zh: #### 估计的使用

paras.en: The preparation of consolidated financial statements in conformity with GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities, revenues and expenses, and related disclosures of contingent assets and liabilities in the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. Actual results could differ materially from those estimates. Significant items subject to such estimates and assumptions include the determination of the fair value of common stock, valuation of deferred tax assets and the related valuation allowance, the potential outcome of uncertain tax positions that have been recognized in the consolidated financial statements or tax returns, valuation of the simple agreements for future equity (“SAFEs”), valuation of convertible notes, valuation of goodwill, stock-based compensation, the assessment of useful lives of long-lived assets and intangible assets, contingencies, the valuation of financial instruments, and incremental borrowing rates for operating and finance leases.
paras.zh: 按照 GAAP 编制合并财务报表要求管理层作出估计和假设，这些估计和假设会影响合并财务报表及随附附注中资产和负债、收入和费用的报告金额，以及或有资产和负债的相关披露。实际结果可能与这些估计存在重大差异。受此类估计和假设影响的重要项目包括：普通股公允价值的确定、递延所得税资产及相关估值备抵的估值、已在合并财务报表或纳税申报表中确认的不确定税务状况的潜在结果、未来股权简单协议（SAFE）的估值、可转换本票的估值、商誉的估值、股权激励费用、长期资产和无形资产使用寿命的评估、或有事项、金融工具的估值，以及经营租赁和融资租赁的增量借款利率。

paras.en: #### Concentrations of Risk
paras.zh: #### 风险集中

paras.en: Concentration of Credit Risk
paras.zh: 信用风险集中

paras.en: Financial instruments that potentially subject the Company to concentrations of credit risk consist principally of cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, accounts receivable, and short-term investments. The Company maintains cash with financial institutions of high credit quality and has not experienced any losses on such accounts and does not believe it is exposed to any unusual credit risk beyond the normal credit risk associated with commercial banking relationships. Deposits held with these financial institutions are in excess of the amount of Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insured limits provided on such deposits. The Company has not experienced any losses related to these concentrations during the periods presented. The Company’s short-term investments are primarily intended to facilitate liquidity and capital preservation and consist predominantly of highly liquid investment-grade fixed-income securities, diversified among industries and individual issuers. The Company’s investment policy is designed to limit exposure from any particular issuer or institution.
paras.zh: 可能使公司面临信用风险集中的金融工具主要包括现金及现金等价物、受限现金、应收账款和短期投资。公司将现金存放于高信用质量的金融机构，且未发生此类账户的任何损失，并且认为除商业银行关系固有的正常信用风险外，公司不存在任何异常信用风险敞口。存放于该等金融机构的存款金额超过联邦存款保险公司对该等存款提供的保险限额。在所呈报期间内，公司未发生与上述集中相关的任何损失。公司的短期投资主要用于促进流动性和资本保全，主要由高流动性投资级固定收益证券构成，并在行业和单个发行人之间进行分散。公司的投资政策旨在限制来自任何特定发行人或机构的敞口。

paras.en: Other Concentrations

paras.en: Prior to 2026, the Company obtained substantially all of its compute infrastructure from three cloud service providers (“CSPs”) [__] . [__] During the six months ended June [__] 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company obtained a substantial majority of its compute infrastructure from a limited number of CSPs and other suppliers under long-term hosting and lease agreements. This created dependencies and potential vulnerabilities, in that a disruption affecting these counterparties could have adversely affected the Company’s operations. While the Company is expanding its relationships with its existing CSPs, it is also expanding its compute capacity through commitments with additional CSPs and through compute procured from other sources, including leased infrastructure operated on its behalf [__] .
paras.zh: 在 2026 年之前，公司的算力基础设施绝大部分来自三家云服务商（CSP）[__]。[__] 在截至 2026 年 6 月 [__] 30 日止六个月（未经审计）内，公司根据长期托管和租赁协议，从数量有限的 CSP 及其他供应商处获得了其算力基础设施的绝大部分。这形成了依赖关系和潜在脆弱性，即影响这些交易对手的中断可能对公司的运营造成不利影响。公司在扩大与现有 CSP 关系的同时，也通过与其他 CSP 的承诺以及通过其他来源获取的算力（包括为其运营而租赁的基础设施）来扩大其算力容量[__]。

paras.en: The Company also provides access to its intelligence service through CSP marketplaces, with CSPs acting as collection agents for the Company in these transactions [__] . [__] During the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024, and 2025, revenue generated from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented approximately [__] 11%, 32%, and 47% of total revenue, respectively. During the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), revenue generated from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented approximately [__] 44% and 48% of total revenue, respectively. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), net accounts receivable from sales through CSP marketplaces to customers represented [__] 42%, 60%, and [__] 58% of the Company’s net accounts receivable, respectively.
paras.zh: 公司还通过 CSP 市场提供其智能服务的访问渠道，在这些交易中 CSP 作为公司的收款代理[__]。[__] 在截至 2023 年、2024 年和 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度内，通过 CSP 市场向客户销售产生的收入分别约占总收入的 [__] 11%、32% 和 47%。在截至 2025 年和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计）内，通过 CSP 市场向客户销售产生的收入分别约占总收入的 [__] 44% 和 48%。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2025 年 12 月 31 日以及 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），通过 CSP 市场向客户销售产生的应收账款净额分别占公司应收账款净额的 [__] 42%、60% 和 [__] 58%。

paras.en: Certain of the CSPs also hold the Company’s non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock and convertible notes. See Notes [__] 9 and 10 for further information.

paras.en: #### Cash and Cash Equivalents
paras.zh: #### 现金及现金等价物

paras.en: Cash and cash equivalents consist of cash held in checking and interest-bearing accounts as well as investments in money market funds and highly liquid investments with original maturities of three months or less from the date of purchase.
paras.zh: 现金及现金等价物包括存放于支票账户和计息账户的现金，以及对货币市场基金和自购买日起原始到期日为三个月或更短的高流动性投资。

paras.en: #### Restricted Cash
paras.zh: #### 受限现金

paras.en: The Company’s restricted cash is classified as noncurrent based on the contractual or estimated term of the remaining restriction and consists of amounts pledged as collateral for the Company’s lease and other contractual obligations. These amounts are restricted from general corporate use and will be released or applied against the related obligations as the underlying conditions are satisfied.
paras.zh: 公司的受限现金根据剩余限制的合同期限或估计期限分类为非流动，由作为公司租赁及其他合同义务担保而质押的金额构成。该等金额不得用于一般公司用途，并将在相关条件满足时解除限制或用于抵偿相关义务。

paras.en: #### Short-Term Investments
paras.zh: #### 短期投资

paras.en: The Company’s short-term investments primarily consist of debt securities, including: U.S. Treasury and agency securities, corporate debt securities, and commercial paper. The Company determines the appropriate classification of its short-term investments at the time of purchase and reevaluates such designation at each balance sheet date. The Company has classified and accounted for its short-term investments as available-for-sale securities as the Company may sell these securities at any time for use in its current operations or for other purposes, even prior to maturity. As a result, short-term investments, including securities with stated maturities beyond 12 months, are classified within current assets in the consolidated balance sheets.
paras.zh: 公司的短期投资主要由债务证券构成，包括：美国国债及机构证券、公司债务证券和商业票据。公司在购买时确定其短期投资的适当分类，并在每个资产负债表日重新评估该等指定。公司已将其短期投资分类为可供出售证券并进行相应会计处理，因为公司可随时出售该等证券用于其当前经营或其他目的，即使在到期之前亦可如此。因此，短期投资（包括标明到期日在 12 个月以上的证券）在合并资产负债表中归类为流动资产。

paras.en: Available-for-sale securities are recorded at fair value each reporting period and are periodically evaluated for impairment at the individual security level. For unrealized losses in securities that the Company intends to hold and will not-more-likely-than-not be required to sell before recovery, the Company further evaluates whether declines in fair value below amortized cost are due to credit or non-credit related factors.
paras.zh: 可供出售证券在每个报告期按公允价值记录，并按单项证券定期评估减值。对于公司拟持有且不太可能（not-more-likely-than-not）被要求在恢复前出售的证券的未实现损失，公司进一步评估公允价值低于摊余成本的下降是否由信用或非信用相关因素所致。

paras.en: The Company considers credit-related impairments to be changes in value that are driven by a change in the creditor’s ability to meet its payment obligations and records an allowance and recognizes a corresponding loss in other income (expense), net when the impairment is incurred. Unrealized non-credit related losses and unrealized gains are reported as a separate component of accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) in the consolidated balance sheets until realized. Realized gains and losses are determined based on the specific identification method and are reported in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 公司将信用相关减值视为由债权人履行其付款义务能力的变化所驱动的价值变动，并在减值发生时记录减值准备，同时在其他收入（费用）净额中确认相应损失。未实现的非信用相关损失和未实现收益在实现之前，作为累计其他综合收益（损失）的单独组成部分在合并资产负债表中列报。已实现收益和损失按个别认定法确定，并在合并经营报表的其他收入（费用）净额中列报。

paras.en: **Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)**
paras.zh: **Anthropic, PBC 合并财务报表附注（续）**

paras.en: #### Variable Interest Entities
paras.zh: #### 可变利益实体

paras.en: The Company evaluates its ownership, contractual, and other interests in entities to determine if it has a variable interest in an entity. These evaluations are complex, involve judgment, and use estimates and assumptions based on available historical and prospective information, among other factors. If the Company determines that an entity for which it holds a contractual or ownership interest is a VIE and that the Company is the primary beneficiary, the Company consolidates such entity in its consolidated financial statements. An enterprise having a controlling financial interest in a VIE must consolidate the VIE if it is considered the primary beneficiary, which is described as having both (1) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the VIE’s economic performance and (2) the right to receive benefits or the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE that potentially could be significant to the VIE. The Company consolidates certain VIEs formed to finance and deploy compute and infrastructure capacity. Refer to Note 7 for further information.
paras.zh: 公司评估其在各实体中的所有权、合同及其他权益，以确定其是否在某一实体中拥有可变利益。该等评估较为复杂，涉及判断，并使用基于可获得的历史和前瞻性信息等因素作出的估计和假设。如果公司确定其持有合同或所有权权益的某一实体为 VIE，且公司为该 VIE 的主要受益人，则公司将该实体纳入其合并财务报表。对 VIE 拥有控制性财务利益的企业，如果被视为主要受益人，则必须合并该 VIE；主要受益人是指同时具备以下两项条件者：(1) 有权主导对 VIE 经济表现影响最重大的 VIE 活动，以及(2) 有权获得可能对 VIE 而言属重大的 VIE 利益或承担 VIE 损失的义务。公司合并了若干为融资和部署算力及基础设施能力而设立的 VIE。更多信息请参见附注 7。

paras.en: Long-Term Benefit Trust
paras.zh: 长期利益信托

paras.en: In 2023, the Company established the Long-Term Benefit Trust (“LTBT”). The LTBT is intended to operate as an independent body of financially disinterested trustees with expertise in AI safety, national security, public policy, and social enterprise. In connection with establishing the LTBT, the Company created a class of common stock (the “Class T common stock”) that is held exclusively by the LTBT and gives the LTBT authority to elect and remove certain of the Company’s directors.
paras.zh: 2023 年，公司设立了长期利益信托（"LTBT"）。LTBT 旨在作为一个独立的、在财务上无利害关系的受托人机构运作，其受托人具备 AI 安全、国家安全、公共政策和社会企业方面的专业知识。在设立 LTBT 的过程中，公司创设了一个普通股类别（“T 类普通股”），该类别普通股仅由 LTBT 持有，并赋予 LTBT 选举和罢免公司若干董事的权力。

paras.en: The LTBT is considered a consolidated VIE as it relies on the Company for financial support. The Company is the primary beneficiary of the VIE as it has the power to direct the activities that most significantly impact the LTBT’s economic performance, provides financial support to the LTBT, and would receive the LTBT’s financial assets (other than the Class T common stock) in the event that the LTBT terminates. The Company consolidated the VIE at inception and will perform on-going reassessments of the VIE based on any reconsideration events to reevaluate whether a change to the consolidation conclusion is required each reporting period. The consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2024 and [__] 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited) include assets of the LTBT, which can only be used to settle obligations and liabilities of the LTBT. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), total assets and liabilities of the LTBT were not material [__] .
paras.zh: LTBT 被视为合并 VIE，因为其依赖公司提供财务支持。公司是该 VIE 的主要受益人，因为公司有权主导对 LTBT 经济表现影响最显著的活动，向 LTBT 提供财务支持，并且在 LTBT 终止的情况下将获得 LTBT 的金融资产（T 类普通股除外）。公司在设立时即合并该 VIE，并将基于任何重新考虑事项对 VIE 进行持续重新评估，以在每个报告期重新评估是否需要改变合并结论。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2025 年 [__] 以及 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）的合并资产负债表包含 LTBT 的资产，该等资产仅可用于清偿 LTBT 的义务和负债。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2025 年以及 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）,LTBT 的总资产和负债并不重大 [__] 。

paras.en: #### Fair Value Measurements and Financial Instruments
paras.zh: #### 公允价值计量与金融工具

paras.en: Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date. In accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 820, Fair Value Measurement (“ASC 820”), the Company uses the fair value hierarchy, which prioritizes the inputs used to measure fair value. The hierarchy, as defined below, gives the highest priority to unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities and the lowest priority to unobservable inputs. The three levels of the fair value hierarchy are set forth below:
paras.zh: 公允价值定义为在计量日市场参与者之间进行的有序交易中，出售资产所收取或转移负债所支付的价格。根据会计准则汇编（"ASC"）第 820 号《公允价值计量》（"ASC 820"），公司使用公允价值层级，该层级对用于计量公允价值的输入值进行优先排序。如下文所定义，该层级将相同资产或负债在活跃市场中的未经调整报价价格赋予最高优先级，将不可观察输入值赋予最低优先级。公允价值层级的三个层次如下所述：

paras.en: Level 1: Observable inputs such as quoted prices in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.
paras.zh: 第 1 层：可观察输入值，例如相同资产或负债在活跃市场中的报价价格。

paras.en: Level 2: Observable inputs other than Level 1 prices such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets, quoted prices in markets that are not active or inputs other than the quoted prices that are observable either directly or indirectly for the full term of the assets or liabilities.
paras.zh: 第 2 层：第 1 层价格以外的可观察输入值，例如类似资产或负债在活跃市场中的报价价格、在非活跃市场中的报价价格，或在资产或负债整个存续期内可直接或间接观察到的报价价格以外的输入值。

paras.en: Level 3: Unobservable inputs in which there is little or no market data and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.
paras.zh: 第 3 层：市场数据很少或没有市场数据、且对资产或负债公允价值具有重要意义的不可观察输入值。

paras.en: The Company’s financial instruments include accounts receivable, short-term investments, prepaid expenses and other current assets, other assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities, convertible notes payable, SAFE liabilities, and certain derivative contracts. The estimated fair value of other financial instruments, including cash and restricted cash, are stated at their carrying value which approximates fair value due to the short time to the expected receipt or payment date. Additionally, the carrying amounts of accounts receivable, prepaid expenses and other current assets, accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities approximate fair value due to their short-term nature.
paras.zh: 公司的金融工具包括应收账款、短期投资、预付费用及其他流动资产、其他资产、应付账款、应计费用及其他流动负债、应付可转换票据、SAFE 负债以及某些衍生品合约。其他金融工具（包括现金及受限现金）的估计公允价值按账面价值列示，由于预计收款或付款日期较短，账面价值近似于公允价值。此外，应收账款、预付费用及其他流动资产、应付账款、应计费用及其他流动负债的账面金额因其短期性质而近似于公允价值。

paras.en: #### Accounts Receivable and Allowances
paras.zh: #### 应收账款与坏账准备

paras.en: Accounts receivable represent uncollected payments from customers and payments collected by channel partners from customers on the Company’s behalf which have not yet been remitted to the Company. Accounts receivable are recorded at the invoiced amount net of the allowance for credit losses and do not bear interest. The Company’s accounts receivable balances as of December 31, 2023, [__] 2024, and 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited) were $10 million, $95 million, $909 million, and $5.8 billion, respectively.
paras.zh: 应收账款指尚未向客户收取的款项，以及渠道合作伙伴代公司向客户收取但尚未汇付给公司的款项。应收账款按扣除信用损失准备后的开票金额入账，且不计息。公司截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日、[__] 2024 年及 2025 年 12 月 31 日以及 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）的应收账款余额分别为 $10 million、$95 million、$909 million 和 $5.8 billion。

paras.en: The Company regularly monitors collections and payments from customers and maintains an allowance for credit losses for estimated losses resulting from the inability of customers or channel partners to make or remit required payments. Management estimates the Company’s allowance for credit losses by considering factors such as historical credit loss experience and current conditions, the length of time accounts receivable are past due, customer payment histories, any specific customer collection issues identified, and current market conditions which may affect customer financial condition. This assessment is performed on an aggregate basis when similar characteristics exist within a customer group and on an individual basis when specific customers with collectability risks are identified. The Company writes off accounts receivable against the allowance when management determines a balance is uncollectible and no longer actively pursues collection of the receivable.
paras.zh: 公司定期监控客户回款及付款情况，并针对客户或渠道合作伙伴无法支付或汇付应付款项所导致的估计损失计提信用损失准备。管理层在估计公司信用损失准备时，会考虑历史信用损失经验和当前状况、应收账款逾期时长、客户付款历史、已识别的任何特定客户收款问题，以及可能影响客户财务状况的当前市场状况等因素。当客户群体内存在相似特征时，该评估以汇总基础进行；当识别出存在可收回性风险的特定客户时，则以个别基础进行。当管理层确定某笔余额无法收回且不再积极追收该应收账款时，公司将该应收账款与准备进行核销。

#### Property and Equipment, Net
paras.zh: #### 物业及设备净额

paras.en: Property and equipment is stated at cost less accumulated depreciation. Depreciation is recorded using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the related asset, ranging from three to five years [__] . Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of estimated useful life or the remaining lease term [__] .
paras.zh: 物业及设备按成本减累计折旧列示。折旧采用直线法在相关资产的估计可使用年限内计提，估计可使用年限为三至五年 [__] 。租赁改良按估计可使用年限或剩余租赁期孰短进行摊销 [__] 。

paras.en: The Company estimates the useful lives of property and equipment upon initial recognition and periodically evaluates the useful lives and whether events or changes in circumstances warrant a revision to the useful lives.
paras.zh: 公司在初始确认时估计不动产及设备的可使用年限，并定期评估可使用年限以及是否存在事件或情况变化表明需要修订可使用年限。

paras.en: Maintenance and repair costs that do not extend the useful life of the assets are expensed as incurred.
paras.zh: 不延长资产可使用年限的维护和修理费用在发生时计入费用。

paras.en: When assets are retired or otherwise disposed of, the cost and accumulated depreciation are removed from the accounts and any resulting gain or loss is reflected in the consolidated statements of operations in the period realized.
paras.zh: 当资产报废或以其他方式处置时，其成本及累计折旧从账目中转出，由此产生的任何利得或损失在实现当期计入合并经营报表。

paras.en: #### Software Development Costs
paras.zh: #### 软件开发成本

paras.en: Software development costs include costs to develop advanced AI models and related software solutions used to deliver the Company’s services to external users. Software development costs also include costs to develop software solely for internal use and applications used to support the Company’s operations. Model development costs are generally expensed as incurred due to the significant development uncertainty inherent in the development process.
paras.zh: 软件开发成本包括开发先进 AI 模型及相关软件解决方案的成本，该等软件解决方案用于向外部用户提供公司服务。软件开发成本还包括仅为内部使用而开发软件的成本以及用于支持公司运营的应用程序的成本。由于开发过程本身存在重大开发不确定性，模型开发成本一般在发生时计入费用。

paras.en: The Company capitalizes qualifying software development costs when (i) management, with relevant authority, has authorized and committed to fund the software project and (ii) it is probable that the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform its intended function. Capitalization ceases when the software is substantially complete and ready for its intended use, including the completion of all significant testing. Software development costs capitalized were not significant for the years presented.
paras.zh: 当(i)拥有相关权限的管理层已授权并承诺为软件项目提供资金，且(ii)项目很可能完成且软件将用于履行其预期功能时，公司将符合条件的软件开发成本予以资本化。当软件基本完成并可供其预期使用时（包括完成所有重大测试），资本化即停止。所列示年度内资本化的软件开发成本并不重大。

paras.en: #### Evaluation of Long-Lived Assets for Impairment
paras.zh: #### 长期资产减值评估

paras.en: Long-lived assets, such as property and equipment, right-of-use (“ROU”) assets, and finite-lived intangible assets subject to amortization, are reviewed for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset or asset group (collectively, the “asset group”) may not be recoverable. Recoverability of asset groups to be held and used is measured by comparing the carrying amount to the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to be generated. If the carrying amount exceeds the undiscounted cash flows, the asset groups are determined to be impaired, and an impairment charge is recognized as the amount by which the carrying amount exceeds its fair value.
paras.zh: 长期资产，如不动产及设备、使用权（“ROU”）资产以及需摊销的有限寿命无形资产，在发生事件或情况变化表明某项资产或资产组（统称“资产组”）的账面金额可能无法收回时，进行减值审查。拟持有并使用的资产组的可收回性，通过将账面金额与预期产生的估计未折现未来现金流量进行比较来衡量。如果账面金额超过未折现现金流量，则资产组被确定为已减值，并按账面金额超过其公允价值的部分确认减值费用。

paras.en: #### Intangible Assets, Net
paras.zh: #### 无形资产净额

paras.en: Intangible assets which are subject to amortization are amortized on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, which range from one to six years. The Company reviews intangible assets which are subject to amortization for impairment under the long-lived asset model.
paras.zh: 需摊销的无形资产在其估计可使用年限内按直线法摊销，可使用年限为一年至六年。公司根据长期资产模型对需摊销的无形资产进行减值审查。

paras.en: #### Goodwill

Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price in a business combination over the fair value of net tangible and intangible assets acquired. Goodwill is not subject to amortization but is tested for impairment on an annual basis, performed in the fourth quarter of each year, or whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of the reporting unit may be in excess of the reporting unit’s fair value.
paras.zh: 商誉是指企业合并中的购买价格超过所收购有形及无形资产公允价值的部分。商誉不进行摊销，但需每年进行减值测试，测试于每年第四季度进行，或在发生事件或情况变化表明报告单元账面价值可能超过其公允价值时进行。

paras.en: Goodwill is tested for impairment at the reporting unit level by first assessing the qualitative factors to determine whether it is more likely than not that the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. Qualitative indicators assessed include consideration of macroeconomic, industry, and market conditions, the Company’s overall financial performance, and personnel or strategy changes. Based on the qualitative assessment, if the Company determines that it is more likely than not that the Company’s single reporting unit’s fair value is less than its carrying amount, a quantitative analysis is performed by comparing the fair value of the Company’s single reporting unit to its carrying value. If the carrying amount of the reporting unit exceeds its fair value, an impairment loss is recognized in an amount equal to that excess, limited to the total amount of goodwill allocated to the reporting unit. The Company did not recognize any goodwill during the years ended December 31, 2023 and [__] 2024. No impairment losses related to goodwill were recognized during the year ended December 31, 2025 or the six months ended June 30, 2026 (unaudited).
paras.zh: 商誉在报告单元层面进行减值测试，首先评估定性因素，以确定公司单一报告单元的公允价值是否很可能低于其账面金额。所评估的定性指标包括对宏观经济、行业及市场状况、公司整体财务表现以及人员或战略变化的考量。基于定性评估，如果公司确定其单一报告单元的公允价值很可能低于其账面金额，则通过将公司单一报告单元的公允价值与其账面价值进行比较来进行定量分析。如果报告单元的账面金额超过其公允价值，则确认减值损失，金额等于该超出部分，但以分配至该报告单元的商誉总额为限。公司在截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日和 [__] 2024 年 12 月 31 日止年度内未确认任何商誉。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度或截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计）内，未确认与商誉相关的减值损失。

paras.en: #### Acquisitions

The Company accounts for acquisitions of entities or asset groups that qualify as businesses in accordance with ASC 805, Business Combinations (“ASC 805”). The purchase price of the acquisition is allocated to the tangible and intangible assets acquired and liabilities assumed based on their estimated fair values at the acquisition date. The excess of the purchase price over those fair values is recorded as goodwill. During the measurement period, which may be up to one year from the acquisition date, the Company may record adjustments to the assets acquired and liabilities assumed with the corresponding offset to goodwill. Upon the conclusion of the measurement period or final determination of the values of assets acquired or liabilities assumed, whichever comes first, any subsequent adjustments are recorded in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 公司按照 ASC 805《企业合并》（“ASC 805”）对符合企业定义的实体或资产组的收购进行会计处理。收购的购买价格根据收购日各项资产和承担负债的估计公允价值，分配至所收购的有形及无形资产和承担的负债。购买价格超过上述公允价值的部分记为商誉。在计量期内（可能长达自收购日起一年），公司可能对所收购资产和承担负债记录调整，并相应调整商誉。在计量期结束或对所收购资产或承担负债的价值作出最终确定之日（以较早者为准）之后，任何后续调整均计入合并经营报表。

paras.en: #### Leases

The Company determines if an arrangement is a lease at inception. The Company evaluates the classification of leases at commencement and, as necessary, at modification. The Company, as the lessee, classifies leases with lease terms longer than [__] 12 months as either operating or finance. A lease is classified as a finance lease if it meets any of the finance lease classification criteria in ASC 842 at lease commencement; all other leases are classified as operating leases. The Company’s finance leases are generally those leases that allow the Company to utilize the asset for a major part of its estimated economic life, that have discounted lease payments that are substantially all the estimated fair value of the asset, or that include a purchase option which the Company is reasonably certain to exercise.
paras.zh: 公司在租赁开始日判断一项安排是否为租赁。公司在租赁开始日评估租赁的分类，并在必要时于租赁修改时进行评估。公司作为承租人，将租赁期长于 [__] 12 个月的租赁分类为经营租赁或融资租赁。如果一项租赁在租赁开始日符合 ASC 842 中融资租赁分类标准中的任何一项，则分类为融资租赁；所有其他租赁均分类为经营租赁。公司的融资租赁通常是指那些允许公司在资产的估计经济寿命的主要部分内使用该资产的租赁、其折现后的租赁付款额实质上等于该资产估计公允价值的租赁，或包含公司合理确定将行使的购买选择权的租赁。

paras.en: The Company leases facilities and equipment under operating and finance leases. The Company determines whether an arrangement is or contains a lease at inception and records lease liabilities and right-of-use assets
paras.zh: 公司根据经营租赁和融资租赁租赁设施和设备。公司在租赁开始日判断一项安排是否为租赁或包含租赁，并在合并资产负债表上记录租赁负债和使用权资产

paras.en: on its consolidated balance sheets at lease commencement. Where the Company’s leases do not provide an implicit rate, the Company determines its incremental borrowing rate based on the information available at commencement date in determining the present value of lease payments. The determination of the incremental borrowing rate is based on an estimate of the Company’s unsecured borrowing rate, adjusted for tenor and collateralized security features. Lease liabilities are recognized at the present value of the future lease payments at the lease commencement date. ROU assets are measured based on the corresponding lease liability adjusted for (i) payments made to the lessor at or before the commencement date, (ii) initial direct costs incurred and (iii) tenant incentives received, incurred or payable under the lease. The Company does not assume renewals or early terminations of its leases unless it is reasonably certain to exercise these options at commencement.
paras.zh: 于租赁开始日。如果公司的租赁未提供隐含利率，公司在确定租赁付款额现值时，根据租赁开始日可获得的信息确定其增量借款利率。增量借款利率的确定基于对公司无担保借款利率的估计，并根据期限和抵押担保特征进行调整。租赁负债按租赁开始日未来租赁付款额的现值确认。使用权资产按相应的租赁负债计量，并调整 (i) 在租赁开始日或之前向出租人支付的款项、(ii) 发生的初始直接成本以及 (iii) 根据租赁收到、发生或应付的租户激励。除非公司在租赁开始日合理确定将行使续租或提前终止选择权，否则公司不假设租赁续租或提前终止。

paras.en: Operating lease cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term. Finance lease ROU assets are amortized on a straight-line basis over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the underlying asset or, where title does not transfer at the end of the lease term and the Company is not reasonably certain to exercise a purchase option, the lease term, and are recognized within operating expenses based on the nature of the leased asset. The interest component of a finance lease is recognized using the effective interest method over the lease term and is presented separately from the amortization of the related ROU asset.
paras.zh: 经营租赁成本在租赁期内按直线法确认。融资租赁使用权资产在相关资产估计使用寿命或租赁期（以较短者为准）内按直线法摊销；如果租赁期结束时所有权不转移且公司合理确定不会行使购买选择权，则按租赁期摊销，并根据租赁资产的性质在经营费用中确认。融资租赁的利息部分在租赁期内采用实际利率法确认，并与相关使用权资产的摊销分开列示。

paras.en: Operating lease ROU assets and operating lease liabilities are presented separately on the consolidated balance sheets. Finance lease ROU assets are included in property and equipment, net. Finance lease liabilities are included in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities, and in other noncurrent liabilities.
paras.zh: 经营租赁使用权资产和经营租赁负债在合并资产负债表上单独列示。融资租赁使用权资产计入物业和设备净额。融资租赁负债计入应付账款、应计费用和其他流动负债，以及其他非流动负债。

paras.en: The Company’s lease agreements may contain lease and non-lease components. Non-lease components related to the asset being leased are not separated from the lease components and are accounted for as a single lease component for all existing classes of assets.
paras.zh: 公司的租赁协议可能包含租赁组成部分和非租赁组成部分。与被租赁资产相关的非租赁组成部分不与租赁组成部分分离，对所有现有资产类别均作为单一租赁组成部分进行会计处理。

paras.en: The Company made an accounting policy election for lease agreements with a term of 12 months or less and does not recognize ROU assets and lease liabilities in respect of those agreements. Any payments related to short-term leases are expensed as incurred.
paras.zh: 公司对期限为 12 个月或更短的租赁协议作出了会计政策选择，不就该等协议确认使用权（ROU）资产和租赁负债。与短期租赁相关的任何付款均在发生时计入费用。

paras.en: Variable lease payments are expensed as incurred and are mainly composed of utilities, common area maintenance, and other operating expenses.
paras.zh: 可变租赁付款在发生时计入费用，主要由公用事业费、公共区域维护费及其他运营费用构成。

paras.en: Similar to other long-lived assets discussed above, management assesses ROU assets for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of such assets may not be recoverable. Finance lease ROU assets are assessed for impairment together with the Company’s other property and equipment. For leased assets, such circumstances would include the decision to enter into a sublease for which estimated cash flows do not fully cover the costs of the associated lease.
paras.zh: 与上文讨论的其他长期资产类似，当事件或情况变化表明此类资产的账面价值可能无法收回时，管理层会对 ROU 资产进行减值评估。融资租赁 ROU 资产与公司其他不动产和设备一并评估减值。对于租赁资产，此类情况将包括决定签订转租协议，而该协议的估计现金流量不能完全覆盖相关租赁的成本。

paras.en: #### Revenue Recognition
paras.zh: #### 收入确认

paras.en: The Company generates revenue from customers, including enterprises and prosumers, utilizing its intelligence service, which enables customers to submit text, documents, and other materials (“Prompts”), and receive AI-generated results (“Results”) from its proprietary Claude model family. Prompts and Results are measured in the number of tokens consumed. The Company provides the intelligence service through its web, mobile, and desktop interfaces and APIs as well as through CSP marketplaces that distribute the intelligence service to the Company’s customers. The intelligence service is not available for on-premise download or hosting by customers.
paras.zh: 公司通过其智能服务向客户（包括企业和专业消费者）产生收入，该服务使客户能够提交文本、文档和其他材料（“提示词”），并从公司专有的 Claude 模型系列获得 AI 生成的结果（“结果”）。提示词和结果以消耗的 token 数量计量。公司通过其网页、移动端和桌面端界面及 API，以及通过向公司客户分发该智能服务的 CSP 市场，提供该智能服务。该智能服务不可供客户进行本地下载或托管。

paras.en: The Company accounts for revenue under ASC 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Revenue is recognized based on the amount of consideration the Company expects to receive when the Company provides its intelligence service to customers. Revenue excludes amounts collected on behalf of third parties, such as sales and indirect taxes, as well as estimated concessions, credits, and refunds.
paras.zh: 公司根据 ASC 606《与客户之间的合同产生的收入》对收入进行会计处理。收入按公司预计在向客户提供智能服务时有权收取的对价金额确认。收入不包括代第三方收取的金额（如销售税和间接税），以及估计的折让、抵用金和退款。

paras.en: The Company’s intelligence service is provided on a consumption or subscription basis. Revenue is recognized when customers use the Company’s intelligence service, based on the quantity of tokens consumed. Intelligence service provided on a subscription basis is subject to usage limits that reset over short periods, which results in revenue being recognized ratably over the subscription period, which is generally 12 months or less. Payment terms vary by customer and sales channel but are generally less than 60 days. Subscription fees are generally prepaid. Certain enterprise contracts may include minimum spend commitments.
paras.zh: 公司的智能服务按消费或订阅方式提供。收入在客户使用公司智能服务时，根据消耗的 token 数量确认。按订阅方式提供的智能服务受使用限额约束，该限额在较短期间内重置，因此收入在订阅期内按比例确认，订阅期通常为 12 个月或更短。付款条款因客户和销售渠道而异，但通常少于 60 天。订阅费通常为预付。某些企业合同可能包含最低消费承诺。

paras.en: **Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)**
paras.zh: **Anthropic, PBC 合并财务报表附注（续）**

paras.en: When the Company utilizes CSP marketplaces that distribute the intelligence service to customers, the customer receives the same intelligence service as is available through its web, mobile, and desktop interfaces and APIs, and the intelligence service represents a single promise in customer contracts. In these arrangements, the Company is the principal and recognizes revenue on a gross basis because the Company has a direct contractual relationship with customers, is primarily responsible for providing the intelligence service to customers, and establishes pricing. The CSPs in these arrangements do not obtain control of the Company’s intelligence service at any point prior to transfer to the customer.
paras.zh: 当公司利用向客户分发智能服务的 CSP 市场时，客户获得的智能服务与通过其网页、移动端和桌面端界面及 API 提供的智能服务相同，且该智能服务在客户合同中构成单一履约义务。在此类安排中，公司为主要责任人，并按总额确认收入，因为公司与客户存在直接合同关系，主要负责向客户提供智能服务，并制定定价。此类安排中的 CSP 在向客户转让之前，任何时候均未取得公司智能服务的控制权。

paras.en: #### Deferred Revenue
paras.zh: #### 递延收入

paras.en: Deferred revenue consists of amounts billed or received in advance of the Company satisfying its performance obligations, and is recognized as revenue as services are delivered to customers. Deferred revenue relates primarily to subscriptions that are subject to usage limits that reset over short periods, which results in revenue being recognized ratably over the subscription period, which is generally 12 months or less.
paras.zh: 递延收入由公司在履行履约义务之前已开票或已收取的金额构成，并在向客户提供服务时确认为收入。递延收入主要涉及受短期重置的使用限额约束的订阅，这导致收入在订阅期内按比例确认，订阅期通常为 12 个月或更短。

paras.en: #### Compute and Infrastructure
paras.zh: #### 算力与基础设施

paras.en: Compute and infrastructure expenses primarily consist of costs attributable to operating the Company’s technology infrastructure, which supports the full range of workloads for the Company’s models, including research, model development, serving customers, and internal usage of Claude. These costs primarily consist of cloud compute fees paid to CSPs under committed and on-demand arrangements, including storage, networking and connectivity, and related support costs, infrastructure costs associated with serving customer workloads through partner channels, colocation facility costs, equipment leases and committed power costs associated with the Company’s data center operations, and third-party application infrastructure software costs directly related to the Company’s compute operations.
paras.zh: 算力与基础设施费用主要包括运营公司技术基础设施所产生的成本，该基础设施支持公司模型的全方位工作负载，包括研究、模型开发、服务客户以及 Claude 的内部使用。这些成本主要包括根据承诺和按需安排向 CSP 支付的云计算费用，包括存储、网络和连接及相关支持成本、通过合作伙伴渠道服务客户工作负载相关的基础设施成本、托管设施成本、与公司数据中心运营相关的设备租赁和承诺电力成本，以及与公司算力运营直接相关的第三方应用基础设施软件成本。

paras.en: #### Personnel

Personnel expenses primarily consist of stock-based compensation, including expense related to stock options, restricted stock units (“RSUs”), and restricted stock awards, cash compensation, including base salaries and bonuses, employee benefits, including health and welfare benefits, and employer payroll taxes.
paras.zh: 人员费用主要包括股权激励费用，包括与股票期权、限制性股票单位（“RSU”）和限制性股票奖励相关的费用，现金薪酬，包括基本工资和奖金，员工福利，包括健康和福利福利，以及雇主工资税。

paras.en: #### Bartz Settlement
paras.zh: #### Bartz 和解

paras.en: Bartz settlement consists of the charge the Company recorded in 2025 to settle the Bartz copyright infringement suit. Refer to Note 13 for further information.
paras.zh: Bartz 和解由公司于 2025 年记录的和解 Bartz 版权侵权诉讼的费用构成。更多信息请参见附注 13。

paras.en: #### Sales, Marketing, and Partnerships
paras.zh: #### 销售、营销与合作伙伴关系

paras.en: Sales, marketing, and partnerships expenses primarily consist of channel partner costs and marketing and advertising costs, including media and public relations spend.
paras.zh: 销售、营销与合作伙伴关系费用主要包括渠道合作伙伴成本以及营销和广告成本，包括媒体和公共关系支出。

paras.en: Advertising costs are expensed as incurred. Advertising expenses were $33 million and $147 million for the years ended December 31, 2024 and [__] 2025, respectively. Advertising expenses incurred in [__] 2023 were not material [__] .
paras.zh: 广告成本在发生时计入费用。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 [__] 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的广告费用分别为 $33 million 和 $147 million。 [__] 2023 年发生的广告费用不重大 [__] 。

paras.en: #### Other Operating and Administrative
paras.zh: #### 其他运营及行政费用

paras.en: Other operating and administrative expenses primarily consist of charitable donations expense related to the Company’s donation matching program, vendor costs related to data quality and performance evaluation services, information technology and cloud software costs, payment processing and platform fees, facility and occupancy costs, non-income taxes, professional services costs, bad debt expense, and depreciation and amortization related to non-data center assets.
paras.zh: 其他运营及行政费用主要包括与公司捐赠配比计划相关的慈善捐赠费用、与数据质量和绩效评估服务相关的供应商成本、信息技术和云软件成本、支付处理和平台费用、设施和占用成本、非所得税、专业服务成本、坏账费用，以及与数据中心以外资产相关的折旧和摊销。

paras.en: #### Stock-Based Compensation
paras.zh: #### 股权激励费用

paras.en: The Company’s equity incentive plan provides for the granting of stock options, RSUs, and restricted stock awards to employees, consultants, officers, and directors. The Company measures compensation cost for stock-based awards at grant-date fair value and recognizes it over the requisite service period. The Company accounts
paras.zh: 公司的股权激励计划规定可向员工、顾问、高管和董事授予股票期权、限制性股票单位（RSU）和限制性股票奖励。公司按授予日公允价值计量股权激励奖励的补偿成本，并在必要的服务期内确认。公司在

paras.en: **Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)**
paras.zh: **Anthropic, PBC 合并财务报表附注（续）**

paras.en: for forfeitures when they occur. The fair value of stock-based awards, granted or modified, is determined on the grant date (or modification or acquisition dates, if applicable) using appropriate valuation techniques. Stock-based compensation is included within personnel expenses in the consolidated statements of operations. The Company incurred stock-based compensation expense of $29 million, $192 million, and $1.2 billion for the years ended December 31, 2023, [__] 2024, and 2025, respectively. The Company incurred stock-based compensation expense of $286 million and $2.2 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), respectively. The tax benefits recognized in the consolidated statements of operations for stock-based compensation arrangements were not material during the years ended December 31, 2023, [__] 2024, and 2025 and during the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited).
paras.zh: 实际发生没收时进行会计处理。已授予或修改的股权激励奖励的公允价值，在授予日（或修改日或收购日，如适用）采用适当的估值技术确定。股权激励费用计入合并经营报表中的人事费用。截至 2023 年、[__] 2024 年和 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，公司分别发生股权激励费用 $29 million、$192 million 和 $1.2 billion。截至 2025 年和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计），公司分别发生股权激励费用 $286 million 和 $2.2 billion。截至 2023 年、[__] 2024 年和 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度以及截至 2025 年和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计）期间，合并经营报表中就股权激励安排确认的税收利益并不重大。

paras.en: Stock Options
paras.zh: 股票期权

paras.en: Stock-based compensation expense is recognized on a straight-line basis over the period during which an employee is required to provide services in exchange for the award (generally the vesting period of the award). The Company determines the fair value of stock options on the date of grant using the Black-Scholes-Merton option pricing model which is impacted by the estimated fair value of the Company’s common stock, as well as changes in assumptions regarding a number of highly complex and subjective variables. These variables are summarized as follows:
paras.zh: 股权激励费用在员工需提供服务以换取奖励的期间（通常为奖励的归属期）内按直线法确认。公司于授予日使用 Black-Scholes-Merton 期权定价模型确定股票期权的公允价值，该模型受公司普通股估计公允价值以及若干高度复杂且主观的假设变量变动的影响。这些变量概述如下：

paras.en: - Fair value of common stock – Until the Company’s common stock is publicly traded, the Company must estimate the fair value of common stock. The Company’s board of directors (the “Board”) considers numerous objective and subjective factors to determine the fair value of the Company’s common stock including: contemporaneous third-party valuations of the Company’s common stock, price paid by investors for the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, actual and forecasted operating and financial performance, market conditions, performance of comparable publicly traded companies, developments and milestones within the Company, the rights, preferences, and privileges of the Company’s common and redeemable convertible preferred stock, and the likelihood and timing of achieving a liquidity event, among other factors.
paras.zh: - 普通股公允价值 – 在公司普通股公开交易之前，公司必须估计普通股的公允价值。公司董事会（“董事会”）考虑众多客观和主观因素以确定公司普通股的公允价值，包括：公司普通股的同期第三方估值、投资者为公司普通股和可赎回可转换优先股支付的价格、实际和预测的经营与财务业绩、市场状况、可比上市公司的表现、公司内部的发展和里程碑、公司普通股和可赎回可转换优先股的权利、优先权和特权，以及实现流动性事件的可能性和时间等。

paras.en: - Expected volatility – Expected volatility is a measure of the amount by which the stock price is expected to fluctuate. Since the Company has no trading history of its common stock, it estimates the expected volatility of its underlying common stock as of the grant date of its stock options by taking the weighted-average historical volatility of a group of comparable publicly traded companies over a period equal to the expected life of the options.
paras.zh: - 预期波动率 – 预期波动率是衡量股票价格预期波动幅度的指标。由于公司普通股没有交易历史，公司通过取一组可比上市公司在等于期权预期期限的期间内的加权平均历史波动率，来估计其标的普通股在股票期权授予日的预期波动率。

paras.en: - Expected term – Expected term represents the period over which the Company anticipates stock-based awards to be outstanding. The Company estimates the expected term based on the options’ vesting term and contractual terms, such that the expected life is equal to the average of the stock-based award’s weighted-average vesting period and its contractual term.
paras.zh: - 预期期限 – 预期期限代表公司预计股权激励奖励将存续的期间。公司根据期权的归属期限和合同条款估计预期期限，使预期期限等于股权激励奖励的加权平均归属期与其合同期限的平均值。

paras.en: - Risk-free interest rate – The risk-free interest rate used is based on the implied yield in effect at the time of grant of U.S. Treasury securities with maturities similar to the expected term of the stock options.
paras.zh: - 无风险利率 – 所使用的无风险利率基于授予时与股票期权预期期限相近的美国国债的实际收益率。

paras.en: - Expected dividend yield – The expected dividend yield is zero, as the Company has never declared or paid any dividends and has no current plans to do so.
paras.zh: - 预期股息率 – 预期股息率为零，因为公司从未宣布或支付任何股息，且目前没有这样做的计划。

paras.en: Restricted Stock Units
paras.zh: 限制性股票单位

paras.en: The Company measures and recognizes stock-based compensation expense for RSUs based on the estimated fair value of the underlying common stock on the date of grant. The Company’s RSUs vest upon the satisfaction of both service and performance conditions. The service condition for these awards is generally satisfied over a four-year vesting period. The performance condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of either (i) a qualifying change in control of the Company or (ii) a listing of the Company’s equity securities on an established securities market (including through a traditional public offering, direct listing, or business combination with a special purpose acquisition company), in each case, on or before the seventh anniversary of the grant date, as further defined in such RSU agreements. If the performance condition is not satisfied within seven years of the grant date, all unvested RSUs are forfeited. Compensation cost related to these RSUs must be recognized over the
paras.zh: 公司根据授予日标的普通股的估计公允价值，计量并确认限制性股票单位（RSU）的股权激励费用。公司的 RSU 在服务条件和业绩条件均满足时归属。这些奖励的服务条件通常在四年归属期内满足。业绩条件在以下任一情形发生时满足：(i) 公司发生符合条件的控制权变更，或 (ii) 公司股权证券在成熟证券市场上市（包括通过传统公开发行、直接上市或与特殊目的收购公司进行业务合并），且在任何情况下均须在授予日起第七个周年日或之前发生，具体以该等 RSU 协议中的进一步定义为准。如果业绩条件未在授予日起七年内满足，所有未归属的 RSU 将被没收。与这些 RSU 相关的补偿成本必须在

paras.en: **Anthropic, PBC Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements (Continued)**
paras.zh: **Anthropic, PBC 合并财务报表附注（续）**

paras.en: requisite service period using the accelerated attribution method, if it is probable that the performance-based vesting condition will be satisfied. The performance-based vesting condition will be deemed probable of being satisfied upon either the consummation of an acquisition or change in control or the Company’s initial public
paras.zh: 采用加速归属法在所需服务期内确认，前提是业绩归属条件很可能得到满足。业绩归属条件在完成收购或控制权变更或公司首次公开[__]时，将被视为很可能得到满足。

paras.en: offering. As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized for the RSUs because management determined that it is not probable that the performance condition will be achieved.
paras.zh: 发行。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），尚未就 RSU 确认任何股权激励费用，因为管理层判定业绩条件很可能无法实现。

paras.en: #### Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock
paras.zh: #### 可赎回可转换优先股

paras.en: The Company records shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock at their respective fair values on the dates of issuance, net of issuance costs. The redeemable convertible preferred stock is recorded outside of permanent equity because it is not mandatorily redeemable and redemption is contingent upon the occurrence of certain deemed liquidation events that are not solely within the Company’s control. The Company has not adjusted the carrying values of the redeemable convertible preferred stock to the liquidation preferences of such shares because it is not probable that a deemed liquidation event would occur that would obligate the Company to pay the liquidation preferences to holders of shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock. Subsequent adjustments of the carrying values to the liquidation preferences will be made only when it becomes probable that such a deemed liquidation event will occur.
paras.zh: 公司按发行日各自的公允价值扣除发行费用后记录可赎回可转换优先股。可赎回可转换优先股记录在永久性权益之外，因为其并非强制可赎回，且赎回取决于并非完全由公司控制的一定被视为清算事件的发生。公司未将可赎回可转换优先股的账面价值调整至该等股份的清算优先权，因为很可能不会发生使公司有义务向可赎回可转换优先股持有人支付清算优先权的被视为清算事件。仅当该等被视为清算事件很可能发生时，方会将账面价值后续调整至清算优先权。

paras.en: #### Foreign Currency

The functional currencies of the Company’s foreign subsidiaries are the local currency or the U.S. dollar depending on the nature of the subsidiaries’ activities. Monetary assets and liabilities, and transactions denominated in currencies other than the functional currency are remeasured to the functional currency at the exchange rate in effect at the end of the period and are recorded in the current period consolidated statements of operations. Gains and losses resulting from remeasurement are recorded in foreign exchange gains (losses), net within other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. Subsidiary assets and liabilities with non-U.S. dollar functional currencies are translated at the month-end rate, retained earnings and other equity items are translated at historical rates, and revenue and expenses are translated at average exchange rates during the year. Cumulative translation adjustments are recorded within accumulated other comprehensive income (loss), a separate component of total stockholders’ deficit in the Company’s consolidated balance sheets.
paras.zh: 公司境外子公司的功能货币为当地货币或美元，取决于子公司活动的性质。以功能货币以外的货币计价的货币性资产和负债以及交易，按期末有效汇率重新计量为功能货币，并计入当期合并经营报表。重新计量产生的利得和损失计入合并经营报表其他收入（费用）净额中的汇兑收益（损失）净额。功能货币为非美元的子公司资产和负债按月末汇率折算，留存收益和其他权益项目按历史汇率折算，收入和费用按年度平均汇率折算。累计折算调整额计入累计其他综合收益（损失），作为公司合并资产负债表股东权益赤字总额的单独组成部分。

paras.en: #### Loss Contingencies
paras.zh: #### 或有损失

paras.en: The Company is periodically involved in various legal claims, proceedings and other regulatory and administrative proceedings that may arise in the ordinary course of business. Certain of these matters may include speculative claims for substantial or indeterminate amounts of damages. The Company routinely reviews the status of each significant matter and assesses its potential financial exposure. The Company records a liability when it believes that it is both probable that a loss has been incurred and the amount can be reasonably estimated. If the Company determines that a loss is reasonably possible and the loss or range of loss can be reasonably estimated, the Company discloses the possible loss in the consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 公司会不时涉及在日常经营过程中可能产生的各类法律索赔、诉讼程序及其他监管和行政程序。其中某些事项可能包含针对大额或不确定金额损害赔偿的推测性索赔。公司定期审查各项重大事项的进展状况，并评估其潜在的财务风险敞口。当公司认为损失很可能已经发生且金额能够合理估计时，即确认相应负债。如果公司认定损失有可能发生且该损失或损失区间能够合理估计，公司会在合并财务报表中披露该或有损失。

paras.en: Because of inherent uncertainties related to these legal matters, significant judgment is required to determine both the probability and the estimated amount of loss. These estimates have been based on the Company’s assessment of the facts and circumstances at each balance sheet date and are subject to change based on new information and future events. As additional information becomes available, the Company reassesses its potential liability and may revise its estimates. If one or more matters were resolved against the Company for amounts in excess of management’s expectations, the Company’s results of operations and financial condition, including in a particular reporting period in which any such outcome becomes probable and estimable, could be materially adversely affected.
paras.zh: 由于这些法律事项存在固有的不确定性，确定损失发生的可能性及估计金额均需要作出重大判断。上述估计基于公司对各资产负债表日事实与情况的评估，并可能因新信息和未来事件而发生变化。随着更多信息的获取，公司会重新评估其潜在责任并可能修订其估计。如果一项或多项事项以超出管理层预期的金额对公司作出不利裁决，公司的经营业绩和财务状况（包括在任何此类结果变得很可能且可估计的特定报告期内）可能受到重大不利影响。

paras.en: #### Share Repurchase
paras.zh: #### 股份回购

paras.en: Share repurchases are recorded on the trade date. When shares are immediately retired, the value of repurchased shares is deducted from stockholders’ deficit through common stock with the excess over par value recorded to accumulated deficit.
paras.zh: 股份回购在交易日记账。当股份被立即注销时，回购股份的价值通过普通股从股东权益赤字中扣除，超出面值的部分计入累计赤字。

paras.en: #### Income Taxes
paras.zh: #### 所得税

paras.en: The Company uses the asset and liability method to account for income taxes. Current income tax expense or benefit represents the amount of income taxes expected to be payable or refundable for the current year. Under this method, deferred income tax assets and liabilities are determined based on differences between the financial statement reporting and tax bases of assets and liabilities and net operating loss and credit carryforwards. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are measured using enacted tax rates applied to taxable income in the years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or settled. Valuation allowances are established when necessary to reduce deferred tax assets to the amounts that are more-likely-than-not expected to be realized based on the weighting of positive and negative evidence. Future realization of deferred tax assets ultimately depends on the existence of sufficient taxable income of the appropriate character (for example, ordinary income or capital gain) within the carryback or carryforward periods available under the applicable tax law. The Company regularly reviews the deferred tax assets for recoverability based on historical taxable income, projected future taxable income, the expected timing of the reversals of existing temporary differences and tax planning strategies. The Company’s judgment regarding future profitability may change due to many factors, including future market conditions and the ability to successfully execute the business plans and/or tax planning strategies. Should there be a change in the ability to recover deferred tax assets, the Company’s income tax provision would increase or decrease in the period in which the assessment is changed. The Company treats Net CFC Tested Income (formerly referred to as Global Intangible Low-Taxed Income or “GILTI”) as a period cost.
paras.zh: 公司采用资产负债法核算所得税。当期所得税费用或收益代表本年度预计应缴纳或可退还的所得税金额。在该方法下，递延所得税资产和负债根据财务报表报告基础与资产和负债的计税基础之间的差异以及净经营亏损和税收抵免结转确定。递延所得税资产和负债采用已颁布的税率计量，该税率适用于预计该等暂时性差异将被收回或结算的年度内的应纳税所得额。在必要时设立估值备抵，以将递延所得税资产减至根据正面和负面证据的权重更可能实现（more-likely-than-not）的金额。递延所得税资产的未来实现最终取决于在适用税法允许的结转期内是否存在足够数量的适当性质（例如，普通所得或资本利得）的应纳税所得额。公司根据历史应纳税所得额、预计未来应纳税所得额、现有暂时性差异转回的预期时间以及税务筹划策略，定期审查递延所得税资产的可收回性。公司对未来盈利能力的判断可能因多种因素而发生变化，包括未来市场状况以及成功执行业务计划和/或税务筹划策略的能力。如果可收回递延所得税资产的能力发生变化，公司的所得税拨备将在评估发生变化的期间增加或减少。公司将净 CFC 测试所得（Net CFC Tested Income，原称全球无形资产低税所得或“GILTI”）作为期间费用处理。

paras.en: The Company accounts for uncertain tax positions in accordance with ASC 740-10, Accounting for Uncertainty in Income Taxes. The Company recognizes the tax effects of an uncertain tax position only if such position is more likely than not to be sustained based solely on its technical merits as of the reporting date and only in an amount more likely than not to be sustained upon review by the tax authorities. The Company recognizes accrued interest and penalties related to unrecognized tax benefits in the provision for income taxes in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 公司根据 ASC 740-10《所得税不确定性的会计处理》核算不确定的税务立场。公司仅在某一不确定税务立场仅基于其截至报告日的技术依据更可能（more likely than not）得以维持时，且仅以经税务机关审查后更可能得以维持的金额，确认该不确定税务立场的税务影响。公司在合并经营报表的所得税拨备中确认与未确认税收利益相关的应计利息和罚款。

paras.en: #### Net Loss per Share
paras.zh: #### 每股净亏损

paras.en: Basic and diluted net loss per share attributable to common stockholders is computed in conformity with the two-class method required for participating securities. The two-class method requires income available to common stockholders for the period to be allocated between common stock and participating securities based upon their respective rights to receive dividends as if all income for the period had been distributed.
paras.zh: 归属于普通股股东的每股基本和稀释净亏损按照参与性证券所要求的两类法计算。两类法要求将当期可供普通股股东分配的收益在普通股和参与性证券之间按其各自收取股息的权利进行分配，如同当期全部收益均已分配。

paras.en: The Company considers all series of its redeemable convertible preferred stock to be participating securities as the holders of such stock have the right to participate on a pari passu basis in any distributions to common stockholders.
paras.zh: 公司将各系列可赎回可转换优先股视为参与性证券，因为该等股票的持有人有权按同等顺位（pari passu）参与向普通股股东的任何分配。

paras.en: The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock would be entitled to dividends in preference to common stockholders, at specified rates, if declared. Any remaining dividend amounts would then be distributed to the holders of common stock, restricted common stock, and the holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock on a pro-rata basis assuming conversion of all redeemable convertible preferred stock into common stock. These participating securities do not contractually require the holders of such shares to participate in the Company’s losses. As such, net losses for the periods presented were not allocated to the Company’s participating securities.
paras.zh: 可赎回可转换优先股的持有人有权在宣派股息时按指定比率优先于普通股股东获得股息。任何剩余股息金额随后将按假设全部可赎回可转换优先股转换为普通股的比例，分配给普通股持有人、限制性普通股持有人及可赎回可转换优先股持有人。该等参与性证券在合同上不要求其持有人参与公司的亏损。因此，所列示期间的净亏损未分配给公司的参与性证券。

paras.en: Basic net loss per share is computed by dividing the net loss attributable to common stockholders by the weighted-average number of shares of common stock outstanding during the period, less shares subject to repurchase. The diluted net loss per share is computed by giving effect to all potentially dilutive securities outstanding for the period using the treasury stock method or the if-converted method if the effect is dilutive. For periods in which the Company reports net losses, diluted net loss per share is the same as basic net loss per share, because all potentially dilutive securities are anti-dilutive.
paras.zh: 每股基本净亏损的计算方法为：将归属于普通股股东的净亏损除以该期间发行在外的普通股加权平均股数（减去须予回购的股份）。每股稀释净亏损的计算方法为：采用库存股法或转换法（若具有稀释效应），计入该期间所有发行在外的潜在稀释性证券的影响。在公司报告净亏损的期间，每股稀释净亏损与每股基本净亏损相同，因为所有潜在稀释性证券均具有反稀释效应。

paras.en: In July 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-05, Financial Instruments—Credit Losses (Topic 326): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets (“ASU 2025-05”). ASU 2025-05 provides all entities with a practical expedient when estimating expected credit losses for current accounts receivable and current contract assets arising from transactions accounted for under ASC 606. All entities may elect a practical expedient that assumes that current conditions as of the balance sheet date do not change for the remaining life of the asset. The amendments in this ASU will be effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2025, and interim reporting periods within those annual reporting periods. Early adoption is permitted in both interim and annual reporting periods in which financial statements have not yet been issued or made available for issuance. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-05, effective January 1, 2025, electing the practical expedient and applying the guidance prospectively. This ASU did not have a significant impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 2025 年 7 月，FASB 发布了 ASU 2025-05《金融工具——信用损失（主题 326）：应收账款和合同资产的信用损失计量》（"ASU 2025-05"）。ASU 2025-05 为所有主体在估计由按 ASC 606 核算的交易产生的当期应收账款和当期合同资产的预期信用损失时，提供了一项实务简便方法。所有主体均可选择一项实务简便方法，即假设资产负债表日的当前状况在资产剩余寿命内不会发生变化。本 ASU 中的修订将对 2025 年 12 月 15 日之后开始的年度报告期以及这些年度报告期内的中期报告期生效。在财务报表尚未发布或尚未可供发布的中期和年度报告期内，允许提前采用。公司已提前采用 ASU 2025-05，自 2025 年 1 月 1 日起生效，选择该实务简便方法并前瞻性应用该指引。本 ASU 未对公司的合并财务报表产生重大影响。

paras.en: In September 2025, the FASB issued ASU 2025-06, Intangibles—Goodwill and Other—Internal-Use Software (Subtopic 350-40): Targeted Improvements to the Accounting for Internal-Use Software (“ASU 2025-06”). ASU 2025-06 modernizes the guidance for costs incurred in connection with internal-use software by removing references to prescriptive development stages. Under ASU 2025-06, an entity may begin capitalizing internal-use software costs when (a) management, with the relevant authority, implicitly or explicitly authorizes and commits to funding a computer software project and (b) it is probable that the project will be completed and the software will be used to perform the function intended (the “probable-to-complete recognition threshold”). ASU 2025-06 is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after December 15, 2027, and interim periods within those annual reporting periods; early adoption is permitted. The ASU may be adopted prospectively, retrospectively, or via a modified prospective transition. The Company early adopted ASU 2025-06, effective January 1, 2025, applying the guidance on a prospective basis. This ASU did not have a significant impact to the Company’s consolidated financial statements.
paras.zh: 2025 年 9 月，FASB 发布了 ASU 2025-06《无形资产——商誉及其他——内部使用软件（子主题 350-40）：内部使用软件会计处理的针对性改进》（"ASU 2025-06"）。ASU 2025-06 通过删除对规定性开发阶段的引用，使与内部使用软件相关的成本指引现代化。根据 ASU 2025-06，主体可在以下条件满足时开始将内部使用软件成本资本化：(a) 拥有相关权限的管理层隐含或明确地授权并承诺为某一计算机软件项目提供资金，且 (b) 该项目很可能完成且该软件将被用于执行预期功能（“很可能完成确认门槛”）。ASU 2025-06 将对 2027 年 12 月 15 日之后开始的年度报告期以及这些年度报告期内的中期期间生效；允许提前采用。本 ASU 可采用前瞻性、追溯性或经修改的前瞻性过渡方式采用。公司已提前采用 ASU 2025-06，自 2025 年 1 月 1 日起生效，并前瞻性应用该指引。本 ASU 未对公司的合并财务报表产生重大影响。

The Company is currently evaluating the impact of the new standard on the Company’s consolidated financial statements.

paras.en: The Company holds investments accounted for under the equity method of accounting where the Company can exercise significant influence, but not control, over an investee. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company’s carrying value of such investments was not material. The Company has made funding commitments of up to [__] $325 million, of which $265 million remained unfunded as of June 30, 2026 (unaudited).
