paras.en: The Company measures cash equivalents and short-term investments at fair value. Level 1 instrument valuations are based on quoted market prices of the identical underlying security. Level 2 instrument valuations are obtained from readily available pricing sources for comparable instruments, identical instruments in less active markets, or models using market observable inputs.
paras.zh: 公司以公允价值计量现金等价物和短期投资。第 1 层级工具的估值基于相同基础证券的市场报价。第 2 层级工具的估值取自可比工具、较不活跃市场中的相同工具的现成定价来源，或使用市场可观察输入的模型。

paras.en: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company entered into a contract to receive warrant rights to acquire common shares of a privately-held company as consideration under an agreement entered into but not yet commenced. The warrant rights are freestanding financial instruments that meet the definition of a derivative as they contain a net settlement feature. The warrants have not been designated as hedging instruments and will be granted and recognized as lease incentives upon commencement of the related arrangements and recognized as a reduction of the related ROU assets. The Company estimated the fair value of the warrant rights using a probability-weighted expected return method. In applying this method, the Company utilized Level 3 valuation inputs based on information available, including terms and features of the warrant rights and other outstanding classes of the issuer’s equity securities, observable transactions in the issuer’s securities such as its most recent financing round, estimates of equity volatility, and expected time to a liquidity event. The initial fair value of the warrant rights was recognized as a derivative asset classified within other assets on the consolidated balance sheets, with a corresponding deferred liability classified within other noncurrent liabilities.
paras.zh: 在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度内，公司签订了一份合同，作为已签订但尚未开始的协议项下的对价，获得收购一家非上市公司普通股的认股权证权利。该认股权证权利为独立金融工具，因其包含净额结算特征而符合衍生工具的定义。该认股权证未被指定为套期工具，并将在相关安排开始时作为租赁激励授予并确认，同时作为相关使用权资产的减少予以确认。公司采用概率加权预期回报法估计该认股权证权利的公允价值。在应用该方法时，公司基于可获得的信息使用了第 3 层级估值输入，包括认股权证权利的条款和特征、发行人其他已发行类别权益证券、发行人证券的可观察交易（如其最近一轮融资）、股权波动率估计以及预期实现流动性事件的时间。该认股权证权利的初始公允价值确认为衍生资产，分类为合并资产负债表中的其他资产，相应递延负债分类为其他非流动负债。

paras.en: The estimated fair value of the note purchase agreements was determined by using a probability-weighted expected return method. The fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock was determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a contingent claims analysis (“CCA”) and a common stock equivalent (“CSE”) method. Assumptions included assumed future liquidity and financing events, the terms and features of the agreement, weights applied to each scenario, discount rates, applicable risk free rates, the fair value of the Series G-2 redeemable convertible preferred stock, and a discount for lack of marketability.
paras.zh: 本票购买协议的估计公允价值采用概率加权期望回报法确定。G-2 系列可赎回可转换优先股的公允价值采用由或有索偿分析（“CCA”）与普通股等价物（“CSE”）法构成的混合方法确定。所采用的假设包括假定的未来流动性和融资事件、协议的条款与特征、各情景适用的权重、折现率、适用的无风险利率、G-2 系列可赎回可转换优先股的公允价值，以及缺乏市场流通性折价。

paras.en: Level 3 liabilities consist of the SAFE liabilities (Note 9), convertible notes (Note [__] 9), derivative liabilities (Note 9), donation matching program liability (Note [__] 10), and a holdback liability for a portion of shares issuable in the acquisition of Codeblog Corp. (“Bun”) (Note 15). There is no current market for these liabilities such that determination of fair value requires significant judgment or estimation. Changes in fair value measurements categorized within Level 3 of the fair value hierarchy are analyzed each period based on changes in estimates or assumptions and recorded as appropriate. The Company recorded a $3 million change in fair value of the holdback liability during the year ended December 31, 2025 in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 第 3 层级负债包括 SAFE 负债（附注 9）、可转换本票（附注 [__] 9）、衍生工具负债（附注 9）、捐赠配捐计划负债（附注 [__] 10），以及就收购 Codeblog Corp.（“Bun”）中部分可发行股份计提的暂扣款负债（附注 15）。这些负债目前没有市场，因此公允价值的确定需要重大判断或估计。公允价值层级中第 3 层级内的公允价值计量变动，每期根据估计或假设的变动进行分析并酌情记录。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，公司在合并经营报表的其他收入（费用）净额中记录了暂扣款负债公允价值变动 $3 million。

paras.en: The SAFE liabilities are recorded at fair value, which is determined based on a third-party valuation utilizing a scenario-based analysis and a CCA, that considers specific scenarios that factor in timing, probability, and financing size. This model takes into account the contract terms as well as multiple inputs, such as the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock price, risk free interest rates, and expected volatility, some of which the Company could not corroborate with observable market data. The assumptions used in valuing the SAFE liability upon conversion on December 31, 2023 and on January 30, 2024, include volatility, risk free interest rate, and term to liquidity. Changes in the fair value measurement of the SAFE liabilities relate to the conversion scenarios and are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. All SAFEs have been converted as of December 31, 2024 [__] .
paras.zh: SAFE 负债按公允价值记录，其公允价值基于第三方估值确定，该估值采用情景分析和 CCA，考虑纳入时间、概率和融资规模的特定情景。该模型考虑合同条款以及多项输入值，例如公司可赎回可转换优先股价格、无风险利率和预期波动率，其中部分输入值公司无法以可观察市场数据加以印证。在 2023 年 12 月 31 日和 2024 年 1 月 30 日转换时对 SAFE 负债进行估值所使用的假设包括波动率、无风险利率和至流动性事件的期限。SAFE 负债公允价值的变动与转换情景相关，并在合并经营报表中记录为可转换本票、衍生工具负债和 SAFE 的公允价值变动。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，所有 SAFE 均已转换 [__]。

paras.en: The estimated fair value of the convertible notes is determined by using a hybrid approach comprising a CCA and a CSE method. The analysis estimates the fair value of the convertible notes based on the probability-weighted expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock, and maturity. Assumptions include weight applied to the CCA and CSE methods, assumed volatility, time to a liquidity event, need for and terms of financings or expected financings, and the risk free interest rate. Changes in fair value of the convertible notes are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 可转换本票的估计公允价值采用由 CCA 与 CSE 方法构成的混合方法确定。该分析基于概率加权的预期未来投资回报估计可转换本票的公允价值，并考虑本票持有人可获得的可能结果，包括转换为可赎回可转换优先股、N 类普通股以及到期。假设包括应用于 CCA 与 CSE 方法的权重、假设波动率、距流动性事件的时间、融资需求及条款或预期融资，以及无风险利率。可转换本票公允价值的变动在合并经营报表中记录为可转换本票、衍生负债及 SAFE 的公允价值变动。

paras.en: #### Convertible Notes
paras.zh: #### 可转换本票

paras.en: The Company has entered into note purchase agreements which provide for the issuance of one or more convertible notes. To the extent that the note purchase agreements create an obligation to issue notes in the future, these obligations are accounted for as derivative liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets until the related note is issued.
paras.zh: 本公司与各方签订了票据购买协议，约定发行一笔或多笔可转换本票。若票据购买协议产生未来发行票据的义务，则在相关票据发行之前，该等义务在合并资产负债表上作为衍生负债核算。

paras.en: Google 2023 Note Purchase Agreement
paras.zh: Google 2023 年票据购买协议

paras.en: In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2023 NPA”) with Google LLC (“Google”), for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to [__] $2.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $500 million in September 2023, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $750 million in September 2024, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of [__] $750 million in September 2025.
paras.zh: 2023 年 9 月，本公司与 Google LLC（"Google"）签订了一份票据购买协议（“Google 2023 年 NPA”），用于发行本金总额最高为 [__] $2.0 billion 的可转换本票，可分三批发行。本公司于 2023 年 9 月发行了本金总额为 $500 million 的第一批票据，于 2024 年 9 月发行了本金总额为 $750 million 的第二批票据，并于 2025 年 9 月发行了本金总额为 [__] $750 million 的第三批票据。

paras.en: The notes issued under Google 2023 NPA bore interest at a rate of [__] 10.0% per annum, compounded annually, and payable upon maturity, 48 months after the respective issuance date. The Company also has a commercial agreement with Google for the provision of intelligence service.
paras.zh: 根据 Google 2023 年 NPA 发行的票据按年利率 [__] 10.0% 计息，按年复利，并于各自发行日期后 48 个月到期时支付。本公司还与 Google 签订了一份商业协议，以提供智能服务。

paras.en: In connection with the Company’s Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into an aggregate of 12.7 million shares of the Company’s Series E-3 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $44.8692 per share and an aggregate of 15.3 million shares of Series E-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of [__] $50.4779 per share, respectively. The conversion prices reflect the contractual discounts to the Series E-1 original issuance price of [__] $56.0865 per share. As of December 31, 2025, $750 million aggregate principal amount remained outstanding under the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA [__] .
paras.zh: 就本公司 2025 年 E-1 系列可赎回可转换优先股融资而言，根据 Google 2023 年 NPA 发行的第一批和第二批票据已分别按每股 $44.8692 的转换价格全额转换为合计 12.7 million 股本公司的 E-3 系列无投票权可赎回可转换优先股，以及按每股 [__] $50.4779 的转换价格全额转换为合计 15.3 million 股 E-4 系列无投票权可赎回可转换优先股。该等转换价格反映了相对于 E-1 系列原始发行价格 [__] $56.0865 每股的合同折扣。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，根据 Google 2023 年 NPA 发行的第三批票据项下仍有本金总额 $750 million 未偿还 [__] 。

paras.zh: **Anthropic, PBC 合并财务报表附注（续）**

paras.en: In January 2026, in connection with the initial closing of the Series G-1 financing, the third tranche of notes issued under Google 2023 NPA converted in full into 3.3 million shares of Series G-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of $233.2228 per share. The conversion price reflects the contractual discounts to the Series G-1 price of $259.1364 per share. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2023 NPA.
paras.zh: 2026 年 1 月，就 G-1 系列融资的首次交割而言，根据 Google 2023 年 NPA 发行的第三批票据已按每股 $233.2228 的转换价格全额转换为 3.3 million 股 G-4 系列无投票权可赎回可转换优先股。该转换价格反映了相对于 G-1 系列价格每股 $259.1364 的合同折扣。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）,Google 2023 年 NPA 项下无未偿还金额。

paras.en: Google 2024 Note Purchase Agreement
paras.zh: Google 2024 年票据购买协议

paras.en: In August 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Google 2024 NPA”) with Google for the issuance of a convertible promissory note in an aggregate principal amount of approximately $1.3 billion. Such note bore interest at a rate of [__] 8.5% per annum compounded annually, and, unless earlier converted or repaid, was payable upon maturity in August 2030.
paras.zh: 2024 年 8 月，本公司与 Google 签订了另一份票据购买协议（“Google 2024 年 NPA”），用于发行本金总额约为 $1.3 billion 的可转换本票。该票据按年利率 [__] 8.5% 计息，按年复利，且除非提前转换或偿还，否则于 2030 年 8 月到期时支付。

paras.en: In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the note issued under Google 2024 NPA was converted in full into an aggregate of 24.2 million shares of Series E-5 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of [__] $53.2822 per share, reflecting a contractual discount to the Series E-1 original issuance price of [__] $56.0865 per share. As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), no amounts remain outstanding under Google 2024 NPA [__] .
paras.zh: 就 2025 年 E-1 系列可赎回可转换优先股融资而言，根据 Google 2024 年 NPA 发行的票据已按每股 [__] $53.2822 的转换价格全额转换为合计 24.2 million 股 E-5 系列无投票权可赎回可转换优先股，该转换价格反映了相对于 E-1 系列原始发行价格 [__] $56.0865 每股的合同折扣。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）,Google 2024 年 NPA 项下无未偿还金额 [__] 。

paras.en: Google 2026 Note Purchase Agreement (Unaudited)
paras.zh: Google 2026 票据购买协议（未经审计）

paras.en: In March 2026 (unaudited), the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Google 2026 NPA”) under which, subject to certain conditions, up to $30.0 billion of convertible promissory notes or non-voting common stock through December 31, 2030 may be issued. Non-voting common stock would be issued at the 30-day trailing volume-weighted average price and, to the extent issued, the notes will bear interest at [__] 9.0% per annum compounded annually, payable at maturity, and mature six years after issuance, unless earlier repaid or converted pursuant to the terms of the agreement.
paras.zh: 2026 年 3 月（未经审计），本公司与 Google 订立票据购买协议（"Google 2026 NPA"），根据该协议，在满足若干条件的前提下，本公司可在 2030 年 12 月 31 日之前发行最高 $30.0 billion 的可转换本票或无表决权普通股。无表决权普通股将按 30 日追踪成交量加权平均价格发行，且就已发行的部分而言，该等票据将按年利率 [__] 9.0% 计息，按年复利计算，于到期时支付，并自发行之日起六年到期，除非根据协议条款提前偿还或转换。

paras.en: In May 2026 (unaudited), Google invested $10.0 billion in the Company’s Series H redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, which reduced the amount available for issuance under the Google 2026 NPA to $20.0 billion. As of June 30, 2026, no non-voting common stock or notes had been issued under the Google 2026 NPA [__] .
paras.zh: 2026 年 5 月（未经审计）,Google 向本公司 H 系列可赎回可转换优先股融资投资 $10.0 billion，使 Google 2026 NPA 项下可供发行的金额减少至 $20.0 billion。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，Google 2026 NPA 项下尚未发行任何无表决权普通股或票据 [__] 。

paras.en: Amazon 2023 and 2024 Note Purchase Agreements
paras.zh: Amazon 2023 及 2024 年票据购买协议

paras.en: In September 2023, the Company entered into a note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2023 NPA”) with Amazon for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to $4.0 billion issuable in two tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.2 billion in September 2023, and the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $3.4 billion in March 2024, reflecting an issuance premium to the $2.8 billion in proceeds received for the second tranche of notes.
paras.zh: 2023 年 9 月，本公司与 Amazon 签订了一份票据购买协议（"Amazon 2023 NPA"），约定发行本金总额最高达 $4.0 billion 的可转换本票，可分两批发行。本公司于 2023 年 9 月发行了本金总额为 $1.2 billion 的第一批票据，并于 2024 年 3 月发行了本金总额为 $3.4 billion 的第二批票据，该金额反映了第二批票据所收到 $2.8 billion 收益之上的发行溢价。

paras.en: In November 2024, the Company entered into an additional note purchase agreement (“Amazon 2024 NPA”) with Amazon for the issuance of convertible promissory notes in an aggregate principal amount of up to [__] $4.0 billion, issuable in three tranches. The Company issued the first tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in November 2024, the second tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion in May 2025, and the third tranche of notes in an aggregate principal amount of $1.4 billion in November 2025.
paras.zh: 2024 年 11 月，本公司与 Amazon 签订了另一份票据购买协议（"Amazon 2024 NPA"），约定发行本金总额最高达 [__] $4.0 billion 的可转换本票，可分三批发行。本公司于 2024 年 11 月发行了本金总额为 $1.3 billion 的第一批票据，于 2025 年 5 月发行了本金总额为 $1.3 billion 的第二批票据，并于 2025 年 11 月发行了本金总额为 $1.4 billion 的第三批票据。

paras.en: The notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA bear interest at a rate of [__] 8.0%per annum compounded annually and payable upon maturity, and mature 10 years after the respective issuance date, unless earlier repaid or converted. The first tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA bears interest at a rate of [__] 8.5% per annum, compounded annually and payable at maturity, and matures in November 2034, unless earlier repaid or converted. The second and third tranche of notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA are each non-interest bearing and mature in May 2035 and November 2035, respectively, unless earlier repaid or converted.
paras.zh: 根据 Amazon 2023 NPA 发行的票据按 [__] 8.0% 的年利率计息，按年复利计算并于到期时支付，且自各自发行日起 10 年后到期，除非提前偿还或转换。根据 Amazon 2024 NPA 发行的第一批票据按 [__] 8.5% 的年利率计息，按年复利计算并于到期时支付，且于 2034 年 11 月到期，除非提前偿还或转换。根据 Amazon 2024 NPA 发行的第二批和第三批票据均不计息，分别于 2035 年 5 月和 2035 年 11 月到期，除非提前偿还或转换。

paras.zh: 根据 Amazon 2023 NPA 发行的票据而言)，或 [__] 每股 $50.4779（就根据 Amazon 2024 NPA 发行的票据而言），以及 (ii) 本公司最近一次 (1) 优先股股权融资（就根据 Amazon 2023 NPA 发行的票据而言）或 (2) 合格股权融资（就根据 Amazon 2024 NPA 发行的票据而言）中的每股价格，在每种情况下均受下述 Amazon 持股上限的约束。

paras.en: In connection with certain liquidation transactions, Amazon may, in lieu of converting such notes at the applicable conversion price, elect to receive cash in an amount equal to the outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon. Pursuant to the terms of Amazon 2024 NPA, the Company may be required to make additional cash payments to Amazon calculated as set forth in Amazon 2024 NPA in connection with certain liquidation transactions. In addition, in connection with an initial public offering, direct listing, or special purpose acquisition company transaction, any outstanding principal amount and accrued but unpaid interest thereon under the applicable Amazon NPA will automatically convert into shares of the Company’s Class N common stock at a conversion price equal to the lower of (i) [__] $2.0928 per share, in the case of Amazon 2023 NPA, or [__] $5.0478 per share, in the case of Amazon 2024 NPA, and (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in such transaction. Any portion of Amazon’s notes that cannot convert due to Amazon’s ownership cap will automatically convert, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap, into shares of Class N common stock at the close of each fiscal quarter following an initial public offering at a conversion price equal to the lowest of (i) the applicable conversion price set forth above, (ii) the price per share of the common stock offered to the public in connection with such initial public offering, and (iii) the then-current market price of the Company’s common stock based on a 10-day volume-weighted trailing average trading price. The notes issued under an Amazon NPA may also be settled in cash at maturity or, at Amazon’s election, by set-off against amounts Amazon owes the Company under certain commercial agreements with Amazon.
paras.zh: 在若干清算交易中，Amazon 可选择不按适用转换价格转换该等本票，而是收取相当于未偿本金金额及其应计未付利息的现金。根据 Amazon 2024 NPA 的条款，在若干清算交易中，公司可能被要求向 Amazon 支付额外现金款项，具体计算方式载于 Amazon 2024 NPA。此外，在首次公开发行、直接上市或特殊目的收购公司交易中，适用 Amazon NPA 项下的任何未偿本金金额及其应计未付利息将自动转换为公司 N 类普通股，转换价格等于以下两者中的较低者：(i) 就 Amazon 2023 NPA 而言为 [__] $2.0928 每股，或就 Amazon 2024 NPA 而言为 [__] $5.0478 每股，以及 (ii) 该交易中向公众发售的普通股每股价格。Amazon 本票中因 Amazon 持股上限而无法转换的任何部分，将在首次公开发行后的每个财季末自动转换为 N 类普通股（受 Amazon 持股上限约束），转换价格等于以下三者中的最低者：(i) 上文所列的适用转换价格，(ii) 与该首次公开发行相关的向公众发售的普通股每股价格，以及 (iii) 基于 10 日成交量加权移动平均交易价格计算的公司普通股当时市场价格。Amazon NPA 项下发行的本票亦可在到期时以现金结算，或经 Amazon 选择，以 Amazon 根据与 Amazon 的若干商业协议欠付公司的款项进行抵销结算。

paras.en: Any conversion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA is subject to Amazon’s aggregate ownership cap, which is waivable at Amazon’s option. If any portion of the notes issued under an Amazon NPA cannot be converted without exceeding the ownership cap, the portion that could not be so converted will be re-issued as a non-interest bearing convertible rollover note, with a maturity date that is 10 years from the issuance date of such rollover note. Upon the occurrence of certain events of default as specified in the applicable Amazon NPA, the Company may be required, depending on the nature of the event of default, to repay in cash the then-outstanding principal amount that has not been converted either (i) in full upon demand of the holder or (ii) in equal installments over a four-year period.
paras.zh: Amazon NPA 项下发行的任何本票的转换均受 Amazon 合计持股上限约束，该上限可由 Amazon 选择豁免。若 Amazon NPA 项下发行的本票的任何部分在不超过持股上限的情况下无法转换，则该无法转换的部分将作为无息可转换展期本票重新发行，其到期日为该展期本票发行日起 10 年。在适用 Amazon NPA 规定的若干违约事件发生时，视违约事件的性质而定，公司可能被要求以现金偿还未转换的当时未偿本金金额，方式为 (i) 应持有人要求全额偿还，或 (ii) 在四年期间内分期等额偿还。

paras.en: In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing in 2025, the first and second tranches of notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA were converted into an aggregate of 95.3 million shares of Series E-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at a conversion price of [__] $20.9280 per share. A portion of the notes issued under Amazon 2023 NPA did not convert pursuant to Amazon’s ownership cap, and were re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note with an aggregate principal amount of $3.1 billion, maturing in March 2034. The rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, subject to Amazon’s ownership cap. In connection with the Series E-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock financing, the conversion provisions of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA were triggered. However, due to Amazon’s ownership cap, none of the notes issued under Amazon 2024 NPA converted. As a result, the first tranche was re-issued as a non-interest bearing rollover note with an aggregate principal amount of $1.3 billion maturing in January 2035 and the second and third tranches remained outstanding. Such rollover note has substantially identical conversion and repayment terms as set forth above, in each case, and converts subject to Amazon’s ownership cap.

Conversion prices were determined

paras.en: The Company determined that the SAFEs are not legal form debt (i.e., no creditors’ rights). The monetary settlement amount of the SAFEs is based upon a fixed or determinable amount known at inception, and the number of equity shares received upon conversion is variable. In such circumstances, equity classification is not appropriate because such contracts that are settled based upon a fixed amount do not expose the holder to risks and rewards similar to those of an equity-holder, therefore, the SAFEs would have been classified as marked-to-market liabilities pursuant to ASC 480.
paras.zh: 本公司认定，该等 SAFE 在法律形式上并非债务（即不赋予债权人权利）。SAFE 的货币结算金额基于在初始确认时已知的固定或可确定金额，而转换时收到的股权股份数量是可变的。在此情况下，权益分类并不适当，因为此类以固定金额结算的合同并不使持有人承担与权益持有人类似的风险和收益，因此，该等 SAFE 本应根据 ASC 480 分类为按市值计量的负债。

paras.en: As of December 31, 2024 and 2025, as well as June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company had no outstanding SAFEs.

paras.en: #### Fair Value Option
paras.zh: #### 公允价值选择权

paras.en: The Company elected to account for the SAFEs and the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 and changes in fair value related to the SAFEs and convertible notes are recorded in change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the Company’s consolidated statements of operations (Note 4). The Company elected to account for the convertible notes using the fair value option pursuant to ASC 825 to eliminate the accounting complexity that would otherwise result from separately accounting for the liability and equity components of the convertible notes under the traditional bifurcation model.
paras.zh: 公司选择依据 ASC 825 采用公允价值选择权对 SAFE 和可转换本票进行会计处理，SAFE 和可转换本票相关的公允价值变动计入公司合并经营报表中的可转换本票、衍生负债和 SAFE 的公允价值变动（附注 4）。公司选择依据 ASC 825 采用公允价值选择权对可转换本票进行会计处理，以消除若按传统分拆模型对可转换本票的负债和权益组成部分分别核算本会产生的会计复杂性。

paras.en: The estimated fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs is determined by using a scenario-based analysis that estimated the fair value of the convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs based on the probability-weighted present value of expected future investment returns, considering possible outcomes available to the SAFE and convertible note holder, including conversions to redeemable convertible preferred stock, Class N common stock and maturity. Issuance costs were expensed as incurred and are reflected in other income (expense), net in the consolidated statements of operations. Changes in fair value of the SAFEs and convertible notes and accrued interest are recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 可转换本票、衍生负债和 SAFE 的估计公允价值通过情景分析法确定，该方法基于预期未来投资回报的概率加权现值估计可转换本票、衍生负债和 SAFE 的公允价值，并考虑 SAFE 和可转换本票持有人可获得的可能结果，包括转换为可赎回可转换优先股、N 类普通股以及到期。发行成本于发生时计入费用，并反映在合并经营报表中的其他收入（费用）净额中。SAFE 和可转换本票的公允价值变动以及应计利息计入合并经营报表中的可转换本票、衍生负债和 SAFE 的公允价值变动。

paras.en: #### Derivative Liability
paras.zh: #### 衍生负债

paras.en: As of December 31, 2024, the Company had a derivative liability representing the subsequent note tranche rights on Amazon 2024 NPA. The Company applied the terms of the subsequent note tranche rights for a written call option and purchased put option scenarios and calculated a derivative liability. The changes in the fair value of the derivative liability were recorded as change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFEs in the consolidated statements of operations. Upon the second closing and third closing of the Amazon 2024 NPA during 2025, the related tranche rights were exercised and thus the derivative liability was settled and derecognized in full through the issuance of the convertible notes, with no remaining tranche rights outstanding as of December 31, 2025 [__] .
paras.zh: 截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，公司存在一项衍生负债，代表 Amazon 2024 NPA 项下的后续票据批次权利。公司就后续票据批次权利适用了写入看涨期权和购入看跌期权情景的条款，并计算了衍生负债。衍生负债的公允价值变动计入合并经营报表中的可转换本票、衍生负债和 SAFE 的公允价值变动。在 2025 年 Amazon 2024 NPA 第二次交割和第三次交割时，相关批次权利被行使，因此衍生负债通过发行可转换本票全额结算并终止确认，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日 [__] 无剩余未行使的批次权利。

The Credit Agreement provides for a senior secured revolving credit facility in an aggregate principal amount of $2.5 billion, with a $400 million letter of credit sublimit. The obligations under the Credit Agreement mature on May 14, 2030, subject to an earlier springing maturity date that is contingent upon the outstanding amount of convertible notes issued by the Company on the date that is 91 days prior to the maturity of such notes. The proceeds of the credit facility may be used for working capital, general corporate purposes, and other lawful purposes. The Company may request borrowings in U.S. dollars or certain other agreed currencies, subject to the terms of the Credit

Such dividends

paras.en: Liquidation Preference
paras.zh: 清算优先权

paras.en: In the event of any Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event), the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to receive, prior and in preference to any distribution of any of the assets of the Company to the holders of common stock, by reason of their ownership thereof, an amount per share equal to the OIP for each outstanding share of redeemable convertible preferred stock then held (as adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends, reclassifications and the like), plus any declared but unpaid dividends on such shares. If, upon the occurrence of such event, the assets and funds thus distributed among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be insufficient to permit the payment to such holders of the full aforesaid preferential amounts, then the entire assets and funds of the Company legally available for distribution shall be distributed ratably among the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock in proportion to the preferential amount each such holder is otherwise entitled to receive, and provided that the holders of redeemable convertible preferred stock will be treated on an as-converted basis if, as a result of an actual conversion, such holder would receive, in the aggregate, an amount greater than the amount that would be distributed to such holder if such holder did not convert such series of preferred stock into shares of such series of common stock.
paras.zh: 在任何清算交易（一般定义为公司的任何自愿或非自愿清算、解散或停业，或视为清算事件）发生时，可赎回可转换优先股持有人有权优先于公司普通股持有人因其所有权而获得的任何公司资产分配，就当时持有的每股可赎回可转换优先股获得相当于 OIP 的每股金额（经股票拆分、股票股息、重分类等调整），加上该等股份上任何已宣布但未支付的股息。如果在该事件发生时，如此在可赎回可转换优先股持有人之间分配的资产和资金不足以向该等持有人支付上述全部优先金额，则公司合法可用于分配的全部资产和资金应按各该持有人原本有权获得的优先金额的比例，在可赎回可转换优先股持有人之间按比例分配，并且如果由于实际转换，该持有人合计将获得的金额大于该持有人未将该系列优先股转换为该系列普通股股份时将获得的分配金额，则可赎回可转换优先股持有人将按转换后基准处理。

paras.en: Conversion
paras.zh: 转换

paras.en: Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into fully paid and non-assessable shares of Class A common stock, in the case of the Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock. Each share of non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into fully paid and non-assessable shares of Class N common stock (non-voting common stock), in the case of the Series B, Series C-2, Series D-3, Series E-2, Series E-3, Series E-4, Series E-5, Series F-2, Series F-3, Series F-4, Series G-2, Series G-3, Series G-4, Series H-2, Series H-3, and Series H-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock.
paras.zh: 每股可赎回可转换优先股可转换为缴足且不可加缴的 A 类普通股股份，就 A 轮、C-1 轮、D-1 轮、D-2 轮、E-1 轮、F-1 轮、G-1 轮和 H-1 轮可赎回可转换优先股而言。每股无表决权可赎回可转换优先股可转换为缴足且不可加缴的 N 类普通股（无表决权普通股）股份，就 B 轮、C-2 轮、D-3 轮、E-2 轮、E-3 轮、E-4 轮、E-5 轮、F-2 轮、F-3 轮、F-4 轮、G-2 轮、G-3 轮、G-4 轮、H-2 轮、H-3 轮和 H-4 轮无表决权可赎回可转换优先股而言。

paras.en: - Optional conversion – Each share of redeemable convertible preferred stock is convertible into Class A common stock or Class N common stock, as applicable, at any time after the issuance of shares at the option of the holder. The conversion rate is determined by dividing the applicable original issue price by the conversion price. As of December 31, 2024, the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was [__] 10:1. In connection with the Series E redeemable convertible preferred stock financing during the year ended December 31, 2025, the issuance of Series E-2 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock at $20.9280 per share triggered weighted-average antidilution adjustments to the conversion prices of the Series D-1, D-2, and D-3 redeemable convertible preferred stock. As of December 31, 2025, the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was 10: [__] 1, except for the Series D-1, Series D-2, and Series D-3 redeemable convertible preferred stock, which were approximately [__] 10.5, 10.4, and [__] 10.5, respectively. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the conversion ratio for all series of redeemable convertible preferred stock was [__] 10:1, except for the Series D-1, Series D-2, and Series D-3, which were approximately [__] 10.6:1, 10.4:1, and [__] 10.6:1, respectively. Upon conversion, no adjustments to the conversion price shall be made for any declared but unpaid dividends on the redeemable convertible preferred stock surrendered for conversion or on the common stock delivered upon conversion.
paras.zh: - 可选转换——每股可赎回可转换优先股可在股份发行后任何时间由持有人选择转换为 A 类普通股或 N 类普通股（如适用）。转换比率通过将适用的原始发行价格除以转换价格确定。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日，所有系列可赎回可转换优先股的转换比率为[__] 10:1。在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度的 E 轮可赎回可转换优先股融资中，以每股$20.9280 发行 E-2 轮无表决权可赎回可转换优先股触发了对 D-1 轮、D-2 轮和 D-3 轮可赎回可转换优先股转换价格的加权平均反稀释调整。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，所有系列可赎回可转换优先股的转换比率为 10: [__] 1，但 D-1 轮、D-2 轮和 D-3 轮可赎回可转换优先股除外，其转换比率分别约为[__] 10.5、10.4 和[__] 10.5。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），所有系列可赎回可转换优先股的转换比率为[__] 10:1，但 D-1 轮、D-2 轮和 D-3 轮除外，其转换比率分别约为[__] 10.6:1、10.4:1 和[__] 10.6:1。转换时，不得就交回转换的可赎回可转换优先股或转换时交付的普通股的任何已宣派但未支付股息对转换价格作出任何调整。

paras.en: The holders of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to the same voting rights and powers as the holders of the Class A common stock and to notice of any stockholders’ meeting in accordance with the bylaws of the Company, and the holders of Class A common stock and the holders of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall vote together as a single class on all matters. Each holder of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock shall be entitled to the number of votes equal to the number of shares of Class A common stock into which such shares of Series A, Series C-1, Series D-1, Series D-2, Series E-1, Series F-1, Series G-1, and Series H-1 redeemable convertible preferred stock, respectively, could be converted.
paras.zh: A 轮、C-1 轮、D-1 轮、D-2 轮、E-1 轮、F-1 轮、G-1 轮和 H-1 轮可赎回可转换优先股的持有人应享有与 A 类普通股持有人相同的投票权和权力，并有权根据公司章程获得任何股东大会的通知，A 类普通股持有人与 A 轮、C-1 轮、D-1 轮、D-2 轮、E-1 轮、F-1 轮、G-1 轮和 H-1 轮可赎回可转换优先股的持有人应就所有事项作为单一类别共同投票。A 轮、C-1 轮、D-1 轮、D-2 轮、E-1 轮、F-1 轮、G-1 轮和 H-1 轮可赎回可转换优先股的每位持有人有权获得的投票数等于该等 A 轮、C-1 轮、D-1 轮、D-2 轮、E-1 轮、F-1 轮、G-1 轮和 H-1 轮可赎回可转换优先股分别可转换成的 A 类普通股股数。

paras.en: The holders of Series B, Series C-2, Series D-3, Series E-2, Series E-3, Series E-4, Series E-5, Series F-2, Series F-3, Series F-4, Series G-2, Series G-3, Series G-4, Series H-2, Series H-3, and Series H-4 non-voting redeemable convertible preferred stock shall not be entitled to vote and shall have no voting rights, except as required by law or as specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation, and shall have no right to vote in any election of the Board.
paras.zh: B、C-2、D-3、E-2、E-3、E-4、E-5、F-2、F-3、F-4、G-2、G-3、G-4、H-2、H-3 和 H-4 系列无表决权可赎回可转换优先股的持有人不享有表决权，且无任何表决权，但法律要求或公司章程中明确规定的除外，并且在任何董事会选举中均无表决权。

paras.en: Redemption
paras.zh: 赎回

paras.en: The holders of the redeemable convertible preferred stock have no voluntary rights to redeem shares. The redeemable convertible preferred stockholders have liquidation preferences in the event of any Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event). Although the redeemable convertible preferred stock is not mandatorily or currently redeemable, a deemed liquidation event could constitute a redemption event outside the Company’s control. Therefore, all shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock have been presented outside of permanent equity.
paras.zh: 可赎回可转换优先股的持有人不享有自愿要求赎回股份的权利。可赎回可转换优先股股东在任何清算交易（一般定义为公司的任何自愿或非自愿清算、解散或停业清理，或视为清算事件）发生时享有清算优先权。尽管可赎回可转换优先股并非强制赎回或当前可赎回，但视为清算事件可能构成公司无法控制的赎回事件。因此，所有可赎回可转换优先股股份均在永久性权益之外列示。

paras.en: The Company recorded shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock issued for cash at their respective issuance price less issuance costs on the dates of issuance. Shares of redeemable convertible preferred stock issued upon conversion of convertible notes were recorded at the fair value of the respective convertible note immediately prior to conversion. The carrying values of the Company’s redeemable convertible preferred stock have not been accreted to their redemption values as the liquidation event is not considered probable of occurring. Subsequent adjustments of the carrying values to redemption values will be made only if and when it becomes probable the convertible preferred stock will become redeemable.
paras.zh: 公司按发行日的各自发行价格减去发行费用，记录以现金发行的可赎回可转换优先股股份。因可转换本票转换而发行的可赎回可转换优先股股份，按紧接转换前各可转换本票的公允价值记录。由于清算事件被认为不太可能发生，公司可赎回可转换优先股的账面价值未增加至其赎回价值。只有在可转换优先股很可能变为可赎回时，才会对账面价值进行后续调整至赎回价值。

paras.en: #### Common Stock
paras.zh: #### 普通股

paras.en: The Company has one class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” and another class of capital stock designated “Class T common stock.” The class of capital stock designated “participating common stock” is divided into two series, designated “Class A common stock” and “Class N common stock.” The certificate of incorporation, as amended and restated August 27, 2025, authorized the Company to issue up to 8,162.8 million shares of Class A common stock, 5,547.2 million shares of Class N common stock, and [__] 1 share of Class T common stock. The certificate of incorporation, as amended and restated May 27, 2026 (unaudited), authorized the Company to issue up to 10,991.0 million shares of Class A common stock, 7,044.0 million shares of Class N common stock, and [__] 1 share of Class T common stock. Holders of Class A common stock are entitled to one vote per share. The holders of Class N common stock shall have no right to vote, generally, except as required by law, including no right to vote in any election of the Board, except as required by law. The holders of Class T common stock have no right to vote generally, except as required by law or specifically set forth in the certificate of incorporation. The participating common stock is subordinate to the redeemable convertible preferred stock with respect to dividend rights and rights upon liquidation, winding up, and dissolution of the Company. The Class T common stock is not mandatorily redeemable and does not entitle the holder thereof to receive dividends or any distribution of assets upon the liquidation, winding up, or dissolution of the Company or the occurrence of a Liquidation Transaction (defined, generally, as any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution or winding up of the Company or deemed liquidation event).
paras.zh: 公司有一类股本被指定为“参与普通股”，另一类股本被指定为“T 类普通股”。被指定为“参与普通股”的股本类别分为两个系列，分别指定为“A 类普通股”和“N 类普通股”。经修订和重述于 2025 年 8 月 27 日的公司章程授权公司发行最多 8,162.8 百万股 A 类普通股、5,547.2 百万股 N 类普通股和 [__] 1 股 T 类普通股。经修订和重述于 2026 年 5 月 27 日的公司章程（未经审计）授权公司发行最多 10,991.0 百万股 A 类普通股、7,044.0 百万股 N 类普通股和 [__] 1 股 T 类普通股。A 类普通股持有人每股享有一票投票权。N 类普通股持有人一般无投票权，但法律另有规定者除外，包括在董事会任何选举中无投票权，但法律另有规定者除外。T 类普通股持有人一般无投票权，但法律另有规定或公司章程另有明确规定者除外。参与普通股在股息权以及公司清算、歇业和解散时的权利方面次于可赎回可转换优先股。T 类普通股不可强制赎回，且其持有人无权在公司清算、歇业或解散或发生清算交易（一般定义为公司的任何自愿或非自愿清算、解散或歇业或视为清算事件）时获得股息或任何资产分配。

#### Equity Compensation Plan
paras.zh: #### 股权激励计划

paras.en: In January 2021, the Board approved the 2021 Stock Plan (the “Plan”). The Plan allows for the award of incentive stock options, non-statutory stock options, restricted stock awards, and RSUs to employees, non-employee directors, and consultants of the Company. As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), there were 3,112.4 million shares and 3,864.8 million shares, respectively, of common stock reserved for issuance under the Plan, with 287.6 million shares and 569.1 million shares, respectively, available to be issued. Options issued under the Plan generally are exercisable for periods not to exceed ten years and generally vest over either four years with [__] 25% vesting after one year and with the remainder vesting monthly thereafter in equal installments, or over one year with 100% vesting after one year. Effective January 2026 (unaudited), options issued under the Plan generally are exercisable for periods not to exceed 10 years and generally vest over either four years with [__] 12.5% vesting after six months and with the remainder vesting monthly thereafter in equal installments, or over one year with [__] 50% vesting after six months and with the remainder vesting monthly thereafter in equal installments.

paras.en: #### Restricted Stock Units
paras.zh: #### 限制性股票单位

paras.en: The Company grants RSUs to employees and the RSUs vest upon the satisfaction of both a service condition and a performance condition. The service condition for these awards is generally satisfied over a four-year vesting period. The performance condition is satisfied upon the occurrence of an “initial event” which is defined as either (i) a qualifying change in control of the Company or (ii) a listing of the Company’s equity securities on an established securities market (including through a traditional public offering, direct listing, or business combination with a special purpose acquisition company), in each case, on or before the seventh anniversary of the grant date, as further defined in such RSU agreements. If the performance condition is not satisfied within seven years of the grant date, all unvested RSUs are forfeited.
paras.zh: 公司向员工授予 RSU，该等 RSU 在同时满足服务条件和业绩条件后归属。该等奖励的服务条件通常在四年归属期内满足。业绩条件在发生“初始事件”时满足，该初始事件定义为 (i) 公司发生符合条件的控制权变更，或 (ii) 公司股权证券在成熟证券市场上市（包括通过传统公开发行、直接上市或与特殊目的收购公司进行业务合并），且在任何一种情况下均须在授予日起第七个周年日或之前发生，具体以该等 RSU 协议中的进一步定义为准。如果业绩条件未在授予日起七年内满足，则所有未归属的 RSU 将被没收。

paras.en: As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), no stock-based compensation expense had been recognized for the RSUs because management determined that it is not probable that the performance condition will be achieved. If management had determined the performance condition was probable of achievement as of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company would have recognized $671 million and $2.9 billion, respectively, of cumulative stock-based compensation expense as of the respective dates and would have had $5.2 billion and $23.7 billion, respectively, of unrecognized compensation cost that represents the RSUs that have not satisfied the service condition for vesting. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), unrecognized compensation cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of 2.1 years [__] .
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），由于管理层判定业绩条件很可能无法达成，公司未就 RSU 确认任何股权激励费用。如果管理层在 2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）判定业绩条件很可能达成，公司本应分别在相应日期确认 $671 million 和 $2.9 billion 的累计股权激励费用，并分别拥有 $5.2 billion 和 $23.7 billion 的未确认补偿成本，该成本代表尚未满足归属服务条件的 RSU。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），未确认补偿成本预计将在 2.1 年的加权平均期间内确认 [__] 。

paras.en: #### Restricted Stock Awards (“RSAs”)
paras.zh: #### 限制性股票奖励（“RSAs”）

paras.en: In January and February 2021, the Company granted a total of 1,731.3 million RSAs to founders and early employees that vested based on the passage of time (i.e., a service condition). The Company also grants RSAs to certain non-employee service providers. The RSAs are shares of common stock that are issued and outstanding and are subject to repurchase by the Company (for a minimal amount) if the holder’s service terminates before the restricted shares vest. Compensation cost is measured at the grant-date fair value of the underlying common stock and is recognized over the vesting period.

paras.en: #### Share Repurchases
paras.zh: #### 股份回购

paras.en: During the year ended December 31, 2025, the Company repurchased and immediately retired 27.9 million shares of common stock from certain former and current service providers at a purchase price of [__] $5.61 per share, which was in excess of the then-current fair market value at the time of repurchase. The aggregate fair value of the shares repurchased was $149 million, which was recorded as an increase in accumulated deficit. The excess of the repurchase price over the fair market value of the shares at the date of repurchase was recognized as stock-based compensation expense of $7 million in the consolidated statement of operations.
paras.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，公司以每股 [__] $5.61 的购买价格向若干前任及现任服务提供者回购并随即注销了 27.9 百万股普通股，该价格高于回购当时的现行公允市场价值。所回购股份的公允价值合计为 $149 百万，已计入累计亏损的增加。回购价格超过回购日股份公允市场价值的部分，已在合并经营报表中确认为 $7 百万的股权激励费用。

paras.zh: 截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计），公司未回购任何股份。

paras.en: In February 2026 (unaudited), the Company’s Board of Directors approved an offer by a group of third-party buyers to purchase shares of the Company’s Class A common stock at a price of [__] $25.9136 per share from sellers that included current and former employees, non-employee service providers, and donor advised funds. The tender offer closed in April 2026, and an aggregate of 179.9 million shares were sold. Shares sold in the tender offer were sold at fair value, and accordingly, no stock-based compensation expense was recognized in connection with the transaction.
paras.zh: 2026 年 2 月（未经审计），公司董事会批准由一组第三方买方以每股 [__] $25.9136 的价格向包括现任及前任员工、非雇员服务提供者以及捐赠人建议基金在内的卖方购买公司 A 类普通股的要约。该要约收购于 2026 年 4 月完成交割，合计售出 179.9 百万股。要约收购中售出的股份按公允价值出售，因此未就该交易确认任何股权激励费用。

paras.en: #### Donation Matching Plan
paras.zh: #### 捐赠配比计划

paras.en: In November 2021, the Company adopted its donation matching plan (“Donation Matching Plan”) whereby eligible employees of the Company can pledge to donate to eligible nonprofit organizations, including 501(c)(3) tax exempt organizations, and have the Company match such donation on the terms set forth in the Donation Matching Plan. The Company may elect, at its sole discretion and per the terms of the Donation Matching Plan, to match the donation in shares of Class N common stock or in cash in an equivalent value. As of December 31, 2024 and 2025, 964.3 million shares of common stock were reserved for issuance under the Donation Matching Plan, and no shares are issued or outstanding. As of June 30, 2026 (unaudited), 933.7 million shares of common stock were reserved for issuance under the Donation Matching Plan. During the six months ended June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company recognized a change in fair value of $126 million of the donation matching program liability within other operating and administrative expense in the consolidated statements of operations and issued 30.6 million shares of Class N common stock upon settlement of its donation matching obligation in the first quarter of 2026 (unaudited). As of December 31, 2024 and [__] 2025 and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), the Company accrued zero, $541 million, and zero, respectively, within accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets, representing the estimated fair value of the current obligations to match employee donations under the donation matching program based on observable and unobservable inputs, specifically considering the price of the Company’s common stock. Donation matching expense is included within other operating and administrative expenses in the consolidated statements of operations.
paras.zh: 2021 年 11 月，公司通过了其捐赠配比计划（“捐赠配比计划”），据此，公司合资格员工可承诺向合资格非营利组织(包括 501(c)(3) 免税组织)捐赠，并由公司按捐赠配比计划所载条款对该等捐赠进行配比。公司可自行决定并根据捐赠配比计划的条款，选择以 N 类普通股股份或等值现金进行配比捐赠。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日和 2025 年 12 月 31 日，已预留 964.3 百万股普通股供捐赠配比计划项下发行，且无已发行或流通在外的股份。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），已预留 933.7 百万股普通股供捐赠配比计划项下发行。截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计），公司在合并经营报表的其他经营及管理费用中确认了 $126 百万的捐赠配比计划负债公允价值变动，并于 2026 年第一季度（未经审计）在结算其捐赠配比义务时发行了 30.6 百万股 N 类普通股。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日、[__] 2025 年及 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），公司分别在合并资产负债表上的应付账款、应计费用及其他流动负债中计提了零、$541 百万和零，代表根据可观察和不可观察输入（特别是考虑公司普通股价格）估算的捐赠配比计划项下当前配比员工捐赠义务的公允价值。捐赠配比费用计入合并经营报表的其他经营及管理费用。

paras.en: In determining the need for a valuation allowance, the Company reviewed both positive and negative evidence bearing upon its ability to realize the deferred tax assets. Management has considered the Company’s history of cumulative net losses incurred since inception and has concluded that it is more likely than not that the Company will not realize the benefits of the deferred tax assets. Accordingly, a full valuation allowance was established against the Company’s U.S. and foreign net deferred tax assets as of December 31, 2025 [__] . Management reevaluates the positive and negative evidence at each reporting period.
paras.zh: 在确定是否需要计提估值备抵时，公司审查了与实现递延所得税资产能力相关的正面和负面证据。管理层已考虑公司自成立以来累计净亏损的历史，并得出结论：公司很可能无法实现递延所得税资产的利益。因此，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日 [__]，公司已就其美国及境外递延所得税资产净额全额计提估值备抵。管理层在每个报告期重新评估正面和负面证据。

paras.en: carryforwards that can be utilized annually to offset future taxable income and future income tax, respectively. In general, an ownership change as defined by Section 382 results from transactions increasing the ownership of certain stockholders or public groups in the stock of a corporation by more than 50% over a three-year period. The Company last completed a Section 382 analysis as of December 31, 2023, and has determined that ownership changes have taken place in October 2021 and September 2023. However, no limitations on the utilization of tax attributes were identified as of that date. A Section 382 study has not been conducted subsequent to December 31, 2023. Ownership changes that may have occurred in 2024 and 2025 may therefore subject tax attributes to a yearly limitation.
paras.zh: 结转额，分别可在每年用于抵减未来应纳税所得额和未来所得税。一般而言，第 382 条所定义的所有权变更，是指某些股东或公众群体在一家公司股票中的持股比例在三年期内增加超过 50%的交易。公司最近一次完成第 382 条分析是在 2023 年 12 月 31 日，并已认定所有权变更曾于 2021 年 10 月和 2023 年 9 月发生。但是，截至该日并未识别出对税收属性使用的限制。2023 年 12 月 31 日之后未再进行第 382 条研究。因此，2024 年和 2025 年可能发生的所有权变更可能使税收属性受到年度限制。

paras.en: The Company files tax returns in the United States and various state and foreign jurisdictions in which the Company conducts business activities. The federal and state income tax returns are subject to examination for all tax years, the tax returns in the United Kingdom are open from 2023 onwards and the Ireland tax returns are open from 2024 onwards. To the extent the Company has tax attribute carryforwards, the tax years in which the attribute was generated may still be adjusted upon examination by the Internal Revenue Service (“IRS”) or state tax authorities to the extent utilized in a future period. Additionally, the Company is subject to tax examinations by tax authorities in foreign jurisdictions where it has business operations. There are currently no federal, state, or foreign audits in progress by the IRS or any other jurisdictions for any tax years.
paras.zh: 本公司在开展业务活动的美国及多个州和外国司法管辖区提交纳税申报表。联邦和州所得税申报表在所有纳税年度均可能接受审查，英国纳税申报表自 2023 年起处于开放状态，爱尔兰纳税申报表自 2024 年起处于开放状态。在本公司存在可结转税务属性的范围内，产生该属性的纳税年度在日后期间被使用时，仍可能因美国国税局（“IRS”）或州税务机关的审查而被调整。此外，本公司在其开展业务运营的外国司法管辖区还须接受税务机关的税务审查。目前，IRS 或任何其他司法管辖区均未对任何纳税年度开展联邦、州或外国审计。

paras.en: Given the Company’s full valuation allowance, none of the unrecognized tax benefits, if recognized, would affect the Company’s effective tax rate. paras.en: The Company is involved from time to time in claims, proceedings, and litigation, including the following:
paras.zh: 公司不时涉及索赔、诉讼程序及诉讼，包括以下事项：

paras.en: In August 2024, various authors filed suit against the Company alleging infringement of copyrighted books in the case of Bartz, et al. v. Anthropic in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California (“Bartz”). The complaint alleged, among other things, copyright infringement related to the use of literary works used in the training of the Company’s large language models. The complaint sought certification as a class action, unspecified amounts of damages, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees, costs, and interest. The Company reached a settlement in the amount of $1.5 billion and the interest earned thereon, which was approved by the district court in July 2026. The Company paid $300 million during the year ended December 31, 2025 and recorded liabilities of $750 million in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities and $450 million in other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2025, and $1.2 billion in accounts payable, accrued expenses, and other current liabilities as of June 30, 2026 (unaudited).
paras.zh: 2024 年 8 月，多名作者在加利福尼亚州北区美国联邦地区法院对该公司提起诉讼，案名为 Bartz 等人诉 Anthropic（“Bartz 案”），指控其侵犯受版权保护的书籍。起诉状指控，除其他事项外，该公司在训练其大语言模型时使用文学作品构成版权侵权。起诉状请求认定为集体诉讼，并寻求未明确金额的损害赔偿、禁令救济、律师费、诉讼费用及利息。公司达成金额为$1.5 billion 的和解协议及相应利息，该和解已于 2026 年 7 月获地区法院批准。公司在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度内支付了$300 million，并在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的合并资产负债表上确认应付账款、应计费用及其他流动负债$750 million 和其他非流动负债$450 million，以及在截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计）确认应付账款、应计费用及其他流动负债$1.2 billion。

paras.en: In October 2023, Concord Music Group et al. filed a complaint against the Company in the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Tennessee (“Concord I”). The complaint alleges, among other things, that in the process of building and operating the Company models, the Company unlawfully copied and disseminated copyrighted lyrics controlled by the publishers. It also asserts a claim for unlawful removal of copyright management information. The complaint seeks unspecified amounts of damages, injunctive relief, attorneys’ fees, costs, and interest. The case was later transferred to the Northern District of California. Both parties filed motions for summary judgment and the court held a hearing on October 21, 2026. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in this matter.
paras.zh: 2023 年 10 月，Concord Music Group 等人在田纳西州中区美国联邦地区法院对该公司提起诉讼（“Concord I 案”）。起诉状指控，除其他事项外，该公司在构建和运营公司模型的过程中非法复制和传播由出版商控制的受版权保护的歌词。起诉状还主张非法移除版权管理信息。起诉状寻求未明确金额的损害赔偿、禁令救济、律师费、诉讼费用及利息。该案随后被移送至加利福尼亚州北区。双方均提交了简易判决动议，法院于 2026 年 10 月 21 日举行了听证。公司否认存在不当行为的指控，并打算在本案中积极抗辩。

paras.en: The Company is also subject to four copyright actions in Canada. In May and July 2025, two putative class actions were filed on behalf of purported classes of Canadian authors - one in British Columbia (“MacKinnon”) on behalf of all Canadian authors, and one in Québec (“Grescoe”) on behalf of all Québec authors - each alleging violations of Canada’s Copyright Act based on the Company’s copying and use of copyrighted books to train its large language models. Grescoe has been stayed pending a final judgment in MacKinnon. In July 2026, La Presse Inc., a Québec news publisher, filed a copyright infringement action against the Company in the Québec Superior Court alleging that the Company reproduced its journalistic works in the data used to train the Company’s models. In October 2026, a group of Canadian news publishers filed a claim against the Company in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice. The plaintiffs allege the Company copied their content from their websites to develop its Claude models. They further allege the Company breached the websites’ terms of service and circumvented technological protection measures. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these matters.
paras.zh: 公司还在加拿大面临四起版权诉讼。2025 年 5 月和 7 月，有人代表所谓的加拿大作者集体提起了两起推定集体诉讼——一起在卑诗省提起（“MacKinnon 案”），代表全体加拿大作者；一起在魁北克省提起（“Grescoe 案”），代表全体魁北克作者——两案均指控该公司复制和使用受版权保护的书籍以训练其大语言模型，违反了加拿大《版权法》。Grescoe 案已中止审理，等待 MacKinnon 案的最终判决。2026 年 7 月，魁北克新闻出版商 La Presse Inc.在魁北克高等法院对该公司提起版权侵权诉讼，指控该公司在用于训练其模型的数据中复制了其新闻作品。2026 年 10 月，一群加拿大新闻出版商在安大略省高等法院对该公司提起诉讼。原告指控该公司从其网站复制内容以开发其 Claude 模型。他们还指控该公司违反了网站的服务条款并规避了技术保护措施。公司否认存在不当行为的指控，并打算在这些事项中积极抗辩。

paras.en: In June 2025, Reddit, Inc. filed suit against the Company in California state court alleging various claims, including breach of contract and trespass to chattels, stemming from allegations about the Company’s use of Reddit data in building and operating its models. In September 2026, the state court narrowed the case to Reddit’s breach of contract, interference with contract, and unfair competition claims. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in this matter.
paras.zh: 2025 年 6 月，Reddit, Inc.在加利福尼亚州法院对公司提起诉讼，指控多项诉由，包括违约和侵害动产，其依据是关于公司在构建和运营其模型时使用 Reddit 数据的指控。2026 年 9 月，该州法院将案件范围缩小至 Reddit 的违约、干涉合同和不正当竞争诉由。公司否认有关不当行为的指控，并打算在此事项中积极抗辩。

The complaints allege, among other things, that the Company unlawfully copied the plaintiffs’ copyrighted song lyrics and musical compositions, and assert claims for direct and indirect copyright infringement based on both the acquisition and use of copyrighted materials to train the Company’s

paras.zh: 公司面临多起推定集体诉讼，指控其通过虚假、误导性和欺骗性广告行为营销和销售 Claude 订阅计划。这些事项一般处于早期阶段。公司否认有关不当行为的指控，并打算在这些诉讼中积极抗辩。

The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing in these remaining opt-out actions and intends to defend itself vigorously in all matters. These proceedings remain in various stages.
paras.zh: 多名作者和出版商已选择退出 Bartz 案中达成的集体诉讼和解，并对公司提起单独诉讼，一般指控直接版权侵权、帮助版权侵权以及删除与用于训练公司大型语言模型的文学作品相关的版权管理信息。公司否认这些剩余选择退出诉讼中的不当行为指控，并打算在所有事项中积极抗辩。这些程序仍处于不同阶段。

paras.en: The Company has received notices, demands, and other communications from several authors and individual rights-holders, publishers (including, but not limited to, book, news, and music publishers), platforms and website operators, and trade associations, in the United States and other jurisdictions (collectively, “Rights-Holders”) alleging unauthorized acquisition or use of content, removal of copyright management information, violation of terms of service, and violation of copyrights. Some Rights-Holders have also sought to have their content removed from the Company’s training corpus or sought more information on how their content was used in the development of the Company’s models. Other Rights-Holders have argued that the mere crawling of their sites has harmed them. The Company expects to continue to receive similar notices from Rights-Holders, which may ultimately result in litigation against the Company. The Company disputes the allegations of wrongdoing and intends to defend itself vigorously in these matters.
paras.zh: 公司已收到来自美国及其他司法管辖区若干作者和个人权利持有人、出版商（包括但不限于图书、新闻和音乐出版商）、平台和网站运营商以及行业协会（统称“权利持有人”）的通知、要求和其他函件，指控未经授权获取或使用内容、删除版权管理信息、违反服务条款以及侵犯版权。部分权利持有人还要求将其内容从公司的训练语料库中删除，或要求提供有关其内容在公司模型开发过程中如何被使用的更多信息。其他权利持有人则主张，仅对其网站进行爬取即已对其造成损害。公司预计将继续收到权利持有人的类似通知，最终可能导致针对公司的诉讼。公司对不当行为的指控予以否认，并打算在此类事项中积极抗辩。

paras.en: From time to time, the Company is subject to inquiries, investigations, subpoenas and requests for information from federal, state, and foreign governmental authorities, including the U.S. Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general, regarding, among other things, consumer protection, data protection and privacy, and the safety and security of the Company’s products.
paras.zh: 公司不时受到联邦、州和外国政府机构（包括美国联邦贸易委员会和各州总检察长）的询问、调查、传票和信息请求，涉及的事项包括消费者保护、数据保护和隐私，以及公司产品的安全与保障等。

paras.en: In addition, from time to time, the Company is subject to claims, litigation, and other proceedings, including potential regulatory proceedings, involving patent and other intellectual property matters, taxes, labor and employment, competition, privacy and data protection, consumer protection, commercial disputes, and services offered by the Company, and other matters. The outcomes of the Company’s legal proceedings and other contingencies are inherently unpredictable, subject to significant uncertainties, and could be material to its operating results and cash flows for a particular period. The Company evaluates, on a regular basis, developments in its legal proceedings and other contingencies that could affect the amount of liability, including amounts in excess of any previous accruals and reasonably possible losses disclosed, and makes adjustments and changes to its accruals and disclosures as appropriate. For the matters the Company discloses that do not include an estimate of the amount of loss or range of losses, such an estimate is not possible or is immaterial, and the Company may be unable to estimate the possible loss or range of losses that could potentially result from the application of non-monetary remedies. Until the final resolution of such matters, if any of the Company’s estimates and assumptions change or prove to have been incorrect, the Company may experience losses in excess of the amounts recorded, which could have a material effect on its business, consolidated financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.
paras.zh: 此外，公司不时面临索赔、诉讼和其他程序（包括潜在的监管程序），涉及专利和其他知识产权事项、税务、劳动与就业、竞争、隐私与数据保护、消费者保护、商业纠纷以及公司提供的服务和其他事项。公司法律程序及其他或有事项的结果本质上不可预测，存在重大不确定性，并可能对特定期间的经营业绩和现金流量产生重大影响。公司定期评估其法律程序及其他或有事项中可能影响负债金额（包括超过以往任何计提金额和已披露的合理可能损失金额）的进展，并酌情调整和变更其计提和披露。对于公司披露但未包含损失金额或损失区间估计的事项，该等估计不可能作出或并不重大，且公司可能无法估计适用非金钱救济可能导致的潜在损失或损失区间。在此类事项最终解决之前，如果公司的任何估计和假设发生变化或被证明不正确，公司可能遭受超过已记录金额的损失，这可能对其业务、合并财务状况、经营业绩或现金流量产生重大影响。

paras.en: #### Indemnification Agreements
paras.zh: #### 赔偿协议

paras.en: The Company enters into standard indemnification agreements in the ordinary course of business. Pursuant to these arrangements, the Company indemnifies, holds harmless, and agrees to reimburse the indemnified parties for losses suffered or incurred by the indemnified party, in connection with any trade secret, copyright, patent, independent testing and evaluation of the Company’s models, or other intellectual property
paras.zh: 本公司在日常业务过程中订立标准赔偿协议。根据该等安排，本公司就任何第三方针对其技术提出的商业秘密、著作权、专利、对本公司模型的独立测试与评估或其他知识产权侵权索赔，对受赔偿方遭受或发生的损失予以赔偿、使其免受损害并同意予以补偿。该等赔偿义务在若干情形下不受上限限制。该等赔偿协议的期限通常为协议签署后永久有效。本公司根据该等协议未来可能被要求支付的最高潜在金额无法确定，因为其涉及未来可能对本公司提出但尚未提出的索赔。本公司迄今未因与该等赔偿协议相关的诉讼抗辩或索赔和解而发生费用。

paras.en: #### Employee Benefit Plan
paras.zh: #### 员工福利计划

paras.en: The Company has a qualified defined contribution plan under Section 401(k) of the Internal Revenue Code covering eligible employees. A portion of employee contributions are matched up to a fixed maximum dollar amount per year per eligible employee. During the years ended December 31, 2023, [__] 2024, and 2025, matching contributions related to the plan were $2 million, $7 million, and $15 million, respectively, and during the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), matching contributions were $7 million and $20 million, respectively [__] .
paras.zh: 本公司设有符合《美国国内税收法典》第 401(k) 条规定的合格固定缴款计划，覆盖符合条件的员工。员工缴款的一部分可按每名符合条件的员工每年固定最高美元金额获得匹配缴款。截至 2023 年 12 月 31 日、[__] 2024 年及 2025 年止年度，与该计划相关的匹配缴款分别为 $2 million、$7 million 和 $15 million；截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日及 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计），匹配缴款分别为 $7 million 和 $20 million [__] 。

paras.en: The Company’s chief operating decision maker (“CODM”) is the leadership team consisting of the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and President. The Company operates its business in one operating segment and, therefore, has one reportable segment. The CODM utilizes financial information presented on a consolidated basis for purposes of making operating decisions, assessing financial performance, and allocating resources including, but not limited to, the Company’s consolidated net loss.
paras.zh: 公司的首席经营决策者（“CODM”）是由公司首席执行官和总裁组成的领导团队。公司以单一经营分部运营业务，因此拥有一个报告分部。CODM 利用以合并基础呈列的财务信息进行经营决策、评估财务业绩并分配资源，包括但不限于公司的合并净亏损。

paras.en: The CODM uses consolidated net loss as the measure of segment profit or loss. The CODM uses consolidated net loss to evaluate overall financial performance, monitor budget-to-actual results, assess the return on the Company’s investments in compute and infrastructure, personnel, and other operating activities to inform decisions regarding the allocation of capital and personnel resources across the Company’s operations. There are no other expense categories regularly provided to the CODM that are not already included in the primary consolidated financial statements, except that stock-based compensation expense is separately provided to the CODM as a discrete component within the Personnel line item. Stock-based compensation expense was [__] $29 million, $192 million, and $1.2 billion for the years ended December 31, 2023, [__] 2024, and 2025, and [__] $286 million and $2.2 billion for the six months ended June 30, 2025 and 2026 (unaudited), respectively. The CODM does not evaluate operating segments using asset information.
paras.zh: CODM 将合并净亏损作为分部损益的衡量指标。CODM 利用合并净亏损评估整体财务业绩、监控预算与实际结果的对比、评估公司对算力和基础设施、人员及其他经营活动的投资回报，从而为公司在各项业务之间分配资本和人员资源的决策提供依据。除股权激励费用作为人员费用项目中的一项单独组成部分另行提供给 CODM 外，不存在其他定期提供给 CODM 且未包含在主要合并财务报表中的费用类别。截至 2023 年、[__] 2024 年和 2025 年 12 月 31 日止年度，股权激励费用分别为 [__] $29 million、$192 million 和 $1.2 billion；截至 2025 年和 2026 年 6 月 30 日止六个月（未经审计），股权激励费用分别为 [__] $286 million 和 $2.2 billion。CODM 不使用资产信息评估经营分部。

paras.en: Long-lived assets, which consist of property and equipment, net, and operating lease right-of-use assets, by geographic location are based on the physical location of the assets. As of December 31, 2024, December 31, 2025, and June 30, 2026 (unaudited), approximately [__] 94%, 95%, and [__] 95%, respectively, of the Company’s long-lived assets were located in the United States.
paras.zh: 长期资产由物业及设备净额和经营租赁使用权资产构成，其按地理位置的划分以资产的实物所在地为依据。截至 2024 年 12 月 31 日、2025 年 12 月 31 日和 2026 年 6 月 30 日（未经审计），公司分别约有 [__] 94%、95% 和 [__] 95% 的长期资产位于美国。

paras.en: #### 2026 Acquisition Activity (Unaudited)
paras.zh: #### 2026 年收购活动（未经审计）

paras.en: On May 18, 2026, the Company acquired Stainless Software, Inc., to advance developer experience and agent connectivity. This acquisition was primarily funded by shares of the Company’s Class A common stock with fair value of $295 million. The total purchase price of $306 million consisted of $12 million cash and cash equivalents, $65 million of intangible assets, $24 million of other net liabilities, and $253 million of goodwill. Goodwill primarily relates to expected synergies and assembled workforce and is not expected to be deductible for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
paras.zh: 2026 年 5 月 18 日，公司收购了 Stainless Software, Inc.，以推进开发者体验与智能体连接能力。该收购主要以公司 A 类普通股股份提供资金，公允价值为 $295 million。总购买价格为 $306 million，包括 $12 million 现金及现金等价物、$65 million 无形资产、$24 million 其他净负债以及 $253 million 商誉。商誉主要与预期协同效应和已组建的员工团队相关，预计不可用于美国联邦所得税目的的扣除。

paras.en: The fair value of equity issued was determined based on the estimated fair value of the Company’s Class A common stock immediately prior to the acquisition and includes 8.6 million shares of Class A common stock issued to Bun stockholders and a number of replacement options to purchase shares of the Company’s Class A common stock issued to continuing employees that are subject to service-based vesting conditions over a three-year period, of which a portion was attributable to pre-combination services and therefore included within the total consideration noted above.
paras.zh: 已发行权益的公允价值根据紧接收购前公司 A 类普通股的估计公允价值确定，包括向 Bun 股东发行的 8.6 million 股 A 类普通股股份，以及向持续任职员工发行的若干可购买公司 A 类普通股股份的替代期权，该等期权须遵守三年期内基于服务的归属条件，其中一部分归属于合并前服务，因此计入上述总对价。

paras.en: Equity issued excludes 1.6 million shares of Class A common stock held back and not legally issued, which serve as partial security for the sellers’ general representation and warranty obligations. The holdback shares are subject to an 18-month holdback period, after which any remaining shares will be released to the former Bun stockholders, net of any shares necessary to satisfy breaches of the sellers’ general representations and warranties or other post-closing adjustments.
paras.zh: 已发行权益不包括被暂扣且未合法发行的 1.6 million 股 A 类普通股股份，该等股份作为卖方一般陈述与保证义务的部分担保。暂扣股份须遵守 18 个月的暂扣期，此后任何剩余股份将在扣除满足卖方一般陈述与保证违约或其他交割后调整所需的任何股份后，释放给前 Bun 股东。

paras.en: The holdback shares were recorded at their acquisition date fair value and classified as a liability within Other noncurrent liabilities on the consolidated balance sheets. The holdback liability will be settled in shares of Class A common stock and is recorded at fair value through its settlement date, with changes in fair value recorded to other income (expense), net on the consolidated statements of operations. The estimate of fair value of the holdback liability used both observable and unobservable inputs, specifically considering the price of the Company’s Class A common stock and the probability of payout at the end of the holdback period.
paras.zh: 暂扣股份按收购日公允价值入账，并在合并资产负债表上分类为其他非流动负债中的负债。暂扣负债将以 A 类普通股股份结算，并按公允价值计量至其结算日，公允价值变动计入合并经营报表上的其他收入（费用）净额。暂扣负债的公允价值估计使用了可观察和不可观察输入值，具体考虑了公司 A 类普通股的价格以及暂扣期结束时支付的概率。

paras.en: The purchase price was allocated on a preliminary basis to goodwill of $154 million and cash and cash equivalents of $17 million. Goodwill primarily relates to expected synergies and assembled workforce and is not expected to be deductible for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
paras.zh: 购买价格已初步分配至商誉 $154 million 以及现金及现金等价物 $17 million。商誉主要与预期协同效应和已组建的员工队伍相关，预计不可用于美国联邦所得税抵扣。

The incremental expense recognized as a result of these stock option modifications was not material.
paras.zh: - 2026 年 1 月，本公司对尚未达到一年悬崖归属期的全部未行权股票期权进行了修改，将悬崖归属期调整为六个月。因该等股票期权修改而确认的增量费用不重大。

paras.en: - A portion of the Company’s revenue is derived from contracts with various agencies of the United States Government (“USG”). On February 27, 2026, the President of the United States ordered the USG to stop using the Company’s models and the U.S. Department of War designated the Company as a Supply-Chain Risk to National Security (the “Risk Designation”). The Company may experience material revenue losses or business disruptions attributable to these events. On March 9, 2026, the Company filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California challenging the Risk Designation as unlawful and simultaneously filed a petition for review in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit. The U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California has largely granted summary judgment in the Company’s favor, ruling that the Department of War’s actions were retaliatory acts meant to punish the Company for speech protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution and violated the Company’s rights under the Due Process Clause under the Fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution, and that the Secretary of War’s Risk Designation, particularly with respect to 10 U.S.C. § 3252, violated the Administrative Procedure Act because they were in excess of statutory authority, contrary to law, and arbitrary and capricious. The defendants have filed a notice of appeal of the preliminary injunction. The D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals, however, in a 2-1 split decision, has denied the Company’s petition for review, ruling that the Department of War’s Risk Designation was proper under Federal Acquisition Supply Chain Security Act (“FASCSA”) Section 4713, and that the Company’s rights under the First Amendment and Due Process Clause of the Fifth Amendment were not violated. The Company is evaluating its next steps with respect to the D.C. Circuit’s decision.
paras.zh: - 本公司部分收入来自与美国政府（USG）各机构签订的合同。2026 年 2 月 27 日，美国总统下令美国政府停止使用本公司的模型，美国战争部将本公司指定为国家安全供应链风险（下称“风险认定”）。本公司可能因该等事件而遭受重大收入损失或业务中断。2026 年 3 月 9 日，本公司向美国加利福尼亚州北区联邦地区法院提起诉讼，主张该风险认定不合法，并同时向美国哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院提交复审申请。美国加利福尼亚州北区联邦地区法院已基本作出有利于本公司的简易判决，裁定战争部的行为属于报复行为，旨在惩罚本公司受美国宪法第一修正案保护的言论，侵犯了本公司在美国宪法第五修正案正当程序条款下的权利，且战争部长的风险认定（尤其是就 10 U.S.C. § 3252 而言）因超越法定权限、违反法律以及任意专断而违反了《行政程序法》。被告已就初步禁令提交上诉通知。然而，哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院以 2 比 1 的分歧裁决驳回了本公司的复审申请，裁定战争部的风险认定依据《联邦采购供应链安全法》（FASCSA）第 4713 条属适当，且本公司在美国宪法第一修正案和第五修正案正当程序条款下的权利未受侵犯。本公司正在评估针对哥伦比亚特区巡回上诉法院裁决的下一步措施。

paras.en: Item 14.Indemnification of Directors and Officers.
paras.zh: 第 14 项。董事及高级管理人员的补偿。

paras.en: Section 145 of the DGCL authorizes a corporation’s board of directors to grant, and authorizes a court to award, indemnity to officers, directors, and other corporate agents.
paras.zh: 《特拉华州普通公司法》第 145 条授权公司董事会给予、并授权法院判给高级管理人员、董事及其他公司代理人补偿。

paras.en: We expect to adopt an amended and restated certificate of incorporation, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and which will contain provisions that limit the liability of our directors and certain officers for monetary damages to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law. Consequently, neither our directors nor certain officers will be personally liable to us or our stockholders for monetary damages for any breach of fiduciary duties as directors or officers, as applicable, except liability for the following:
paras.zh: 我们预计将通过经修订和重述的公司章程，该章程将在本次发行完成前立即生效，其中将包含在特拉华州法律允许的最大范围内限制我们的董事及某些高级管理人员金钱损害赔偿责任的规定。因此，对于任何违反其作为董事或高级管理人员（视情况而定）的受信义务的行为，我们的董事及某些高级管理人员均不会对我们或我们的股东承担金钱损害赔偿的个人责任，但下列责任除外：

paras.en: - any breach of the director’s or officer’s duty of loyalty to our company or our stockholders;
paras.zh: - 董事或高级管理人员违反其对我们公司或我们股东的忠实义务的任何行为；

paras.en: - any act or omission not in good faith or that involves intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law;
paras.zh: - 任何非善意的作为或不作为，或涉及故意不当行为或明知违反法律的行为；

paras.en: - for our directors, unlawful payments of dividends or unlawful stock repurchases or redemptions as provided in Section 174 of the DGCL;
paras.zh: - 对于我们的董事，指《特拉华州普通公司法》第 174 条所规定的不合法支付股息或不合法回购或赎回股票；

paras.en: - any transaction from which the director or officer derived an improper personal benefit; or
paras.zh: - 董事或高管从中获取不当个人利益的任何交易；或

paras.en: - for our officers, any action by or in the right of the corporation.
paras.zh: - 对于我们的高管，指由公司提起或代表公司提起的任何诉讼。

paras.en: Any amendment to, or repeal of, these provisions will not eliminate or reduce the effect of these provisions in respect of any act, omission, or claim that occurred or arose prior to that amendment or repeal. If the DGCL is amended to provide for further limitations on the personal liability of directors or officers of corporations, then the personal liability of our directors and officers will be further limited to the greatest extent permitted by the DGCL.
paras.zh: 对本条款的任何修订或废止，均不会消除或减少本条款对在该等修订或废止之前发生或产生的任何作为、不作为或索赔的效力。如果《特拉华州普通公司法》经修订对董事或高管的个人责任作出进一步限制，则我们的董事和高管的个人责任将在《特拉华州普通公司法》所允许的最大范围内进一步受到限制。

paras.en: In addition, we expect to adopt amended and restated bylaws, which will become effective immediately prior to the completion of this offering, and which will provide that we will indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any person who is or was a party or is threatened to be made a party to any action, suit, or proceeding by reason of the fact that they are or were one of our directors or officers or is or was serving at our request as a director or officer of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, or other enterprise. Our amended and restated bylaws are expected to provide that we may indemnify to the fullest extent permitted by law any person who is or was a party or is threatened to be made a party to any action, suit, or proceeding by reason of the fact that they are or were one of our employees or agents or is or was serving at our request as an employee or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, or other enterprise. Our amended and restated bylaws will also provide that we must advance expenses incurred by or on behalf of a director or officer in advance of the final disposition of any action or proceeding, subject to limited exceptions.
paras.zh: 此外，我们预计将通过经修订和重述的公司章程细则，该等细则将在本次发行完成前立即生效，并将规定：我们将在法律允许的最大范围内，对任何因担任或曾担任我们的董事或高管，或应我们的请求担任或曾担任另一公司、合伙企业、合资企业、信托或其他企业的董事或高管，而成为或 threatened to be made a party to 任何诉讼、起诉或程序的人，予以赔偿。我们经修订和重述的公司章程细则预计将规定：我们可在法律允许的最大范围内，对任何因担任或曾担任我们的员工或代理人，或应我们的请求担任或曾担任另一公司、合伙企业、合资企业、信托或其他企业的员工或代理人，而成为或 threatened to be made a party to 任何诉讼、起诉或程序的人，予以赔偿。我们经修订和重述的公司章程细则还将规定：我们必须在任何诉讼或程序最终处置之前，先行支付董事或高管本人或代表其发生的费用，但有限的例外情形除外。

paras.en: Further, we have entered into or will enter into indemnification agreements with each of our directors and executive officers that may be broader than the specific indemnification provisions contained in the DGCL. These indemnification agreements require us, among other things, to indemnify our directors and executive officers against liabilities that may arise by reason of their status or service. These indemnification agreements also require us to advance all expenses incurred by the directors and executive officers in investigating or defending any such action, suit, or proceeding. We believe that these agreements are necessary to attract and retain qualified individuals to serve as directors and executive officers.
paras.zh: 此外，我们已与或将与我们的每位董事和执行官签订赔偿协议，该等协议的范围可能比《特拉华州普通公司法》所载的具体赔偿条款更为宽泛。该等赔偿协议要求我们（除其他事项外）就我们的董事和执行官因其身份或服务而可能产生的责任予以赔偿。该等赔偿协议还要求我们先行支付董事和执行官在调查或抗辩任何该等诉讼、起诉或程序中所发生的全部费用。我们认为，该等协议对于吸引和留住合格人士担任董事和执行官是必要的。

paras.en: The limitation of liability and indemnification provisions that are expected to be included in our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, amended and restated bylaws, and the indemnification agreements that we have entered into or will enter into with our directors and executive officers may discourage stockholders from bringing a lawsuit against our directors and executive officers for breach of their fiduciary duties. They may also reduce the likelihood of derivative litigation against our directors and executive officers, even though an action, if successful, might benefit us and other stockholders. Further, a stockholder’s investment may be adversely affected to the extent that we pay the costs of settlement and damage awards against directors and executive officers as required by these indemnification provisions. At present, we are not aware of any pending litigation or proceeding involving any person who is or was one of our directors, officers, employees, or other agents or is or was serving at our request as a director, officer, employee, or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, or other enterprise, for which indemnification is sought, and we are not aware of any threatened litigation that may result in claims for indemnification. Under Delaware law and our amended and restated certificate of incorporation, in the absence of a conflict of interest, no failure to satisfy the balancing obligations associated with our status as a PBC shall, for purposes of the exculpation, advancement, and indemnification rights of our directors and officers, constitute an act or omission not in good faith, or a breach of the duty of loyalty.
paras.zh: 我们预期将纳入经修订和重述的公司章程、经修订和重述的公司细则以及我们已与或将要与董事和高级管理人员签订的责任赔偿协议中的责任限制与赔偿条款，可能会使股东不愿就违反信义义务的行为对我们的董事和高级管理人员提起诉讼。这些条款还可能降低针对我们的董事和高级管理人员提起衍生诉讼的可能性，即使该等诉讼若胜诉可能使我们及其他股东受益。此外，若我们须按该等赔偿条款支付针对董事和高级管理人员的和解费用及损害赔偿金，股东的投资可能会受到不利影响。目前，我们并不知悉任何涉及现任或曾任我们董事、高级管理人员、员工或其他代理人，或应我们请求现任或曾任其他公司、合伙企业、合资企业、信托或其他企业董事、高级管理人员、员工或代理人且正寻求赔偿的未决诉讼或程序，亦不知悉任何可能导致赔偿请求的威胁性诉讼。根据特拉华州法律及我们经修订和重述的公司章程，在不存在利益冲突的情况下，就我们的董事和高级管理人员的免责、费用预付及赔偿权利而言，未能履行与我们作为公益公司（PBC）身份相关的平衡义务，不构成非善意的作为或不作为，亦不构成对忠实义务的违反。

paras.en: We have obtained insurance policies under which, subject to the limitations of the policies, coverage is provided to our directors and executive officers against loss arising from claims made by reason of breach of fiduciary duty or other wrongful acts as a director or executive officer, including claims relating to public securities matters, and to us with respect to payments that may be made by us to these directors and executive officers pursuant to our indemnification obligations or otherwise as a matter of law.
paras.zh: 我们已获得保险保单，根据该等保单的限制，为我们的董事和高级管理人员就其因违反信义义务或作为董事或高级管理人员的其他不当行为而被提出的索赔（包括与公开证券事项相关的索赔）所遭受的损失提供保障，并就我们根据赔偿义务或法律其他规定可能向该等董事和高级管理人员支付的款项向我们提供保障。

paras.en: Certain of our non-employee directors may, through their relationships with their employers, be insured or indemnified against certain liabilities incurred in their capacity as members of our board of directors.
paras.zh: 我们的某些非雇员董事可能通过其与雇主的关联关系，就其以董事会成员身份产生的某些责任获得保险保障或赔偿。

paras.en: The underwriting agreement to be filed as Exhibit 1.1 to this registration statement will provide for indemnification by the underwriters of us and our officers and directors for certain liabilities arising under the Securities Act or otherwise.

paras.en: None of the foregoing transactions involved any underwriters, underwriting discounts or commissions, or any public offering. We believe the offers, sales, and issuances of the above securities were exempt from registration under the Securities Act (or Regulation D or Regulation S promulgated thereunder) by virtue of Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act because the issuance of securities to the recipients did not involve a public offering, or in reliance on Rule 701 because the transactions were pursuant to compensatory benefit plans or contracts relating to compensation as provided under such rule. The recipients of the securities in each of these transactions represented their intentions to acquire the securities for investment only and not with a view to or for sale in connection with any distribution thereof, and appropriate legends were placed upon the stock certificates issued in these transactions. All recipients had adequate access, through their relationships with us, to information about us. The sales of these securities were made without any general solicitation or advertising.
paras.zh: 上述交易均不涉及任何承销商、承销折扣或佣金，亦不涉及任何公开发行。我们认为，上述证券的要约、销售和发行依据《证券法》第 4(a)(2) 条（或据此颁布的 D 条例或 S 条例）豁免《证券法》的注册要求，原因是向接收方发行证券不涉及公开发行；或者依据 Rule 701 豁免注册，原因是该等交易系根据补偿性福利计划或与该规则所规定的薪酬相关的合同进行。上述各项交易中证券的接收方均声明其仅为投资目的而取得该等证券，并非意图或为与任何分销相关的目的而出售该等证券，且该等交易中发行的股票证书均已加注适当图例。所有接收方均可通过其与我们的关系充分获取有关我们的信息。该等证券的销售未进行任何一般性招揽或广告宣传。

In the event that a claim for indemnification against such liabilities (other than the payment by the registrant of expenses incurred or paid by a director, officer, or controlling person of the registrant in the successful defense of any action, suit, or proceeding) is asserted by such director, officer, or controlling person in connection with the securities being registered, the registrant will, unless in the opinion of its counsel the matter has been settled by controlling precedent, submit to a court of appropriate jurisdiction the question whether such indemnification by it is against public policy as expressed in the Securities Act and will be governed by the final adjudication of such issue.
paras.zh: 就《证券法》项下产生的责任而言，若依据前述规定或其他规定允许对注册人的董事、高级管理人员及控制人进行赔偿，注册人已被告知，美国证券交易委员会认为此类赔偿有违《证券法》所表达的公共政策，因此不可执行。若该等董事、高级管理人员或控制人就正在注册的证券提出针对此类责任的赔偿请求（注册人支付该董事、高级管理人员或控制人在成功抗辩任何诉讼、起诉或程序中所发生或支付的费用除外），注册人将提交至具有适当管辖权的法院，由其裁定该等赔偿是否有违《证券法》所表达的公共政策，除非其法律顾问认为该事项已由具有约束力的先例解决，并将受该问题最终裁决的约束。
